Some OBD2 diagnostic tools identify the vehicle as "Besturn" or "Bestune" rather than "FAW X80" in their software — this is just a naming/branding variation in the tool's vehicle database (FAW's domestic brand name for this model line), not a sign of the wrong vehicle profile or a different underlying car. Reasoning given in the thread: the diagnostic software is somewhat rough around the edges and the vendor didn't bother adding the correct "R" or otherwise distinguishing the export badge — they lumped the whole FAW model lineup under "Bestune" to save the trouble 17181920. Expect to see "Besturn"/"Bestune" in fault-code readouts and treat it as equivalent to X80.

ECU physical location. The ECU is located under the dashboard, behind the instrument cluster panel/shroud, and is reachable from below the steering wheel after removing the panel — visible looking upward from the driver's footwell 2122. A second, independent thread confirms the same general area — "under the steering column, slightly to the right" — describing it as an easy reach 2324. On how much disassembly is required to get there: one owner reported not removing any lower/undershield components at all, only the hose/tubing routing in the way 25 — consistent with the "easy reach" framing above, though the amount of disassembly needed may vary by what other work is being done in that area at the same time.

General check-engine-light procedure. When the check-engine light appears with no other clue: (1) first disconnect the negative battery clamp for several minutes and see if the light clears on reconnection — a low-cost first step, though not a reliable fix on its own (compare the winter-autostart card, which found battery disconnect doesn't clear vehicle-specific DTCs the way an actual scan/clear does); (2) if the light persists, connect an OBD reader (an ELM327-type adapter with an app such as CarScanner) to read the actual error code; (3) if it still recurs after that, visit a service center for professional diagnosis and code-clearing — a check-engine light left un-diagnosed by guesswork can change how the car drives and increase fuel consumption 262728.

Fuel-quality as a check-engine trigger. One documented case traced the check-engine light to poor-quality fuel from a substandard filling station rather than any component fault. Fix: partially drain the tank and refill with better-quality fuel (95+ octane), or switch filling stations; the error typically needs roughly 20–50km of driving on clean fuel to clear on its own, and may re-trigger once and then clear for good after a further top-up of good fuel 29.

OBD adapter scope: engine-only visibility. ELM327-type OBD adapters (Bluetooth or USB) reliably read only the engine/ECU's own fault codes. Other control modules — transmission, ABS, body electronics/BCM — are not visible through the standard OBD-II port with these adapters; for those, professional/module-specific diagnostic equipment (see the Diagon/Launch/MUCAR BT200 options above) is needed 303132.

Diagzone Pro — confirmed to recognize the vehicle. Diagzone Pro diagnostic software/scanner reliably recognizes and supports the FAW Besturn X80, reading vehicle parameters and diagnostic codes — useful context given some dealerships report the X80 missing from their service databases entirely; a shop lacking a scanner with X80 in its database simply won't be able to diagnose the car at all 3334.

Budget option: ELM327 Bluetooth v1.5. An ELM327 v1.5 Bluetooth scanner with a dual-PCB design and a PIC18F25K80 chip supports basic FAW X80 diagnostics. Available on Ozon.ru for roughly 800 RUB as of April 2026. Reads and clears error codes via a companion smartphone app. Not a substitute for a professional scanner (e.g. for TPMS programming — see that card), but sufficient for basic home troubleshooting 35 3637.

X-DIAG PRO-3 reads hidden fault codes other scanners miss. Standard OBD scanners — including basic Foxwell units and generic OBD2 tools — cannot read all of the X80's fault codes. The X-DIAG PRO-3 scanner can retrieve hidden/manufacturer-specific codes invisible to those other tools, for example climate-sensor faults B150112, B150297, and B150C12, and parking-brake errors that appear after brake-pad service. Recommended specifically for chasing persistent electrical gremlins after water damage, where a generic scanner comes back clean but the symptom persists 3839.

docs.title: Component locations — electrical
docs.text:
Tags: #reference · #ecu

Quick-reference locations for electrical components, each a single community-reported data point.

Gateway module. The Gateway module (the electronic control unit responsible for vehicle communication/networking between other control modules) is located behind the glove box. Exact position/coordinates vary; check vehicle service documentation or search the Telegram group's media files for detailed photo guides if precise access instructions are needed 12.

Outside (ambient) air temperature sensor. Located on the radiator, in the upper-left corner when viewed frontally (i.e. on the driver's side, at the top of the radiator core) 34.

docs.title: Electrical connector disassembly technique
docs.text:
Tags: #connector · #airbag

To disconnect electrical connectors on the X80 (e.g. airbag-sensor connectors), locate the fixator tabs — especially any yellow-colored ones, which some connectors have several of. Carefully bend the fixator tabs outward to release the connector. On some connectors, a black lever/clip needs to be pried out/unhooked first before the fixator tabs release. Work gently to avoid damaging the connector housing 123.

docs.title: Part numbers and prices — electrical
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number · #price · #reference · #relay

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Quick-reference part numbers and prices for electrical-adjacent components, each a single community-reported data point.

Fuel filler door release cable. The fuel filler door (lyuchok) release cable/mechanism has OEM part number 5CA056880, available from suppliers such as Kitparts for approximately 2,461 RUB (RU market, Jan 2025) 1. Before replacing it, one owner asked how difficult the job is and whether the front seat needs to be removed for access — no answer confirming the access procedure was recorded in this thread 2.

Starter FC1118400A. Kitparts lists the FAW Besturn X80 starter FC1118400A from 9,477 RUB (RU market, Oct 2025) 3. See also Starter relay sticking — intermittent no-crank.

Relay 4290064. A 4-pin 12 V automotive relay sold in lots of 3 on Ozon is listed as number 4290064 and also marked FC01-67730-A 012 (1) -1H 12VDC; the thread does not say which circuit it serves or whether it fits the X80, so fitment is unverified 4.

CR2450 HR coin cell. A coin cell labelled CR2450 with the HR suffix is cold-resistant; the thread does not name the device it powers. A member replaces such cells himself for ~80 RUB each (RU market, Jul 2026), while a service quoted ~1,500 RUB for four cells plus about two hours of labour (RU market, Jul 2026) 56.

docs.title: Quick facts — electrical
docs.text:
Tags: #coolant · #reference

Single-fact community reports that don't warrant their own page.

Coolant color specification. The X80 uses red-colored antifreeze/coolant. Red and green antifreeze types should not be mixed — they are built on different chemical bases and mixing them can cause compatibility problems within the cooling system. When topping up or replacing coolant, use red coolant and keep the color/type consistent throughout the system rather than switching types 1.

Factory-applied window tint film. The X80 comes from the factory with a light tinting film already applied to the windows. This is original equipment, not an aftermarket installation — owners who notice it and wonder whether a previous owner tinted the car can be reassured it left the factory this way. The film shows up as a slight ribbed texture visible under certain light conditions 23.

docs.title: No common chassis ground in X80 wiring
docs.text:
Tags: #wiring

The FAW X80's electrical system does not use a single common chassis/body ground point for all circuits, unlike many vehicles where accessories can simply be grounded to any convenient metal point on the body. Both the positive (+) and negative (-) power lines must be run independently, all the way, to each electrical component. This matters most in practice for anyone installing LEDs or other accessories: you cannot rely on grounding to a single nearby chassis point the way you might on other cars — a complete positive and negative circuit has to be wired to each accessory individually, or it may not work reliably or at all 1.

docs.title: ELM327 Bluetooth adapter — setup and X80 coverage
docs.text:
Tags: #elm327 · #obd · #diagnostics · #scanner

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

A standard ELM327 Bluetooth adapter is the cheapest way to read live data on the X80, but it sees only part of the car. For the wider tool comparison see ECU diagnostic tools — Diagon/Launch vs OBD, Diagnostic tools: USB endoscope and VD70Lite OBD2 and DIAGZONE PRO diagnostic software.

What it can read on the X80. On the pre-restyle X80 a standard ELM327 reads only the engine ECU (ЭБУ). On the restyle car it also reads the automatic gearbox (АКПП); one owner saw a gearbox fault logged after a low-battery-voltage event that the dashboard never showed. Clearing a gearbox fault requires the engine to be switched off. One member claims an ELM327 cannot see the car's data at all, so results are reported as inconsistent 123.

Live-data example. A cheap ELM-type scanner app shows fuel trims, MAP and the O2 sensor. A video frame at idle shows engine load 23.9 %, coolant 90 C, short-term fuel trim -0.8 %, long-term fuel trim 0.8 %, intake manifold absolute pressure 33 kPa and bank-1 O2 sensor 0.115 V; the same thread notes that a DiagZone-based scanner costs more than about 4,000-5,000 RUB (RU market, Feb 2026), a lower bound rather than a quote 456.

Product listed. DriveSync Pro ELM327 OBD2 v1.5 (Bluetooth 5.1, PIC18F25K80 chip, Android and iOS) is listed on Ozon as an adapter for reading the X80; no price was given and no one reported using it 7.

Manual specifications (ELM 327 Bluetooth, Shenzhen JiaWei Technology). Supply 12 V, current up to 150 mA, operating temperature -25 to +40 C, dimensions 87 x 48 x 25 mm, warranty 12 months from sale. OBD-II protocols: ISO 9141-2, ISO 14230-2 (KWP2000), SAE J1850 VPW, SAE J1850 PWM and ISO 15765-4 CAN. It presents a Bluetooth virtual COM port with default pairing name ELM327 (or OBDII) and PIN 1234. The manual also names an ELM 327 Bluetooth Mini; only the standard model has LED indicators 8.

Pairing steps from the manual. Plug the adapter into the OBD-II socket and make sure Bluetooth is on in the device, search for "ELM327" (or "OBDII") and pair with PIN 1234. On a PC install the Bluetooth chipset driver, find the outgoing COM port in the driver settings (or create one for "ELM327"), tick "connect automatically" if offered, and enter that outgoing port in the diagnostic software. On Android go to Settings > Wireless networks > Bluetooth, pair "ELM327", start the diagnostic app, choose a Bluetooth connection and assign ELM327 as the paired device. The software is not supplied: the user has to find and install it 8.

docs.title: Engine cranks but won't start — diagnostic checklist
docs.text:
Tags: #fuel-pump · #ignition · #immobilizer

This card covers the scenario where the starter does crank the engine but it fails to actually start — distinct from the no-crank-at-all scenarios covered in starter-relay-no-crank.md (thermal relay sticking) and no-crank-rke-relay-harness-damage.md (RKE permission-signal path).

Three common causes, in a sensible check order:

  1. Fuel system failure. Check fuel-pump operation and fuel pressure at the rail first — a pump that isn't running or delivering pressure will crank-but-not-start every time.
  2. Spark failure. Inspect spark plugs and ignition-coil function if fuel checks out.
  3. Immobilizer. If the immobilizer fails its check, the starter will crank normally but the engine gets no spark and the fuel pump won't engage — this can look identical to a fuel or ignition fault at first glance, so don't rule it out just because cranking sounds normal.

Recommended diagnostic order: start with fuel-pump operation and fuel pressure, then spark-plug condition, before assuming a deeper mechanical or immobilizer-specific problem 1234.

docs.title: EPB (electronic parking brake) issues
docs.text:
Tags: #parking-brake · #fuse · #connector · #water-ingress · #glonass

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

EPB error from a shared EPB/GLONASS connector short. A separate case: an EPB error was caused by a failed connector in the comfort module, with corroded/shorted yellow and blue wires — this connector was shared between the EPB circuit and the GLONASS block under the driver's seat. After rewiring and isolating the short, the parking brake worked normally again. This points to a design weakness: using one dual-function connector for both EPB and the GLONASS emergency-call system (see the GLONASS card) means a fault in one can present as a fault in the other 1 2.

Two related EPB (electric parking brake) failure patterns are reported.

Repeatedly blown 5A fuse. Symptom: the EPB's fuse keeps blowing every time the electric parking brake is activated, leaving the parking brake non-functional 3. Cause: moisture/corrosion in the connector located under the driver's seat 456. Fix options: (1) replace the connector block with a fresh set of male/female pins and proper sealing grommets — one owner did this by simply buying a replacement connector pair ("колодка с папой и мамой") with a sealing collar rather than trying to repair the corroded original 4; (2) if the connector itself isn't salvageable, replace the entire brake module. Related procedure for setting the electric parking brake noted in this thread: hold the button while the engine is running, then turn the engine off, and leave the key in the lock/off position.

EPB warning light after road impacts (bumps/potholes). A separate symptom: the EPB warning light can illuminate after hitting bumps or potholes, sometimes together with the airbag warning light triggering from the same kind of road impact 7. Troubleshooting sequence: (1) check and clean the electrical contacts under the driver's seat — the same general area implicated in the blown-fuse case above 89 10; (2) inspect all ABS sensor connections for corrosion or loose wires, since ABS-sensor faults were flagged as a contributing area for similar warning-light triggers in this thread 11. Diagnostic note: this may be a firmware/program glitch specific to the restyle (facelift) model requiring a scanner to properly diagnose the underlying EPB system fault rather than a purely mechanical/connector issue 12. Also note: pre-restyle models are described as generally more prone to sensor faults in winter, which is a relevant seasonal risk factor even if not the direct cause in a given case. Important limitation: simply disconnecting the battery does not clear this fault on its own if the underlying contacts are intermittent/marginal rather than fully failed — contact cleaning is needed in addition to any reset attempt.

Disabling the EPB on a lift — the correct engine shutdown sequence. A separate, non-fault-related procedure worth documenting here: on restyle (facelift) models with an electronic handbrake, raising the car on a lift requires a specific shutdown sequence to prevent the EPB from automatically re-engaging when the engine is cut, which would otherwise clamp the rear wheels while they're off the ground. Procedure: (1) shift the transmission to Neutral; (2) press and hold the brake pedal; (3) while still holding the brake pedal, press and hold the electronic parking-brake button; (4) turn off the engine while still holding the button; (5) only then release the brake pedal. Skipping this sequence (e.g. shutting off the engine normally) causes the EPB to engage automatically the moment the engine dies, defeating the point of having the car up on a lift 131415.

EPB stops engaging after brake-pad replacement — caused by ignition being on during caliper work. A specific trigger pattern distinct from the connector-corrosion cases documented above: if the electronic parking brake stops engaging right after a brake-pad job, the cause is having the ignition on while working on the caliper (the EPB motor can end up mid-travel/out of sync when the caliper is manipulated with power live). Recovery procedure: (1) disconnect the battery negative terminal for 2-3 minutes, then reconnect; (2) turn the ignition on and shift to Park; (3) pull the parking-brake button repeatedly while holding it up until it engages. If that doesn't work, read and clear ECU error codes with a diagnostic tool. Park on a flat surface while doing this recovery, to avoid transmission strain when the brake re-engages 16171819.

EPB shows an ERB error and won't engage — rear pads hold by mechanical pressure alone. Another EPB failure pattern reported: an ERB error appears and the electronic parking brake won't engage, leaving the rear pads holding the car only via whatever mechanical clamping pressure remains (not actively engaged). Troubleshooting sequence: (1) have a dealer attempt a brake-adaptation reset; (2) reset via battery disconnect (10 minutes); (3) check the fuses under the driver-side footwell panel; (4) if none of that resolves it, suspect a BCM (body control module) fault. On restyled models, the EPB control block is located under the cargo-area trim on the driver side — useful to know when accessing it for inspection 2021222324252627 2829303132.

docs.title: ESP warning light from clock spring fault
docs.text:
Tags: #esp · #diagnostics

An ESP warning light can be caused by a faulty steering column spring ("подрулевая спираль" / clock spring) — a ribbon-like wire harness located under the steering wheel that connects the wheel buttons, airbag, and horn circuits. When this component fails or a connector develops an intermittent contact, it can flicker on and off ("то потухнет то погаснет") and generate false error codes further downstream, including ESP faults.12

Diagnosis requires a scanner capable of reading FAW-specific codes — community members mention Diagon or Launch scanners with FAW firmware — to identify the specific fault code before deciding on a fix.12

docs.title: ESP/traction-control "drunk road" warning
docs.text:
Tags: #esp · #abs

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Additional causes and fixes (ESC light specifically). Beyond the wheel-spin trigger and firmware fixes above, the ESC warning can also be caused by: (1) dirt/mud contamination on the ABS sensors from off-road driving or poor road conditions; (2) loose wiring shaken by suspension vibration; (3) in some cases, an aftermarket radio installation with improper grounding affecting the ESC module. Suggested checks in order: visually inspect all four ABS sensors for dirt/damage; check all connections; if the light appeared right after a radio replacement, revisit that installation's grounding. A diagnostic scanner is recommended; without one, a professional diagnostic visit is the fallback 12345678 910.

Multiple owners report an ESP/traction-control warning light — nicknamed "drunk road" (пьяная дорога) after the on-dash slippery-road icon — firing after wheel-spin events, sometimes together with an automatic parking-brake engagement. Reported triggers: backing up with the wheel at full lock while spinning the wheels 111213; accelerating hard from a standstill in 1st–3rd gear on snow/gravel causing wheel slip 14151617; and sliding/skidding at speed 18. This is largely normal ABS/ESP operation on low-traction surfaces — the "drunk road" indicator lights up as part of the stability system reacting to detected slip, and the felt handbrake intervention is usually less prominent than expected 1619. Disabling ESP via its dashboard button reduces false activations and lets the wheels spin more freely, which some owners deliberately do on inclines or in sand/snow 2021. Tire tread/compound appears to affect sensitivity — some owners report no issue at all under similar conditions 22 2324.

Light can persist after triggering until cleared. Fixes reported: a firmware update flashed via USB resolves it permanently on some units, with firmware files circulated in the community 25262728 29; disconnecting the negative battery terminal overnight also resolved it for some 3031; a full ECU reflash at a service center is another documented fix, at roughly 1500 RUB just to read the error code (RU market, December 2024) 323334. Alternative causes raised for a stuck/lit indicator specifically (as opposed to the transient wheel-spin trigger): incorrect brake-pad installation affecting the hill-hold function, or a malfunctioning tire-pressure sensor 29.

Conflict: the exact mechanical trigger and the most reliable fix are both disputed — reported fixes (battery reset vs. rewiring by an electrician vs. full ECU reflash) worked for different owners, suggesting more than one underlying cause depending on trim/configuration 3536 37.

ESP error after steering-wheel replacement — clearable with a Launch tool. A Launch X431 diagnostic tool can read X80 parameters and clear ESP error codes that appear on base-model vehicles after a steering-wheel replacement. This is a practical workaround where local service centers lack full dealer-level diagnostic capability 3839.

Steering-angle-sensor false error at certain steering angles — likely a self-check quirk, not a real fault. A warning light/error code can appear at certain steering angles (especially mid-turn), which looks like sensor self-check behavior specific to early ownership: it beeps continuously on the very first startup, then behaves differently on subsequent startups. One way to sanity-check whether it's a real fault: drive slowly next to a wall/straight reference and see whether the error clears on its own. One experienced member's advice: avoid buying replacement steering-angle sensors from Ozon, as they're considered unreliable 404142434445.

ESP light after multimedia/head-unit replacement — steering-angle calibration loss. A distinct trigger from the "drunk road" cases documented elsewhere in this card: the ESP warning light often comes on after a multimedia (head) unit replacement on 2018+ models. Root cause: the ECU loses its steering-angle-sensor calibration during the swap. This is not a mechanical failure — the fix is to have a certified technician run a steering-angle-sensor calibration through diagnostic software, or update the comfort-module firmware 46474849505152.

"Slippery road" warning — unequal tire pressure or ESP miscalibration. Another ESP-adjacent warning, "slippery road" (скользкая дорога), has two leading causes: (1) unequal tire pressure between wheels — the most common cause, check all four pressures first; (2) ESP sensor miscalibration. Troubleshooting: turn the steering wheel hard right then hard left (a basic recalibration procedure) and verify all four tire pressures are equal. If the warning persists after both checks, official service is needed for a proper ESP recalibration 53545556.

docs.title: Wiring diagram (EWD) circuits and connectors
docs.text:
Tags: #wiring · #reference · #can-bus · #airbag

Components, connectors and signal lines read from the factory wiring-diagram (EWD) pages shared in the group. The text extracted from the PDFs is layout-scrambled, so connector pin-to-wire mapping is mostly not recoverable; use the PDF itself for exact pin work. For fuse ratings see Wiring diagram (EWD) fuses and relays.

Gateway and CAN networks (page 1113). The gateway control unit R25 (20-pin connector, pins 1-10 and 11-20) bridges four CAN-H/CAN-L pairs named Diagnosis, Comfort, PT (powertrain) and INFO. Pin pairs visible in the text are 1/11, 2/12, 3/13, 5/15 and 6/16, but which pair belongs to which bus cannot be recovered from the extraction. Modules cross-referenced on the page: diagnostic interface, PKE controller, A/C control unit, BCM, audio, combination meter, EPB actuator, airbag control unit, ABS/ESP, reversing radar, tire pressure alarm, panoramic view monitor and the three ECUs (pages 1101-1122) 1.

Generator and charging (page 1112). Battery feed through Si13 (125 A) and generator fuse Si71 (175 A). Generator connectors by engine - 2.0L: E1 generator, E14 generator A, E42 generator; 1.8T: E40 generator power source, E34 generator excitation, E41 generator and a generator adjuster; 1.8TD: E51 generator, E65 generator power source, E52 generator excitation. Feeds go to the ECUs (pages 1101-1103) and the combination meter (page 1120) 2. See also Alternator replacement.

Ground points (page 1116). Ground points G1-G25 are listed with the consumers bonded to them and the connector pin after "#": engine hood switch 2#, ESP/start-stop OFF switch 1#, low and high horn 2#, front wiper motor 5#, rear wiper motor 1#, headlights left/right 6# and 8#, fuel pump 4#, electric vacuum pump (1.8T) 1#, electric water pump (1.8T and 1.8TD) 2#, ABS/ESP control unit 13# and 38#, tire pressure alarm 16#, EPB actuator 1#, driving recorder 1# and 7#, sunroof unit 10#, rain sensor 2#, diagnostic interface 4# and 5#, driver seat heating cushion 2#, luggage-compartment lock 1# and 3#. G3, G4, G5, G8, G10 and G11 are drawn per engine (2.0L, 1.8T, 1.8TD) but their exact mapping is garbled 3. This is the diagram behind the community observation in No common chassis ground.

Immobilizer / anti-theft (page 1118). The anti-theft controller is split into connectors I32 (controller A, pins 1-8) and I33 (controller B, pins 1-3); the engine immobilizer coil is I40 (pins 1-3, wires B/Y and L/O). Signal lines SL, IM-H and IM; references to gateway unit pins 129 and 130, ECU(2.0L) pin 15, diagnostic interface pin 133 and the combination meter (page 1120) 4. Compare Immobilizer antenna coil winding.

Keyless entry and start, PKE (page 1119). PKE controller with connector pins A1-A40; PKE antennas A and B, antennas 1-4 and sensing antennas 5 and 6; request switches (outer and inside) at the front door handles; engine switch, electrical steering-column lock (I27), smart key (remote controller) and immobilizer coil. Fuses Si27, Si42, Si58, Si60 and Si66 are listed in the fuse card 5. Window and mirror controllers also talk to the PKE controller 6.

Tire pressure alarm (page 1106). The tire pressure alarm unit is connector R11 (pins 1-16) with a 5 V supply and CAN-H/CAN-L; related items are an RF antenna, LFI, transponder IC, power-source chip, ACC relay, IGN1/IGN2 relays and links to the gateway and PKE controller 7. For sensors, part numbers and programming see TPMS tire pressure sensors.

Parking radar (page 1111). Reversing-radar control unit R7; front sensors FF4 (L), FF5 (CL), FF6 (CR), FF7 (R); rear sensors RA5 (L), RA4 (CL), RA3 (CR), RA2 (R) (L = left, CL = centre left, CR = centre right, R = right); parking-radar switch, gateway (page 1113), PKE controller (page 1119) and combination meter; fuse Si59 "Meter" 5 A 8. See Parking sensor system.

BCM labels (page 1117, partial). Fuse and circuit labels legible in the extraction: Meter, Hazard Warning Light, Front Fog Light (FFL), Rear View Mirror Motor (RH and LH), Brake Light, Horn, BCM, Door Lock, BNT, Rear Wiper, BCM Washer Motor, Low Beam, High Beam, Small Light, Light Relay, TNS Relay, Dimmer Switch and Room Light; amperage tags cannot be matched to the names 9.

Page 1121 components. Cigarette lighter R35 (2-pin), backup power source R36 (2-pin) and inner rear-view mirror H3 (10-pin); the back-up light switch and relay are referred to the BCM (page 1117) 10. See Cigarette lighter and 12V outlet fuses.

Airbag system (page 1122). Airbag control unit connectors R14 (A4), R15 (A6) and R19 (A8); front airbags left I41 and right I11, driver airbag R16, front passenger airbag R13, curtain airbags left R28 and right R5; seat-belt pretensioners left R17 and right R2; driver-side collision sensor R18, right side collision sensor R1 and the seat-belt occupancy sensor (page 1123). The squib loops are labelled "Gas Generator" and "Short Circuiter". No test values are given; work on airbag circuits only per the service manual 11. See Airbag warning light stuck on.

Seats (page 1123). Driver: adjustment switch DS4, seat-back motor DS7, forward/back motor DS5, height motor DS3, heating cushion DS6, buckle switch DS1. Front passenger: adjustment switch FPS4, seat-back motor FPS6, forward/back motor FPS5, buckle switch FPS1, heating cushion FPS3, occupancy sensor FPS2. Heater relays C30 and C31 12.

Switch circuits (page 1125). ESP OFF switch, idle start-stop OFF switch, EPB switch, small-light dimmer switch, multi-function control panel, central door-lock switch, two shift switches, front and rear room-light switches, spiral cable, sunroof switch, parking-radar/panoramic-view switch and headlight-leveling switch; fuse Si59 "Meter" 5 A 13.

Power windows (pages 1126-1127). Five controllers: front window left (driver), outer rear-view mirror controller, front-passenger window controller and the two rear-door window controllers. The driver window motor shows UP/DOWN outputs on connector pins 5, 4, 12, 14, 15; other motors use FR10 (front passenger), RL5 (rear left) and RR5 (labelled as the front passenger door in the text, probably a typo for the rear right door). Mirror fold/unfold motors (left and right) are driven together with the PKE controller; BCM pins A1-A9 and B1-B14, connectors IC1, IC2, FL8 and FR10. Page 1127 ("single door") shows the same controller set, so its title probably refers only to the driver-door circuit. Both files are truncated in the extraction 614. See Power windows and remote functions.

docs.title: Wiring diagram (EWD) fuses and relays
docs.text:
Tags: #fuse-box · #relay · #reference · #ignition

The factory electrical wiring diagram (EWD, "electrical wiring diagram" pages 1101-1128, files Z001-Z027) shared in the group prints each fuse with an "Si" id, a name and a rating. The text extracted from these PDFs is layout-scrambled, so the pairings below are the ones where a label and rating sit together; on the engine pages (1101-1103, 1105) the pairing of ratings with circuits is not reliable and the fuse box in the car (or the fuse and relay map) must be used to confirm a position 1234.

Main and ignition feeds (repeated on every page). Si13 "Main Fuse" 125 A (battery feed); Si71 "Generator" 175 A; Si72 "Main Fuse" 175 A (the 1.8TD pages show both 175 A generator fuses); Si2 "IG KEY2" 40 A; Si35 "IG KEY1" 30 A; Si62 "Engine IG1" 5 A; Si26 "Engine B+" 10 A; Si1 "BNT" 40 A; Si59 "Meter" 5 A. The ignition switch (connector I34) is drawn with the positions (OFF), (ACC), (IG1), (IG2), (ST), (SL), (B1), (B2); the relay block I25/I26 carries IGN1 Relay 1, IGN2 Relay 2 and the ACC supply, with the ACC relay on connector B2 and IGN1/IGN2 on A2/A4 and A6/A3 (order as printed) 567. Engine tags on the diagrams are 2.0L, 1.8T and 1.8TD 6.

Circuit fuses read from page 1115 (Z015). Si9 "Medium Speed Fan" 40 A; Si11 "High Speed Fan" 30 A (the 1.8T page shows a 50 A "PWM Fan"); Si25 "Compressor" 10 A; Si36 "Fuel Pump" 20 A; Si37 "ECU2" 5 A; Si44 "Oxygen Sensor" 15 A; Si45 "Ignition Coil" 15 A; Si46 30 A (printed beside the oxygen-sensor and ignition-coil fuses); Si47 "Valve Body" 20 A; Si48 "ECU1" 5 A; Si52 "Audio" 25 A; Si53 "TCU" 15 A; Si55 5 A (shift valve, outer rear-view mirror, ignition-lock solenoid); Si56 "Cigarette Lighter" 15 A; Si57 "ABS/ESP" 5 A; Si58 "PKE/EPB" 5 A; Si60 "Audio/PKE" 5 A; Si61 "Backup Power Source" 15 A; Si63 "Airbag" 10 A; Si64 "Back-up Light" 10 A (relay R19); Si70 "Starter (SL)" 5 A (SL and automatic-gearbox starter circuit on the 2.0L) 8. Page 1119 adds the keyless-entry fuses Si27 "PKE2 (PK)" 25 A, Si42 "PKE1 (PK)" 10 A and Si66 "BCM/PKE" 5 A 9; pages 1120-1121 repeat Si56, Si59 and Si61 710; page 1122 shows Si63 "Airbag" 10 A 11. The ratings match the cabin and under-hood diagram (fuel pump 20 A, TCU 15 A, airbag 10 A, audio 25 A, ignition coil 15 A) 12.

Relays. R2 "Main Relay" (contacts 87/30); R10 "Starter Relay" and R6 "Starter Additional Relay" drive the starter; R17 "Fuel Pump Relay"; R1 "A/C Compressor Relay"; R19 back-up light relay; on the 2.0L page medium-speed and high-speed fan relays; on the 1.8T page R10, R17, R20 and R21 sit beside the electric water pump, PWM fan, fuel pump and compressor relays; the 1.8TD page lists R2, R10 and R17-R21 with a supercharger label 1238. ECU pin references: fuel pump relay R17 - ECU(2.0L) 70#, ECU(1.8T) 41#, ECU(1.8TD) C_D1# and C_Q3#; main relay R2 - ECU(2.0L) 45#, 44#, 63#, 14#, ECU(1.8T) 5#, ECU(1.8TD) C_F1#; starter - ECU(1.8TD) C_B2#, C_G3#, C_H4#, ECU(1.8T) 22#, 10#, 58#, 13#, ECU(2.0L) 77#, 56#, 52#, plus pin 2# of the select-position switch (automatic) or neutral switch (manual gearbox) 8. Front seat heater relays are C30 (left) and C31 (right) with terminals 30, 85, 86, 87 13.

Per-page notes. Page 1101 (2.0L ECU) shows a 125 A main fuse (Si13), IG KEY2 40 A, IG KEY1 30 A and relays R2, R10, R12, R16, R17 1. Page 1102 (1.8T) adds the electric water pump, PWM fan, fuel pump and compressor relays and the BCM, A/C control unit, PKE controller, gateway and generator control units 2. Page 1103 (1.8TD) adds the electric vacuum pump, intake OCV, DCDC converter and ESP/start-stop units 3. Page 1105 (automatic gearbox, "3rd-generation transmission") shows the back-up light relay, battery sensor, combination meter, PKE controller and gateway 4. Page 1106 (TPMS) lists a 5 A meter fuse beside the main and IG KEY fuses 14.

docs.title: Fog light installation methods
docs.text:
Tags: #fog-light · #led · #installation

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Installing fog lights without full bumper removal (DIY shortcut): carefully cut rectangular openings in the bottom bumper panel, insert the fog light assemblies, and secure the cutout pieces back in place with self-tapping screws. Wiring is routed through the existing bumper openings. This avoids unnecessary A-pillar or fender disassembly 12.

BI-LED fog light module retrofit (Lada Vesta-compatible): BI-LED fog light modules compatible with the Lada Vesta have been successfully installed on the pre-facelift X80. The modules give even lighting with good brightness, and owners report stable operation after 1+ year with no degradation. Installation requires removing the original fog light housing; the modules are available through the Ozon marketplace 345678910111213141516171819.

Fog lamp installation with factory lever control (facelift vs pre-facelift wiring differs): a complete fog lamp installation guide is available on Drive2 (Part 1): https://www.drive2.ru/l/582439072975448486/. The factory setup uses a lever control mounted below the steering wheel. Pre-facelift base-trim models may lack the wiring/connectors entirely; facelift models require a different connector configuration than pre-facelift models — check which generation's harness is present before ordering parts 2021222324.

Fog light control button — restyle variant: some restyle X80 models (2018+) have a non-factory fog light control button installed by previous owners. On restyle models with genuine fog lights that activate together with the parking lights, this custom button can provide independent on/off control of the fog light separate from the parking lights 25262728.

Replacing the fog light bulb without removing the bumper: access to the fog light bulb on a restyle X80 (if fog lights were installed by a previous owner) is possible through the air-filter area without fully removing the bumper. The space is tight but sufficient to manipulate the tool/bulb. Bumper removal isn't required, though it may make the job easier 29303132.

Installing fog lights into pre-existing bumper slots (no modification needed, 2017–2021): on trims that lack factory fog lights, the front bumper already has rectangular slots below the headlights ready to accept them — no cutting or permanent modification is required, unlike the cut-opening method described above. Compatible fog light sets for the 2017–2021 X80 are available on both AliExpress and Ozon 3334353637.

docs.title: Fog light LED bulb fitment (H11 socket)
docs.text:
Tags: #fog-light · #fitment

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Fog-light switch: Chinese-restyle vs Russian-domestic wiring difference. Separate from bulb fitment, the fog-light switch differs by market variant: the Chinese-restyle X80 has front AND rear fog-light control on the steering-column switch stalk, with a separate connector plug for it; the Russian-domestic version's stalk only controls the front fogs. This is a wiring/harness difference at the switch, not a difference in the fog-light motor/hardware itself — front-wheel-drive models use the same physical fog-light motor regardless of switch variant. For anyone wanting rear-fog control the Russian-domestic stalk doesn't provide, aftermarket options exist: full AliExpress fog-light kits with add-on buttons (non-OEM appearance) 1234 56789.

The fog lights use an H11 socket, so an H11-based LED bulb is the correct starting point 10. However, many LED bulbs sold generically as "H11" are actually designed for headlight (low-beam) housings rather than fog lights, and won't physically fit: their lens/heatsink shroud extends to roughly 20mm in diameter, while the fog-light housing opening is only about 18mm — close enough on paper to cause confusion when ordering, but too large in practice 1112. A specific failure mode reported: bulbs bought as "H11" turned out to be H11 LED units with an integrated lens, meant for headlight/high-beam-style projector housings — what's actually needed for a fog light retrofit is a plain diode-style H11 bulb without that lens assembly 13. Fog light housing depth is 84mm — check bulb length against this before buying, in addition to the diameter issue 1415. Practical advice: measure/compare diameter and length carefully (or search specifically for "fog light" LED variants rather than generic H11 headlight LEDs) before ordering, and be prepared to return a bulb that doesn't physically fit even though the socket type matches.

Bulb type by model year — front vs rear, pre- vs post-facelift. Consolidating community reports on socket types: pre-facelift models use H11 for the front fog lamps and W16W for the rear fog lamps 16. Post-2020 facelift models also use H11 for the front; some facelift trims may use P21W instead, but H11-based universal aftermarket alternatives are reported to give noticeably better illumination than the factory fog bulbs regardless of which stock type your car has 1718192021. LED upgrade kits for these sockets are widely available on AliExpress, with discounts up to roughly 54% reported 20.

Aftermarket fog lamps with integrated lens (ZMB brand). Beyond straight bulb swaps, some owners have upgraded to complete ZMB-brand fog lamp units with an integrated lens (giving a sharp light/dark cutoff line rather than a diffuse beam), still using the H11 bulb type and fitting directly into the factory fog-light housing. Reported benefit: noticeably improved visibility in dark conditions, especially illuminating the area just ahead of the bumper that factory fogs light poorly 222324.

Rear fog light activation on restyled 2019+ automatic models — no separate switch. Directly extending the switch-difference notes above: on restyled (2019+) automatic-transmission X80s, the rear fog lights are not controlled by a separate button — activation is via rotating the ring element on the steering-column light stalk itself to its maximum position. This only works when low beams are already switched on; if rotating the ring doesn't produce rear fog light, check the fuse next 252627282930. This resolves what otherwise looks like a missing feature — the control exists, it's just non-obvious (a rotatable ring rather than a discrete switch) if you don't already know to look for it.

Aftermarket LED fog-light options and "lensed" terminology confusion. LED fog lights can be successfully adapted to the X80. Regular diode LED fog lights (light pattern formed via an internal reflector, not a lens) are commonly sold at 30W, 50W, or 70W power levels; true lensed fog lights (with an external protruding or internal lens element that actually shapes the beam) are a separate product category. Some owners mounted lens-less LED flood units behind aftermarket housings; multiple owners confirmed 360°-type LEDs also fit in the fog-light housings. Brightness at 6000K (white) is excellent and may warm toward 4300K over time as the LEDs age. 30W units are the most common choice; 50–70W units are extremely bright 3132 3334353637383940 4142434445464748. Conflict: owners frequently debate whether their installed LED fog lights are genuinely "lensed" (линзованные) — most are actually reflector-based LEDs, not true lensed units; true lensed fog lights have a distinct external/internal lens element forming the beam, whereas reflector-based LEDs shape light purely via internal reflector geometry.

Fog-light bulb spec for the 2018 restyle: H11. The 2018-restyle X80 uses H11 halogen bulbs for the front fog lights. One owner found the previous owner had installed mismatched LED bulbs between the left and right fenders — the recommendation is to stick with standard H11 halogen, or if going LED, use a matched pair rather than mixed brands 4950.

Universal 70 W fog lamps (EAL, 5500K), September 2026. One owner fitted universal fog lamps (ПТФ, противотуманные фары) from EAL: 70 W, 5500K white, 12 V, 120-degree beam, listed on Ozon at ~2,131 RUB (RU market, September 2026; struck-through price 6,990 RUB), 365-day warranty. The brackets had to be improvised and the headlight levelling re-aimed to fit them 5152. Another owner warned that such bright white fog lamps blind oncoming drivers, while the installer says they do no harm when properly aimed 5352.

docs.title: Fog light part numbers (front and rear)
docs.text:
Tags: #fog-light · #part-number · #led

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Front fog lights (shared with FAW Besturn B50): FC025189X (right), FC025169X (left). For the X80 New (2018+): frame brackets 5CA250C1102 (right), 5CA250C2102 (left). LED lamp alternatives available from 460–580 RUB per lamp (RU market, April 2024), readily available from online retailers 123.

Fog light bezel pricing confirmation and light/dark variants: separately confirms the facelift (2018+) frame bracket/bezel part 5CA250C1102 noted above — available in both light and dark finish versions, priced around 1,200 RUB, from COOVE.ru and similar retailers. A comparable pre-facelift bezel is also available at similar pricing 45678.

Rear fog lamp: right-side part number 5CA0515L5A (red housing), used for an affected 2018 restyle model. Available through Russian auto-parts retailers such as kitzapchasti.ru 910.

Auto Mento H11 LED retrofit: aftermarket LED fog lights (Auto Mento H11 spec) sourced from Ozon (link: https://ozon.ru/t/vdK1bKB) work as a drop-in replacement for the stock halogen fog lights. Fitment requires 4 self-tapping screws (vs. 3 stock) and minor mounting-bracket adjustment. The LED version shows significantly improved brightness over stock halogen 1112131415.

Fog light fastener count differs stock vs. aftermarket: the stock fog light mounts with 3 self-tapping screws; aftermarket units (e.g. Auto Mento H11) need 4 screws, since mounting-hole positions differ between OEM and universal aftermarket housings. Fitment works with adjustment — using 4 screws holds better than 3, and the resulting gap/misalignment is minimal ("small displacement" after adjustment). Shims on the horizontal axis may be needed to center the beam properly 16171819202122232425.

Fog light physical dimensions (X80 vs. aftermarket): stock X80 fog light mounting dimensions — 8.5 cm inner lens diameter, ~10.5 cm outer height, 11.5 cm outer width at full assembly width, 15.5 mm cross-section/bracket depth. AliExpress-sourced aftermarket fog lights show a similar overall envelope but minor mounting-hole position differences (4-screw vs. stock 3-screw). Universal fog lights sold for Lada Priora/Gazelle do NOT fit the X80 due to different mounting-bracket geometry 26272829.

Front fog lamp bulb replacement without full bumper removal (restyle): on the restyle version, the bulb can be accessed without removing the whole bumper — left side: remove the air-filter housing; right side: pull back the fender liner or remove a trim panel. Takes minimal time compared to full bumper removal 3031.

Left fog light reliability issue (7-year ownership): one owner experienced repeated failures of the left fog light only over 7 years of ownership — the left side kept overheating and bulbs burned out, while the right factory light never needed replacement. Suggests either a heat/ ventilation problem or a wiring/connector issue specific to that side's circuit 3233343536.

Brightness comparison — LED retrofit vs. stock halogen: side-by-side testing of Auto Mento H11 LED fog lights against 7-year-old stock halogen units shows the LED version gives significantly brighter, whiter illumination and a more uniform beam, eliminating the yellowish halogen tint. A near/far beam-pattern video comparison after retrofitting both sides showed roughly equal intensity between them 14373839.

Cracked/chipped lens — temporary and permanent repair: a fog-light lens cracked/chipped by a road stone can be temporarily sealed with aquarium silicone sealant plus waterproof tape to keep water out until a proper replacement is sourced. Do not use a car wash/high-pressure spray until sealed — water entering the lamp housing through the crack causes a short circuit and an expensive lamp failure (700+ RUB); avoid turning the fog light on at all if the lens is compromised, since running it while cracked risks the lens shattering if water contacts the hot glass. Apply the sealant carefully and let it fully dry, then order a replacement lens as the permanent fix — some owners report success sealing small cracks with epoxy as well 40414243444546.

Rear fog lights — factory part number and sourcing: FAW factory part number for the rear fog light is 5CA1515M5 (restyle, 2018+) — separate from the right-side part 5CA0515L5A noted above; the two numbers likely correspond to different sides/positions of the housing. Non-OEM sources on Ozon are often cheaper than Yandex Market for the same part number; some vendors also offer circular (round-lens) fog-light variants. Price varies significantly for the same nominal part number across platforms — 1,200–2,700 RUB (RU market, June 2025) — so it's worth comparison-shopping. Pre-restyle and restyle parts differ in appearance despite similar part numbering 4748495051525354555657585960.

Rear fog light removal procedure (no bumper removal needed): (1) disconnect the two bolts at the fog-light housing; (2) detach the clips accessible from the inner panel; (3) remove the two bolts at the top of the assembly; (4) slide the fog light out. Replacement units (left rear: part 5CA1515M5) are available on Wildberries and on Avito as used parts. The lens cover is not sold separately — a cracked/damaged lens requires replacing the full assembly 61626364656667686970.

Pre-facelift fog light diameter (measured): standard pre-facelift X80 fog lights measure approximately 70 mm in diameter, as measured with a caliper. Useful for sourcing replacement fog lights or matching optics 7172.

Rear fog-lamp trim bezels — pre-restyled only, extremely rare (January 2026): rear fog-lamp trim rings/bezels (окантовка задних ПТФ) for the pre-restyled (first-generation) FAW X80 are an extremely rare OEM part. As of January 2026, one seller reported having the last unit available in Russia. Originally sourced from Taobao ~4 years prior for 3,800 RUB (RU market, January 2026); asking price for the piece: 3,000 RUB (RU market, January 2026) 73.

docs.title: Fog lights (PTF) — bulb replacement & install
docs.text:
Tags: #wiring

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Bulb replacement (pre-facelift X80): 1. Unclip the plastic frame around the fog lamp using a plastic spoon/lever tool. 2. Unscrew 3 bolts. 3. Pull the lamp unit out toward you. 4. Replace the bulb.

No bumper removal or wheel-well liner removal is required for this job. A YouTube guide is available: https://youtu.be/KtJ0d6EOrsg12

Full fog light installation (2019 Kaliningrad-assembled X80, no factory harness). This particular 2019 unit came from the factory with the relay and fuse pre-installed for fog lights, but no wiring harness — indicating the car is pre-wired at the infrastructure level for an optional fog-light upgrade even when the harness/lamps themselves aren't fitted.34

Installation procedure followed by the owner: purchased fog-light frames/housings and a switch button from AliExpress, then connected them to the existing pre-installed relay/fuse infrastructure. Labor cost for the installation: 5,000 RUB (RU market, April 2024).34

Caveat — dashboard indicator. After installation, the fog-light telltale/indicator light on the instrument panel was not functional on this particular install.3456 By contrast, another community member with a similarly aftermarket-installed setup reports their panel indicator does work7 — so indicator functionality may depend on the specific installation method or model-year variant, and is not guaranteed either way.

If your car has NO factory fog-light wiring at all — full custom-wiring DIY approach (2021 facelift, 2026-08 report). Unlike the pre-wired 2019 unit above, this owner (a 2021/facelift car) had no pre-existing relay/fuse/harness infrastructure for fog lights and had to wire everything from scratch. Parts used: - LED bulbs: H8/H10/H11/HB4 CANBUS, yellow-white, 2000 Lm, sold as a 2-piece set ("2Pcs 2000Lm CANBUS H8 LED Yellow White HB4 H10 H11 Led Fog Lights H16JP LED Bulb Car Driving Lamp for Toyota Skoda Ford Lada") — 1,529 RUB (2026-08-28, RU market, AliExpress, 30% discount applied). - Fog lamp assembly/frame: "For FAW Besturn X80 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 Car Front Bumper Fog Lamp Light Frame Cover Halogen Bulbs Auto Fog Lights Assembly", specific to the X80 2017–2021, includes blanking caps/covers to replace (needed since the bumper originally had halogen-bulb blanks) — 4,969 RUB (2026-08-28, RU market, AliExpress, 50% discount applied). - Switch: a plain button switch, DIY-wired to the fuse block, rather than sourcing/fitting the factory steering-column stalk switch — the owner explicitly chose not to hunt for the original 2021-model switch and instead ran their own wiring and button.

Procedure notes from the thread: the owner built their own wiring harness/loom ("коса" — cable run) from the fog lights to the fuse block, then routed wiring from the fuse block into the cabin to the button. The bumper did not need to be removed to complete this installation ("получилось без скидывания" — done without taking it off). The original bumper's bulb blanks/caps do need to be swapped for the fog-lamp-specific frame's caps.

Plug-and-play alternative (same market, same date). A complete kit is also available pre-bundled — "Передний бампер, противотуманная фара, рамка, крышка галогенных ламп, жгут проводов с переключателем for FAW Besturn X80 2017-2021" (bumper trim/frame + halogen-bulb caps + wiring loom + switch, all included) — 7,309 RUB (2026-08-28, RU market, AliExpress, 50% discount applied). Per a community member who did the custom build, this bundled kit costs more than buying the LED bulbs, fog-lamp frame, and switch separately — buying components individually works out cheaper.891011121314151617181920212223

docs.title: Fog/parking light fuse (5A) blowing
docs.text:
Tags: #fuse · #fog-light

WSM module as a third diagnostic path. For the case where rear fog lights don't illuminate and/or parking lights cut out when the rear fogs are engaged, a third module worth checking (alongside the fuse and rear door harness above) is the WSM (body control module variant) mounted on the driver-side door pillar. Access: peel back the rubber sill trim, remove a 10mm bolt securing the plastic cover, and the module is accessible behind it. Cleaning or reseating its connections has restored function in this scenario 12.

Symptom: fog lights and parking lights (габариты/противотуманки) not illuminating. Inspection found a blown 5A fuse supplying these circuits 345. Simple fix is to replace with a new 5A fuse. If the fuse keeps blowing (2+ times), investigate wire chafing in the rear (fifth) door's electrical harness — moisture ingress or the harness rubbing against something can short the circuit there, and this is called out as a known weak point 67. One owner also found loose connector contacts in the fuse block itself and recommends making sure contacts are clean and dry when replacing a fuse 89.

Same symptom, front bumper wiring instead of the rear-door harness. A separate case: front and rear parking lights plus the rear fog lights all stopped working together, while the turn signals kept working normally on the same circuit area — turn signals are wired independently from parking lights/headlights, confirmed by continuity-testing the fuses per the wiring diagram 101112. Diagnostic order: (1) check the fuse — note it may not be blown, since if the turn signals still work the fault could be downstream of a shared fuse; (2) if a blown fuse is found, look for wire chafing under the front bumper, along the bumper reinforcement bar — this is a recurring failure point separate from the rear-door harness case above 13.

docs.title: Front fog light (PTF) install — restyle wiring
docs.text:
Tags: #fog-light · #restyle · #relay

Restyle-generation X80 models come with complete factory wiring for several advanced features — including fog lights and parking sensors — pre-installed but left unpowered. The factory wiring is not cut or removed at the factory, it's simply not energized, which makes a later fog-light install significantly easier than wiring from scratch.

Installation steps. (1) A multi-position steering-wheel stalk (sourced from AliExpress) with 2 positions is needed to control front/rear fog lights from the wheel. (2) The relay needed for the fog circuit is already present in the electrical block — no need to source a separate relay. (3) A new 10-pin connector block with its own wiring harness is required; 3 of its pins already carry power for the DRL circuit, and the remaining spare pins are available for the fog lights. (4) The washer-fluid tank bracket needs to be modified with an angle grinder to make room for the new connector block. (5) The front bumper needs to come off for full wiring access, though careful work without a full bumper removal is possible if the wiring is otherwise accessible. (6) Ground connection is taken from the vehicle body. A service shop can do the install if you'd rather not DIY it. Detailed installation photos and documentation from a forum member ("ГАЗЛОИД") on the FAW X80 forum are available for reference. Before buying any other components, verify the correct relay is actually already present in your car's electrical block 1234567 891011121314 15.

LED daytime-running/"walking" light can be set to switch off with the turn signal, and sourcing options. A separate report adds a feature detail relevant to a fog-light install: the FAW X80 supports configuring the LED walking light (daytime running light) to deactivate whenever the turn signals are engaged, rather than staying lit throughout — useful to know when wiring a fog-light kit into the same area. On sourcing: fog lights themselves can be bought from AliExpress or similar marketplaces, with various bezel styles available in both light and dark trim finishes 161718192021.

Complete wiring kit. One owner bought a complete front fog-light wiring kit for a 2018 FAW Besturn X80 (CA4GD1) from AliExpress, and adds that any such harness can be assembled yourself as long as the connector at the bulb is the right one 2223. For bulbs and fitment see Fog light part numbers (front and rear).

docs.title: Battery warning at startup — fuel delay
docs.text:
Tags: #fuel-pump

A vehicle intermittently showed the battery warning light during the key-turn/startup sequence, then would go on to start normally. The warning appeared once at first, then sporadically (roughly once a week) 1. The owner's working theory, after ruling out an actual battery problem (since the light appeared only once per failed attempt and the car otherwise started fine), was the fuel delivery system — filter or fuel pump — not supplying fuel immediately on key-turn, rather than a real electrical/battery fault 2. Plan was to get an OBD scan and diagnostic check at an official dealer to confirm. Lesson for troubleshooting: a battery-warning light at startup doesn't always mean a battery/charging problem — intermittent, self-resolving occurrences are worth checking against fuel-delivery timing too.

docs.title: Fuel gauge stuck at empty after refueling
docs.text:
If the fuel gauge stays stuck at "empty" after adding fuel, the likely cause is that the fuel pump module's float mechanism is stuck mechanically or electrically disconnected 1. Suggested diagnostic procedure: (1) remove the fuel pump module assembly from the tank; (2) manually move the float up and down to verify it's mechanically free; (3) inspect the connectors, wiring, and ground point for corrosion or poor contact; (4) with the ignition on and the car in reverse, listen near the sensor for solenoid clicks, which indicates the electrical connection is live 2345. This can be tested without draining the full tank. A related report from the same owner: with all lights suddenly not working, a blown fuse and a possible water-damaged sensor (shorted after water ingress) were both suspected — the sensor float can sometimes be felt clicking under a finger if you press on it directly 6745.

Erratic jumping readings (not just stuck-at-empty) — loose fuel-pump connector. A related but distinct symptom: instead of sticking at empty, the gauge jumps erratically between empty and half-full, or gets stuck at inconsistent positions — reported even shortly after a new fuel pump was installed and driven for two weeks 8. Diagnosis found the pump itself tested fine (continuity end-to-end) 9, but the connector on top of the fuel pump module — accessed by lifting the rear seat — was loose 10111213. Fix: firmly press/reseat that connector; optionally apply sealant around the joint to prevent it working loose again over time 14. Diagnostic order recommendation: after installing a new pump, check this connector first if erratic readings appear — before assuming the new pump is defective or that ECU adaptation/relearning is needed 15. A useful external reference on this general fuel-pump-connector fault pattern: https://www.drive2.ru/l/559273462489679893/ 8.

Fuel-level gauge reading fluctuation — oxidized sender contacts. A separate symptom from the stuck-empty case: the fuel-level gauge read consistently lower than the tank's actual level. Cause: oxidized contacts on the fuel-level sender. Fix: clean the sender's contacts — the same underlying oxidation pattern also showed up on the trunk-button connectors (green corrosion) on the same car, suggesting a broader contact-corrosion tendency rather than a fuel-sender-specific defect. After cleaning, the gauge reading stabilized and read correctly. Side note on trip-computer accuracy: average fuel-consumption figures should be spot-checked against actual pump receipts, since the onboard computer under-reports by roughly 4–5% at a full tank 1617 18.

Related, lower-confidence report: an unspecified sensor "pops out" after ~5 minutes of driving. In the same conversation thread, a different, not-fully-identified sensor (possibly TPMS-related, not confirmed) was reported to trigger/pop an alert roughly 5 minutes into a drive. The suggested diagnostic approach mirrors the fuel-sender fix above: check the onboard computer for which sensor is triggering, locate its connector, and clean the contacts — the same oxidized-contact pattern documented throughout this card and the water-ingress card is the leading suspect for this kind of intermittent, unspecific sensor complaint 19202117 22.

Sensor location — inside the fuel tank. As a baseline reference: the fuel gauge sensor sits inside the fuel tank itself (part of the fuel pump module assembly, consistent with the diagnostic steps above). If the gauge reads incorrectly or fails to update, a sensor malfunction inside the tank is the most likely cause. Community reports describe the gauge occasionally resetting/glitching over time — this is considered a known design weak point on early X80 models rather than a one-off defect 2324252627.

Loose sender contact causing incorrect readings — a recurring complaint. A separate report of the same underlying weak point: the fuel-gauge sender's electrical contact works loose over time, making the gauge display an incorrect level — it appears to show something closer to "average consumption until the next gas station" rather than the tank's actual level. Fix: disassemble the sender and crimp the contact tight again. Multiple owners report hitting this same problem independently, reinforcing that it's a recurring design weakness rather than a one-off fault 282930.

docs.title: Fuel reserve warning light behavior
docs.text:
Tags: #warning-light

The fuel reserve indicator light — shown on the instrument cluster once roughly 70 km of estimated range remains — is triggered by the car's calculated remaining range, which is based on recent fuel-consumption history (the last 30–50 km driven), not by a fixed remaining-liters threshold 12. Practical consequence: the exact fuel level (liters) that triggers the light varies with driving style. Under urban driving with high consumption (~15 L/100km), the light comes on around 10–11 liters remaining; under highway driving at ~7–8 L/100km, it comes on around 5–7 liters remaining 34. Because the range estimate recalculates continuously from recent consumption, the light's on/off status can change mid-trip: e.g. exiting a city (high consumption) onto a highway (lower consumption) can cause the estimated range to climb back above the trigger threshold and the warning to clear itself, purely because the car recalculated based on the new driving pattern rather than because fuel was added 4.

Displayed range is a consumption-based estimate, separate from the tank float sensor. Consistent with the range-based trigger logic above: the fuel gauge display shows a calculated estimated driving range (e.g. "250 km remaining") derived from recent fuel-consumption history, not a direct read of the tank float sensor. Resetting the trip/consumption data via the steering-wheel buttons resets this calculation, which can make the displayed range jump because the car now assumes a different (fresh) consumption baseline. The physical fuel float sensor in the tank reads the actual liquid level but is a separate signal from what's shown as "range remaining" on screen — the two can appear to disagree without either being wrong 5678.

docs.title: Fuse box layout — pre-facelift vs facelift
docs.text:
Tags: #fuse-box · #pre-facelift · #restyle · #fog-light · #relay · #airbag

Fuse type. The X80's electrical panel uses mini-type fuses throughout 123.

Layout differs completely between generations. Pre-facelift and facelift X80 models have completely different fuse-box schematics and circuit layouts — generic schematics found online often don't match either variant exactly. The facelift fuse box has multiple power distribution blocks for the cabin, passenger side, and rear-passenger side circuits, with different amperage ratings across them. Reference diagrams circulate from Drive2.ru, but even those may not precisely match an individual vehicle's configuration — treat any diagram as a starting point, not gospel, and verify against the physical fuse-box labeling 45678.

Front fog-light fuse. Front fog lights (sometimes labeled as DRL on the fuse diagram) are protected by a 10A fuse in the engine-bay fuse box. Exact fuse location varies by year/model — cross-check against your fuse-box diagram or ask the community for your specific variant rather than assuming a universal slot number 91011 12131415.

Why removing different fuses has different effects. The fuse block contains multiple protective fuses feeding different circuits. Some circuits are powered before reaching their protective fuse ("preload" circuits), while others are powered only after the fuse — this is why pulling one fuse may kill only part of a system while pulling a main/master fuse kills all electrical power. Do not use fuse removal as a way to shut the vehicle down 1617.

Complete diagrams for both cabin and under-hood fuse blocks are available in group files. Confirming and extending the diagram-caution above: full fuse and relay diagrams exist covering (1) cabin fuse-block locations and amperage ratings, (2) engine-compartment fuse-block layout, and (3) power relay assignments. One reference image (подкапотный блок предохранителей) circulated in the community, detailing fuse locations, amperage ratings, and relay assignments including compressor relay, fan relays, engine control, transmission, lighting, and accessory circuits — as with the diagrams noted above, cross-check the specific labels against your own fuse box before relying on any single diagram 1819202122.

Full "Предохранители.pdf" fuse/relay table — cabin, under-hood, and under-hood relay blocks, with every label. A complete reference file ("Fuses.pdf"/"Предохранители.pdf") circulates in the group's shared files; a screenshot of it gives every labeled position in all three blocks, which corroborates and fills out the diagrams above in detail 2324: - Cabin fuse block: driver window 25A, audio system 25A, BCM (body control) 20A, TCU (transmission control) 15A, rear wiper 15A, cigarette lighter 15A, 12V power outlet 15A, airbag 10A, room lamp 10A, start/ ignition-lock 5A, ECU 5A, ABS/ESP 5A, PKE/EPB (keyless-entry electric handle) 5A, seat heating 5A, backup light 5A, meter/instrument-panel 5A, keyless-entry audio chime 5A, valve/mirror 5A, plus relays for the front and rear wiper motors. - Under-hood fuse block: main fuse 125A, compressor 40A, blower (heater fan) 40A, radiator fan 1 and fan 2 40A each, defrost 40A, BTN (misc. circuit protection) 40A, ABS/ESP-2 40A, power windows 30A, door lock (central locking) 30A, sunroof 30A, ignition coil 15A, ECM (engine control module) 15A, IG KEY 1/2 (ignition-key/keyless circuits) 15A each, hazard lights 15A, driver/passenger power-seat circuits 20A each, front/rear seat heating 20A each, PKE 2 (keyless-entry) 25A, ABS/ESP-1 25A, engine control module power (B+) 30A, brake lamp 10A, oxygen sensor 10A, outside mirrors 10A, headlight low-beam (both sides) 5A each, headlight high-beam (both sides) 5A each, night/cabin lamp 5A, turn-signal/parking-light circuit 5A, plus an empty/spare position and a fuse-clip spare-fuse holder. - Under-hood relay block (next to the fuse block): start relay, horn relay, blower relay, fuel-pump relay, left front seat-heating relay, plus the front/rear radiator fan relays and compressor relay already noted above.

This directly confirms the airbag circuit's rating (10A, cabin block) — relevant when troubleshooting an airbag warning light (see that card) — and shows several distinct 30A-rated circuits under the hood (power windows, central locking, sunroof, and engine-control-module power), any of which could be the "30A fuse under the hood" referenced in generic troubleshooting reports elsewhere in this section; always confirm the exact position against this diagram or the physical labeling rather than assuming which 30A fuse is meant.

docs.title: GLONASS emergency alert (ЭРА-ГЛОНАСС) module
docs.text:
Tags: #glonass

The FAW X80 has a GLONASS emergency-call module mounted under the front seats; several owners initially mistook it for a speaker 12 34. It uses a built-in free SIM card whose only purpose is connecting to the MCS emergency operator — it does not provide general connectivity or real-time tracking 5. It determines the car's location via GNSS (GLONASS) satellites and refines it with cellular tower triangulation, then transmits the coordinates to emergency services over the cellular network on activation 678. Activation is manual, via the dashboard SOS button; automatic activation on airbag deployment is also possible depending on model/trim 910 11. Because the system is safety equipment, owners are advised to test it periodically (e.g. via a documented test procedure, mentioned as existing in the manual) rather than leave it completely unverified — one owner reported a friend's unit genuinely helped after a serious accident 1012131411.

Water damage to the module — irreversible failure. The GLONASS/GPS module (a Fort Telecom FORT-4128B-type unit) sits under the driver's seat with its wiring harness and connectors 1516. Water entering from above corrodes the connectors, and the resulting damage is effectively irreversible: photos of an affected unit show green verdigris corrosion on connectors and interior components, with multicolor wiring oxidized 1718192021. One owner reports the module did not respond during an actual accident — i.e. once corroded, the module can silently stop functioning for emergency response despite showing no obvious external symptom 22.

Owner's manual chapter. The Russian owner's manual (Besturn-X80-new.pdf) has chapter 10, 'Эксплуатация терминала ЭРА-ГЛОНАСС Fort-112EG' (operation of the ERA-GLONASS Fort-112EG terminal). Its sub-sections, with page numbers read from the garbled table of contents: 1. using the ERA service, p.460; 2. checking the terminal's current state, p.461; 3. testing the terminal, p.462; 4. possible faults, critical failures and how to fix them, p.466; 5. 'Автосервис' (auto service) mode, p.467; 6. remote control of the terminal, p.467. A 'what to do if...' troubleshooting chapter is at p.478. The extracted text does not contain the procedures themselves, so use the PDF for the steps 23.

docs.title: GLONASS transducer — location
docs.text:
Tags: #glonass

The GLONASS (Russian satellite positioning system) speaker/transducer is mounted under the driver's seat, related to the integrated navigation/ tracking system. The component can be identified by its location and shape during an interior inspection 123.

Connection status varies between cars: some owners report the under-seat GLONASS speaker/transducer is present but not connected to any audio input on their car, while other owners report having it connected. It's not consistent across the fleet — check your own vehicle rather than assuming based on another owner's report 456789.

Reinforcing report — mistaken for a speaker: a separate report confirms the same identification point above: the box-like component under the driver's seat that resembles a speaker is in fact the GLONASS module, a standard vehicle component — not an audio speaker 1011.

docs.title: Aftermarket head unit — install and CAN-bus
docs.text:
Tags: #head-unit · #can-bus · #infotainment · #antenna · #tpms

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

CANBUS module for Android head-unit replacement (pre-facelift vs facelift). Pre-facelift models (2016-2019) do not have a built-in CANBUS module; facelift models (2020+) have one but may still need reconfiguration. A CANBUS adapter module is included in a typical replacement Android head-unit kit and must be programmed in the vehicle's settings menu; when properly installed and programmed, it preserves steering-wheel controls, climate control, the door-open sensor, and air direction mode, and comes with its own wiring harness and RCA connectors 12345678 91011. Real-world confirmation: 4GB/64GB Android units with a 4-inch touchscreen successfully replaced OEM units, with all of steering-wheel buttons, climate control, door-open detection, and air distribution modes (front/defrost/rear) working correctly once the CANBUS adapter was installed 1213141516 1718.

Wiring/power-polarity troubles on Chinese Android units. Installation is complicated by non-standard wiring on Chinese head units versus Russian-market wiring conventions — commonly reversed polarity on CAN-bus connectors and mismatched wire assignments. Fixing this typically requires weeks of back-and-forth with the seller/tuner over firmware variants and a test-and-correct approach; a competent installation shop is recommended over DIY 192021.

Radio antenna access via the control block. The antenna wire connects through the rear control block that also houses the climate and radio controls, secured with 4 bolts; this block must be fully removed (both the upper screen section and lower climate/switches section) to reach the antenna connector — there is no shortcut to it 2223.

Restyled monitor head unit — USB storage support. The restyled X80 head unit with monitor supports external USB media, but only in FAT32 format. Owners have used an external 320GB HDD successfully; an SSD is suggested as preferable to a HDD for vibration resistance. The unit plays both music and video from USB 242526.

Installation basics. Fitting an aftermarket head unit (ЦИУ/магнитола): disassembly takes about 10 minutes, the connector is plug-and-play, and reassembly/integration takes about 15 minutes 27. A common snag is that the antenna extension wire may be too short and needs extending or splicing by someone skilled in wiring 27. The harder part is CAN-bus configuration — especially on Chinese units — which requires protocol knowledge; one owner spent a year going back and forth with the manufacturer through multiple firmware updates, while others got it right in one pass. Researching a specific unit before buying is recommended 28. A CAN-bus 4-wire adapter cable needed for tablet-style head-unit installs is sold on Ozon (ozon.ru/t/5njoqp); pre-facelift and facelift X80 models need different cable versions 293031.

"Drunk road" (пьяная дорога) display glitch on FrontCam units. FrontCam brand head units (2/32GB RAM version) can show a "drunk road" graphical glitch tied to reverse-gear activation; related symptoms include the park sensors not activating or the rear-view camera glitching 323334. Community fixes tried: a head-unit firmware update; updating CAN-bus settings from the unit's menu; a firmware update on the MCU (auxiliary display module) 35363738. The issue can reoccur after some time 394041. A firmware downgrade to a monochrome interface can mask it temporarily but doesn't fix it permanently 3642. Note: similar symptoms have separately been reported on manual-transmission cars with a different root cause (see the ESP/traction-control false-warning card).

Antenna extension recommended. Confirming the point above: the factory antenna cable is short, so an antenna extension cable is specifically recommended whenever installing an aftermarket audio system, to ensure proper signal reception 4344.

No subwoofer/RCA output on the stock head unit. The factory head unit (non-facelift/"resto" trim confirmed) has no dedicated subwoofer RCA output 4546. To add an amplifier for aftermarket audio, use a high-level line converter/adapter (a "преобразователь") connected to the factory speaker outputs to derive an amplifier input signal 47 48. Some line converters generate their own REM (remote turn-on) signal automatically on audio detection; others need a separate dedicated 12V remote wire run from the head unit — check which type before buying 47. If not already buying an amplifier, get one with a high-level input built in from the start, to avoid needing a separate converter 49. Note: connector color coding at the factory harness may vary between "Resto" (restyled) trim units, so verify wiring before assuming a guide made for a different trim applies directly 50.

Carlinkit 5.0 wireless CarPlay/Android Auto adapter — confirmed compatible. The Carlinkit 5.0 CPC200-2air adapter is confirmed compatible with the X80, enabling wireless CarPlay and Android Auto on a compatible head unit 5152. Prerequisite: the head unit itself must already support the CarPlay protocol before the adapter will do anything — the adapter alone doesn't add CarPlay support to a unit that lacks it 53. In practice this means a firmware update on the head unit is typically required first to unlock CarPlay support before the wireless adapter becomes useful; one owner sourced the required firmware privately rather than from a public source 5354 55.

"Drunk road" error after a head-unit swap — CAN bus module mismatch. The "drunk road" (пьяная дорога — unstable steering-input) error code can appear on the multimedia/head unit right after changing the radio/multimedia system. Root cause: the CAN bus module ("коробочка"/камбус) fitted is from a different model year than the vehicle. Fix: replace the CAN bus module with one matching the vehicle's year. Alternative fix used by one owner: add a specific wire connection (yellow and brown wires soldered together, then run to a brown connector pin — see message 43104's video for the exact routing), per the multimedia installer's instructions; some installations also need a parking-sensor configuration adjustment afterward 5657 58596061. Conflict: one owner (Марина) fixed it with the wire-connection method, while another (Jürgen@73) preferred replacing the CAN bus module outright — both approaches are reported to work, though the wire method looks like the quicker initial fix based on the video evidence 5859.

Error can reappear after OBD-scanner clearing — the underlying cause wasn't fixed. The "drunk road" error can be cleared temporarily with an OBD scanner, but returns after driving or after some time. This indicates the root cause (CAN bus module mismatch, or the wiring fix above) wasn't actually addressed — a permanent fix requires replacing the mismatched component or completing the correct wiring change, not just clearing the code 6263.

Android head-unit "drunk road" fix — CAN bus cable routing, step by step. A separate case of the same "drunk road"/unstable-steering-input warning showing on an Android aftermarket head unit, traced instead to an incorrect or missing CAN bus connection from the head unit to the vehicle's ECU. Fix sequence: (1) identify the correct CAN bus cable connector — typically a yellow or brown wire from a numbered pin; (2) check the marketplace listing for the harness/adapter to confirm whether it's the pre-restyling or restyling connector variant, since they differ; (3) connect to the correct ECU CAN bus pin.
