A video tutorial (circulated on the marketplace where the harness was bought) walks through wiring 5 pins from the dashboard connector; after following it, the false warning cleared. This error originates from head-unit CAN bus misconfiguration, not from the vehicle's own ECU 6465 666768697071.

Firmware error persists with non-stock head unit paired to the stock "Wonder Monitor" display. Installing a non-stock head unit (магнитола) while keeping the stock "Wonder Monitor" instrument display causes a persistent error message, particularly visible while in reverse. With a non-original head unit the error cannot be permanently cleared. Two options: revert to the original head unit — which requires a single firmware flash to clear the error — or keep the aftermarket unit and accept the persistent warning. Some owners diagnosed the underlying fault with a professional diagnostic scanner rather than guessing 727374757677787980.

CAN-bus adapter enables steering-wheel controls and climate/door integration on aftermarket units. A CAN-bus adapter module is what lets an aftermarket head unit read steering-wheel button presses and display climate and door-open status. Some replacement units come with the adapter factory-included; others require sourcing it separately, and quality/functionality vary significantly between manufacturers. Tatarstan-based suppliers were specifically noted by one owner as a source of reliably high-quality CAN-bus adapters 8182.

RAM recommendation for aftermarket Android head units: 6GB over 4GB. A navigation app plus a couple of others (YouTube, VKontakte) running together consume roughly 4GB of RAM on their own, so while a 4GB unit may work, 6GB gives meaningfully more headroom. One owner also reports the 6GB variant they bought had a better audio processor, for only a small price difference over the 4GB version 8384.

Head-unit compatibility requires matching firmware/version to the vehicle. An X-REAKO 9-inch 2DIN Android unit (6GB RAM / 128GB storage) was confirmed to fit the X80, but compatibility in general depends on picking a unit software version that has documented compatibility with FAW vehicles specifically — not every listing that fits physically will integrate correctly 858687.

Teyes CC3L 4/64GB — a specific, well-reviewed Android unit. The Teyes CC3L (4GB RAM/64GB storage) fits the X80 (2018-2022), with an 8-core processor, IPS display, DSP audio, 4G and WiFi. It requires the CANBUS connection for proper integration. One owner reports over 4 years of reliable operation and recommends it over some newer Android 8.0 units 88899091 (product link: https://ozon.ru/t/DynXuLM).

Teyes CANBUS connection resolves — or at least changes — the "drunk road" (пьяная дорога) dashboard error. After installing a Teyes unit with its CANBUS module properly connected, the "drunk road" ESP-related dashboard error may clear, because the CANBUS module properly integrates the aftermarket unit with the vehicle's electronics. If the error persists after installation, it may point to a steering-wheel-control incompatibility rather than a wiring fault, and can generally be ignored if the rest of the stereo functions normally 929394 9596.

Replacing the head unit with a Chinese Android unit — pick matching TPMS sensors to avoid a reprogramming headache. When replacing the original head unit, Chinese Android options are available (e.g. Canbox H-Line models) 97. User recommendation: when replacing, buy a compatible tire-pressure-sensor set from the same brand (TAIS) rather than mixing brands — this avoids signal incompatibility and an expensive reprogramming step to get a different sensor brand talking to the new unit 97. See the TPMS card for more on sensor part numbers and programming.

docs.title: Headlight adjustment and common faults
docs.text:
Tags: #headlight · #connector

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Basic bulb replacement is plug-and-play. Ordinary headlight bulb replacement doesn't require a service visit or dealer equipment — the old bulb unplugs and the new one plugs directly into the housing, no disassembly needed, and standard sockets don't require reaiming/ recalibration afterward 1234.

Adjustment procedure. Headlight aim can be adjusted two ways: (1) interior — a dial to the left of the steering wheel controls vertical aim across 5 positions (the dial on the right controls dash brightness) 56; (2) under the hood — a plastic wheel/screw near the headlight for fine vertical and horizontal tuning 78. The interior control is enough for most cases; the under-hood adjustment is for fine-tuning. Confirming detail from a separate thread: the headlight assembly has two mechanical adjustment bolts, one for horizontal (left/right) aim visible from behind the headlight and one for vertical (up/down) aim that's partially hidden; the interior dial provides only limited-range correction (e.g. for load-induced height changes), while the two screws set the actual beam direction. LED bulb orientation matters here too — an incorrectly oriented replacement bulb will still throw the beam off even with the screws correctly set (see the LED-specific troubleshooting below) 91011 121314151617.

Failure from a burnt connector. Both high and low beams can go out simultaneously; root cause reported was a burnt electrical connector at the lamp socket, from contacts loosening over time 18. Fix: replace the connector — an inexpensive part, "costs only kopecks" 1920. Several owners report replacing headlight connectors annually because they keep burning 21. Conflict: one alternative raised is to convert to LED headlights instead of replacing stock bulbs — at least one owner switched to LED with success 22.

Whistling/squeaking noise. A whistling or squeaking sound from inside the headlight assembly is most likely the automatic headlight-leveling corrector (the vertical beam-adjuster motor) 2324. To diagnose: check whether the corrector moves smoothly when adjusted from the steering-wheel control, or park facing a wall and watch the beam shift as the corrector cycles 2526. If it's stuck or noisy, it may need replacement 2728. Separately noted: in winter, mirrors won't auto-fold until manually cycled once after a cold night — a related but distinct issue with electronic actuators 2930.

Auto mode behavior. With the headlight switch in AUTO, the light sensor turns on full headlights (not just DRLs) when ambient light drops enough — e.g. entering a tunnel or going under an overpass; this is normal sensor behavior 313233. In winter or for highway driving, some owners prefer manual control, because the auto-unload relay energizes at startup then delays the load, creating a transient voltage sag on the battery 34353637383940 41424344454647.

Repeated headlight fuse blowout despite the bulb looking fine. A distinct fuse-specific failure mode: the headlight fuse blows repeatedly even though the bulb itself appears functional. Suspected causes, in check order: (1) wrong bulb voltage rating installed — one shop reported a case where a 24V bulb had been fitted in place of the correct 12V, which kept blowing the fuse until a wiring "jumper" workaround overheated and melted the wiring harness ("коса") — check bulb voltage rating first 484950; (2) if the bulb voltage is confirmed correct, look for a shorted/damaged wire insulation or water intrusion into the light assembly instead — one experienced member pushed back on the wrong-voltage theory as the general explanation, noting standard 12V bulbs have historically been used across old Soviet and imported cars without issue, and that a colleague's repeated-blow case was ultimately traced to a specific short/miswire rather than bulb voltage generally 51.

Front turn signal not working — headlight-connector contact fault. A separate connector-related fault: the front-left turn signal stopped illuminating while the mirror and rear-bumper repeater indicators kept working normally — pointing to a fault isolated to that one bulb's circuit rather than the turn-signal system broadly. Relay-cycling and fuse checks found nothing. Fix: physically wiggling/jostling the wire bundle where it enters the headlight assembly restored function, indicating a loose or moisture-affected contact inside the headlight connector rather than a bulb or relay fault 52. Consistent with this card's broader theme, a community member noted X80 connector contacts generally are "not great" ("не айс") — i.e. treat marginal/ intermittent lighting faults as a connector-contact suspect first, before assuming a bulb or relay is bad 53.

Poor headlight beam pattern and adjustment — LED-specific troubleshooting. If headlights point upward into oncoming/following traffic rather than the road (poor beam pattern, hard to see lane markings at night), check in this order: (1) use the interior aim-height dial described above — left of the steering wheel, under the dash — to lower the beam pattern 5455565758; (2) if the issue appeared right after an LED bulb conversion, the diode orientation inside the bulb may be reversed on one side — LED diodes must face the correct direction (perpendicular to the ground, per one LED maker's instructions) for the beam shutter/cutoff shield inside the headlight housing to shape the beam correctly; diodes facing upward instead of sideways will flare light everywhere instead of forming a proper cutoff 5960616263; (3) verify the replacement LED bulb is specifically speced for this car's socket — bulbs "made specifically for our socket, marked for the factory fitment" avoid this problem entirely according to one owner who had no issues 646566; (4) if a shim/adjustment ring exists on the bulb's base, confirm it rotates freely so the beam direction can be fine- tuned in the socket, not just via the interior dial 67. Stock halogen bulbs already have a weak beam pattern by comparison, so a properly-oriented LED conversion is reported to meaningfully improve visibility once correctly aimed 61.

Complete headlight failure — fuse and relay diagnosis. A distinct failure case: the right headlight (both near and far beam) failed completely, then both headlights failed after the owner swapped fuses between circuits while troubleshooting; the relay is heard clicking when switching to high beam. Recommendation: check all fuses first and verify relay operation before going further. Because incorrect DIY electrical work on this car can cascade into worse damage, this is flagged as a case where consulting a professional auto-electrician is safer than continued trial-and-error swapping 686970.

Bulbs burning out rapidly — traced to factory connector corrosion, not bulb quality. A separate failure pattern from the connector-burn case above: the factory headlight connectors (grey/brown colored) corrode over time, and this corrosion — not the bulbs themselves — is what causes replacement bulbs to burn out rapidly. Community reports repeatedly point to the connector rather than bulb quality once this is diagnosed. Connector replacement is an affordable fix. Bulb part numbers seen in this socket: 9012, 9013, or HiR-type bulbs. When chasing this kind of early bulb failure, check the whole wiring harness for load issues and corrosion, not just the connector at the bulb itself 717273747576.

Factory misalignment risk on LED headlamps. LED headlamps on the X80 may arrive misaligned from the factory. If the beam pattern is off-standard, workshop adjustment (see the adjustment procedure above) is required to prevent dazzling oncoming traffic and to avoid a road-safety/legal violation. Verify the beam pattern against relevant Russian traffic/technical standards after installation or if the factory alignment is suspect 7778798081.

Headlight levelling knobs (STG) on the lamp housing. The headlight levelling adjusters (STG, корректор фар) are knobs on the back of each headlamp. One owner describes one knob near the radiator grille and the other between the wing and the radiator support, and says a torch is needed to see them 8283. Another owner at first saw only one knob 84.

docs.title: Headlight LED bulb conversion options
docs.text:
Tags: #headlight

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

More bulb options and pricing (Aug 2025, RU market). DawnKnight K7C 150W 9012 (HIR2) 6000K and MTF Light HS12H2 (HIR2 Standart+30%) both available on Ozon; MTF Light's price dropped from 2×750 RUB to ~840 RUB per bulb during this window 1234 5.

HIR2 (9012) confirmed as the socket standard, with a TNP option. Reconfirming the HIR2/9012 socket noted elsewhere: TNP LED BRENDY 9012 HIR2 bulbs (sold on Wildberries, among other bright options) gave one owner excellent night visibility; caution — some units arrive defective, so request a visual inspection from the seller before payment 6789.

LED 360° conversion — spec and heat. LED 360° conversion lamps (8000K color temperature) run at 85°C normally, with diodes rated for continuous 105°C — example brand: Carshark 12V, sold as a 2-pack. This level of heat is normal and not a concern; fans on the unit may feel warm, which is expected 10111213.

Brand comparison — 360° vs directional. Multiple LED options exist: 360° rotation bulbs (adjustable direction after installation) vs. traditional fixed-focus bulbs 1415. Tested brands: Carshark 360° (lower performance on the highway) 1617; Philips (well-regarded) 1819; DawnKnight (good light output but dark spots noted, from its flat-diode design) 2021; AILEO 360° (tunable 3000K–6500K color temperature, 80W, rated highest among those tried) 222324. Prices are variable and some listings drop ~50% shortly after purchase 2526. The flat-diode design can cause dark spots specifically in lens-equipped headlights; proper adjustment can mitigate this 27282930 3132333435363738 3940.

Conflict: owner experiences diverge — some rate 360° LEDs as giving superior light output, others prefer Philips or stock halogen; reported results also depend on individual fuse/wiring quality 1634.

Real-world upgrade result. Stock halogen bulbs were reported to give very poor night visibility ("couldn't see the road at night") 41. DawnKnight 12V LED bulbs, bought from Ozon (product 842925366), gave a large improvement — full road visibility in rain and on the highway 4243. A side-by-side comparison of HIR2 LED vs. stock halogen on one side of the car showed a dramatic brightness difference 4445. The one minor cosmetic downside on highway night driving: two bright spots visible from the LED/HID units in front of the hood.

Bulb options and pricing (Dec 2024, RU market). MTF Light halogen (Ozon) — OEM-equivalent 4647. Carshark 360° warm 4300K LED — budget option, ~2000 RUB (RU market, December 2024), a solid upgrade over halogen 4849. Red Stil LED — an alternative LED option (Ozon) 50. MTF Light Cyber Light HIR2 (9012) 6000K — premium LED option (WildBerries), ~5000+ RUB, praised by auto-lighting studios 5152. HB4 is a cheaper alternative to HIR2 where the sockets have already been modified. Any LED lamp must include a built-in load resistor ("обманка"/decoder) to avoid dashboard errors; cheap LEDs often lack this, causing a permanent low-brightness glow and error codes.

Connector types — HIR2 vs HB4. HIR2 connectors have a notch/key pin; HB4 connectors are smooth without it, so HB4 bulbs will not fit a standard HIR2 socket without modification 5354. If the original sockets have already been replaced (e.g. after melting from overheating), both HB4 and HIR2 may fit the replacement socket. HB4 is significantly cheaper (~400–600 RUB, RU market, December 2024) than HIR2 (~2000+ RUB pre-2024, ~5000 RUB for current premium LED units, RU market, December 2024) 55.

More brand/pricing data points (Dec 2025). DawnKnight K7C and K9C Pro (H7/H4/H11 sockets, copper cooling tubes) continue to come up as an option, though one owner's K7C produced an uneven light pattern with dark spots despite correct installation — consistent with the flat-diode dark-spot issue already noted above; he ultimately swapped to a 360-degree circular LED design instead and had no further issue 5657585960. K9C Pro was seen on AliExpress at ~2,060 RUB (RU market, December 2025) with a 50% discount during this window 57. Wattage vs. lumens — a recurring buyer confusion. Stock halogen bulbs are rated 55W; a 20W rating on an LED replacement refers to power consumption, not light output — lumens (light output) is the metric that actually determines brightness, and a lower-wattage LED can still out-light a 55W halogen because LEDs are far more efficient per watt 616263. After any LED headlight install, booking a proper beam-adjustment/alignment at a shop (~3,000+ RUB) is recommended, since LED conversions commonly need re-aiming even when the bulb itself fits correctly 60.

HB4 socket confirmed for low beam, plus HB4→HIR2 conversion notes. The FAW X80's low-beam headlight socket is HB4 6465. Replacement HB4 connectors are available through ordinary auto-parts shops 6667. Confirming and extending the HIR2-vs-HB4 connector-shape difference documented above: HB4 and HIR2 sockets are close but not identical — converting an HB4 socket to accept an HIR2 bulb requires filing/trimming a small key/tab on the socket to make it fit 6869. A salvageable option when swapping to LED: the old HB4 connector/pigtail can be cut and rewired directly onto new LED bulb leads rather than buying a separate adapter harness, if the LED bulb is a bare halogen-style (not integrated-connector) design 707172.

HIR2 (9012) LED installation and aiming — a consolidated procedure. Combining several installation reports into one sequence for a 9012/HIR2 LED swap (this batch centers on a 185W-equivalent "DLED premium" listing on Ozon, ~2,000–3,000 RUB/pair, RU market, December 2025) 73: (1) verify bulb polarity/ connector orientation before inserting — the connector is keyed but double-check anyway 74757677; (2) insert with the ground wire pointing DOWN — this is called out as critical for correct beam shape, distinct from the diode-orientation issue covered in the headlight-adjustment card 7879; (3) if one side's beam looks wrong after install, suspect the LED diode array being mounted backwards relative to the other side — compare orientation side-to-side rather than assuming a bad bulb 8081; (4) after installation, use the interior aim-height control (left of the steering wheel) to set the beam height, and check for a rotatable adjustment shim/ring on the bulb's base itself that lets you fine-tune direction independent of the bulb's fixed diode orientation 8283 84858687888990 9192; (5) keep the wiring routed neatly and disconnect the negative battery terminal before starting the install; test at low speed/in a controlled area before highway driving 9394. Despite the multi-step process, LED bulbs are consistently reported as a significant illumination improvement over halogen once correctly installed and aimed — see the headlight-adjustment card for the beam- pattern troubleshooting steps if the result still isn't right after following this sequence.

Headlight connector pin-count query — verify before ordering from AliExpress. A minor, low-confidence but practical note: a buyer sourcing a pre-facelift headlight assembly from AliExpress couldn't tell from the listing whether the connector was 11-pin or 12-pin, and the community's answer was that this needs to be physically verified on the actual vehicle before ordering rather than assumed from a generic listing photo — connector pin-count on AliExpress listings for this car isn't reliably accurate 959697.

K7C (HIR2 9012) LED bulb spec and color temperature. The FAW X80 uses K7C-type (HIR2 9012) bulbs for its headlights. LED replacements are available in 4300K (warmer, yellowish) and 6000K (cooler, bluish) color temperatures. Color temperature (K) affects only the color of the light, not brightness (lumens) — both variants deliver the same light output. Community consensus favors 4300K for reduced glare to oncoming drivers; 6000K is considered too bright/harsh by comparison. The DawnKnight brand (models DK_LED_K7C_9012_4300K and the 6000K variant) is available on the Ozon marketplace 9899100101102103 104105106.

General LED headlight-bulb upgrade — improved brightness, no housing mods. Aftermarket LED headlight bulbs, more broadly, provide significantly improved brightness over the stock bulbs and are a direct replacement with no housing modification needed. Professional beam realignment is recommended after installation. Available on the Ozon marketplace 107108.

Three-tier options summary, with the professional-conversion tier not covered elsewhere in this card. A separate thread summarizes the choices at three price/quality tiers, adding a tier not otherwise documented here: (1) cheap LED drop-in bulbs (~3,000-5,000 RUB, RU market, September 2024) — often poor color rendition and imprecise fitment, not generally recommended; (2) branded aftermarket LEDs (Carshark, DawnKnight, and OLED variants on Ozon) — mixed results, brightness varies by unit, and even when output is good it's often not dramatically better than halogen; expect 4300-6000K color temperatures, consistent with the ranges documented elsewhere in this card; (3) a full professional headlight conversion (~30,000 RUB, RU market, September 2024) — the OEM optic is removed and a diode/HID unit is professionally installed inside the lens itself, with some shops offering a lifetime warranty and notably better light quality than a simple bulb swap. Regardless of which tier is chosen, the recurring safety caveat applies: headlights must be professionally aimed (регулировка СТГ) after any bulb/conversion change, since white LEDs in a misaligned housing blind oncoming traffic 109110111112113114115116 117118119120121122123.

Further confirmations from a second Telegram group — pricing, socket type, and the 360°-vs-2-sided trade-off. A separate community group independently reconfirms and adds pricing/technical detail to the K7C (HIR2/9012) picture documented above. Socket/bulb type: FAW X80 headlamps use the HIR2 (9012) socket; K7C-branded LED bulbs are the widely-recommended, cost-effective choice here, sold on Ozon at roughly 2,500 RUB per pair (RU market, March 2026) and rated as giving good light output for the price 124125126127128129. A broader options round-up from the same group largely matches the tiered summary above — cheap drop-ins, branded LED (Dawnknight K7C/K9C among them), and a full conversion — with the same emphasis on professional beam aiming afterward 130131132133134135136137 138139140141142143144145146147 148149. Specific product data: HB4-fitment white 6000K LED bulbs, 19,000-lumen rated, CSP chips, 106W (pair) — Dawnknight K7C and K9C models specifically recommended for the X80 (product link: https://ozon.ru/t/jhFxooM) 132134145146148. More detailed part numbers: DawnKnight K7C LEDs in 4300K or 6000K, rated 40W, 8000lm output — part numbers DK_LED_K7C_H1_6000K and DK_LED_K7C_9012_4300K; a fallback option is filing down one connector lobe on an HB3/HB4 bulb to force-fit the HIR2 socket. Installation takes 5-10 minutes: remove the old bulb, fit the retaining ring separately, then insert the new lamp 150151152153154155 156157158159160161162163164 165166167168169170.

360°-vs-2-sided LED technology comparison, with the dark-zone trade-off quantified. Adding specific angular figures to the 360° vs directional comparison already documented in this card: 2-sided lamps like the K7C emit across roughly 170-175 degrees, which creates a dark zone directly ahead/below on the road once installed — its main advantages are low cost (~1,500-2,000 RUB, RU market, January 2026) and simple installation. 360-degree lamps (8+ matrix diode designs) emit across the full circle, eliminating that dark zone entirely, at a higher cost (~2,500-3,000 RUB or more, RU market, January 2026), a wider mounting envelope that needs fine adjustment after install, and — even among 360° lamps — differing matrix counts (6 vs 8) produce different light-overlap patterns. Despite the optical downside, K7C-type lamps remain the popular default because of their cost-performance ratio 171172173174175176 177178.

Stock low-beam judged inadequate at night — another independent 9012/HIR2 4300K upgrade report. A separate owner reported the stock low beams give insufficient night illumination (possibly because previous owners had swapped in mismatched bulbs), forcing them to run the front fog lights as a supplement just to see 179180. The recommended fix: a 9012 HIR2 LED upgrade — one example cited was "TNP Brendy" (TNP LED, sold on Wildberries) with active cooling 181; another owner linked a similar 9012 HIR2 LED listing on Ozon.ru that they had installed and aimed on a proper alignment stand 182. Color-temperature guidance, reinforcing the 4300K-vs-6000K consensus already documented above: 6000K was described as "like welding" (too much glare), while 4300K doesn't blind oncoming traffic and performs noticeably better in bad/wet weather; when the low beams are paired with the fog lights running, the combination gives a daytime-like appearance and excellent road coverage 183. As with every LED upgrade in this card: get the beam re-aimed at a service center after installation, since a bright but misaimed beam blinds oncoming drivers rather than helping the owner see better.

Low-beam socket dispute and colour temperature (September 2026, RU market). One owner states the X80 low-beam socket is HIR2 (9012) only, not HB4 or HB3, and asks whether the retaining-claw geometry of an HB4 bulb really matches; another owner thinks HB4 looks identical and has seen an HB4 listing with the same base, and a third notes that universal HB4/HB5/HIR2 LED bulbs now exist and that earlier owners adapted HB5 bulbs 184185186. This disagrees with the reports above that the low beam takes an HB4 socket; both positions are reported as stated.

Owners fitting DawnKnight K7C 9012 (HIR2) LED bulbs report good light in snow and rain 187188. One owner bought cheap look-alike units on Ozon that were not the brand, returned them and bought a dearer pair that matched the listing 189. Listings in September 2026 showed the 6000K K7C HIR2/9012 pair at ~2,171 RUB and ~2,829 RUB, and a 6000K HIR2 unit at ~2,889 RUB (RU market, September 2026); the 4300K 9012 version was sold out 190187191. Listing text: 25,000 lm, 110 W, built-in CANBUS decoder, 12-month warranty.

On colour temperature, one owner says 4300K is warmer, close to halogen, and dazzles oncoming drivers less in rain and fog, while 6000K looks blinding; another owner running 4300K agrees it is enough 192193. An owner running 6000K argues that lens quality and beam pattern matter more than colour 194. He recalls paying ~3,000 RUB for an X80 LED set (RU market, September 2026) against ~8,000 RUB for bulbs for his earlier Chery Tiggo 194. One member claimed that a canbus box is only for the car radio and modern LED bulbs need nothing extra; nobody confirmed it, and it conflicts with the usual purpose of a canbus decoder (preventing bulb-error warnings and flicker) - the DawnKnight listings state the decoder is built in, so check before buying 195.

docs.title: Heater/cabin blower fan issues
docs.text:
Tags: #bearing · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Intermittent operation, fixed by cleaning out dust. If the heater fan only spins after the car is jostled or bumped (e.g. only starts after a tap/knock, or stops working entirely and needs a physical hit to restart), the most common and easiest-to-check cause is dust/debris accumulation inside the fan motor housing — not a wiring or electrical fault. Access: the fan is located behind/under the glovebox area, and reaching it is described as straightforward once the glovebox is out. Fix: remove the fan assembly and blow it out thoroughly with compressed air; one owner reported a surprising amount of dust and leaf debris came out, and the fan resumed fully normal operation after cleaning 12 3. Before assuming the motor itself is bad, check fuses and the relay first, since oxidized contacts there can produce similar intermittent symptoms 2. In one case a simple tap/knock under the glovebox was enough to get it running again even without disassembly, confirming a loose/dirty mechanical contact rather than an electrical fault 4.

Bearing wear as the next suspect if cleaning doesn't fix it. If cleaning out dust doesn't resolve rough or noisy operation, the motor's bearing may be worn or failing and should be checked/replaced next 5. Bearing replacement is possible without buying a whole new blower motor: one owner successfully replaced just the bearing, reporting that while the first attempt takes longer because of unfamiliarity with full disassembly, it isn't difficult once you've done it once 6789. Confirmed bearing part: 608-ZZ (also referenced as 80018), NSK brand, sourced via Wildberries; a 35mm FORCEKRAFT bearing-puller tool assists with extracting the old bearing during the swap 910.

Fan/blade breakage — parts sourcing. A separate report describes physical blade breakage on a cooling fan assembly, with a temporary patch of soldering the broken blade(s) back on to extend service life a little longer — but this is explicitly a stopgap, not a real fix, since the fan blades and motor are not sold as separable parts; a full fan-assembly replacement is the only permanent fix once blades are physically broken 1112. Part reference for the complete cooling-fan assembly (5DA015025): available through the KitZapchasti catalog, with a second listing also found on kitparts.ru 13. For budget-conscious owners, checking salvage yards/junkyards and classifieds (Avito) for a used take-off fan assembly is a cheaper alternative to a new unit 11.

docs.title: Horn/acoustic sensor part number
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number

A component with part number FS43X0L5-180C05-0503AAC7 was photographed and identified in this thread as appearing to be a horn or acoustic-sensor element used in the X80's electrical system. This identification is low confidence and unverified — treat the part number as a starting point for further research (e.g. cross-referencing against parts catalogs) rather than a confirmed horn part 1.

docs.title: Hot air leak — steering column vent damper
docs.text:
Tags: #hvac · #heat-shield · #unresolved

One owner experienced strange hot air blowing onto their knees from under the steering column, even with the climate control set to cold. The problem occurred in summer and specifically on the highway, intensifying at speed. Possible causes investigated included a thermal heat shield passing engine heat into the cabin — but on inspection the shield was found intact, ruling that out as the cause. The problem resolved itself spontaneously after some time, with no mechanical fix ever applied. A later, unrelated diagnostic scan on the same car did turn up an error code related to the thermal/ventilation damper system, which may or may not be connected to this earlier symptom — treat this as a lower-confidence, unresolved report rather than a documented fix 123.

docs.title: Ignition coil replacement (open question)
docs.text:
Tags: #unresolved

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

A community member asked whether anyone had replaced the ignition coil(s) on a FAW X80, but the source thread recorded no responses in this batch 1. This is logged here as an open question rather than folded into the spark-plug card, since ignition coils are a distinct component from spark plugs even though both sit in the same ignition-system family — the lack of any reported replacement experience (part numbers, symptoms that led to the question, cost, procedure) suggests either this is a rare failure on the X80, or reports exist elsewhere in the archive not yet linked to this card. Revisit and merge into a fuller card once real replacement reports surface.

Supplier note. Ignition coils for the FAW X80 ("Катушка зажигания FAW X80 / ФАВ Х80") are available on the Ozon.ru marketplace — check the listing for current pricing and availability 2.

docs.title: Ignition lock cylinder sticking in cold
docs.text:
Tags: #cold-weather

General binding/seizing — both keys affected. One owner reported both the primary and spare keys suddenly stopped turning in the ignition lock cylinder, suspecting the lock mechanism itself rather than either individual key (since both were affected) 12. This is described as a known, recurring FAW X80 issue — the lock mechanism has a tendency to bind/grip keys generally, not just as a cold-weather problem 34. Temporary fix: spray silicone lubricant into the lock cylinder to ease the binding. One relevant detail affecting binding severity: steering-wheel position — having the wheel in the fully straight/centered position is recommended, as an off-center wheel position can worsen the lock's tendency to bind 4. This is a temporary mitigation rather than a permanent fix; a genuine repair likely requires lock-cylinder replacement or professional service, though no owner in this thread had gone that far yet.

Cold-and-wet-specific variant — ice inside the lock. A related but distinct presentation: the ignition lock freezes and becomes difficult to turn specifically in cold, wet weather — for example after a car wash in freezing conditions, where water that got into the lock mechanism froze 56. Fix for this variant: spray WD-40 (not silicone, for this specific ice-related case) into the lock mechanism, then gently work the key back and forth to distribute the lubricant and free the ice — don't force it. If you suspect water/ice specifically (rather than just general binding), an alternative approach is to gently warm the lock area through a towel, using a hot-water bottle (not boiling water directly) or the car's own heater, to melt the ice before attempting the key again. One owner reports the WD-40 approach ("вдшка" — colloquial for WD-40) resolved the acute freeze-up, though the underlying lock still occasionally binds afterward, at a level described as "not critical" 7.

Background: the lock mechanism is purely mechanical, independent of the battery/immobilizer. Useful context for diagnosing binding symptoms above: the X80's steering-wheel/ignition lock is a purely mechanical (not electronic) mechanism and needs no battery power to operate. It works by key insertion and rotation to the "off" position, which causes a pin to engage into a groove once the steering wheel is turned. This mechanical lock function operates independently of the immobilizer (which instead uses an induction coil to verify the key) — so a dead battery or immobilizer fault won't by itself prevent the physical lock from engaging/disengaging, and conversely, fixing a stuck lock (see above) doesn't touch the immobilizer circuit at all. On manual-transmission cars, the battery only powers the central door locks in relation to this system; on automatics with free-hand parking, the battery also powers additional convenience functions layered on top 8910.

docs.title: Immobilizer antenna coil winding
docs.text:
Tags: #immobilizer

The immobilizer chip is read by a wire wound in a spiral pattern acting as an antenna, transmitting to a reader coil (typically around the ignition-lock barrel). The number of turns and the winding tension are both critical — even a slight variation in either can break the signal and prevent the immobilizer from recognizing the key. Rewinding the coil with the identical original specifications (same turn count, same tension) restores function 123456.

docs.title: Immobilizer module — location and water damage
docs.text:
Tags: #immobilizer · #water-ingress · #cold-weather · #connector

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Normal blinking of the immobilizer icon. The dashboard immobilizer lock symbol (подкова / horseshoe icon) shows on startup and blinks to confirm ongoing key-to-vehicle communication. Continued blinking after ignition-off, once the car is locked/armed, is normal — it indicates the immobilizer is active, and does not meaningfully drain the battery 1234. Reconfirmed in a separate thread: a blinking red "lock" icon (красный замок) with the ignition off and the car locked is normal operation, confirming the engine is immobilized as an anti-theft measure; the light extinguishes once the correct key is detected at startup 5678.

Location. Reports place the immobilizer (anti-theft) control module in two nearby but distinct spots depending on trim/generation: (1) on the left side of the dashboard, behind the small glove box compartment 910; (2) near the front passenger's right foot area, under the plastic trim, above floor level, on Restyling-generation cars 11121314. Both are consistent with an under-dash location reachable from inside the cabin without major disassembly — check whichever spot matches your specific generation/trim first.

Cold-weather failure from corrosion (not a hard module failure). Symptom: smart-key and keyless-entry (bless-key) functionality stops working reliably once ambient temperature drops below roughly +5°C, while working fine in warm weather — one owner's car worked perfectly warm and completely failed keyless functions any time it was +5°C or colder 1516. A remote-autostart "обходчик" (bypass module) tied into the same circuit showed the same temperature-dependent failure pattern 17. Root cause: water intrusion into the immobilizer module causing contact oxidation (окислы), not a full module failure — the temperature dependency itself is diagnostic, since corrosion's electrical resistance is temperature-sensitive in a way a fully dead module wouldn't be 1819. In this case water didn't get directly into the module housing — general cabin moisture caused the oxidation via a more indirect path 20. The car in question was about 3 years old, first developed symptoms in its first winter, and needed the immobilizer block itself dealt with (see next section) 2115.

Repair: clean, don't necessarily replace. Community consensus, contradicting a dealer's more aggressive recommendation: open the immobilizer case and thoroughly clean all contacts and circuit-board elements rather than replacing the whole unit — this community approach was reported successful, while the dealer had instead recommended full replacement 18. Photos from this case show visible white oxidation coating (окислы) specifically around connector areas and solder joints.

Related failure: "key not recognized" after rain, connector reseating fix. A different but related symptom on a Restyling-generation car: after rain/moisture exposure, the dash shows "key not recognized" and the car won't start, despite the keys themselves working normally and ignition otherwise behaving normally 22. Suggested root cause path to check first: moisture in the VSM causing the steering-column lock to disengage incorrectly, and separately the Gateway module (see the PKE/smart-key card for more on Gateway) 23. Fix that resolved this for multiple owners even with no visible corrosion or standing water present: locate the immobilizer block (right passenger footwell area) and remove/reseat all of its connector plugs — oxidized or simply loose contacts were enough to prevent key-signal detection without any deeper module damage 122414. This car had been parked outside in rain for three to four days before the fault appeared, supporting the moisture- triggered-contact-issue theory over a hard failure 25.

No-start with the dashboard on: reseat the connector blocks. An owner had a no-start where the dashboard lit and the ignition came on but pressing start did nothing and the starter did not crank. Members suggested water from a sunroof drain may have corroded the comfort block (комфорт) under the driver's left-foot trim, and that the key-reading (immobilizer) block sits under the front passenger's right foot. After one owner unplugged and reseated all the connectors on that block the car started; another member suggests pressing the start button with the key itself, because the button has its own antenna 26272829. See also Comfort/BSM-VSM block — electrical hub.

docs.title: Smart-key covers — prices and compatibility
docs.text:
Tags: #aliexpress · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Compatibility: metal smart-key covers with bolt fasteners fit standard 3-button smart keys but do NOT fit retractable/flip-blade keys. Simple leather covers (no metal case) fit both key types — verify which key type you have before ordering the metal-case version 123.

Prices (AliExpress, RU market, September 2024): - Leather cover with metal case and bolt fasteners: 529 RUB with a 50% discount (regular price ~1,058 RUB); a similar listing at 531 RUB was also seen 456. - Simple leather cover (no metal case): 391 RUB (RU market, September 2024) with a 20% discount 7. - Delivery to Moscow: ~9 days; a small screwdriver is included in the package 8.

Steel/metal case alternative vs. AliExpress silicone/leather covers: factory keys often show wear/scratches from previous handling. Two alternatives compared: (1) AliExpress silicone/leather covers (~500 RUB+, RU market, January 2026) — bulky, and signal-blocking issues are common (remote range reduced by 1–2 floors), which affects key transmission; (2) steel/metal case alternative — sturdier appearance, better durability (~1,000 RUB, RU market, January 2026), shows wear less, includes color options (brown-leather accents, black), and preserves a slim profile. The steel case requires disassembling the original key; the buttons and key ring fit inside the new case without modification. One user reports the steel case works reliably and the battery still lasts normally after the swap 91011121314151617.

Folding key cover/case — cross-model compatibility (X40, B50, R7, B70, T99, X80): a folding key cover/case is available that fits the FAW Besturn X80 as well as the X40, B50, R7, B70, and T99. Available on AliExpress (SKU links shared in the community) and via Chinese retailers on Ozon. AliExpress pricing: ~893.80 RUB (RU market, March 2026) with a 48% discount; build quality varies slightly, with cosmetic wear reported by some buyers (чуть коцки). Delivery: ~10 days on AliExpress, slower on Ozon. Used/secondary-market units have sold for around 750 RUB (RU market, March 2026) 18192021.

Key-fob case assembly — relayed AliExpress purchase cost: sourcing a keypad/key-fob case assembly from AliExpress via a purchasing relay costs approximately 1,000 RUB total (RU market, August 2024) with shipping (roughly 500 RUB for the case itself, 450–500 RUB for delivery). Cases include the hardware needed for installation. A lighter-weight alternative: universal leather cases, though fitment varies 22.

Folding metal key cover, September 2026. A folding metal-body key-fob cover listed for the FAW Besturn X80 (2013 to 2018) sold on AliExpress for ~954.65 RUB after a 23% discount (RU market, September 2026); a buyer confirmed it is a good metal case 2324.

docs.title: Start/Stop key fob battery replacement
docs.text:
Tags: #key-fob · #battery · #part-number

Battery type: CR2032 (12V) per one owner 1; another owner who opened a fob found a Maxell (Hitachi Maxell, Japan) CR1620 coin cell on the circuit board and says it is not a CR2032, and describes opening it by pressing a tool into the slot at the top and twisting to split the shell 23. The two reports conflict, so check the cell in your own fob before buying.

Procedure: 1. Press the logo button to eject the physical spare key blade. 2. Insert a flat tool (a small flathead screwdriver or a dental spatula works well) into the slot on the side of the fob body. 3. Rotate/twist to open — the fob splits apart on internal snap clips, similar to opening a TV remote. 4. Replace the CR2032 battery, then snap the case back together.456

Care tips. The plastic housing scratches easily, so avoid metal tools with sharp edges where possible; a dental instrument (spatula) is gentler. Some owners lightly heat the case edge with a lighter to soften/smooth burrs before prying, which also helps avoid visible damage to the housing.56

docs.title: Key fob programming and battery
docs.text:
Tags: #key-fob · #immobilizer · #battery · #bsm · #normal-behavior

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Battery-disconnect trick for general fob glitches. Beyond the keyless-entry-specific recovery below, a battery-terminal disconnect (a few minutes, negative terminal) is a broadly useful fix for a fob that won't lock/unlock even with a fresh battery — it resets electronic module memory and often resolves false error states and "hiccups" without a dealer visit 123456 7.

CR1620 battery, confirmed part and photos. The remote key fob uses a CR1620 tablet-type cell, confirmed with battery-compartment photos 891011 — consistent with the CR1620 pricing already noted below.

Rapid CR2032 drain from proximity to the car; reliable brands. A separate, common battery complaint: the fob's CR2032 depletes in as little as 2-3 weeks for some owners. Cause: storing the key close to the car causes constant RF-signal drain from the central-locking system. Fixes: (1) replace the CR2032 (~150-300 RUB on Ozon, RU market, August 2025); (2) store the key away from the car (a different room, 10m+ away). Reported brand reliability: Renata lasted 1+ year, Energizer/Duracell/Varta all eventually wear out; generic/no-name batches were flagged as unreliable — Renata CR2032 from Ozon was the most reliable option in this thread 1213141516171819 2021222324252627 28.

Fob stops responding to door unlock — reset via ignition/door cycling. If the fob stops responding to unlock commands specifically: (1) cycle the ignition on/off five times; (2) open and close the doors six times. This resets the adaptive locking system. Caution: on some vehicles this procedure can cause doors to unlock instead of lock if buttons are pressed mid-adaptation; a YouTube tutorial exists, and some vehicles need extra configuration beyond this basic sequence 2930 3132333435.

Home DIY reprogramming, no dealer. X80 fobs can be reprogrammed at home following a YouTube tutorial matched to the model year, without a dealer visit — useful when the nearest dealer is 300+ km away, as in one owner's case 36373839.

Contact cleaning restores sync after a battery swap. When both remote keys stopped opening/closing doors after a battery replacement, cleaning the key contacts (not just swapping the battery) resolved it — the keys reprogrammed and stopped losing sync. Moisture/oxidation on fob contacts is a common X80 electrical issue, not unique to one key 40.

Mechanical key as smart-key-battery-dead fallback. If the smart-key fob's battery dies (or the key is lost), the mechanical key hidden inside the fob can open the doors manually, and the immobilizer/engine-start still work with just the mechanical key even without fob battery power. No alarm sounds when using the mechanical key if no aftermarket alarm is installed; if a StarLine-type aftermarket alarm is installed, it may sound when the door is opened this way — check the alarm settings or find its hidden panic/disarm button 4142434445.

Cloning is not possible — only physical keys are registerable. X80 smart keys cannot be cloned or programmed without factory tools; only a physical key with a personal cut can be registered via the DIY algorithm/procedures above. Cloning attempts in Russia (including Moscow) have not succeeded; one report of a full replacement key available from a person in Siberia, but they were rarely reachable 4647 48.

Unresponsive fob, fresh battery. If a key fob stops responding to lock/unlock commands despite a fresh battery and a working LED indicator, it likely needs reprogramming; a DIY procedure found on YouTube worked for one owner without a dealer visit 49505152.

Pairing a second key knocks out the first. When pairing new key fobs with the factory signaling system, one key can pair successfully while the other becomes inoperative. Fix: make sure new keys are bound to a free/unused memory cell in the ECU, not to a previously-used one; this may also require adapting the engine control unit to recognize the new keys in addition to immobilizer programming 53545556.

Recovery after a battery disconnect. Disconnecting the car battery terminal makes the keyless-entry system stop responding to lock/unlock commands. Fixes reported: slam the doors hard 3–5 times (a mechanical pairing trick), or follow a ~3-minute YouTube procedure searchable as "прописать ключ на фав х80" (can be done at home or by a technician) 57585960. One owner needed a second attempt after rushing the first 61. Note: the fob's LED indicator lighting up is not a reliable indicator of battery health — a low key battery is still worth checking as a first step 6263.

Battery type and price. The remote key uses a CR1620 battery, about 22 RUB per unit or 100 RUB for a 5-pack at the Всеинструменты retailer (RU market, Dec 2024) 64. Battery compartment design differs by trim: the base mechanical-key trim and the AKPP push-button-start trim have physically different battery compartments 65666768.

Troubleshooting order when a fob stops responding. (1) First try a fresh battery — typically CR2032 69; note flaky/intermittent non-response can happen occasionally even without a dead battery 70. (2) If a fresh battery doesn't fix it, attempt key rebinding/pairing — YouTube tutorials specific to the X80 exist and were used successfully 71. (3) If multiple key fobs fail simultaneously (not just one), suspect the BSM (body/brake control module) with oxidized contacts from moisture ingress — this needs disassembly, cleaning the contacts with electrical contact spray, drying thoroughly, and reassembly 72737475. (4) A mechanical "door-pounding" trick — slamming doors hard — can sometimes help reinitialize communication as a stopgap while sourcing a proper fix 76. One owner's case: both key fobs stopped responding simultaneously despite battery replacement and a battery-terminal reset, and only one fob was recovered after extensive troubleshooting — the second stayed dead, suggesting the root cause in stubborn cases can be partial/inconsistent rather than a single clean fix 7775.

CR2032 → CR3032 battery upgrade. Stock CR2032 batteries reportedly died quickly in some owners' fobs (as fast as 2–3 weeks); CR3032 was tried as a longer-lasting alternative and one owner reports it lasting about a year. Caution: CR3032 is slightly thicker than CR2032 and can damage the top contact spring if forced in carelessly, so install gently 78. Reported battery-brand quality difference: Energizer-branded CR2032s performed poorly for one owner (repeated failures within weeks, enough to make him order replacements in bulk); ordinary/shop-brand batteries performed better for him 7980. Always test the actual contact/terminal voltage (e.g. touch-test on the tongue, or a multimeter) rather than assuming a battery is dead or fine from age alone — "charge seems present but electronics don't respond" was reported as a distinguishing symptom pointing to something other than a simple dead battery 80.

Requires multiple presses / intermittent no-response — battery vs. chip degradation. A separate symptom pattern: pressing the fob's button sometimes fails to unlock/start the car, requiring repeated presses; the car has also started intermittently not being "seen" and needing the fob physically inserted into the start/stop button as a fallback 81. Suspected causes, in order to check: (1) fob battery degradation — try this first, it's the cheap/easy fix; (2) chip degradation inside the fob itself, which is not something a battery swap will fix 81 82. X80 push-button (proximity) fobs cannot be reprogrammed or cloned locally — no protocol/procedure for this was found, at least in the Samara region, meaning a chip-degraded push-button fob likely needs outright replacement rather than reprogramming 82. By contrast, the mechanical-key fob variant does have a known programming algorithm, and there's a good chance it also applies to the push-button variant's underlying chip — but reprogramming it without proper tools/training carries real risk of bricking the key, and even some dealers who attempt mechanical-key reprogramming report uncertain results, so treat this as a specialist job with no guaranteed outcome, not a DIY fix 82.

"Key not detected" in cold/wet weather — check the fob battery first. Symptom: a "key not detected" message appears sporadically during rain or snow, then clears on its own. Cause: low battery in the key-fob remote. Fix: replace the fob battery (check its charge level before assuming a deeper fault). Workaround for wet weather while the battery issue is unresolved: place the key directly on the instrument panel within the driver's line of sight — some owners report this improves detection reliability. Root cause is likely RF signal attenuation in wet conditions combined with an already-weak battery; the occurrence is rare (roughly once per 10–100 km) and does not affect engine operation once the car is already running 8384 85868788. A related, milder report: some owners see the same "key not detected" warning specifically while braking, intermittently and especially in wet weather — this can resolve itself after a few occurrences without any intervention, which is consistent with the same weak-signal/weak-battery pattern rather than indicating a separate fault 8990.

Fob unresponsive after a battery swap or fuse work — needs re-learning. Consistent with the battery-disconnect fix documented above: if a key fob stops responding after the car's battery was swapped or fuses were replaced, the key(s) may have simply become unpaired from the vehicle rather than having a hardware fault. The fix is the standard re-learning procedure, followed step-by-step; if any step in the sequence fails, restart the whole procedure from the beginning rather than trying to resume partway through — this resolves the majority of fob-responsiveness complaints seen in this thread 9192939495969798.

Central-lock key fob stops working after a battery replacement — reprogramming required. A related report: after replacing the key fob's own battery, central locking stopped responding, requiring the key to be reprogrammed. The exact button-press/timing sequence for this varied and wasn't fully pinned down in the thread — it involves inserting the key in the lock cylinder and turning it several times while performing a specific sequence of actions — and the owner in this case ultimately had it resolved by having the dealer reprogram the key rather than working out the DIY sequence 99100101102103 104105106107108109110111112113 114115116117118.

"Key out of zone" warning after a battery swap — normal, self-resolving. After replacing the remote key's battery, the dashboard may show a "Key out of zone" (ключ вне зоны) warning even when the key is inside the vehicle 119120. This is normal behavior, not a malfunction — it can appear intermittently during operation for a while after a battery swap 121122. No action is needed; it resolves on its own.

docs.title: Keyless entry fails on driver door
docs.text:
Tags: #antenna

If keyless entry works on the passenger door but fails on the driver door, the likely cause is antenna oxidation inside the driver door handle 1234. Fix requires professional disassembly of the door and handle to repair/clean the antenna connector; the door handle may need to come off entirely to reach the connector, and it isn't guaranteed to be accessible even then — a full door strip-down is more likely needed 567. This is electrical work best left to a competent auto-electrician, not a DIY fix 5. The problem can recur, and at least one owner reports having had the same issue resolved quickly by the dealer in the car's first year of ownership 89.

Keyless-access reset via battery disconnect. A keyless-access malfunction (door unlock fails, engine start button fails) was resolved by disconnecting the car battery for 10 minutes, then reconnecting it — this resets the relevant electronics. Symptom pattern: the keyless button becomes unresponsive while the remote key fob itself keeps working normally (i.e. the fob-based unlock/lock always still works, only the proximity/button-based keyless functions fail). This looks like a case needing an ECU/module reset rather than an actual component replacement 1011.

PEPS not recognized inside the cabin — interior antenna connector unplugged. If the key fob works fine from outside the car but the PEPS (passive-entry/passive-start) system fails to recognize it once inside the cabin, check whether the interior antenna connector — located near the cup holders — has simply come unplugged; this is a surprisingly simple oversight that fully explains the symptom once found 1213.

Driver-side keyless entry stops responding — general troubleshooting order. When keyless entry (бесключевой доступ) stops working on the driver's side specifically, work through in order: (1) check/replace the remote key fob's battery first; (2) clean the contacts on the door-handle assembly, a common failure point; (3) test the emergency unlock procedure with the key in the ignition — press the fob's lock button three times in quick succession and watch for a door-lock feedback response. If none of these resolve it, an official-service ECU diagnostic session is needed to identify which sensor or module is at fault 141516.

docs.title: LED headlight bulbs — recommendations and fitment
docs.text:
Tags: #led · #headlight · #fog-light

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Fitment fix: LED lamp sockets often have thinner contact tabs than OEM halogen lamps, causing a loose fit in the lamp holder. Fix: wrap electrical tape around the LED lamp's base contacts to build up thickness and get a snug fit — this prevents lamp vibration and intermittent contact 1234.

Recommendations: Carshark 12V LED lamps (available on Ozon) are recommended for cost and light quality. Use a warm 4300K color temperature for both headlights and fog lights to match the factory aesthetic. Previous HID/Xenon lamps can burn the reflector/lens coating; LED lamps don't have this issue. LED 360° 4300K lamps give good output for nighttime visibility 56789.

LED tail-light bulb replacement: LED replacement bulbs for the brake lights can be installed without additional adapters or circuits — a direct replacement works with the OEM socket (low-confidence report) 1011.

Bulb replacement without removing the bumper: headlight bulbs can be swapped without pulling the front bumper, by working through the wheel arch. Procedure: pop out the ~3 plastic plugs/caps in the wheel arch liner to create a gap between the liner and the fender. The driver side is easier — a hand can be threaded in from above, between the air filter housing and the headlight. The passenger side is harder, obstructed by the washer-fluid reservoir; reaching around it and back out through the gap between the arch liner and fender takes more effort (thin/small hands help). For a fully cracked lens that needs replacing (not just the bulb), partial bolt removal via a ratchet from the top, combined with working through the wheel-arch gap, is enough — the lens can be pulled out (and back in) through the same gap without full bumper removal. Wearing gloves/mitts is recommended, since the gap has sharp edges that can cut hands 12.

Yellow-tinted H11 bulbs — poor brightness (avoid for primary use): H11 yellow-tinted bulbs produce the intended yellow glow but with very poor brightness/light output — described as inadequate. Not recommended as primary headlight bulbs 13.

Headlight bulb type and recommended LED replacement: the X80 uses a single HIR2 (9012) bulb socket for both high beam and low beam. Recommended LED alternatives: DAWNKNIGHT K7C at 4300K (110W) — praised by multiple owners for brightness and color temperature; Red Stil brand also performs well. Caveat: LED bulbs with heat sinks struggle in the X80's sealed headlight housing, which limits cooling airflow — output can be ~20% lower than in open-design headlight fixtures on other cars. Cost: LED bulb pairs run 1,600–1,700 RUB (RU market, July 2025); halogen alternatives are cheaper but have a shorter lifespan 14151617181920212223242526.

Xenon vs. LED — community split, no clear consensus: when asked which low-beam bulb upgrade is best, community opinions split. One long-time owner runs xenon, purchased a while ago (specific product links no longer saved/available), and reports not liking LED due to unspecified "nuances," though acknowledges many other owners are happy with LED. This suggests the LED-vs-halogen fitment/output caveats noted above (sealed housing limiting cooling, ~20% output loss) may be part of why some owners still prefer xenon despite LED being the community's more commonly recommended path 2728.

LED bulb single-diode failure — halogen swap workaround: LED headlight bulb failure can show as one side burning white (normal) while the other burns weak/blue — a sign that one internal LED diode has died. To replace: remove the LED bulb's adapter/mounting ring from the headlight housing, pull out the old bulb, and insert a halogen bulb as a temporary fix while sourcing a replacement LED. ⚠️ Note: the adapter/mounting rings are fragile and may break during removal 29303132333435363738.

Headlamp socket type, self-installation, and beam-height adjustment: the X80 headlamps use an HIR2/9012 socket (both near and far beam share one bulb). LED bulbs fit this socket and can be self-installed by removing the lamp housing — no special tools needed, and installation takes only minutes. Polarity does not matter for some LED bulbs (per one owner's confirmed test). After installing new bulbs, beam height can be adjusted using the exterior adjustment dial — no professional alignment stand is required, though a proper alignment remains optional/recommended. If new bulbs cause glare to oncoming traffic, lower the beam dial slightly. Popular upgrade options: MTF Cyber Light (~6,000 RUB, RU market, March 2026); budget alternatives (~1,500 RUB, RU market, March 2026); and Novsight N37 LED (recommended, see below) 394041424344454647484950515253545556.

Novsight N37 LED bulbs (HIR2/9012, 120W-equivalent pair): the Novsight N37 LED headlamp bulbs, sized for the HIR2/9012 socket above, are sold as a 120W-equivalent pair and available on OZON. One owner ordered them and confirmed they're a good fit for the X80 54.

DawnKnight K7C — full part number confirmed: the full part number for the DawnKnight HIR2/9012 4300K 110W bulb set (2 bulbs) referenced above is K7C-4300K-110W-9012. Owners describe it as a "light bomb" upgrade — reportedly excellent brightness improvement over stock 575859.

Early independent corroboration — HIR2 single-bulb type and K7C 110W brand, with a power-rating clarification: an earlier, independent thread corroborates two points above: (1) the X80 headlight uses a single HIR2 bulb type for both beams; (2) a K7C 110W HIR2 upgrade bulb (available via online retailers) was recommended and purchased successfully for improved low-light penetration over the stock 55W bulbs. Power clarification: the "110W" rating is the combined power of both headlight bulbs (2×55W each) — this matches the factory-stock bulbs' total power as well, so a "110W" aftermarket bulb set is not inherently more powerful than stock on a per-bulb basis; any brightness gain comes from bulb efficiency/technology rather than raw wattage 6061626364.

In-progress LED headlight install — Ozon sourcing, price (low confidence): one owner installed a set of aftermarket LED headlight lamps purchased on Ozon for 2,452 RUB (RU market, July 2026) and booked a professional headlight-adjustment appointment for the following week to finish dialing in the beam; performance evaluation was still pending at report time 65.

docs.title: LED sequential turn signals and custom lighting
docs.text:
Tags: #led · #turn-signal · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

LED sequential/blinker lamps: aftermarket LED sequential (running- light style) turn-signal lamps in the 500–700 RUB (RU market, as of August 2025) price range can replace the factory indicators. Installation involves cutting a standard H11/H7-style LED bulb to separate its base, removing the original contacts, and reassembling with a custom sequential-lighting module — video instructions are available in the community for this modification.

Custom acrylic grille emblems: custom grille emblems made from 3mm acrylic/composite material can be sourced from local signage/printing shops, costing roughly 1,000–2,500 RUB (RU market, August 2025) for a full set (front badge, rear badge, steering-wheel badge). Materials used: 3mm acrylic or similar, printed with a vinyl or enamel finish 1234567.

DIY DRL retrofit with sequential turn-signal function: aftermarket LED strip tape can add daytime running lights (DRL) with sequential turn signals to the headlights (product searchable on Ozon, e.g. https://ozon.ru/t/mz8BnEa). Features: 7-color or plain-white DRL options, a "bungee" turn-signal function (the strip turns sequential when the turn signal is engaged), USB charging. Installation: connect to the wires inside the headlight assembly — full headlight disassembly is not always required. Connector types vary between MT (manual) and AT (automatic) trim versions. A white DRL with a yellow sequential turn signal is the most common configuration 8910111213141516.

Custom LED turn signal replacement units: custom turn-signal installations replace the original turn-signal locations with LED units that combine DRL and turn-signal functions, using integrated circuits and decoders. Sourcing: a fully custom job is typically ordered through advertising/sign shops that can fabricate the housing; ready-made units with a DRL + turn-signal "Mini LED" function (P21W / 1156 base) are also available on Wildberries. Avoid "corn-type" bulbs (кукурузинки) — they burn out quickly; dedicated LED turn-signal modules are recommended instead 17181920.

DRL + factory front turn-signal integration — decoder gap: LED daytime running lights can be integrated with the front turn signals for dual functionality, but this requires finding LED modules with an integrated turn-signal capability or doing custom wiring. Most off-the-shelf modules sold on Wildberries come without an "обманка" (decoder) for turn-signal flashing, so getting the factory dashboard turn-signal indicator to work correctly needs either custom integration or specifically sourcing a unit with a built-in decoder 2122.

Custom rear signal/marker light integration into the bumper: an advanced customization integrates the turn signal, brake light, and reverse-light functions into the rear bumper as a unified light assembly. Procedure: (1) route light power and signal wires from the existing tail-light harness to custom LED elements mounted in the bumper; (2) optionally add a "night disco mode" (flashing/sequential light show) synced with the turn signals or rear fog lights; (3) relay modules may be needed to handle multiple light circuits independently. One user demonstrated the installation with video evidence of the turn signals and brake lights working correctly once integrated into the bumper; the kit was purchased from AliExpress (roughly 1 year before March 2024, estimated USD 7–10 (RU market, March 2024)) 23242526272829.

LED lighting retrofit guide — Drive2 write-up: a complete LED lighting installation guide for the X80 is available on Drive2: https://www.drive2.ru/l/580702944115032920/ 30.

docs.title: Disabling automatic mirror folding
docs.text:
Tags: #mirrors · #alarm · #winter

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

To stop the mirrors from automatically folding every time the alarm is armed/disarmed (annoying in winter), one owner documented a hardware modification: locate the pink wire in the driver-door wiring harness (under the door card), cut it, extend both ends out, and wire in a manual push-button switch. This lets the mirrors fold only on a deliberate button press, rather than automatically with the siren/alarm — requires opening up the door card 123. Alternative without opening the door: a dealer can disable auto-fold via software reprogramming, at roughly 1000–1500 RUB (RU market, 2024) 1.

Confirmation of the dealer-side disable option, plus other settings in the same menu. Corroborating the dealer-reprogramming alternative already documented above: automatic mirror folding on lock can indeed be disabled at an official FAW dealer, via a "comfort block" settings module in the dealer service menu — this is not accessible via OBD or any user-facing menu. The same dealer-side settings module reportedly also allows customizing other comfort features, including the speed threshold for automatic door locking (20+ km/h) — the same feature documented in this card's sibling "disable automatic door locking" card. This capability is referenced in the owner's manual 456.

Fob-vs-key selective fold, battery-disconnect trick, and why the mechanism is safe to fight. Three more no-dealer-visit approaches reported by different owners: (1) Most reliable in practice: on cars with an alarm/starter system tied to a remote fob, mirrors fold only when locking with the fob — locking with the physical key does not trigger folding, giving selective control without any wiring or reprogramming 7. (2) Battery-disconnect workaround: disconnecting the battery terminal stops the mirrors from folding at all, because the fold-on-lock behavior has to be "relearned"/retrained after a reset — it does not just skip once, it stays off until retrained 89. (3) Door-open trick — reported unreliable: opening a door at the exact moment central locking engages was also mentioned as a way to skip a fold, but one report says it worked only once by accident rather than consistently 10. Separately, the mirror-fold mechanism has built-in force-limiting protection, so it will not break even if it meets resistance while folding/unfolding — relevant if experimenting with any of the above 11. Motivation for all of this: unstable regional climate (rain followed by frost) makes automatic folding particularly annoying to owners in some regions during winter 12. Combined with the dealer-side "comfort block" reprogramming already documented above, an authorized dealer can also do this with a factory diagnostic scanner rather than only the informal service-menu route 13.

docs.title: Mirror auto-fold mechanism — winter plastic gear issues
docs.text:
Tags: #mirrors · #winter

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

The mirror auto-fold feature can experience issues in winter: the plastic gears may freeze or resist folding in cold weather 12. A configuration guide exists (see media 13072) showing the button sequence on the door panel to enable/configure automatic mirror folding 3.

Conflict: Some owners report no problems even after 3 years of ownership in cold climates, while others recommend applying WD-40 or silicone lubricant around the fold-joint mechanism preventatively 45. There is also a safety concern raised: mirrors may fail to unfold automatically after a remote-start car unlock, which some owners consider a hazard when pulling away 67.

Asymmetric folding is a separate, unrelated design trait: independent of the winter freezing issue, multiple owners report the mirrors fold unevenly/asymmetrically (one side folds further than the other) regardless of season. One owner who raised the question found that other members hadn't specifically paid attention to it before checking their own car, suggesting the asymmetry is common enough to be easily overlooked. This is treated by the community as a design characteristic of the folding mechanism itself rather than a defect or a warranty/repair issue 8910.

docs.title: Monochrome head unit intermittent power loss
docs.text:
Tags: #head-unit · #fuse

The stock monochrome (single-color-display) head unit can stop powering on after previously working intermittently — one owner had it happen again after a prior recovery a year earlier that had lasted a couple of days before returning to normal 1. Root cause is most likely in the fuse/power-supply circuit rather than the unit itself. Diagnostic steps: pull the head unit out and test for power presence at its connector using a simple test lamp (not a multimeter) — a test lamp makes a dead-power condition obvious even with a weak/partial connection that a multimeter might misleadingly read as "present" 2. Specifically check the 5A fuse in the driver-side fuse block 2. One owner found the failure traced to an internally blown fuse inside the head unit itself, separate from the main cabin fuse block 3. This is not a one-off — multiple owners have hit the same monochrome head-unit power issue.

Complete power loss while driving, with an audible relay click. A related but distinct case: the head unit doesn't just glitch, it cuts power entirely while driving, and a relay can be heard clicking each time 45. Recommended diagnostic order for this variant: (1) check the main power-supply fuses first, not only the head-unit-specific one 6; (2) inspect the power connector for oxidation or a loose pin — the same connector issue described above 6; (3) rule out the circuit being wired to share power with the ECU, which is a suspected wiring mistake distinct from a simple blown fuse 7.

Stock radio not powering on after the car sits idle. If the stock radio fails to power on after the vehicle has been sitting, first disconnect the battery negative terminal and reconnect it — this resets the unit and is the standard first step. Also check that the power on/off button isn't mechanically stuck pressed. If it still won't power up, an internal fuse inside the unit itself may have failed, or the unit needs service; several owners in this thread ended up preferring an aftermarket-unit replacement over repair, citing better reliability and features 891011121314.

Burned fuse in the driver-footwell fuse block cuts head-unit power. A separate, unrelated case: if the head unit (radio) suddenly stops working entirely, check for a burned fuse in the fuse block located in the driver's footwell (near the left leg space) — this specific fuse controls power to the head-unit circuit and is a distinct failure point from the internal-fuse case above 1516171819.

docs.title: No-crank — RKE relay and harness damage
docs.text:
Tags: #immobilizer

Symptom: pressing the start button gives no starter cranking at all — the immobilizer warning light flashes, but the green start-button "ready" indicator shows normally, and no relay clicks can be heard anywhere in the car 1. This is a distinct scenario from the simple starter-relay thermal-sticking issue documented elsewhere in this section (see starter-relay-no-crank.md) — here the absence of any relay click at all points further upstream, toward the permission/enable signal for the starter relay rather than the relay itself.

Diagnostic sequence. (1) Check the RKE (remote keyless entry) relay block first — it's located at the passenger-side door sill/pillar — since the "permission" signal that allows the starter relay to engage originates from the RKE block; inspect its connectors for oxidation 23. (2) Verify fuse integrity throughout, as a basic check 4. (3) Open the RKE block itself and inspect internally for damage/corrosion; after reassembly, re-verify everything again before concluding it's fixed 5.

Root cause found in this case: accident-damaged harness. The owner disclosed that after a prior collision, the wiring harness running under the left front fender had been partially severed/damaged 6. Given that history, the diagnosis converged strongly (99% per one responder) on this damaged harness section as the actual root cause, rather than a component failure — the earlier RKE-relay-block troubleshooting steps were reasonable first checks, but the real fix required tracing and repairing the specific accident-damaged harness run under the left fender 7.

docs.title: Normal dashboard warning-indicator behavior
docs.text:
Tags: #normal-behavior · #dashboard · #pre-facelift

Two frequently-asked "is this normal?" dashboard behaviors, both answered from the same discussion thread.

Oil-pressure indicator light. Normal sequence: the oil-pressure light glows when the ignition is switched on (before the engine starts), then extinguishes once the engine actually starts and oil pressure builds — i.e. it should stay lit only during the pre-start ignition-on phase. One owner reported the light extinguishing even without the engine being started at all, which is abnormal and points to a sensor or bulb fault, not a light that's supposed to constantly glow. Separately: if the light comes on and stays on while driving, that indicates an actual engine oil-pressure loss and should be treated as urgent 12 34.

Warning beeps — door-open and headlights-left-on. Two distinct, normal beep scenarios on recent X80s: (1) the car beeps when the ignition is on and a door is opened — a standard safety reminder, though not present on every trim/variant; (2) the car beeps as a reminder when the engine is off but the headlights were left on. Both are expected factory behavior. Note: some vehicles with an aftermarket alarm installed may add extra beep signals on top of these, which can make it harder to tell factory beeps from alarm-added ones 5678 9101112131415.

Immobilizer (security) indicator light blinking with no key inserted. A third normal-behavior case: the red immobilizer/security indicator blinking continuously while no key is inserted is expected, factory behavior — it indicates the anti-theft system is armed. It turns off once a key is inserted and the engine starts, and resumes blinking again after the engine is turned off and the key removed. This is NOT an error on any modern X80 model. The one abnormal pattern to watch for: the light being solid red (not blinking) while the car is stationary — that would indicate an actual fault, unlike the normal blinking-with-no-key state 1617181920212223 2425262728293031 32. A later report matches this: an owner saw a dashboard indicator blinking after the ignition was switched off, even with the alarm armed; a member confirmed that a flashing security indicator is normal for the factory alarm, another suggested a service check just to be sure 3334.

Hidden "Test" mode on the instrument cluster (pre-facelift). Pre-facelift FAW Besturn X80 models reportedly have a hidden "Test" mode on the instrument cluster, accessed via cluster diagnostics.
