  • One member questioned whether the "no PCV valve" theory for rough idle/jerking actually holds, suggesting a muffler/exhaust modification might be the real fix instead. Not resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: Crankshaft damper failure and cross-sourcing
docs.text:
Tags: #mazda-6-compat · #ford-compat

Failure and mileage. The crankshaft vibration damper (шкив/демпфер коленвала) can fail at relatively low mileage — one reported case failed at just 70,000 km123. The failure mode described is the internal wave-damper element (волной) deteriorating and cracking apart ("демфер разбился")3.

Sourcing difficulty. This part is reported as hard to source, with no significant aftermarket availability — one member's blunt reaction to the failure was that this specific part is "a shame, there's basically nothing available anywhere" ("По данной зч печалька, толком нигде нет")4.

Cross-manufacturer alternative. Potential cross-compatible replacement sources suggested: the Ford Duratec HE (the same engine family used in the X80) or Mazda 6 (GG/GH generation), since both use the same/a very similar engine variant — described as "однотипные двс" (same-type engines)5.

Crankshaft pulley — no keyway, requires a jig for correct positioning. The X80 crankshaft pulley (шкив коленвала) has no keyway (шпонки нет) and no visible timing marks, so its position cannot be set by visual alignment. Correct removal/reinstallation procedure: (1) note the current position before removal if possible; (2) use the factory specification/jig ("спецура") for correct positioning; (3) do not rely on marks or physical features for timing678910.

Crankshaft pulley part number — 100504537K, from the second Telegram group. A separate community (FAW BESTURN X80 group) gives the crankshaft pulley (шкив коленвала) part number for the FAW Besturn X80 2013+: 100504537K. As of that report, this part was listed as discontinued/out of stock at the used-parts retailer checked (iZAP24, Yekaterinburg) — consistent with the sourcing difficulty already documented on this card for crankshaft-damper-related components11.

docs.title: Crankshaft seal inspection and replacement
docs.text:
Tags: #oil-leak · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Symptom and typical mileage. The crankshaft seal ("сальник коленвала") can develop an oil leak around 130,000+ km, typically noticed as oil weeping/seepage at the joint between the engine and transmission — the location makes it easy to mistake for a transmission-side leak, so inspect carefully to identify which side is actually leaking before ordering parts.12345

Labor-intensive job, often bundled with valve work. Replacing the crankshaft seal is labor-intensive because of the disassembly required to reach it, so owners frequently schedule it together with valve-clearance adjustment work (see the separate valve-clearance card) when the engine is already partially suspended/accessed for that job — sharing the labor overhead between the two jobs.12345

Sourcing. Compatible seals from Mazda are available and commonly used as a cross-reference part. Front and rear crankshaft seals are sold separately (not as a combined kit) on Ozon and other retailers — make sure to identify and order the correct one (front vs. rear) for the leak location found on inspection.12345

docs.title: Crankshaft seal oil leak near engine mount
docs.text:
Tags: #oil-leak · #diagnostics

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Symptom and likely source. An oil stain observed in the engine compartment near the engine-mounting area is most likely sourced from the crankshaft seal (сальник коленвала), not the oil pump or camshaft seal. The crankshaft seal is located at the bottom/rear of the engine, near the flywheel12345.

When to worry. Small oil traces alone do not indicate imminent failure — monitor for progression rather than acting immediately. Wet spots on components without any puddling underneath the car are considered acceptable to watch; actual dripping (puddling) is what warrants seal replacement12345.

Front crankshaft seal — part number. Front crankshaft seal (передний сальник коленвала) part number for the FAW Besturn X80: 1005090-37K. Available from multiple Russian suppliers including KitZapchasti67.

Crankshaft seal — Victor Reinz alternative for restyled (2019+) models. A cross-brand alternative crankshaft seal, Victor Reinz 81-53254-00, fits the restyled (2019+) X80. Reported labor cost for the seal replacement: approximately 500 RUB (RU market, Jan 2026), when performed alongside other work on the vehicle at the same time (i.e. incremental labor, not a standalone job price)89.

docs.title: Cruise control activation via diagnostic software
docs.text:
Tags: #cruise-control · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Cruise control can be activated (enabled in the ECU) using DiagZone Pro diagnostic software 1. The hardest part of the job is physically locating the cruise-control switch — an 8-pin connector positioned on the left side of the steering-wheel/column area 23. One owner sourced a pre-restyle cruise-control switch from izap24.ru and confirmed it fits and works on a post-restyle car 4.

Aftermarket cruise-control button + activation-service pricing: physical cruise-control buttons for installation into the existing steering-wheel button panel are available on AliExpress; installation itself is self-serviceable with no special tools needed. However, activation still requires the specialized OBD programming software (per DiagZone note above), which is not widely distributed — the actual activation procedure takes only ~10 minutes once the software/technician is available. Reported service cost: 3,000–8,000 RUB (RU market, March 2026). Some shops quote high prices (8,000 RUB+, RU market, March 2026) without actually having the capability to perform the activation, so it's worth vetting a shop's actual equipment before paying 567891011.

docs.title: Cruise control behavior and limitations
docs.text:
Tags: #cruise-control · #conflict

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Reported limitations. FAW's cruise control is described by some owners as unreliable in several respects: it does not hold the exact set speed (±2-3 km/h error reported), it over-accelerates on hills before correcting itself, and it has a slow resume response after being paused/reactivated. It is compared unfavorably to Renault's cruise-control systems in this report123.

Conflict — some owners report much better precision. Other owners (referenced elsewhere in this KB, e.g. "Fill") report the cruise control holding speed with ±1 km/h precision, suggesting the experience varies — possibly by model year, trim, or individual car/ECU calibration rather than a universal flaw.

Cruise control availability on manual-transmission models. Cruise control is available on manual (MKPP) transmission models of the X80 and is installed on some variants from the factory. Cruise control is not simply a button added to the steering wheel — it requires program/software installation to enable the function, and the configuration differs from the automatic-transmission variant4567891011121314.

Speed increment differs by transmission type. Cruise control's speed adjustment increment (per button press) is factory-programmed differently by transmission: manual (MKPP) increments by 0.4 km/h per step; automatic (AKPP) increments by 0.7 km/h per step. This is fixed in firmware and cannot be changed by the user151617.

Where the community disagrees

  • One report describes cruise control as imprecise (±2-3 km/h, poor hill behavior, slow resume) compared unfavorably to Renault; other owners elsewhere report ±1 km/h precision. Not resolved — may reflect model-year/trim/ECU-calibration variance rather than a single consistent behavior.

docs.title: CV joints and boots — INKO, Motus, tripod case
docs.text:
Tags: #cv-joint · #part-number · #manual-transmission · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Aftermarket CV joint (ШРУС) and boot items for the front drive shafts, plus a manual-gearbox right-shaft inner-joint case. Wear symptoms are in high-speed vibration and CV joint wear and MT right drive shaft — inner CV joint alternatives.

Outer joint INKO 319092A. An owner fitted an outer CV joint for the front drive shaft with 28/30 splines and ABS ring count 44 (ABS 44), brand INKO, catalogue number 319092A; he reports it fitted perfectly and the splines matched. It was bought from Wildberries and then linked again from Ozon12.

Universal boot Motus FBUNI90. A Wildberries listing (May 2025) for a universal CV boot, article FBUNI90 by Motus. The thread does not say whether it fits the X80, so compare the size with the original boot before buying3.

Right shaft, manual gearbox: suspected inner joint wear. On a manual (МКПП) car an owner suspected the inner tripod joint (трипод) of the right drive shaft after finding a listing that seemed to confirm it. He planned to replace the whole shaft with one from a Mazda, matching the outer joint flange and 28 splines and measuring the shaft length. The original tripod number asked about is B5DA022520, with no supplier given. Another member would wait until it fails before pulling the shaft apart45.

docs.title: Vibration at 65-80 km/h — CV joint wear
docs.text:
Tags: #cv-joint · #vibration

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Symptom. A violent vibration appeared suddenly, with no prior warning signs, specifically in the 65-80 km/h speed range, and the car pulled to one side under it; the vibration was much less noticeable outside that speed window1. Over 170,000 km, the owner notes this kind of unexpected repair has come up more than once1.

Diagnosis and elimination process. The recommended approach is methodical elimination of other possible causes — wheel balance, rotor/disc runout, tire condition — before targeting the drivetrain1. In this case, a preliminary inspection found the right inner CV joint ("граната") severely worn, with the left side questionable as well1. The fix combined: wheel balancing, brake rotor machining, winter tire installation, and eventual CV joint/driveshaft replacement1.

Confirmed by a separate case. In an unrelated report, replacing the complete right front drive shaft assembly (root cause: a defective internal SHRUS/CV joint) eliminated a vibration during acceleration; the part was sourced from ooove.ru at what the owner considered a reasonable price for a complete assembly, and the vibration was gone immediately after installation23.

Right inner CV joint — part number and fitment caveat. For the automatic-transmission X80, the right inner CV joint (ШРУС) part number is B5CA022520, priced at roughly 23,640 RUB (March 2025) in the Russian market. Fitment of aftermarket CV joints in general is reported as challenging: many aftermarket analogues have tripod-roller sizes or shaft diameters that don't match the original FAW drive shafts, so verify dimensions carefully before ordering an aftermarket alternative45678.

Internal spline count and dimension research (SHRUS). Community research into CV-joint internal spline compatibility: a Mazda Sedan GG 2.0/141hp (2002-2005) external SHRUS, part MA-44A44, has 28 external splines, 32 internal splines, 62mm hub diameter, 92mm ABS-ring diameter, 27mm inner-shaft spline diameter, and 145mm total height, priced around 3,200 RUB (RU market, May 2025). Mechanical inspection of an X80 inner drive shaft found 24 splines. One owner attempted fitting the Mazda SHRUS but it failed due to spline mismatch910111213. Conflict: spline-count measurements disagree between an owner's own count (24 splines) and other data/photo analysis suggesting a higher count; a caliper-measurement photo was inconclusive without a scale reference.

Left CV joint (tripod bearing) failure — replacement strategy. When the left CV joint's tripod bearing fails (producing a clicking/banging noise), replacing the tripod bearing alone is possible but often leads to fitment/compatibility problems. Recommended approach: replace the complete left drive-shaft assembly — part 5CA12560X for AKPP, 5CA02560X for MКПП — rather than the bearing alone, to avoid complications. Available from retailers such as kitzapchasti.ru and autocraft-kzn.ru; one 2019-model price reported was ~20,702 RUB14151617181920.

Left drive assembly specifications — restyle (2019+). For the restyled X80 (2019+), the left drive-shaft assembly measures 700mm total length, with 27 splines at the wheel end and 28 splines at the gearbox end. Part numbers: 5CA12560X (AKPP), 5CA02560X (MКПП)2122.

Cross-brand CV joint research and replacement risk. Other Mazda CV joints (e.g. Mazda 6 GG 2002-2007: 648mm length, 28 splines on both ends) can theoretically match by dimension, but substitution is risky in practice — inner CV diameter and spline alignment are often incompatible between models and transmission types. Recommendation: don't attempt a cross-brand substitution without full disassembly and individual component matching; the safe path is the exact OEM X80 assembly (5CA02560X for MКПП, 5CA12560X for AKPP)2324252627.

Quick-repair dust boot for the external CV joint. A quick-install dust boot (пыльник) for the external CV joint is available with installation clamps included, advertised for fitting without removing the SHRUS from the car. Useful for a fast interim repair without a full CV-joint replacement28.

Mazda 6 GG external SHRUS reported compatible. The external SHRUS (CV joint) from the Mazda 6 GG generation is reported compatible with the FAW X80, usable either as a direct replacement or as a donor part for custom solutions2930.

Mazda SHRUS adaptation via spline machining. A Mazda donor SHRUS can be adapted to fit the FAW X80 by machining down the shaft spline — roughly 0.35mm removed per side from the spline diameter via lathe turning. This requires access to a machine shop with a lathe313233.

Complete SHRUS replacement cost. A complete SHRUS (CV joint) assembly replacement cost roughly 8,500 RUB at Russian-market shops as of October 2025 — significantly more than a used donor part, but arrives pre-assembled with no custom machining needed34.

Internal CV joint (tripod) failure — diagnosis and pricing. Symptoms of internal CV-joint (tripod) failure: vertical play felt when the joint is pulled toward the cabin, often with a creaking/clunking sound, while the external joint remains solid. The tripod's three rollers act as bearings and fail as they wear; the part structure is a cross-pin with rollers and a splined collar. Automatic-transmission cars use a tripod-type internal joint. Reported pricing: individual internal joint ~20,000 RUB, complete assembly ~28,500 RUB (RU market, Oct 2025); OEM tripod-only parts available from one supplier at 8,500 RUB with a 3-week delivery. Mazda 6 (B50) internal joints may fit, per unverified community consensus35363738394041424344454647484950515253. Conflict: pricing and sourcing disagree — one report of Mazda B50 tripods fitting after a 3-week special order versus another owner's high pricing (28,500 RUB assembled) versus a third owner's cheaper OEM-tripod-only supply (8,500 RUB), all RU market, Oct 2025.

CV joint (ШРУС) replacement — part number, price spread, and AT/MT tooth-count caveat. Standard part code BM1122510 is confirmed on the KitParts catalog. Reported price spread (RU market, Jan 2026): 8,500 RUB (MasterGTR) up to 12,000-18,000 RUB at other vendors, with reports as high as 22,000 RUB. Critical caveat: the inner/outer shafts differ by transmission type — AT and MT versions have different internal CV-joint tooth configurations despite sharing the same catalog part number. Mazda 6 GG/GH shares a platform with the X80 and may cross-compatible (model MZ37A44 mentioned as a potential match), but vendors report the same catalog number exists in 2+ tooth-count versions, so physical inspection/measurement is required before purchase. One vendor (Василий, MasterGTR) requires VIN + transmission type + a photo to confirm the correct variant. Outer CVs are more standardized across variants; inner CVs are transmission-specific54555657585960616263646566676869707172737475767778798081828384858687888990919293949596979899100. Conflict: compatibility reports are contradictory — one user claims a Mazda-sourced CV matches the native X80 CV exactly, others remain skeptical without direct physical comparison; the community consensus is that measurement/testing is required before committing to any cross-brand part.

OEM CV joint restated — pricing and Chinese-supplier sourcing (automatic, pre-restyle). OEM CV joint for the pre-restyled automatic-transmission X80: part BM1122510, priced 8,000-8,500 RUB in the Russian market (Jan 2026). Available from Chinese suppliers (e.g. via Chita), with delivery via SDEK costing roughly 1,000 RUB (RU market, Jan 2026)101102103104105.

Mazda CV joint cross-brand alternative — lathe modification required. Some Mazda CV joints can be fitted to the X80 with modification: the shaft diameter typically needs to be turned down by roughly 0.05mm on a lathe, since Mazda parts have a slightly smaller spline diameter than OEM (measurement needed to confirm fitment on each specific unit). Community members have succeeded with this modification, but it requires precision machine work and post-fit testing106107108109110. Conflict: results vary between owners attempting Mazda alternatives — some succeed with lathe modification, others report uncertain results; overall community preference is OEM parts if the budget allows.

Intermediate shaft bearing — Mazda compatibility, unconfirmed (low confidence). A separate, brief inquiry asked whether the intermediate shaft bearing (a bearing supporting the automatic-transmission driveshaft assembly, distinct from the CV/tripod joints already documented on this card) can be sourced from a Mazda equivalent. The response received suggested checking the specific transmission model before assuming compatibility, but no confirmation either way was reached in this exchange — flagged here as an open, unverified question rather than a resolved cross-compatibility111112.

Right outer CV joint part number — independent confirmation from the second Telegram group. A separate community (FAW BESTURN X80 group) independently confirms the same BM1122510 part number already documented on this card for the outer CV joint (ШРУС наружный), specifically for a 2017 pre-facelift, automatic-transmission X80. Cross-brand/analogue fitment availability was raised but not confirmed in this particular exchange113114115116117118.

Inner SHRUS (manual transmission) — sold only as a complete assembly, ~25,000 RUB. A separate report from the second Telegram group (FAW BESTURN X80): after a torn dust boot was diagnosed on a manual-transmission car, the shop advised that the front right inner SHRUS (ШРУС передний правый) is sold only as a complete assembly, at roughly 25,000 RUB (RU market, Apr 2026) — no individual/partial-repair option was available at that shop, consistent with the sourcing difficulty already documented on this card. A community member flagged that when this joint fails, the intermediate shaft and its support bearing (промежуточный вал с подвесным подшипником) should also be inspected, since this component is often overlooked during a SHRUS repair and can itself be a source of secondary damage119120121122123124125.

Drive shafts are NOT interchangeable between manual and automatic gearbox variants. Confirming and generalizing the AT/MT distinction already documented on this card: the drive shafts (referred to loosely as "CVVT shafts" in this report) differ structurally between manual and automatic transmission variants and cannot be swapped between the two. The manual-transmission shaft has a different spline profile from the automatic's. The right intermediate shaft also differs between the two gearbox types — the two parts look visually similar but are internally different — so identification requires physically checking the spline configuration rather than relying on visual inspection alone126127128.

Right-side CV joint (tripod/ШРУС) spline configuration — manual transmission. Detailed spline spec for the right-side, manual-transmission CV joint: 24 internal splines (sometimes reported as 26 — treat as an open discrepancy), 28 external splines, and a 44-tooth ABS ring. The right drive-shaft assembly includes an internal CV joint that feeds into an extension/intermediate shaft supported by a bearing. Critical part-number caveat: 5CA02550X is for the manual-transmission right drive shaft — this is a different series from the ...2550 numbers used elsewhere on this card, so verify the spline count physically before ordering, since a wrong spline count will prevent proper fitment129130131.

Right drive shaft internal wear — vibration in pedals/steering at 65,000 km. At 65,000 km, one owner's right drive shaft developed internal wear that manifested as vibration felt in the pedals and steering wheel specifically under load/acceleration. The wear appears to be inside the CV joint or the shaft itself, causing an imbalance; the repair requires shaft replacement — consistent with the load/speed-dependent vibration pattern already documented at the top of this card — confidence: medium132.

OEM CV-joint retaining-ring undersizing, and Mazda Tribute CV-joint experience. A separate, detailed thread on OEM vs. Mazda-donor CV joints: the OEM CV joint may ship with an undersized retaining ring, which can allow the joint to pop out of its seat when the steering is turned to full lock. A Mazda Tribute (2000-2007) CV joint is reported to be a close physical match and can be installed, but has developed unexplained spinning/slipping issues in at least one case. The Mazda Tribute's retaining ring (smaller diameter) can be swapped onto the OEM joint, or vice versa, as a workaround for the ring-sizing issue. OEM replacement cost: roughly 8,500 RUB (RU market, Aug 2026). On teardown, if only the external CV joint is damaged, the internal joint can usually be reused — it is disassemblable and can be separated/reassembled with care (a precision job, explicitly not a job for an angle grinder)133134135136137138139140141142143144131145146147148. Conflict: the Mazda Tribute CV joint is reported by one owner as "almost compatible" but caused an unexplained spinning issue after installation; another owner reports a successful swap after modifying the retaining ring. Community takeaway: the exact OEM joint remains the safest choice despite the ~8,500 RUB cost (RU market, Aug 2026), given these mixed Mazda Tribute results.

Where the community disagrees

  • Spline-count data disagrees: one owner's own physical count found 24 splines on the X80 inner drive shaft, while other data/photo analysis in the same thread suggested a higher count; a caliper-measurement photo was inconclusive without a scale reference. Not resolved within this data batch.
  • Pricing/sourcing for internal CV joints (tripods) disagree across reports: one case involved Mazda B50 tripods fitting via a 3-week special order, another owner reports a high price (28,500 RUB assembled), a third reports a cheaper OEM-tripod-only supply (8,500 RUB). Not resolved within this data batch.
  • CV-joint tooth-count/compatibility claims conflict: one user reports a Mazda-sourced CV joint matches the native X80 CV exactly; others remain skeptical absent direct physical comparison. Community consensus is to measure/test before committing. Not resolved within this data batch.
  • Results attempting Mazda CV-joint cross-brand substitution vary: some owners succeed after lathe modification, others report uncertain outcomes. Not resolved within this data batch.
  • Mazda Tribute (2000-2007) CV joint is reported "almost compatible" by one owner but caused an unexplained spinning/slipping issue; another owner reports a successful swap after modifying the retaining ring. OEM original is presented as the safest choice despite the ~8,500 RUB cost. Not resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: High-speed vibration and CV joint wear
docs.text:
Tags: #cv-joint · #vibration · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Clicking on turns — first check hub nuts: clicking or popping heard during turns, especially at full lock, and typically on one side only, indicates CV joint wear. Before assuming a full joint replacement is needed, first check/tighten the front hub nuts — a loose hub nut can produce a similar click; if the noise persists after tightening, the CV joint itself needs replacement 123.

Clicking on turns — CV joint vs. steering rack, unresolved case: in a separate discussion, clicking/popping while turning was debated as either CV joint (ШРУС) or steering-rack wear. CV joint damage typically follows a torn rubber boot letting water/mud into the joint; if it progresses, it can leave the car undriveable and require towing — always have a service center inspect audible clicking promptly. In this particular case, however, one owner's clicking noise disappeared after a steering rack replacement, not a CV joint replacement — so the two causes can sound alike and should both be checked before assuming which part is at fault 456789101112.

CV axle boot cross-fit for manual transmission: CV axle boots labeled "internal front, manual transmission" (пыльник шруса на механику внутренний передний) fit both the internal and external drive-shaft positions. MOTUS FB UNI 90 universal boots are confirmed compatible — high-temperature-stable, quiet in operation; market price ~768₽ (marked down from 1,690₽, RU market) 131415. Vibration diagnosis and fixes: steering-wheel vibration at speeds above 100 km/h can have multiple causes — (1) tire condition/balance, (2) wheel alignment geometry, (3) internal left CV joint wear. In one case, replacing the right drive shaft resolved a strong vibration that had been present in the 60–80 km/h range; residual vibration remaining at 20–40 km/h and returning above 150 km/h suggested the left CV joint was a separate, still-unresolved contributor in a multi-factor vibration 161718. In a separate case, vibration appearing above 120 km/h was resolved by replacing the right inner CV joint together with the complete drive-shaft assembly; wheel balancing and rim condition (possible deformation) are also recommended checks for this symptom 1920.

Unanswered parts query: one owner asked for the part number of the right outer CV joint (ШРУС наружный правый) for the manual transmission variant specifically. No definitive answer was given in the thread — likely available through FAW parts suppliers or by cross-referencing similar Mazda/Chinese-platform vehicles, but this has not been confirmed by the community yet 21.

Whining under acceleration: a whining or grinding noise that increases with engine load/acceleration, especially noticeable while turning, may indicate internal CV joint wear or damage — described as a characteristic audible symptom of a failing constant-velocity joint. Professional inspection of the front axle assembly is recommended 22.

CV boot cross-fit: CV axle (drive shaft) rubber boots from the Mazda 6 fit the X80, confirmed at least for the outer boots; right-side axle fitment has been specifically confirmed 23.

Unresolved: right CV shaft seal: an owner asked about replacing the right front CV shaft seal on a manual-transmission X80, but no exact seal dimensions or part numbers were identified in that thread — a November 2023 replacement date was referenced on another vehicle as context, without further detail 24.

Tangential note — unrelated cross-brand CV/dust-boot compatibility: in a low-confidence, largely off-topic discussion about cross-brand parts, Nissan dust boots were mentioned as fitting the Lada Niva (not the X80) — included here only as a community reference point, not a verified X80 fitment 25.

CV axle shafts differ by transmission — spline count unresolved: outer CV joints differ between manual-transmission (MT) and automatic- transmission (AT) X80 models; inner CV joints also differ by transmission. Aftermarket/replica replacement shafts do not fit reliably, reportedly due to spline/valve size mismatches. The exact spline count is unresolved in the community: the commonly assumed figure of 32 splines was questioned after checking Drive2 documentation, with the facelift MT shaft variously reported as 23, 24, 28, or 20 splines by different contributors — no number was conclusively confirmed. The practical takeaway is unchanged from the rest of this card: always match the replacement shaft to your specific transmission type, and do not assume interchangeability even when spline counts appear to match on paper 26.

Right half-shaft (driveshaft) replacement cost and pre-failure symptom: a right half-shaft (полупривод) replacement was reported at roughly 30,000 RUB (RU market, Oct 2025). Before replacement, the shaft showed excessive horizontal play at the hub — described as moving "like a drum" 27.

CV boot tear — repair strategy depends on whether noise is already present: a torn outer CV-joint dust boot with visible grease leakage/contamination was diagnosed as follows: if there is no clicking or grinding noise yet, prompt boot replacement plus re-greasing can prevent further damage and extend the joint's life significantly; if clicking or other noise is already present, the joint itself is likely damaged and a complete CV-joint replacement is required rather than just the boot. Speed matters — acting quickly on a fresh tear (before grit/water gets in) is what makes the boot-only fix viable 28293031.

CV/tripod-joint construction and lubrication — Renault B0 platform detail: the X80's CV joints derive from the Renault B0 platform and use a tripod design on (at least) one side rather than a conventional ball-type СV joint. Construction: the driveshaft enters the joint housing on one side through a plastic dust boot secured with an aluminum clamp; internally, a bearing/tripod assembly rotates and is lubricated with gear oil, not grease — this design is bolted directly to the transmission case (observed on JH3-128 and related JH/JB gearboxes used across most Renault B0-platform vehicles, e.g. Clio 3, Symbol, Megane, Duster). Do not assume all X80 CV/drive-joints use the same lubricant: different joint types (tripod vs. conventional ball-type ШРУС) require different lubricants, and the correct type depends on the specific joint design — for example, one contributor notes some Renault-platform vehicles use a genuine ШРУС-type joint requiring dedicated CV grease, not gear oil, so always match lubricant to the specific joint construction rather than assuming a single rule for the whole platform 32333435363738394041.

Pre-facelift AT outer CV joint — INKO 28/30 ABS 44 (Wildberries): for the pre-facelift (дорест) automatic-transmission X80, a compatible outer CV joint (наружный ШРУС) replacement is the INKO 28/30 ABS 44, available on Wildberries. Fitment was confirmed by trial-and-error testing of the 30-spline internal shaft engagement. Spec: 28mm outer diameter, 30-spline internal engagement, ABS sensor ring coded 44 424344454647.

Outer CV joint — INKO 28/30 ABS 44 reconfirmed, AT/MT reportedly identical: a second, independent report confirms the INKO 28/30 ABS 44 outer CV joint (Wildberries catalog 186740444) as a perfect spline match, this time on an AT car. The owner's mechanics stated the outer joint is identical between AT and MT variants, so this part should also fit MT cars — though that has not been independently verified on an MT vehicle yet 484950.

Outer CV joint — Masuma MA-44A (Mazda 6 sedan GG, 2002–2005, 2.0L): a second, distinct outer-CV-joint cross-brand option (different part from the INKO above): Masuma MA-44A, sourced from Mazda 6 sedan GG (2002–2005, engines LF17/LF18). Reported as a 1:1 fit. Specifications: 28 external splines, 32 internal splines, spindle-mounting diameter 62mm, ABS-ring diameter 92mm, internal retaining clip, drive-shaft inner spline diameter 27mm, total height 145mm. Price ~3,200₽ (RU market, July 2024). Sold as a kit with grease (MDX-IOB) and boot/clip 5152.

Left/right sides are NOT interchangeable — bore diameter mismatch: even when an aftermarket outer CV joint (e.g. the Masuma MA-44A above) fits the left drive shaft perfectly, it may be loose on the right — the original X80 right drive shaft appears to have a larger diameter than the equivalent Mazda shaft. Recommendation: either keep the original joint+shaft paired on both sides, or replace both the shaft and the joint with Mazda analogs together on that side; do not mix an original shaft with an aftermarket joint or vice versa 53.

Right outer CV joint (SHRUS) for manual transmission — still an open sourcing problem: this question recurs in the community. MT right outer joints are hard to source as an exact analog; while Mazda joints are suggested, diameter/spline mismatches (see left/right note above) can cause vibration. Recommendation: order the specific FAW part from a reliable Chinese supplier rather than improvising a cross-brand substitute 5455.

External CV dust boot — AT-specific Mazda part, and a universal neoprene alternative with dimensions: the external CV dust boot (пыльник ШРУСа наружный) specified for the automatic-transmission driveshaft, sourced from a Mazda 6 part, fits the X80. A universal neoprene alternative — MOTUS FBUNI90 (19.5×63/73/86×128mm, cross-referenced as analog C-5006) — is sold on Ozon; do not confuse it with other universal boots of different sizes, always confirm dimensions before buying. Buyers report the same physical boot is listed on both KitZap and Ozon at different prices — Ozon adds its own markup plus delivery; KitZap's own delivery runs ~500₽ minimum with a ~20% return-shipping penalty if the part doesn't fit 5657585960616263.

CV boot outer part number — B5DA122530: the outer CV-joint dust boot part number is B5DA122530, available from KitZapchasti and AutoPiter; applies to the AT (automatic transmission) driveline 6465.

Boot-only repair can be enough — but don't delay if the boot is fully torn: one owner who had reported a whistling noise near the left front wheel found the CV joint itself was fine — cleaning the area and replacing one rubber seal/boot resolved the whistle completely; a full CV-joint repair kit bought in advance was not needed 66. Contrast: a driver who continued driving ~150 km on a completely torn boot ended up needing a full CV-joint and wheel-hub replacement — early boot replacement is strongly recommended over delaying 67.

CV boot for manual-transmission X80 — hard to source through standard channels: outer CV axle boots are commonly listed by suppliers only for the AT (АКПП) driveline, not MT (МКПП). Workaround: visit parts markets in person and match by inner/outer diameter — boots intended for other Chinese-platform vehicles (one owner successfully used a Lada Lanos boot) can fit if the diameters match 6869707172.

Internal SHRUS sourcing for manual-transmission cars — limited, ask around: owners with MT gearboxes looking for the internal (inner) SHRUS joint report limited cross-referencing options discussed in the group; in one case a member had a right internal joint in stock and offered to arrange a sale privately — worth asking in the group directly rather than assuming no source exists 7374.

Torn outer CV boot — service quoted 45,000 RUB for a full joint, but a universal plastic boot fixed it for 900 RUB: an owner whose outer CV boot tore had it taken to a service shop, where the old boot was cut off but the mechanics couldn't get a new one on, claiming the joint's snap ring made it impossible and that the entire drive shaft would need replacing (~45,000 RUB, RU market, July 2025). The community pushed back hard: universal plastic outer CV boots fit and can simply be stretched over the joint without removing it from the car at all — reported to work reliably ("проверено"), priced around 900 RUB (RU market, July 2025). The specific product confirmed: Masuma MF-2829 drive-shaft boot kit, OEM cross-reference C9241-4ED0A, originally made for the Nissan X-Trail T32R/T32RR (2014+) and Qashqai J11/J11R (2013+) — confirmed to fit the X80. Do not substitute a rubber boot in this application — only the plastic version was confirmed to hold up; the plastic type stretches over the joint without disassembly, which is the key trick that makes the "45,000 RUB" service quote (RU market, July 2025) unnecessary 7576777879808182.

Inner CV boot, manual transmission — part B5DA022540, possible cheaper cross-reference: for the manual-transmission X80's inner CV boot, the part number is B5DA022540. When an owner balked at the price ("a piece of rubber for that much money") and asked for a cheaper equivalent, one alternate part number was suggested — 103835683594 — flagged explicitly as unverified/possibly fitting, not a confirmed cross-reference 83848586.

Outer CV joint, automatic transmission — part BM1122510: for the automatic-transmission X80, the outer CV joint (наружный ШРУС) part number is BM1122510 8788.

Outer CV dust boot — Lifan cross-fit for manual transmission: one contributor reports that the outer CV joint dust boot (пыльник на наружный ШРУС) can be sourced from Lifan parts, specifying this is for the manual-transmission (МКПП) driveline. No further fitment detail (exact Lifan model/part number) was given — treat as a low-confidence lead worth checking against a physical sample before ordering 8990.

Right outer CV joint (SHRUS) for manual transmission, ABS-44 — part 319127A suggested, Mazda Tribute (2000–2007) confirmed as a working temporary fix: an owner with a manual-transmission car needed the right outer CV joint (28-external/24-internal splines, ABS ring code 44) and could not find that exact combination in stock. Arсhi 77 suggested part 319127A as an option. Victor initially pushed back, noting the community had previously found a similarly-numbered part didn't fit MT cars — but Archi 77 clarified that earlier discussion concerned a different, AT-specific part (28/30-spline), whereas 319127A carries a different article number and a 24-spline (not 30-spline) internal count, so the two are not the same part; fitment on MT was unconfirmed pending a report back. Separately, Андрей Б. (also working an MT right outer joint at the same time) ordered the genuine outer+inner joints with shaft from a supplier (@mastergtr75) but, while waiting on the weeks-long delivery from China, found a working temporary substitute: the outer CV joint from a Mazda Tribute (2000–2007) matches by spline count (28 external, 24 internal, ABS ring code 44), but the ABS sensor ring is narrower on the Tribute part than on the original FAW ring — the original ring must be transferred onto the new joint for the ABS sensor to read correctly. This fit and worked for him, though he notes some other owners report a slight play (люфt) with the Mazda-sourced joint; he is still waiting for the genuine FAW parts as the definitive fix rather than treating the Mazda Tribute swap as permanent. He also notes that replacing only the outer joint did not fully resolve a crunching/creaking noise, so he subsequently ordered the inner joint as well — suggesting a compound failure (both inner and outer) can present similarly and both should be inspected 91929394959697.

Inner CV dust boots — the MOTUS FB UNI 90 universal boot already documented on this card also fits the inner position, on either side: reinforcing the MOTUS FB UNI 90 universal boot already noted elsewhere on this card (there sourced for the "internal front, manual transmission" position), a fresh owner thread confirms the same boot in practice: Victor asked for sizes/options for the inner right CV boot on a manual-transmission car; Niko75 replied that he had installed this exact boot, though on the left side, and posted a marketplace photo of the MOTUS FB UNI 90 (neoprene, then discounted to 1,123₽ from 1,287₽, RU market). When Victor asked whether that boot was actually meant for the outer rather than the inner joint, Romanych and Niko75 both confirmed independently that this boot is universal — i.e., not restricted to one specific position/side/joint-type — reinforcing that owners do not need to hunt for a side- or position-specific boot for this particular universal part 9899100101102.

Possible Mazda 6 (GH) inner CV joint / extension-shaft compatibility — unconfirmed, testing planned (conflict/unresolved): Victor, while investigating the manual-transmission inner CV joint sourcing problem described above, found an Ozon customer review that he believes supports his theory that a complete inner CV joint assembly from a Mazda 6 (GH generation) could be compatible, provided the outer CV joint's mounting dimensions match (28 splines on each side, per his notes elsewhere on this card). He explicitly flags this as unconfirmed and plans to verify by physically measuring every dimension when he next disassembles the right-side drive axle. He separately speculates that the extension shaft (вал удлинитель) from a standard GG-generation manual-transmission vehicle might also be compatible, again pending measurement. This is a plan/hypothesis, not a confirmed fitment — treat both claims as unverified until a follow-up report with actual measurements appears 103.

docs.title: CV joint (шрус) factory play and grease quality
docs.text:
Tags: #cv-joint · #drive-shaft · #conflict · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Factory play/slack is reportedly normal (low confidence, 2025-11). X80 CV joints (шрусы) are said to have some factory play/slack by design — this is described as normal rather than a defect. When replacing a worn joint, the new joint may exhibit the same kind of play due to the design's tolerances, not necessarily a bad part. Some owners have experimented with transferring the tripod (трипоид) from a new joint onto an old, worn shaft to avoid reintroducing a joint with the same slack characteristic. There was also discussion of possible Mazda 6 AKPP CV joint compatibility, but spline differences would need to be verified before assuming a fit — this is unconfirmed. Given the low confidence and lack of consensus, treat these claims as anecdotal rather than settled fact.1234567

Grease quality — factory fill is thin, not heavy (2025-11 report). Factory CV joints reportedly contain a thin/liquid grease, not the heavy-viscosity grease typically expected. Some owners found the factory grease quantity to be minimal — just a finger-dab amount — even inside new/original units. Recommendation when refurbishing a joint: repack with proper heavy-duty grease. The same complaint applies to hub bearings, which similarly had inadequate factory greasing — the general recommendation is to repack all sealed components that don't require special factory seals.5689

Dust boot replacement and Mazda upgrade path (2026-03 report). Internal CV joint dust boots on the manual-transmission side reportedly can be replaced with boots sourced from a Lada Granta. Separately, some owners want to upgrade the left-side CV joint (ШРУС) to a Mazda-sourced part — the Mazda shaft is slightly larger in diameter than the FAW original and needs to be turned down (machined) to fit. Reported parts costs (RU market, Mar 2026): an original X80 drive shaft assembly runs about 25,000 RUB; a Mazda-sourced drive shaft is cheaper at roughly 15,000–20,000 RUB but requires the machining step above. A creaking/crunching noise from the left CV assembly suggests boot failure or a worn joint needing attention.1011121314151617181920212223

Diagnosis method — jack-and-rotate test, click vs. vibration symptom split (2024-07 report). To check CV joint (ШРУС) wear without special tools: (1) lift one front wheel on a jack; hold the drive shaft with one hand and rotate the wheel back and forth — small play is normal, but excessive play indicates wear. (2) Outer CV joint wear typically shows as a clicking/chattering sound during turns. (3) Inner CV joint wear typically shows as vibration during acceleration, more noticeable on the right side (longer shaft arm). A separate but related symptom — low-speed metal scraping — may instead indicate CV joint play, worn wheel bearings, or a brake issue, so it should not be assumed to be the CV joint without checking boots for tears/grease leakage and consulting a mechanic for a specific diagnosis.242526272829

Catastrophic failure case and a driveshaft-vs-CV-joint creaking distinction (2026-06 report). One owner replaced both CV joints after a catastrophic failure: a loud crashing/grinding noise plus significant steering-wheel wobble ("жил своей жизнью" — the wheel "lived its own life"). After replacement, a creaking noise persisted when shifting between forward and reverse — this is the key diagnostic takeaway: since the creaking survived a full CV-joint replacement, it is more likely coming from the driveshaft/tripod assembly than the CV joints themselves. Multiple other owners report the same forward/reverse creaking symptom independently.303132

Conflict — right-side "weak" internal CV joint claim vs. driveshaft-creaking evidence (2026-06 report). Some owners believe the right-side internal CV joint is a known weak point on the X80, based on informal community reputation. However, the case above (creaking persisting after both CV joints were replaced) is direct evidence against the CV joint being the source of the creaking specifically — the two claims are not fully reconciled. Read the "right side is weak" claim as an open, only partly-confirmed community belief, and the driveshaft/tripod explanation as better-supported for the forward/reverse creaking symptom specifically.33343530

Boot clamp types and sizing (2026-05 report). Two main clamp types are used to secure the CV boot: worm-screw clamps (standard/universal, but often reported as a poor fit) and band/tape clamps (preferred by experienced owners, but require a special tensioning tool to install). For the tape-clamp type, a 75–90mm size is recommended for the X80's drive-shaft boots — buy the largest tape clamp available, since excess length is simply trimmed off after tensioning. A complete OEM boot+clamp assembly costs about 2,500 RUB (RU market, May 2026). Both clamp types are available at general auto-parts shops, where staff can help match the clamp to the specific joint being serviced. Conflict: owners initially disagreed on whether universal worm clamps would work at all (some said they would not fit properly); the community converged on tape clamps as the more reliable solution.363738394041424344454647484950

docs.title: Burning oil smell from CVT drive-shaft seal weep
docs.text:
Tags: #seal · #water-ingress · #price · #conflict

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Symptom. A burning oil smell occurring during high engine temperatures (95°C+) may originate from the transmission drive-shaft seal (right side, wheel-side) in the transmission housing — not from an obvious leak. The telltale pattern: no visible oil puddles under the car, but an intermittent burnt-oil odor that correlates with driving conditions/temperature.123456789

Mechanism. The seal slowly weeps oil rather than leaking visibly. The small amount of oil reaches hot engine/exhaust components nearby, producing the burnt smell without ever accumulating enough to drip or puddle.123456789

Known issue at moderate mileage. Reported at 53,000–78,000 km — this is a known issue at relatively low mileage, not something exclusive to high-mileage cars.123456789

Fix. Requires seal replacement.123456789

When a seal replacement doesn't fix the leak (2025-09 report, unresolved cause). One owner replaced the drive-shaft seal but the leak continued — continuous dripping with slow fluid accumulation under the car. Suggested investigation steps, in case a first seal replacement doesn't solve it: (1) compare the old and new CV joint (tripod) diameters — a new joint that's slightly undersized relative to the old one can cause the seal to slip/not seat properly; (2) verify the seal wasn't installed upside down or misaligned; (3) inspect the drive shaft itself for wear. Official FAW service, Kaliningrad, pricing (RU market, Sept 2025): 1,200 RUB for the OEM seal + 2,800 RUB labor, with a one-week turnaround. Aftermarket suppliers were also mentioned as an alternative parts source. Cause not conclusively identified — could be tolerance/fitment issues, installation error, or shaft wear; the community treats this as an open, case-by-case diagnostic problem.1011121314151617181920

Part number and what usually fails. The AT drive shaft seal is listed as 90311-40A014, with many aftermarket versions, and a note that it also fits the B50. A member says the seal is not the usual failure point; the inner and outer CV joints (ШРУС) are what fail21.

docs.title: Clean cylinder-1 piston with coolant loss
docs.text:
Tags: #diagnostics · #unresolved

Symptom pattern. On inspection, the 1st cylinder's piston was clean (no carbon deposits), while the other cylinders showed normal brown/tan deposits. No oil consumption evident at the spark-plug well, no cold-start detonation, exhaust smell normal — but coolant level was dropping. This pattern points toward a head-gasket issue rather than a ring/valve-seal problem specifically on cylinder 112345678910111213141516171819202122232425262728.

Engine context. The engine is Mazda-based (closely related to a Mazda/Ford design) with an aluminum block. The owner reporting this case planned to observe the vehicle through the following spring for a more definitive diagnosis before committing to a repair; this case is unresolved and left open as a diagnostic pattern worth cross-referencing if a similar symptom set (clean single-cylinder piston + coolant loss, no other consumption signs) appears elsewhere.

docs.title: Engine cylinder firing order and numbering
docs.text: The engine's cylinder firing order is 1-3-4-21. Cylinders are numbered starting from the front (left) mount side of the engine — e.g. the third cylinder from the left/front mount is cylinder #31. This was given in response to a misfire specifically affecting cylinder 3, though the responder noted the firing order alone likely wouldn't pinpoint the cause of a misfire in a particular cylinder — it's mainly useful for correlating diagnostic-tool cylinder numbers with physical cylinder position21.

docs.title: Cylinder honing/boring — when needed
docs.text:
Not a periodic maintenance item — only two legitimate triggers. Cylinder boring/honing is not something to schedule as routine maintenance on the X80. It's only needed when one of two conditions applies: (1) the engine has over 200,000-300,000 km and significant bore wear has actually occurred, or (2) a power modification is desired, requiring new oversized pistons. Without one of these two triggers, honing is unnecessary and — per this source — can actually cause damage rather than prevent it1234567.

Don't bore without also replacing pistons — and check the liner-thickness limit first. Do not bore the cylinders to increase piston size without simultaneously replacing the pistons with matching oversized units and fully understanding the engine modifications this requires — boring alone, without an oversized piston set, is not a valid procedure. A specific caution for this engine: the X80 has thin cylinder liners, which limits how much material can safely be removed during boring — the safe overbore capacity on this engine is more limited than on engines with thicker liners, so this isn't a job to improvise1234567.

docs.title: Cylinder misfire — coil, plug, or valve
docs.text:
Tags: #misfire · #spark-plug · #fuel-consumption

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

This card collects several distinct root causes found behind cylinder misfires on the X80 — coil-to-cylinder swapping as a cold-weather workaround, a burned exhaust valve causing zero compression, and a coil pack (not the plug) causing a P0301 code in humid weather. Treat these as separate diagnostic patterns, not one single cause1.

Cylinder 3 winter misfire — resolved (temporarily) by coil swap. One owner's cylinder 3 triggered a check-engine misfire specifically in cold weather, with the fault disappearing entirely once warm season arrived — root cause was never confirmed. As a workaround, the owner swapped the ignition coil from cylinder 1 to cylinder 3 (coil 1→3), which resolved the symptom. This is explicitly stated as a temporary workaround, not a permanent fix — the underlying cause (coil, wiring, or something cold-temperature-related) was not identified12.

Zero compression in cylinder 1, misfires in cylinders 2-3 — burned exhaust valve. A more serious pattern: zero compression measured in cylinder 1, combined with misfires in cylinders 2 and 3, points to a burned exhaust valve in cylinder 1. This is a serious mechanical problem requiring valve replacement (not just an ignition-side fix). Internal engine inspection — ideally a borescope — is recommended to confirm valve damage before committing to a teardown345.

P0301 (cylinder 1 misfire) in humid weather — coil pack, not the spark plug. When a P0301 code (cylinder 1 misfire) appears periodically and specifically in humid weather, the first suspect should be the coil pack, not the spark plug. In one case the cylinder-1 spark plug showed oil residue/discoloration when pulled, which looked like an obvious culprit, but replacing the plug alone did not resolve the misfire — the coil pack needed replacement. Conflict: the reporting owner (Фаб) initially blamed and replaced the spark plug with the fault persisting; another member (Печной Двор) advised checking the coil pack specifically, which is presented here as the more likely fix for humidity-linked, periodic P0301 faults6789.

Highway vibration and shift-hunting from budget spark plugs — coils also implicated. A separate case: engine vibration at highway speed and transmission gear-hunting during shifts appeared after installing budget aftermarket spark plugs (Startvolt brand). The problem was resolved by switching to genuine Denso plugs. Some of the vibration/hunting symptoms were separately traced to faulty ignition coils, identifiable by an X mark scratched into the coil casing (a marking convention used by whoever previously diagnosed/swapped it). Diagnostic approach: swap coils between cylinders and see if the symptom follows the coil, or use a multi-pin scanner (X PRO-5) to detect misfires directly — though the X80's OBD-II port may not surface individual per-cylinder misfire codes, limiting how much a basic scanner alone can confirm1011121314.

Intermittent cylinder-1 misfire without an error code — spark plug suspected (medium confidence). A separate, later owner reports an intermittent ignition misfire error on cylinder 1, with occasional engine stumbling that sometimes throws no error code at all. The community's suggested first suspect is the spark plug condition on cylinder 1, consistent with the spark-plug-side patterns already documented on this card. One other owner reported similar sporadic misfire symptoms, but no confirmed fix is recorded in this batch — confidence: medium15.

Ignition coil replacement lowered dashboard-reported fuel consumption. After replacing the ignition coil (part sourced via Ozon), one owner's computer-reported fuel consumption decreased by 2.5 liters (per the dashboard trip computer). The community notes the coil is available on Ozon at an economical price. The likely mechanism is that ignition quality (a marginal/failing coil) was affecting combustion efficiency and hence fuel consumption, tying this fuel-economy improvement to the same ignition-coil failure mode already documented above — confidence: medium (single report, dashboard-reported figure, not a controlled fuel test)161718.

docs.title: Drive belt kits and rollers — listings, prices
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Marketplace listings for the drive (serpentine) belt, kits and pulleys that came up in the group. The long-form fitment and sizing discussion is in drive belt — OEM vs. Mazda part number; removal is in alternator belt removal.

Belt and kits. The X80 drive belt is part number 5DA015909; a Trialli version, 5DA015909TR, is listed on chinaspare.ru under the same number123. A Megamarket listing for a Gates K026PK2260 belt kit (article 100023973057, March 2024) drew the question why a full kit is needed when only the tensioner rollers have failed; no answer is recorded12. Dongil 6PK2263 is cited as the example of a ribbed belt, or any other brand with the same spec4.

Rollers. The idler (tensioner) roller is catalogued as 5CA015980ROLL, a black ribbed pulley with a centre bearing5. The upper belt roller 1023035-37K is on Ozon (listing 2892941100); a member points out that the complete tensioner FP2487 costs ~1,500 RUB (aftermarket, RU market, January 2026) against ~5,000 RUB (RU market, January 2026) for the original-style part67. A member asked if anyone had fitted Gates idler and tensioner pulleys T36263 and T39074 for the accessory belt drive; no answer, so fitment and quality are unverified8.

docs.title: Drive belt part number — OEM vs. Mazda
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The correct original drive belt for the X80 is FAW part number 5DA0159091. Some suppliers erroneously ship a Mazda part (6PK2260) when the order is placed against the FAW OEM number — verify the exact part number printed on the belt packaging before installing23. Similar-looking belts from different manufacturers (Dayco cross-references were mentioned as available) may have different sizing, so cross-checking is important even for "equivalent" listings45.

Length specification and break-in stretch. The factory belt length is exactly 2263 mm. A newly installed belt often feels very tight and won't fully seat at first — this is normal; the belt stretches with use, and after roughly 30,000 km it settles to proper tension. Owners are advised not to force or over-tighten the belt on initial installation678. A separate report gives the same 2263 mm figure and adds that a 2260 mm belt is sometimes reported to fit, but fitment with the shorter size should be verified rather than assumed9101112.

Wear indicator — thin fibers in the oil. A sign of belt wear/degradation: the appearance of thin fibers or strands (волосики) visible in the engine oil during a routine oil change. This indicates the belt is deteriorating and may fail soon; when fibers are observed, prompt belt replacement is recommended13.

6PK2260 as a standalone compatibility question. Separately, a member asked directly whether the 6PK2260 belt specification is a valid aftermarket option for the X80's serpentine belt, without reference to the OEM-vs-Mazda mix-up above. No definitive answer was given in that thread — treat 6PK2260 fitment as needing verification against the owner's manual or a confirmed OEM cross-reference before ordering, consistent with the general caution above14.

Tension roller (ролик натяжителя) part number. The belt tension roller part number is 5CA015980ROLL, available via Ozon and KitZapchasti. Separately, the availability of the power-steering roller specifically (as opposed to the belt tensioner) is unclear from aftermarket listings — it may only be sold bundled as part of a complete power-steering pump assembly rather than standalone15161718.

Post-replacement squeaking — tensioner-roller bearing, not the belt. After replacing the drive belt, if squeaking or rustling noise appears, the cause is more often the tensioner roller bearing than the new belt itself; the bearing may need replacement rather than the belt being at fault9101112.

Dongil 6PK2263 — recommended aftermarket replacement belt. A specific aftermarket belt recommendation: Dongil 6PK2263 (2263mm length, 6-rib profile) — matching the 2263mm factory length confirmed elsewhere on this card. Critical: length should not be shorter than 2263mm or the belt will be over-tensioned. Installation should be snug/tight. Owners report this spec eliminates squealing noise reported with inferior aftermarket alternatives. Price context: search current listings as of 2025-05-0519202122.

6PK2263 — another confirmation with sourcing/availability detail. A separate exchange again confirms the correct belt as Dongil 6PK2263, described as inexpensive but good quality; confirmed compatible with both pre-facelift and facelifted models. Stock was confirmed available through Saratov-based merchants in the Russian market, with roughly a 1-month lead time if ordered2324252627282930313233343536373839404142.

Squealing belt — temporary fix vs. root cause (earlier report). Belt squealing can be temporarily silenced with silicone spray, but this is not a permanent fix. The root cause should be addressed by checking belt tension and inspecting the belt for wear/cracking4344.

Tensioner/idler pulley — part number 1023035-37K, smooth vs. grooved variant. The correct serpentine-belt tensioner (idler guide pulley) is FAW part 1023035-37K, identifiable by its smooth rolling surface — a separate part number from the tension-roller part (5CA015980ROLL) already documented on this card. A similarly numbered variant exists that is 3mm shorter and has a grooved surface; that grooved variant is harder to install and should be avoided. Installation of the correct smooth pulley requires no special tools4546474849505152.

Belt length restated — 2260mm factory vs. 2263-2265mm for proper tension, and installation difficulty. A separate report gives the factory belt as 2260mm, but states that proper tension in practice requires 2263-2265mm (consistent with the 2263mm OEM figure already on this card). Getting the length right matters: too short causes noise/squeaking, too long fails to tension properly. Installation is reported as difficult, sometimes taking 3-4 hours, using knee/body leverage to hold tension while rotating the crank bolt by hand5354555657585960616263.

Tensioner-roller bolt can seize. The bolt holding the belt tensioner/roller can become seized or rusted; if it won't come loose with normal tools, destructive removal techniques may be required. After removal, inspect the roller itself for condition before reinstalling or replacing6465.

Timing-belt tensioner assembly — Mazda aftermarket alternative, with a belt-size caveat. FAW part FP2487 is the complete belt tensioner assembly (not just the roller); OEM price is roughly 5,000 RUB (RU market, Jan 2026). A Mazda-aftermarket equivalent (Zentparts brand) is available on Wildberries for roughly 1,500 RUB (RU market, Jan 2026). Caution: the Mazda tensioner may require a different belt length than the FAW-spec belt (too tight or too loose with the wrong combination) — the 2260mm belt was reported as a tight-but-workable fit; verify belt/tensioner compatibility together before installing6667686970717273.

Whistling generator belt on cold starts. Separately from squealing already documented on this card, a whistling noise from the generator (drive) belt during cold startup — persisting for several minutes as the engine warms — was traced to a stretched serpentine belt. Temporary relief: aerosol belt-friction treatment spray (consistent with the temporary silicone-spray fix already documented on this card). Permanent fix: replace the serpentine belt with a new one7475767778798081.

Cold-start belt whistle fixed by replacing two pulleys (not the belt itself). A separate cold-start whistle case — the noise disappearing once the engine warms up — was resolved not by replacing the belt but by replacing two belt pulleys: the upper belt pulley (FAW 1023035-37K) and the belt tensioner roller (FAW 5CA015980ROLL). One owner confirmed this fix eliminated the unpleasant early-morning sound entirely. If the whistle persists after warm-up (rather than only during cold-start), that points to a different cause — such as worn rollers elsewhere or insufficient lubrication — and this pulley swap should not be assumed to be a universal fix828384858687.

Serpentine belt part number for the manual-transmission restyled model — 6PK2263. A separate, earlier confirmation adds a specific part number to the belt-length figures already on this card: 6PK2263 is the serpentine (drive) belt for the manual-transmission, restyled (facelift) X80. This belt tensions multiple accessories — the alternator, power-steering pump, and water pump — consistent with the multi-component belt routing already discussed on this card8889.

Serpentine belt part number — 5DA015909, with/without tensioner-roller SKU split. A separate, later-confirmed part number for the FAW Besturn X80 serpentine belt (gasoline engine): 5DA015909, available both with and without the tensioner roller as separate SKUs — worth checking which listing is being ordered. Widely available through Chinese parts suppliers9091.

Idler and tensioner roller cold-start squeak — independent confirmation with Ozon links, from the second Telegram group. A separate community (FAW BESTURN X80 group) independently confirms the same fix already documented on this card (replacing the upper pulley and tensioner roller resolves cold-start squeaking): one owner replaced only the rollers, leaving the original tensioner lightly lubricated. Idler/guide roller (обводной ролик): HQ-mech HQ115940, available on Ozon. Belt tensioner roller (ролик натяжителя приводного ремня): FAW X80 5CA015980ROLL, also on Ozon — matching the part number already documented on this card. Upper accessory pulley: part 1023035-37K is available but flagged as a quality risk — one owner's unit started whistling after just 2,000 km, attributed to insufficient bearing lubrication; the recommendation is to source the HQ-mech brand where possible instead. Cold-weather squeaking on an otherwise healthy setup is described as normal9293949596979899100101102103104.

docs.title: ECU chip tuning — performance and cost
docs.text:
Tags: #ecu-tuning

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Chip tuning for automatic-transmission cars needs more than an ECU flash. A Moscow-based chip-tuning service reports that for automatic-transmission X80s, achieving a meaningful performance improvement requires tuning all vehicle systems, not just the ECU — a standard ECU-only remap is described as insufficient for meaningful gains on automatic models123.

Reported result — top speed increase from 180 to 215 km/h. Separately, ECU chip tuning is reported to meaningfully raise top speed: one confirmed case went from 180 km/h to 215 km/h after tuning. Multiple community members report having had their engines chipped45.

(See also the catalytic-converter-removal card for tuning discussion specifically tied to catalyst deletion, lambda-sensor defeat, and the claimed 164hp-vs-142hp factory power debate.)

Firmware-only tuning result — +10% power, mandatory 95+ octane afterward. A separate firmware modification (ECU tuning, without catalyst removal) produced roughly +10% power with noticeably improved throttle response and acceleration. Critical requirement: switching to 95+ octane fuel exclusively afterward — 92 octane is no longer suitable once tuned. No significant change in fuel consumption was observed. Risk noted: the firmware tune can be lost after a service visit where a shop accesses the vehicle's electronics (e.g. a standard diagnostic reflash could overwrite the custom tune)67.

Chip tuning used against catalytic converter and EGR fault codes (Oct 2026). One member (IBRAIM) had fault codes for the catalytic converter (кат) and the EGR valve and had the ECU chipped (чипануть, reflashed) to deal with them; the outcome is not described, so this is a single anecdote 8.

Chipped 2.0 L used car: 157 hp, knocks on 92. An owner of a used chip-tuned X80 says the tune is listed at 157 hp. The engine knocks on 92-octane fuel when cold, pulls hard from a standstill and tops out at about 178 km/h on GPS. He compares it with a 2005 car at 450,000 km on stock software9.

docs.title: ECU tune detection via the second oxygen sensor
docs.text:
Tags: #diagnostics

To check whether a vehicle has an aftermarket ECU tune, inspect the second oxygen sensor (O2 sensor 2 / ДК2) connector in the engine bay — it sits on the lower left, between the battery and the engine 1. If the connector is unplugged but the dashboard shows no fault codes for O2 sensor 2 or catalyst heating, the vehicle likely has a tune: some tuning firmware removes the second sensor from the ECU's calculations. On an untouched (stock) vehicle, unplugging that sensor would normally trigger a fault code 2. A specialist can confirm definitively by reading the ECU's programming/firmware log.

docs.title: EGR valve fouling, sensor issues, and disabling
docs.text:
Tags: #egr · #emissions · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Common failure mode. The FAW X80's EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) system commonly suffers from the DAD sensor and EGR valve getting fouled by crankcase blow-by gases coming from the cylinder head covers and engine block — these gases carry contaminants that coat the sensor and valve over time.12345678

Recurring problem. Cleaning the fouled DAD sensor is a temporary fix — it tends to get re-fouled quickly after cleaning, since the underlying blow-by contamination source isn't addressed.12345678

Solution options: 1. Block/disable the EGR valve completely (requires a mechanical plug). 2. Implement better crankcase ventilation separation to reduce the contaminants reaching the EGR/DAD sensor in the first place.

Side effects of disabling EGR. A disabled EGR system may fail an emissions inspection (TO/ТО in Russia). The current owner's vehicle passes inspection as long as they maintain it themselves, but reselling to a new owner becomes problematic since inspection will then be required and the disabled EGR would need to be caught/addressed. If the EGR is blocked, the crankcase gases it would otherwise help route need a separate disposal/ventilation path.12345678

Replacement cost comparison (Feb 2026). When the EGR chain is broken or voltage is abnormally low, the community view is that full replacement is the only real fix. Reported pricing (RU market, Feb 2026): Kitszap 18,000 RUB (camera-equipped version); Avito Far East 7,500 RUB for an OEM part (FAW part number 120701037K), ~2-week delivery from Vladivostok. Cheaper aftermarket/budget EGR valves around 5,000 RUB (RU market, Feb 2026) exist but carry real defect risk — one owner's 5,000 RUB part failed after just 2 days of use.910

AliExpress listing for the EGR valve (Jan 2026). An AliExpress listing offers the 1207010 recirculation (EGR) valve, "-37K", for the Pentium B70F / X80 (B90EGR) at ~3,577 RUB (RU market, January 2026, after a 3% discount)11.

docs.title: EGR valve part number and disable discussion (2019 X80)
docs.text:
Tags: #egr · #part-number · #emissions

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The EGR valve part number for the 2019 FAW X80 is 1207010-37K1. It can be sourced from kitzap.ru2. Multiple owners note the EGR valve contributes to emissions control, but some choose to disable it, citing perceived engine efficiency gains34. (See also the related community caution elsewhere in this section that removing/disabling emissions hardware such as a catalytic converter is linked to increased detonation risk requiring higher-octane fuel — the same general caution likely applies to EGR modifications, though this was not explicitly confirmed for EGR in this batch.)56

EGR valve function and performance tradeoff (restated). The EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) valve diverts exhaust gases back into the intake at low RPM to reduce emissions, at the cost of reduced engine power; it disengages at higher RPM. Some owners disable or modify the EGR for a perceived performance gain, though this increases emissions and can trigger the check-engine light78.

P0405 — EGR sensor A low signal. Error code P0405 indicates a low signal from EGR sensor A. Typical symptom: check-engine light with no noticeable change in driving performance. Official dealer solution under warranty is sensor replacement; after warranty, some dealers simply disable the sensor since it doesn't affect engine operation. The code can recur after clearing if the underlying sensor issue persists91011.

EGR function and low-RPM emissions role (restated with numbers). The EGR valve redirects roughly 10% of exhaust gases back to the intake manifold at low RPM to reduce emissions, closing above roughly 3000 RPM. Some owners disable EGR to gain low-RPM power; mechanical disabling (spacer plate + deactivating electronic control) is possible but may trigger error codes requiring a programming fix121314151617181920.

EGR sensor replacement fixes 100-110 km/h jerking and cold-start stumbling. EGR sensor failure symptoms: jerking/bucking specifically around 100-110 km/h when releasing the throttle; cold-start stumbling/misfire that smooths out after warmup; check-engine light. Replacing the EGR sensor resolves all of these symptoms. This is described as a common issue on higher-mileage used X80s212223.

"Check engine management system" warning traced to a weak EGR signal. Dashboard warning "проверьте систему управления двигателем" (check engine management system) with the engine icon, confirmed via OBD2 as a weak EGR sensor signal. Troubleshooting steps: fully charge the battery, disconnect the battery terminals to reset, then read the code with an OBD2 scanner. If the warning persists, EGR sensor replacement is likely needed; the fault can be intermittent due to a loose electrical contact2425262728.

EGR valve replacement (not just cleaning) resolves jerking and improves fuel consumption. Cleaning the EGR valve does not reliably help; owners report success ordering a replacement valve from China and installing it, which resolves jerking/hesitation (дергание) and reduces fuel consumption. Diagnostic test: disconnect the EGR connector and test-drive — if jerking stops, the valve is faulty. The valve can be replaced without draining the cooling system. With the connector disconnected, the check-engine light will illuminate (it can be reset with an OBD scanner), so the car remains drivable while waiting for the replacement part29303132333435363738.

Disconnecting EGR — reported benefits. After disconnecting the EGR valve: check-engine light clears, engine roughness/knocking disappears, transmission shifts smoother, and overall engine response improves. The EGR valve is also reported to cause a clacking noise, especially during auto-start attempts (consistent with the aftermarket-alarm remote-start topic covered elsewhere in this section)394041424344.

EGR error returns 2-3 days after valve replacement — connector/wiring diagnosis. A specific failure pattern: the EGR error appears, the valve is replaced, but the error returns 2-3 days later. Possible causes, in diagnostic order: (1) a defective replacement part — even OEM parts can fail early; (2) connector corrosion/moisture at the EGR electrical connector; (3) a wiring-harness circuit fault; (4) a possible ECU memory issue (unconfirmed — resetting the ECU after installing the new valve may help). First step: inspect the connector, clean the contacts, and check wiring continuity; if the error persists, check the fuse/relay in the underhood panel. EGR is treated as a consumable part on the X80, with a typical lifespan of 36,000-70,000 km45464748495051.

OEM EGR valve — FAW part number and Avito sourcing. Original FAW Besturn X80 EGR valve part number: FAW 120701037K. Available through Far East vendors on Avito for roughly 7,500 RUB (RU market, Feb 2026), with about a 2-week delivery from Vladivostok. This is significantly cheaper than the local Kitszap markup, which quoted 18,000 RUB (RU market, Feb 2026) for a similar part — the same vendor comparison (Avito Far East versus Kitszap markup) was separately confirmed on an unrelated part (camera lens: 4,500 RUB via the Avito vendor versus 18,000 RUB at Kitszap), suggesting Kitszap pricing runs consistently high5152.

A second unsuccessful EGR replacement — error persists, root cause unclear. In a separate case, replacing the EGR valve did not clear the error code. This is consistent with the connector/wiring/ECU diagnostic path already documented on this card — suggests the root cause may be a sensor, wiring, or solenoid fault rather than the valve itself, especially when a straight valve swap doesn't resolve the code5354.

EGR fault symptoms — automatic transmission variant. On automatic-transmission cars, an EGR fault typically presents as: check-engine light, elevated idle RPM (4,000-6,000 RPM), and improper/delayed downshifting. Cleaning the EGR connector may resolve the issue without a full valve replacement — worth trying before assuming the valve itself has failed5556.

EGR fault symptoms — manual transmission variant. On manual-transmission cars, an EGR fault instead presents as loss of power and loss of Eco-mode availability (rather than the AT symptoms documented above). In one case, cleaning the EGR connector resolved the issue, confirmed by an official service center5758.

EGR valve location. The EGR valve sits beneath the intake-manifold hoses, with coolant/antifreeze supply lines attached directly to it — worth noting before attempting a DIY removal or cleaning, since coolant lines will need to be managed5960.

EGR blanking and intake-manifold sludge — a separate 140k-km case. One owner blanked off (plugged) the EGR port at the intake manifold rather than replacing the valve — no error code was triggered — and reports no change in fuel consumption or transmission behavior from doing so (their original jerking complaint had a different root cause, the missing-PCV-valve/crankcase-ventilation issue documented on the crankcase-ventilation card).
