By 140,000 km, the EGR system on this car had accumulated significant oil sludge, consistent with the low-mounted-intake-manifold design flaw described on that same card: the electronic-throttle pedal signal delay from the ECU is cited as a contributing factor to the jerking complex as a whole6162636465.

EGR function restated — ~10% of exhaust at low RPM, MAP sensor sees the imbalance if blocked. The EGR valve operates only at low RPM (below roughly 1500-2000 RPM) to reduce cylinder temperature and improve combustion under light load; above that range it closes. Restating the mechanism in more detail: with EGR disabled or its outlet blocked, the MAP sensor detects an increased air volume (since less exhaust is being recirculated) while actual exhaust flow decreases — the ECU interprets this imbalance as a lean-fuel condition and adds fuel to compensate, which is why fully blocking crankcase/EGR outlets can raise fuel consumption. If exhaust flow falls below an expected threshold with EGR disabled (electronically or mechanically), an error code is triggered66676869707172.

Charcoal (fuel-vapor) canister purge valve — one-way, cannot be blown through, do not bypass. Separately, and adjacent to the EGR/crankcase-ventilation troubleshooting on this card: the charcoal-canister purge valve (for fuel-vapor recovery, EVAP) is normally closed while the engine runs and opens only briefly under ECU command (audible click) to vent fuel vapors — it is a one-way check valve by design. Directly connecting the inlet/outlet hoses to bypass the valve causes an RPM drop; the valve cannot be blown through in either direction when working correctly (air blockage is normal, not a fault). One owner directly connecting these hoses did not wait long enough to hear the expected intermittent hiss/click of normal operation before concluding it was faulty. Do not modify or bypass this valve — it must remain in the circuit73747576.

P0405 (EGR position sensor, low signal) and a replacement quote (Sep 2026). On an X80 with code P0405 (EGR = exhaust gas recirculation), the owner IBRAIM was quoted about 12,000 RUB (RU market, Sep 2026; written "12 к", currency assumed to be roubles) to replace the sensor 77. Jürgen@73 advised cleaning it first, as it may simply be dirty 78, and then checking all the tubes and hoses for a crack, an air leak or a vacuum leak 79. The owner will try cleaning first but notes that many say the sensor is clean and the problem is elsewhere 80. Replacement was not confirmed as the fix. The same owner later reported that catalytic converter and EGR fault codes were dealt with by ECU chip tuning (outcome not described) 81.

Clicking from the EGR valve after the engine is switched off is normal. After shutdown the ECU (engine control unit) runs an anti-carbon routine: it sends short electrical pulses to the valve's solenoid or stepper motor so the flap opens and closes several times, knocking soot off the seat before the engine cools and the deposits could jam the valve 82. The advice was still to read the fault codes as a precaution 82; another owner said his clicking stopped on its own 83.

docs.title: Engine and gearbox variants over the years
docs.text:
Tags: #reference

Owner statements about which engines and gearboxes the X80 came with. They are second-hand recollections from the group, not manual data; compare with engine identity.

Early engines. One member says the early X80 engines came in 2.0 L and 2.4 L versions (different stroke) with a compression ratio of 9.5, not the 11.5 of the Ford/Mazda-derived engines. He adds that cast-iron sleeves in an aluminium block were used to save cost and that the engines were homologated to Euro 3/4; only the 2.0 L (Euro 5) stayed in China alongside a 1.8 turbo. Another owner mentions a 2.3 L option and a 1.8 turbo12.

Variants in the wiring diagrams. The factory EWD pages cover three engines, a 2.0 L, a 1.8T and a 1.8TD, with a 2nd-generation automatic (2.0 L and 1.8T) and a 3rd-generation automatic on the 1.8TD; see component codes345. The manual's ignition table names engine codes CA4GD1 (2.0 L) and CA4GC18T (1.8 turbo); see Torch plug codes and gap rules6.

Turbo gearbox. One owner says the turbo X80 he looked at has a 6-speed automatic rather than an 8-speed. The voice transcript is garbled, so trim and year are unclear7.

docs.title: Engine-bay adsorber hose — inspection
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-bay

When inspecting the engine bay, one owner found a cut/damaged hose behind the right headlight, which they believe is part of the adsorber (evaporative-emissions charcoal canister) drainage/vent line — and asked whether this is factory-normal or damage 12. Findings from other owners varied: on at least one other car, the equivalent hose was not cut and instead routed onward from that area (possibly into the fender) rather than ending abruptly 34. One theory offered was that the hose clamps had simply corroded rather than the hose being deliberately cut 5. Recommendation: inspect this hose behind the right headlight on your own car and compare — it should run continuously/be properly routed toward the crankcase ventilation or charcoal-canister system rather than ending in a raw cut, per the service manual; a genuinely cut or missing section is likely not factory-correct and should be traced and repaired to prevent a vapor leak 6789.

docs.title: Engine chip tuning (ECU remapping)
docs.text:
Tags: #ecu · #price · #conflict

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Cost range (2024-07 report). Standard ECU chip tuning for the FAW X80 engine costs approximately 9,000 RUB at market rate (RU market, July 2024). With a personal connection/referral discount, the same service has been obtained for as little as 3,500–8,000 RUB (RU market, July 2024) — a wide range reflecting informal/personal-network pricing rather than a fixed shop rate.

Reported results. Owners who had the tune done report: 0.5–2 L/100km fuel economy improvement, smoother power delivery starting from idle, and improved overtaking power at speed. Using a Euro-2 firmware tune specifically is cited as producing the best results among the variants tried. At least one owner reports a concrete 1.5–2 L/100km fuel savings after tuning, moderate driving style, occasionally opening the engine up on an empty highway.

Conflict — skepticism about cheap/informal tuning (documented disagreement). Some community members are skeptical that a 3,500–8,000 RUB (RU market, July 2024) "by connection" tune matches the quality/safety of professional tuning standards, viewing the cheap rate itself as a red flag. The counter-argument from tuned-car owners: individual/independent tuners may simply work with different margins and business models, so a low price doesn't automatically mean lower quality — but this remains an open disagreement, not a settled community consensus. No independent dyno or long-term reliability data was cited on either side of the debate — treat both the fuel-savings claims and the skepticism as anecdotal.123456789

Specialist contact / network — ADACT2, Kaliningrad partner (2026-08 report). The ADACT2 chip-tuning outfit — described as the creator of the firmware used on this car — runs a network of regional partner installers across Russia. Their Kaliningrad ("Königsberg") partner is Евгений Молчанов (Evgeny Molchanov), address Невского 1206, Калининград, phone +7 963 738-11-27. The partner's offer as shared reportedly includes a 10-day money-back guarantee and an ECU reflashing certificate. A separate community member reported this Kaliningrad partner quoted 12,000 RUB (2026-08-13, RU market, preliminary) for a Euro-2 firmware conversion — a follow-up question asked (unanswered as of this report) whether that firmware also disables EGR.10111213

docs.title: Engine flooding from a pressure wash
docs.text:
Tags: #misfire · #spark-plugs · #water-ingress

Cause. Dealership pressure-washing of the engine bay before delivery can trap water inside the spark-plug wells. One owner traced a rough-idle/misfire issue that appeared about 5,000 km after purchase (on the way to work) back to this: the dealership had washed the engine under pressure before the sale and water had pooled in the spark-plug channel1.

Symptoms. A misfire fault code and rough idle specifically affecting one cylinder — consistent with water sitting in that cylinder's spark-plug well and interfering with ignition1.

Fix. Drain the trapped water out of the well with a syringe, remove the coil pack and spark plug from the affected cylinder, and dry the well thoroughly — a construction/heat gun was used in this case to ensure the area was fully dry before reassembly1.

docs.title: Engine gaskets — cross-brand fitment
docs.text:
Tags: #gasket · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Chinese aftermarket gaskets — fitment problems. Chinese aftermarket parts suppliers frequently ship engine gaskets that don't fit properly. The standard part number 5GA061A10 has specifically been reported to arrive undersized relative to the correct dimensions. Recommendation: prefer original or verified cross-brand alternatives (Mazda or Ford) over generic Chinese aftermarket listings for this part123.

Ford Mondeo cross-compatibility — a better alternative. Engine gaskets from the Ford Mondeo (2008-2013) reportedly fit the X80, with roughly 90% of engine components from the Mondeo showing cross-compatibility overall — consistent with the X80's shared Duratec HE engine lineage. An alternative part number specifically for X80F model variants is GV7D61A10456.

Exhaust manifold gasket alternatives. Exhaust manifold gasket for the X80 (MT or AKPP) can be sourced from Mazda 6 GG/GH models or the FAW V50. The original part costs roughly 14,500 RUB (RU market, Oct 2025). Verify availability with parts suppliers before ordering, as fitment across sources isn't fully standardized789101112.

Plastic oil pan gasket set availability. Gasket/seal kits for the plastic oil pan (carter) are available from Chinese-parts suppliers (китзапчасти); MASTER GTR-brand kits are one confirmed option, including multiple seals for oil-pan mounting. An exact part number was not specified in the source thread, but the packaging carries Cyrillic labeling matching OEM specification13141516.

Cylinder head gasket — metal type, OEM part number. Cylinder head gasket part number: FAW X80 METAL 1003030A-37K. This is a metal gasket (not an asbestos-composite type), available on Ozon. Chinese parts sites offer alternatives for roughly 1,040 RUB (RU market, Mar 2026), but quality relative to the OEM metal version is uncertain — a similar caution to the Chinese-aftermarket fitment problems already documented on this card for other gaskets171819.

Intake manifold gasket set — Ford/Mazda cross-compatible kit. An intake manifold gasket set is available as a Ford/Mazda cross-compatible kit (via an Ozon listing), offered as an alternative to sourcing OEM specifically for the X80's intake manifold. Installation requires removing the intake manifold. One open question raised by owners: whether all 5 gaskets in the kit are needed for the X80, or only 4 square gaskets plus 1 round gasket — verify against the actual manifold before ordering a full kit if only a partial set is needed20212223.

Broader donor-vehicle list for gaskets and rubber/seal parts. Beyond the Mondeo/Mazda 6 cross-references already documented on this card, the X80's 2.0L engine (Ford Duratec-derived architecture) shares common gasket and seal parts with a wider donor family: Ford C-MAX, Escort, Fiesta, Focus, Fusion, Mondeo, and Mazda 3, 6, plus Opel Antara and Chevrolet Captiva. Confirmed cross-fit items sourced from these donors: spark plugs, valve cover gaskets, intake manifold gaskets, the crankcase ventilation (PCV) tube, the transmission oil pan gasket, and the transmission fluid dip tube2425262728293031.

docs.title: Engine shuddering at 2.5k RPM and cruise
docs.text:
Tags: #problem · #jerking · #egr · #catalytic-converter · #conflict

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Symptom. Multiple X80 owners report engine jerking/shuddering that occurs in two related situations: (1) consistently at around 2.5k RPM, and (2) while cruising at a steady 120-150 km/h on constant throttle/RPM. The jerk is described as light, and it stops if the driver accelerates harder, releases the gas completely, or downshifts. A related pulsing sensation at 1.5-2k RPM is also reported. Severity is minor and doesn't meaningfully affect drivability if the throttle is adjusted around it12345678910.

Root cause — community divided. No single cause is agreed on. Candidates discussed: a fouled DAD sensor from crankcase gases, an EGR valve malfunction (a screenshot of an EGR-related fault code was shared in this thread), spark-plug fouling (plugs last checked 40-50k km prior), a catalytic converter issue, or simply a transmission quirk — some owners suggest it's the transmission hesitating/undecided between gears, which would be normal behavior rather than a fault. Similar complaints reportedly exist on Mazda 6 forums, suggesting a shared-platform characteristic rather than an X80-specific defect12345678910. Conflict: root cause disputed between EGR, DAD sensor, catalytic converter, transmission behavior, and spark plugs — not resolved in this data batch.

Where the community disagrees

  • Root cause of the 2.5k RPM / highway-cruise jerking is disputed within the community: candidates include DAD sensor fouling, EGR valve malfunction, spark-plug fouling, catalytic converter issues, and normal transmission gear-hunting behavior. Not resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: Engine "loses sync" and stalls — diagnosis
docs.text:
Tags: #catalytic-converter · #diagnostic

Symptom. After roughly 15 minutes of warm-up, the engine begins to stutter and can stall, described in the community as the engine "losing synchronization"12.

Three primary causes, each with its own check. 1. Timing chain has skipped a tooth. Check the alignment marks on the valve cover/camshaft sprockets against the factory timing marks; a skipped tooth throws off valve timing enough to cause the stutter/stall pattern2. 2. Clogged catalytic converter. Remove the upper (front) lambda/oxygen sensor and attempt to start the engine with it removed; if the stall/stutter disappears or clearly improves, exhaust backpressure from a clogged catalyst is the cause2. 3. Crankshaft position sensor failure. Scan with an ELM327-type OBD2 adapter for a missing or intermittent RPM/crank signal; a failing crankshaft sensor can cause the engine to lose sync with its own crank position, producing the same stutter/stall symptom2.

Each of the three causes has a distinct, low-cost first check (visual timing-mark inspection, sensor-removal start test, OBD2 scan), so the recommended approach is to run through them in that order before assuming a bigger repair (e.g. full timing-chain replacement) is needed2.

docs.title: Engine mounts — aftermarket brands and verdicts
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #aftermarket · #patron

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Related cards:

  • Engine mounts — vibration and replacement
  • Symptoms and inspection
  • Part numbers and cross-fits
  • Replacement tools and procedure
  • Prices and sourcing by date

OEM Mazda hydro-mount vs. aftermarket rubber — cost and durability tradeoffs. OEM Mazda hydro-mount costs roughly 10,000+ RUB, with a noted risk of counterfeits on the market. A cheaper aftermarket rubber-only mount (sourced via the Drive/Драйв forum community) holds the engine but provides less vibration damping than a hydro-mount — it uses no hydraulic fluid, rubber only, vs. the Mazda mount's hydraulic fluid + rubber construction. Even a quality Mazda OEM hydro-mount can sag by ~47,000 km, causing noticeable engine vibration felt on the hood/windshield, especially in winter. One owner's 2020–2021-vintage Mazda mount was still performing well at time of posting. Net assessment from the thread: a rubber-only mount runs quieter than a sagging hydro-mount, but offers less vibration isolation than a fresh hydro-mount12345678910111213.

Patron rear mount — excessive softness, no real improvement. One owner installed a Patron-brand polyurethane rear motor mount and found it excessively soft for the X80: it produced noticeable engine vibration and clutch chatter under acceleration, and did not deliver the expected noise-reduction benefit — an initial improvement felt after installation turned out to be a placebo effect coinciding with a fresh oil change. Recommendation from this report: keep the original (OEM) rear mount rather than switching to the Patron polyurethane version14.

Right-side hydro-mount vs. third-party rubber, and left-mount sourcing — restated. A separate thread reconfirms the general mount guidance: cheap third-party rubber-only mounts (2,500-4,000 RUB, RU market, Apr 2025) are considered less effective and soften quickly. The right-side mount (гидроопора) should be an OEM Mazda hydraulic-damping unit — third-party hydro mounts are considered unreliable. The left mount should also be OEM Mazda original, or the mounting sealant block replaced as a less common alternative. The rear mount typically performs fine even as a non-hydro part. One owner's original rear mount had sagged to just 2mm clearance at 48,000 km; vibration or clunking on startup is cited as the tell-tale symptom of mount failure15161718192021.

Aftermarket mount quality varies — Tzer Li rated poor. Engine mount quality varies significantly by manufacturer. Tzer Li mounts are rated poor quality by community feedback among the aftermarket alternatives tried. Separately, at 48,000 km, OEM mounts can show only minimal visible wear despite the owner still experiencing vibration symptoms — i.e. visual inspection alone may not catch a failing mount2223.

Aftermarket mount comparison — Patron vs. TZerLi vs. ST-GJ6G-39-060E. Further aftermarket engine-mount comparisons: Patron-brand mounts show poor durability, sagging within 5,000-6,500 km with a characteristic noise. TZerLi (when in stock) performs better, reportedly lasting 60,000+ km with a significant vibration reduction versus OEM. ST-GJ6G-39-060E is a hydraulic-type mount that performs well and effectively eliminates vibration. Separately, a LYNXAUTO ME-1068 mount lasted 5 years before needing replacement242526272829303132333435363738. Conflict: vibration-elimination effectiveness is reported to vary — TZerLi users report near-complete elimination, while Patron users report residual vibration plus sagging.

Right mount — OEM lifespan, and a detailed alternatives roundup. OEM part 5CA139060 (right/front mount) has a reported lifespan of roughly 45,000 km before failing. Alternatives compared: Patron PSE3325 lasted 9 months (13,000 km) with slight sag but retained meaningful vibration reduction. Torque AS1111 (cross-referenced OEM number GP9A39060D, sourced from Mazda 6) fits and works well, costing 4,400 RUB (RU market, Feb 2026). Kortex KEM144 (catalogued for Mazda 6 GG 02-07 1.8L) also fits. Avoid the cheap BM213906Z option. Overall, the part is compatible across Mazda 6 GG and FAW B50, consistent with the cross-fit options documented on the part-numbers and cross-fits card39404142434445464748495051.

Engine hydro-support (mount) failure at ~50k km — Stellox replacement, alternative Golf-mount weld fix. On a separate sample X80, the engine hydro-support (гидро опора двс) failed at roughly 50,000 km. Replacement part: a Stellox-brand mount for approximately 1,870 RUB (RU market, Aug 2024) from online parts stores. An alternative workaround mentioned in the same thread (echoing a practice reported among Mazda owners): welding in a VW Golf engine mount with a matching gasket. After replacement, the owner reported a dramatic improvement — near-total elimination of engine vibration at idle52535455.

Right mount = Mazda 6 GG, and how Mazda-type replacements feel (Sep-Oct 2026). Victor 🇷🇺 states that the X80 right mount is the same part as the Mazda 6 GG one 56. He fitted a Patron aftermarket mount in May 2025 after the original failed; it stayed firm, settled only about 2-3 mm, and the gap was 7.5-8 mm (three 10-ruble coins fit, four do not) 57. In September 2026 he fitted an original right mount, found its pin travel very stiff compared with Patron's soft rubber, and the car became "firm, as I like"; he also pushed hard rubber into the gaps of the lower mount's bushing (сайлентблок) 57. A silent video shows engine deflection with the new right mount and two other mounts at 70,000 km (parking brake on, first gear then reverse, clutch released) 58. He says almost all Mazda GG replacement mounts are soft: with Patron the engine rocked forward and back in neutral when he blipped the throttle, and Patron and VTR as a rear mount are "rubbish"; a Patron hydro mount is fine if a replacement is urgent, while the original is excellent 596061. Contrasting experience: Prosto Zuev fitted a Mazda cushion in the lower position and says the car is like new, with no jolts 62.

Where the community disagrees

  • Owners disagree on which aftermarket engine-mount brand best eliminates vibration: TZerLi users report near-complete elimination and 60,000+ km life, while Patron users report sagging within 5,000-6,500 km and residual vibration. Not resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: Engine mount failure — symptoms and inspection
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #vibration

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Related cards:

  • Engine mounts — vibration and replacement
  • Part numbers and cross-fits
  • Aftermarket brands and verdicts
  • Replacement tools and procedure
  • Prices and sourcing by date
  • Engine mounts — wear detection and replacement

Possible related symptom — low-mileage knocking/vibration below 2500 rpm. A new owner (47,000 km, 20 days of ownership) reported engine noise/knocking up to 2500 rpm with accompanying vibration; possible causes discussed include worn engine mounts or an exhaust seal-ring failure. Flagged as worth investigating but not immediately critical on a low-mileage car; not confirmed which cause applied1.

Hydro-mount failure — idle/AC vibration and ~1.5cm engine misalignment. Failed hydro engine mounts allow excessive engine movement, most noticeable as vibration at idle and when the A/C compressor engages. In one case a failed mount produced roughly 1.5cm of engine misalignment; replacing the failed hydro mount resolved the vibration and reduced engine movement. Photos in this report show a Patron PSE3325 rubber damper compared against an OEM mount for reference23.

Roaring/turbine-like noise traced to a sagging right hydro mount. The right (hydraulic) engine mount can sag with age (roughly 1.5 cm of drop observed in one case), losing its damping ability; the engine then rocks backward under throttle and transfers vibration to the body through the left mount, producing a sound described as an engine roar or turbine whistle under acceleration. Replacing the right hydro mount eliminated the noise. Diagnostic tip: listen under hard acceleration — a muffled, vibration-like sound points to a mount problem45.

Bucking/jolting between 1st and 2nd gear — engine mounts as a suspected cause. Symptom: when releasing the clutch between 1st and 2nd gear, the engine abruptly shifts sideways with a mechanical bucking sensation and brief vibration, occurring only on this one shift. Likely causes: (1) worn engine mounts allowing excessive engine sway when load transfers; (2) brakes partially engaged (residual pressure) causing drivetrain bind. Diagnosis: check brake-system pressure hold and inspect the engine-mount rubber for cracks or slop6789.

Mount wear effect on shifts and vibration, with a mileage baseline. At 55,000 km, mounts may show no wear at all — this is a useful low-mileage baseline against the higher-mileage failure figures on the overview card. Once worn, symptoms are: jerking during the 1st-to-2nd gear shift transition, and vibration through the body/cabin/exhaust system, especially noticeable during cold startup/warm-up. Replacing only the right mount reduces the jerking by roughly 80% but does not resolve the vibration; replacing all three mounts resolves both symptoms101112131415.

How to check engine mounts for wear — a practical inspection guide. Right mount: visually inspect the gap between the mounting bracket and the rubber body — when worn, the gap shrinks to a minimum and the rubber visibly bulges from the bottom. Left mount: harder to access; test by pushing/shaking from the gearbox side and feeling for excessive movement. If there's no vibration felt in the cabin at idle, there's no urgent need to replace mounts. Temperature-dependent behavior: vibration is worse on a cold start (below ~70°C) and reduces as RPM/temperature rises1617181920212223.

Clicking on launch with wheels turned — fixed by replacing the right motor mount. A clicking sound occurring specifically during launch/start-off with the steering wheels turned was resolved by replacing the right motor mount (engine cushion/подушка двигателя). The likely mechanism: excessive engine movement under load creates momentary contact between components that only happens under the combined load of launch + turned wheels24.

Left mount degradation — distinctive metal-on-metal rattling under acceleration. The left engine mount's rubber degrades over time, causing vibration and a metallic rattling ("как будто метал об метал" — "like metal on metal") specifically during acceleration/engine load — with a key distinguishing symptom: no noise at idle. This is often combined with concurrent right-mount failure. Factory rubber mounts are prone to cracking and corrosion over time. When any single mount fails, replacing all three is recommended rather than just the failed one2526.

Vibration diagnosis — engine mounts are one of several possible causes, not an automatic conclusion. Strong vibration felt through the cabin and exhaust (with rattling license plates) can stem from worn engine mounts, especially the right mount support — but proper diagnosis requires also checking: spark plugs for cylinder misfire (especially cylinder #1), engine mount condition (press the rubber from below to check for deformation), and exhaust resonance or component-to-component contact. Vibration often occurs at specific RPM ranges under constant engine load rather than across the whole rev range. Conflict: one owner (Фаб) replaced the right mount but the vibration persisted, while Victor argues the community should check multiple potential causes rather than assuming the mount is always the single culprit — consistent with the multi-cause vibration diagnosis already implied elsewhere on this card272829303132.

Right engine mount failure flagged as a pre-purchase check item. A "dead"/worn right-side engine mount is listed by one owner among several items worth checking before buying a used X80, alongside water intrusion under the spare-wheel well and front floor mats, rust under the rear-door molding and driver-side sill trim, and front brake-disc wear33.

Checking the right mount by hand: gap to the bracket (Sep 2026). The right engine mount (опора / подушка двигателя) is checked by feel, and by measuring the gap between the engine bracket (кронштейн) and the top rubber of the mount: Victor 🇷🇺 says it must be at least 5 mm, and if the bracket can sit on the rubber the vibration becomes severe 3435. Arсhi 77 gives 5-7 mm as normal and suggests laying about three coins in the gap as a gauge; he posted a photo of a bracket resting directly on the rubber with no gap, which "should not be like that" 3637. Prosto Zuev measured roughly 5-6 mm on his car 38. Disagreement: Arсhi 77 says a rubber nub (сися) protruding underneath is not a failure sign by itself if the gap is normal and there is no vibration, citing hundreds of Mazda-owner comments on drive2 39; Victor 🇷🇺 considers a 4.5 mm gap (two 10-ruble coins) too small 40. Victor 🇷🇺 adds that vibration thresholds differ between cars, that the left mount need not be inspected before about 100,000 km because its rubber is standard, and warns to tighten the mount bolt carefully: he stripped the thread in the bracket where the bolt screws in, and a nut fixed it 4142. For removing and refitting the mount see the procedure card.

Checking a hydraulic mount (гидроопора) for oil. Press the mount from below: in an oil-filled mount, pressing one spot makes another spot bulge; a stiff mount is just a piece of rubber, and a mount that does not bulge at all has an empty cavity without oil 4344. Disagreement on gurgling: Rus.d1 hears something bubbling when the car shakes over bumps 45; Victor 🇷🇺 says a fully filled mount has no free space to gurgle 46; Prosto Zuev suggests it may still contain oil 47. The cause is not settled.

Where the community disagrees

  • One owner (Фаб) replaced the right engine mount but vibration persisted; Victor argues vibration diagnosis should check multiple potential causes (spark plugs/misfire, mount condition, exhaust resonance) rather than assuming the mount is always the sole cause. Not resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: Engine mounts — part numbers and cross-fits
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #part-number · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Related cards:

  • Engine mounts — vibration and replacement
  • Symptoms and inspection
  • Aftermarket brands and verdicts
  • Replacement tools and procedure
  • Prices and sourcing by date

Cross-brand alternatives — Mazda 6 GG mounts. FAW X80 engine mounts can be replaced with Mazda 6 GG (Mazda6 GG) equivalent parts; multiple owners report success with this swap, sourced via Autodoc and other suppliers. Hydraulic versions are preferable to rubber-metal for durability and vibration isolation. Reported pricing (RU market, Jan 2025) is inconsistent across posts in this thread: one figure cites roughly 50,000 RUB paid for a hydraulic Mazda mount, alongside other mentions of ~3,600 RUB (a year prior) and 5,500+ RUB for newer hydraulic options — treat the exact price as unresolved and check current listings123456789101112131415161718.

Right upper mount — part number 5CA139060. The right upper engine mount (правая верхняя подушка двигателя), OEM rubber type, has part number 5CA139060. A higher-quality alternative is the Mazda 6 GG hydraulic mount (higher cost, better damping). Both available at ooove.ru and kitzapchasti.ru192021.

Left-side mount — MT vs AT part numbers. The left-side engine mount part number differs by transmission type: manual (MT): 5ca039070; automatic (AT): 5ca139070. Mazda catalog research suggests these are interchangeable, though the functional difference (if any) between the two part numbers wasn't fully clarified in-thread; the manual-transmission version is not readily available in parts catalogs22.

Right mount — Mazda 6 GH compatibility (unconfirmed). Separately, the right engine mount's hydro-dampener may be compatible/swappable with Mazda 6 GH parts, which would save roughly 2,300 RUB (RU market, Apr 2025) versus the FAW-branded part; there was also discussion of using only the hydraulic cartridge insert from a non-OEM supplier (Juiki brand) if a full assembly isn't available2324252627282930.

Conflict — GH interchangeability not fully verified. Full Mazda 6 GH interchangeability for the right mount is not confirmed: one owner (Сергей Куликов) reports an aftermarket rubber mount that lasted 4–6 years, but whether the GH hydro-dampener genuinely bolts on/functions as a drop-in was not settled in the thread.

Broader Mazda 6 parts cross-compatibility (same right-mount discussion thread). In the same conversation as the Mazda 6 GH right-mount discussion above, members reported wider FAW/Mazda 6 parts overlap: a coolant tee flange (фланец-тройник) matches 1:1 between FAW and Mazda across all measured parameters3132, and rear wheel-bearing seal blocks (сальники/уплотнения ступицы) were separately discussed as sourceable from Mazda, alongside general engine-mount rubber options — one owner planned to run a Patron mount short-term before eventually fitting an OEM part, noting that mismatched mount height or mount-bracket/stud geometry can force extra fitting work if the wrong part is chosen24252633.

Right engine mount — OEM/Mazda part numbers and brand options, restated. FAW OEM right engine mount part number: 5CA139060. Cross-compatible Mazda 6 GG (Generation II) equivalent: GJ6A39060 — community reports confirm this Mazda mount is a direct bolt-in ("болт в болт"). Also compatible per a separate report: Mazda 6 Atenza (2002-present), sold as SAT ST-GJ6G-39-060E (same OEM number GJ6A39060) — a drop-in that reduces engine vibration and improves overall drivetrain smoothness, installed as easily as the factory mount. Aftermarket brand options: SAT (budget, verified fitment), JIKIU (premium, 10,000+ RUB), and genuine Mazda OEM (cheaper than JIKIU). Newer mounts are sold as hydraulic units, but their quality is questioned by some owners, who prefer the older mechanical-style mounts34353637383940414243444546.

Right mount — FAW B50 cross-fit for cost savings. Right engine mounts (motor-mount supports) for the FAW X80 are reported identical in form and function to FAW B50 mounts. While the physical part is the same, B50 catalog pricing can be significantly lower — check both X80 and B50 catalogs when sourcing474849.

Cross-brand alternative — Mazda 6 GG (restated). First-generation Mazda 6 (GG) engine mounts can fit the FAW X80, giving an additional sourcing option when FAW-specific mounts are unavailable or overpriced50.

Engine/transmission mount bracket ("гитара") — Mazda source and inspection note. The X80's engine/transmission mount bracket assembly, nicknamed "гитара" (guitar) for its shape, is sourced from Mazda. When sourcing replacements, check the rubber/elastomer condition — it can degrade on high-mileage cars — and confirm the correct variant if multiple engine configurations exist5152.

Engine mount specifications — hydraulic right mount and rear mount, alternate part numbers. Suspension-bushing engine mounts: right mount (hydraulic) identified as Tzer Li TZ-GJ6A-39-060; rear mount identified as Metaco 4710-009. The exist.ru catalog was cited as a useful source for detailed compatibility checking of these parts5354.

Right (front) mount — FAW B50 identical part, and a hydraulic-vs-air-filled dispute. The right (front) engine mount is hydraulic. The FAW B50 equivalent uses the identical OEM number FA0139060 on both models, but costs less on the B50 catalog (roughly 1,890 RUB) than on the X80 catalog (2,000+ RUB, RU market, Feb 2026) — consistent with the B50-cross-shopping pattern already documented on this card; B50 catalogs are recommended for cross-checking prices on many interchangeable parts. Conflict: one user claims the right mount is actually air-filled, not hydraulic ("воздушная камера"), contradicted by another owner (Victor) who states the factory mount is hydraulic and that the Patron-brand replacement is also hydraulic55565758596061.

Left mount (over transmission) — X80-unique, OEM only, no Mazda cross-fit. The left mount is confirmed unique to the X80 and does not cross-fit with Mazda parts (unlike the right mount's Mazda/B50 compatibility already documented on this card). Options: source OEM only, or replace the individual silentblock (rubber bushing insert) with an aftermarket brand such as Жуки or Febest rather than the whole assembly. Mount-to-body installation points differ from the other mounts, so cross-shopping generic listings is riskier here62636465.

Left mount — MT vs. AT differ, sourcing difficulty, and cross-brand alternatives. The left engine mount is different between manual (MT) and automatic (AT) transmission variants — the AT version is reinforced. The MT-specific mount is difficult to source. A practical alternative for a worn MT mount: re-press the silencer/rubber ring onto the original mount body rather than replacing the whole unit. Possible cross-brand alternatives: a Mazda 6 (GG, 2002) mount, or SAT ST-GJ6G-39-060E (Mazda 6 Atenza) — both already cross-referenced elsewhere on this card for the right mount, suggesting the same Mazda 6 parts family covers multiple mount positions6667686970.

Rear engine mount — cold-idle vibration diagnosed and fixed with a Mazda 6 cross-fit part. A separate, detailed case: vibration transmitted to the chassis specifically at cold idle led one owner (Arсhi 77) to diagnose the rear engine mount (задняя опора двигателя) as worn/damaged. He sourced a MAZDA 6 02-07 AR00055 mount (MILES brand) as a confirmed compatible fitment, replacing it and resolving the vibration. General guidance from the thread: poor-quality aftermarket mounts degrade faster than OEM or better-quality replacements — worth paying for a known-good brand rather than the cheapest option717273747576.

Mount alternatives and pricing — Mazda 6GG cross-fit for all three positions. Beyond the rear-mount cross-fit already documented on this card, Mazda 6GG mounts are reported compatible as replacements across the mount set. The left and right upper mounts rarely need replacement below 160,000 km (they can still look new at that mileage), while the center lower mount is identified as contributing significantly to cabin vibration when worn. Cost estimate for Mazda-sourced alternatives: roughly 2,000 RUB per mount (RU market, Mar 2024). Replacing the full set (left, right, and center-lower) is reported to substantially reduce overall engine vibration felt in the cabin7778798081.

Where the community disagrees

  • One user claims the right (front) engine mount is air-filled rather than hydraulic ("воздушная камера"); another owner (Victor) states the factory mount is hydraulic and that the Patron-brand replacement is also hydraulic. Not resolved within this data batch.
  • Whether the Mazda 6 GH right-mount hydro-dampener is a genuine drop-in replacement for the FAW X80 right mount was not confirmed within this thread; one owner's separate report of a 4-6-year-lasting aftermarket rubber mount is presented alongside as a related but distinct data point, not confirmation of GH interchangeability.

OEM mount pricing vs. quality — a cautionary report. One owner paid a premium for an OEM right engine support/hydro-mount (7,800 RUB versus 3,000 RUB for an aftermarket alternative; RU market, Sept 2025) and received the part in a plain plastic bag with a stapled paper label simply claiming "original" — raising doubts about whether it was genuine or repackaged stock. Expected lifespan of this OEM unit was only around 3 months before developing a hydraulic-fluid leak, no better than the cheaper aftermarket alternatives. The owner's takeaway: the aftermarket option at roughly 1/3 the price offers comparable reliability12.

Left engine mount (AT) sourcing. For a 2020 X80 with automatic transmission, the left engine support/mount is available from kitzap at roughly 7,700 RUB (RU market, Apr 2026)34.

Rear engine mount — confirmed part number, source, and price (Jul 2026). Following on from the rear-mount diagnosis on the part-numbers and cross-fits card, the specific rear mount cross-fit was confirmed and priced: MAZDA 6 02-07 AR00055 (MILES brand), listed on Wildberries under catalog number 536285010, at 4,800 RUB (RU market, Jul 2026). Arсhi 77 tested and confirmed the fit despite the part having slightly different dimensions from the OEM mount56.

Konstantin Руммель read the Mazda mount price as about 8,000 RUB (RU market, Sep 2026) 7; an AliExpress "original" right mount was about 4,750 RUB (RU market, Sep 2026) 8, and Victor 🇷🇺 cited about 4,000 RUB with a wait of a month (RU market, Sep 2026) 9. Left-mount nut over-tightening — stripped thread and a Niva-nut fix. The left engine mount nut can be damaged by over-tightening with hand tools or an undersized breaker bar. One owner (Victor) stripped the nut at 48,000 km using excessive force, and had to replace it with a Soviet-era Lada Niva nut as a workaround since no exact X80 torque spec was available in this thread. Recommendation: use a proper torque wrench, or an impact wrench with a torque-limiting collar, rather than tightening by hand/feel123456789.

Right-side mount replacement — parts, tools, and procedure. Replacing the right-side engine mount (FEM0053, also called the rear hydro-mount or engine pad) reduces cabin vibration at idle and improves smoothness. Tools needed: 10, 14, 17mm sockets, an extended socket wrench, and a scissor/bottle jack; a quality replacement part costs roughly 2,600 RUB (RU market, Nov 2025). Procedure: safely lift the vehicle under the sump, remove the old mount bolts, install the new mount on the factory brackets101112131415.

Removing and refitting the right mount (Sep 2026). To remove or refit the right mount, turn it over at its position and bend the thick hose aside slightly; it then goes in easily 16.

docs.title: Engine mounts — vibration and replacement
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #vibration · #mazda-6-compat · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

This is the overview of engine-mount vibration and replacement on the X80; the details are split into the sub-topic cards listed below.

Sub-topic and related cards:

  • Symptoms and inspection
  • Part numbers and cross-fits
  • Aftermarket brands and verdicts
  • Replacement tools and procedure
  • Prices and sourcing by date
  • Engine mounts — wear detection and replacement
  • Engine mount wear increases vibration
  • Engine mounts (parts reference)
  • Engine mounts — aftermarket experience and fakes

Symptom and cause. The left and right engine mounts (опоры ДВС) can degrade and tear over time, producing a noticeable engine vibration1. One owner replaced both mounts after finding the right mount torn to shreds; replacing it (and the left, as a precaution) eliminated the vibration completely1.

Parts used — FAW B50 cross-fit. For the replacement, the owner used a right mount sourced from the FAW B50, kept the left mount as OEM/original, and separately ordered a center mount, also from the B50, via Ozon after finding themselves impatient to wait2. On the FAW B50 right mount, the mounting bracket portion unbolts, so you tension/pull it back into place and reinstall3.

Vibration at idle at 37,000 km — three-mount layout. On an automatic-transmission X80, idle vibration at 37,000 km was resolved by replacing the engine mounts. The car has 3 mounts total; the front-right mount is the primary weak point that most often fails and should be inspected first, though vibration can originate from any of the three. Hydraulic mounts are recommended over cheaper rubber-metal mounts for longevity45678910.

Three-mount layout — function and wear pattern by position (with detail). The X80 has three engine mounts: (1) left and right upper mounts, which handle idle vibration and smooth acceleration; (2) the lower mount ("nether"), which prevents engine rocking under throttle/clutch-release cycles, especially during downshift braking. A worn lower mount causes steering-wheel vibration/chatter felt when holding the wheel at idle or during low-speed maneuvers. All three mounts can wear out by around 107,000 km; the right mount fails first most often, the lower mount is softest and can sag earliest, and the left mount typically survives longest. Diagnosis: check whether the steering wheel or pedals chatter, or whether the engine visibly rocks under load111213141516171819.

Mount locations restated — three total, by function. Restating the three-mount layout already on this card with clearer location terms: (1) the right (front) mount holds the engine itself; (2) the left mount, positioned over the transmission, holds the engine to the transmission bracket/longeron; (3) the lower mount, between the transmission and the engine block, is a separate third point20212223.

docs.title: Engine mount wear increases vibration
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #vibration

Engine mounts support and constrain the engine's movement in the engine bay. As hydraulic engine mounts (гидроопоры) wear or fail internally, the engine is able to shift laterally by up to roughly 1.5cm under torque/load, and that movement rocks/transmits vibration through the rest of the car 12. Owners report the vibration is most noticeable at idle and gets noticeably worse when the A/C compressor engages — one owner described it as intense enough that the whole car "shakes" when the A/C kicks in 3. It's reported as perceptible even on mounts considered "normal"/not yet failed, with a sensation compared to an oval (out-of-round) pulley, suggesting the mount's damping characteristic itself, not just outright failure, plays into how much vibration reaches the cabin 4. Fix: replacing the worn/failed hydraulic mount stops the excess engine movement and eliminates the vibration.

Three possible mounts, OEM part number, and non-hydro vs hydro cost trade-off. Vibration on acceleration or with each gearshift can originate from any of three separate engine mounts: right-side, left-side, or the lower mount — not just the hydraulic mount discussed above. One owner's vibration on every shift was traced specifically to the right mount. OEM part number, based on the X80's Mazda 6 GG/GH-derived architecture: 5CA139060. On cost: non-hydraulic mounts sourced from ooove.ru are typically cheaper than equivalent-spec parts, while hydro mounts run 2-3x the price and aren't always necessary as a first replacement — worth trying the cheaper non-hydro option first unless the symptom specifically points to the hydro mount 567 8910.

docs.title: Engine mounts — wear detection and replacement
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #vibration

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Symptoms of worn engine mounts. Noticeable vibration throughout the vehicle, felt primarily on cold start and during idle. The right-side mount typically fails first. A service technician can diagnose by lifting the vehicle and checking mount movement by hand.1234

Complete vibration elimination requires all three mounts, not just one. One owner replaced the right and left engine mounts (the lower central mount was original at 160,000 km and already showed cracks) and saw vibration reduced by ~90% — not fully eliminated. For AKPP (automatic transmission) cars specifically, the transmission mount bushing ("бублик") also needs restoration/replacement to fully eliminate the vibration — a worn transmission mount bushing causes significant body buzz even after the engine mounts themselves have been serviced.56

Full mount replacement vs. bushing-only fix (2025-09 report). Left-side steering-wheel vibration under acceleration was traced to the right engine mount. The owner first tried replacing just the mount's rubber bushing/pad (suspension bush) — this had no effect. Only a full mount replacement, using a Mazda 6 Atenza mount (part number SAT ST-GJ6G-39-060E), completely eliminated the vibration. Photos document the before/after mount gap, changing from ~3 mm to ~0.8 cm. No special tools were required for the installation.7891011121314

Right mount: SAT and Tzer li options (October 2025). For the right-hand mount, the Mazda 6 number GJ6A39060 is cross-listed as SAT ST-GJ6G-39-060E and as Tzer li TZ-GJ6A-39-060, which is a hydraulic version1516. This overlaps with engine mounts — vibration and replacement, which already holds the SAT option and the fitment reports.

docs.title: Engine oil — spec, viscosity, and brands
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-oil

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

This page includes Syrian-market information.

Official spec (CA4GD1 gasoline engine). The manual specifies 5W-30 as the primary motor oil for the CA4GD1 engine, with 5W-20 and 5W-40 as acceptable alternatives depending on ambient temperature (chart range -15°C to +45°C)12. The manual warns against using higher-viscosity oil at low temperatures, as it can cause starting difficulty3. A later manual excerpt confirms: quality grade SM minimum, viscosity 5W-40 / 0W-20 / 5W-30, choose per ambient temperature456. One owner (at ~150,000 km mileage) flagged a nuance worth checking directly against the formal approvals document: despite 5W-40 appearing on general viscosity charts, they found only 5W-30 actually listed under the official approvals ("допуски"), with no 5W-40 entry78.

Oil capacity. 4.3L total with a filter change, or 3.9L for an oil-only change (no filter)49.

API standard hierarchy. For reference, API oil-quality letters improve in this order: SL → SN → SM → SP, with SP being the highest/most current standard as of 20241011. ZIC X9 FE is confirmed usable on the X8012. The engine's minimum requirement is API SM13.

Brand experience reported by owners: - VMPAVTO 5W-30 (synthetic) and TOTACHI 5W-30 (synthetic) — both available on Ozon, good reported performance1415. - Valvoline 5W-40, Repsoil 5W-40, Mobil 5W-40 — also used successfully1617. - Counterfeit warning: imported oil brands are frequently counterfeited; buy only from authorized dealers or brand websites181920. - Lukoil 5W-40 used with no wear issues reported at 55,000 km21. Lukoil 5W-30 also acceptable and reported to give smoother engine operation than 5W-4022. - MANN FILTER W71273 recommended as the oil filter to pair with these oils, specifically for X80 automatic-transmission cars23. - Prices vary by region/store; some shops charge ~500 RUB (RU market, Sept 2024) more for premium brand oil vs. generic2425. - Mitasu 5W-30 SM/CF fully synthetic (King Size 5L bottle) and Valvoline SynPower 5W-40 also used as a Mobil alternative2627. - Base-oil sourcing discussion: community view is that base motor oil commonly comes from a small number (~5-6) of global manufacturers (Lukoil among them), and many "branded" oils (Motul, Idemitsu, etc.) add proprietary additive packages on top of the same base stock282930. One owner adds that Toyota, like most automakers, doesn't manufacture its own oil either — the base could well be Lukoil, blended with additives to the automaker's spec31. As a concrete example, Lukoil's Genesis Armotech was reportedly supplied in Mercedes-branded canisters around 2014-2017, because Mercedes wanted an inexpensive but quality-consistent oil32. The same commenter states that essentially all cars assembled in Russia are filled with Lukoil at the factory, since it's the cheapest/most accessible option for automakers operating there33. On "Japanese" oil brands specifically: the claim is that no genuinely Japanese-made oil is sold in Russia — brands like Idemitsu etc. are not actually shipped from Japan34; similarly, European oil sold in tin canisters is suspect, since storing/selling oil in tin containers is prohibited within the EU itself35. A counter-voice notes Japan itself reportedly has only ~1-2 actual oil producers, with other "Japanese" brands merely registered there while relying on subcontracted base stock36. Counterfeit/low-quality oil is common in the market; poor packaging quality is cited as a tell3738. Lukoil is confirmed as the factory (OEM) fill for Russian-market assembly3940. - Mobil-branded oil reported to extend the practical drain interval: one owner's family car showed reduced oil consumption and could go 8,000 km between changes on Mobil, vs. 4,000-6,000 km on other brands4142. Recommendation: buy from brand-name gas stations to reduce counterfeit risk434445. - GENESIS SPECIAL SPX 5W-40 also reported used for an oil change (with genuine FAW filters and an X40-sourced drain-plug washer), alongside a wheel alignment done at the same service visit; owner reported the car ran more responsively afterward46.

Viscosity and mileage. At ~130,000 km on 5W-30, one owner noticed increased oil consumption under spirited driving; switching to 5W-40 was recommended, as the heavier film holds up better in a worn engine4748. That owner's car had a factory fill (at ~85,000 km) of 5W-40 branded "Luckily" with no consumption issues reported at that mileage4950. General guidance: oil-grade choice should track engine wear — higher-mileage engines often do better on the heavier grade515253.

Recommended viscosity restated, plus a dealership case. Recommended motor oils are 5W-30 or 5W-40 with SM, SN, SP certification or higher. One owner reported using GENESIS SPECIAL SPX 5W-40 at an official dealership, at 86,000 km on the odometer, with good results5455.

A3/B4 vs A5/B5 classification preference. The manual specifies A3/B4 classification, but owners also report using A5/B5 (lower-viscosity oils, e.g. Miraks 0W-30). One owner (Vasily) recommends Teboil Diamond Carat 5W-30 (A3/B4); another (Victor) uses Syntec 9000 5W-30 A3/B4. Stated preference in the thread: A5/B5 if available, A3/B4 otherwise acceptable56575859.

API SN and ACEA A3/B4 restated as the practical recommendation. A separate, later exchange restates the recommended oil classification as API SN and ACEA A3/B4. Higher specs (A5/B5) are noted as more closely aligned with Mazda's own factory specification (consistent with the shared engine lineage), but are not strictly required. Oils meeting the SN/A3B4 combination are confirmed working in the community6061.

Duratec HE oil spec — WSS-M2-C913-C, and brand recommendations. The Duratec HE engine's specified oil standard is WSS-M2-C913-C. Recommended oils meeting or matching it: ROLF GT 5W-30 (made in Russia, Obninsk — the same facility that produces Syntec- and Tatachи-branded oils), Taif Allegro, and Taif Forte (stated to exactly match the WSS-M2-C913-C spec). The engine is described as tolerant: any correctly-viscosity, correctly-volume motor oil will technically work, but matching the spec is preferred. ROLF GT 5W-30 is available on Ozon626364656667686970717273.

Factory-approved viscosity grades — restated, with a caution on 10W grades. The manual specifies 0W-20, 5W-30, and 5W-40. Community consensus favors 5W-30 as the standard per-manual choice, with 5W-40 acceptable for summer driving. 10W-40 is not factory-approved; 10W-30 is acceptable for winter use but not recommended for regular use otherwise. Synthetic/semi-synthetic brands mentioned: Rosneft Magnum Ultratec 5W-40, Sintec ExtraLife 7000 5W-40, Mobil, and Lukoil. Change intervals: 5,000-10,000 km depending on city vs. highway use. One caution: frequent oil changes can wear out the drain-plug threads over time7475767778798081828384.

Choosing viscosity by listening to the engine, not just mileage. A separate framework for the 5W-30-to-10W40 question: stick with synthetic (5W-30 or 5W-40) oil as long as the engine's running sound stays consistent with baseline — i.e. no audible change after an oil change. Only once engine noise noticeably increases following an oil change should a switch to semi-synthetic be considered, since that noise increase signals seal degradation and rising oil consumption consistent with a more worn engine. The recommendation is to base the decision on how the engine actually sounds/behaves rather than on a fixed mileage milestone. Consensus in this thread: stick with 5W-30 or 5W-40 — do not jump directly from 5W-30 to 10W-40 as sometimes claimed online. The "switch to 10W-40 after 100,000+ km" claim circulating online is disputed: some argue it's fine at high mileage, others warn it risks clogging the engine's narrow oil channels (масляные каналы узкие)8586878889909192. Conflict: this directly parallels the existing 10W-40 caution already on this card — both sources agree 10W-40 carries real risk on this engine and should not be adopted casually.

Grade/API summary and counterfeit-avoidance strategy. Summarizing and reinforcing what's already on this card: any synthetic 5W-30 or 5W-40 meeting API SN or SP is acceptable (SL/SM also work but are outdated ratings). To avoid counterfeits: buy only from official/verified sellers, or prefer oil sold in metal canisters (more expensive to counterfeit than plastic). Recommended lower-counterfeit-risk brands in the Russian market: Lukoil, Syntec, Mirax, Gazpromneft (domestic brands, less frequently counterfeited). By contrast, premium international brands (Motul, Total, Elf, Mobil) reportedly see roughly 10x more counterfeiting in this market — buy these with extra caution. Kixx synthetic is considered premium but rarely counterfeited due to relative obscurity; it was previously sold in purple packaging and is now mainly available via online marketplaces93949596979899100101102103104105106107108109110.

Standards restated concisely — SAE, API, ACEA, and a Mazda-3 caution. Recommended viscosity grades: SAE 5W-30 or 5W-40. API standards: SL, SN, or SP. ACEA standards: A3/B4 or A5/B5. Owners are cautioned not to use oils formulated/rated specifically for the Mazda 3 or other vehicles with a different spec, despite the shared Duratec HE engine lineage. Switching to a properly-specified synthetic oil (e.g. Liqui Moly MOLYGEN) is reported to noticeably improve engine noise, throttle responsiveness, and overall smoothness of operation111112113114115.

Liqui Moly MOLYGEN NEW GENERATION 5W-30 — real-world results. One owner installed Liqui Moly MOLYGEN NEW GENERATION 5W-30 synthetic oil (5L bottles sourced from a verified Ozon seller) in May 2026. Reported benefits: a noticeably quieter engine, reduced engine noise/whistle, and smoother overall operation. The recommendation originally came from a Mazda 6 owner but was verified as compatible with the X80 given the shared engine platform; the seller guarantees authenticity116117118119120121.

Viscosity choice restated — Mazda-derived engine, manual minimum vs. practice. The X80's Mazda-derived engine has a manual-specified minimum SM grade; one experienced owner runs SL grade instead. If budget allows, a C3-rated viscosity is recommended. The manual does not state a specific upper viscosity limit — only the minimum detergency/quality standard122123.

API class progression — SM (outdated) → SN → SP, restated across two independent, earlier threads. Two separate, earlier community discussions independently converge on the same guidance already documented on this card: SM is the manual's minimum/outdated baseline; SN is the common current standard; SP is the newest and best. SM-SN are backward compatible with each other; SP is superior to both. Both threads agree that oil quality and brand reliability matter more than chasing the newest classification letter alone, and that timely oil changes matter more than the exact classification chosen124125126127.

Russian VMP-brand oil — positive owner experience, cross-vehicle use. Independent of the counterfeit-avoidance and premium-brand guidance already on this card, the domestic ВМП (VMP) brand — which specializes in engine/gearbox additives — received positive feedback from owners. One owner filled twice with VMP and rated its quality as equivalent to imported oils; another owner uses the same brand on a second vehicle (a Hyundai Kreta), reporting a good additive package for engine longevity per community consensus128129130131.

Brand/viscosity recommendations — restated with concrete change-interval and consumption data. An earlier, independent set of brand recommendations for the X80: VMP Avto (5W-30 or 5W-40 — no oil consumption reported at 120,000 km after two full changes), Lukoil Genesis (the factory fill — no issues reported, available in 5W-40 or 5W-30), and Gazpromneft Premium N 5W-40. ZIC 5W-40 is flagged as one to avoid — reported to increase engine noise and oil consumption. Recommended change interval: 7,000 km. Seasonal viscosity guidance: 5W-30 in winter, 5W-40 in summer. Idemitsu and Shell as listed in the owner's manual are described as recommendations only rather than a strict requirement; the factory-filled Lukoil Genesis is noted as appropriate specifically for Kaliningrad-assembled cars132133134135136137138139140141142143144145146.

5W-40 synthetic, API SN/CF, brand-agnostic — from the second Telegram group. A separate community (FAW BESTURN X80 group) restates the core recommendation independently: 5W-40 synthetic, meeting API SN/CF, is recommended as long as it's genuine (non-counterfeit) — the responder notes brand choice is largely a matter of preference ("depends on your faith") among reputable options like Lukoil, Gazprom, Syntek, and Shell147.

All-weather 5W-40 recommended for hot climates — from the second Telegram group. When asked specifically which oil is best for hot weather, a separate response from the same second group states 5W-40 is the ideal viscosity for the X80 in any weather, including hot climates — directly relevant to owners in warm-climate markets like Syria148149.

Engine oil capacity restated — 4.3-4.4L actual vs. 2L on paper, from the second Telegram group. A separate thread in the second group repeats a capacity discrepancy already documented on this card: the spec sheet states 2 liters, but the actual full capacity is ~4.3-4.5 liters. Multiple owners confirm filling to the upper dipstick mark for 4.3-4.4L with no issues over several years of ownership — consistent with the 4.3L (with filter) figure already on this card150151152153154155.

Where the community disagrees

  • Multiple threads on this card disagree about whether 10W-40 is safe on the X80's engine at higher mileage — some recommend it past 150,000 km, others (including a separate exchange on this same card) warn it risks clogging the engine's narrow oil channels; treat 10W-40 adoption as debated rather than settled.

Fuel tank filler neck seal. Part number FC0142241. The seal can deteriorate with age, leading to fuel leakage at the filler neck. The seal contains an internal spring/wire component; one owner reported removing this spring and discarding it, without needing seal replacement and without further issues afterward12.

Intake actuator motor — broken gear repaired via 3D printing. If the gear inside the intake actuator motor breaks, it can be 3D printed as a replacement part and reinstalled, avoiding the cost of a new motor assembly. One owner (Дмитрий) completed this repair for a total of 600 RUB (RU market, July 2025)3.

Intake manifold ("spider"). Article 5DA32050XB is identified by a member as the intake "spider" (паук), meaning the intake manifold or receiver, in reply to a pre-facelift parts request. No price is given4.

Engine gasket L362102D5A (Mazda listing). An Ozon listing (October 2025) offers a single Mazda engine gasket, article L362102D5A; the listing does not say which gasket it is5.

Exhaust manifold gasket for the Mazda 6 I (GG). A parts-shop link for the exhaust manifold gasket of the Mazda 6 I (GG), 2002-2008, was shared in October 20256.

Gearbox part quoted at ~70,000 RUB. The owner says the dealer quoted about 70,000 RUB (RU market, September 2024, quote from a few years earlier) for a gearbox part, which he calls expensive; the dealer ordered it and he thinks it may be cheaper from China. The exact part is unclear7.

Mazda engine swap as a solution. A Mazda-engine swap was discussed as the practical path forward, given the X80's shared Duratec HE/Mazda engine lineage. Buyers are advised to research which specific Mazda generation engines are a confirmed fit before purchasing.

Sourcing and pricing (RU market, as of 2025-06-05).
