docs.title: Low-speed jerking — multiple causes
docs.text:
Tags: #problem · #jerking · #engine-mount · #clutch · #conflict

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Symptom cluster. Distinct from the higher-speed 2.5k-RPM/120-150 km/h cruise jerking documented elsewhere in this KB, owners also report jerking/lurching specifically at low RPM and while holding a steady low speed. Several independent causes have been identified across different reports — this card catalogs them as a diagnostic checklist rather than a single root cause.

(1) Worn engine mounts, especially the lower rear mount. At higher mileage (one case: 225,000 km), worn mounts — particularly the lower rear mount — are a likely contributor; replacement with a soft/upgraded mount is available and commonly resolves the symptom. See the dedicated engine-mount card for part numbers and brand comparisons123456789101112131415.

(2) Counterfeit spark plugs with burned electrodes. One case: counterfeit NGK 3811 plugs lasted only 15,000 km before burning; switching to Denso TV16TT resolved the jerking. See the spark-plugs card for the full counterfeit-risk writeup123456789101112131415.

(3) Dirty throttle body. A roughly 15-minute cleaning job; a common and easy first check123456789101112131415.

(4) Fuel injectors requiring cleaning. Also raised as a contributing/alternative cause in the same thread123456789101112131415.

(5) Transmission-mount issues. Also flagged alongside engine mounts as a possible contributor to the jerk123456789101112131415.

(6) Throttle-adaptation reset. A suggested fix/diagnostic step: disconnect the battery, then cycle the accelerator pedal for 30-60 seconds with the ignition on (engine not running) to reset throttle adaptation123456789101112131415. Conflict: multiple possible causes were raised in this single thread without a single confirmed diagnosis; owners should diagnose systematically, starting with engine mounts and spark plugs.

(7) Crankshaft position sensor (CPS) fault. A separate report: CPS failure can cause jerking/hesitation with no error codes on basic OBD scanners — detectable only via live data on advanced diagnostic tools. On the X80, the sensor is located near the engine-to-transmission junction; symptoms are jerking on acceleration at specific RPM ranges. A broken tooth on the crankshaft timing reluctor ring is a similar-symptom alternative cause161718192021.

(8) Clutch engagement point (manual transmission only). Jerking at 0-20 km/h in low gears is often caused by insufficient clutch engagement — either a clutch height/adjustment issue, or the pedal not being fully released so the sensor doesn't register full engagement. Fix: ensure full clutch release, or adjust clutch pedal height in the cabin (a mechanism similar to Honda Civic's adjustment). Once properly released, the jerking stops immediately2223242526272829.

(9) Poor fuel quality from a specific gas station. One owner experienced low-speed jerking for 6+ months despite replacing spark plugs and filters and cleaning the throttle/injectors — all without effect. Root cause: consistently poor fuel from one specific gas station; switching to a different station (even within the same nominal chain — quality reportedly varies significantly by individual station) resolved the jerking and improved fuel consumption. The injector seal rings had hardened/carbonized from the poor fuel303132.

Where the community disagrees

  • In the single thread covering causes (1)-(6), multiple plausible root causes for low-RPM jerking were proposed without a single confirmed diagnosis: worn engine/transmission mounts, counterfeit spark plugs, a dirty throttle body, dirty injectors, and throttle-adaptation drift. Owners should diagnose systematically rather than assume one cause; causes (7)-(9) on this card were identified in separate, unrelated threads and are more specific/confirmed.

docs.title: LPG (GBO) conversion — reliability and cost
docs.text:
Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Long-term reliability — 85,000 km on gas. One owner (Eduard) installed an LPG (GBO — газобаллонное оборудование) system and has run 85,000 km on gas fuel with the system reported as reliable; he is available for consultation within the community12.

Cost-benefit — only pays off over a long ownership horizon. LPG conversion is only economical if the owner plans to keep the vehicle 10+ years; the payback period typically requires that timeframe given the high upfront installation cost12.

Effect on engine — cleaner burn, higher octane, slightly higher combustion temperature. LPG burns cleaner than petrol, producing less carbon buildup on pistons and valves, and — unlike petrol — does not wash oil film off the cylinder walls. LPG's higher octane rating (~105 vs. 92-95 for petrol) helps prevent detonation and reduces shock loads on engine parts. However, gas combustion temperature runs 4-5°C higher than petrol, slightly raising engine operating temperature. One owner reported the engine's compression ratio increased from 10-11 to 12.6 after 40,000 km on a properly tuned gas system (total mileage at time of report: 158,000 km)34567. Conflict: a mechanic with 10 years' experience (Валерий) argues gas reduces engine life and stresses the cylinder head/gasket (ГБЦ); another owner (Игорь) argues proper ECU tuning minimizes this risk, citing gas's cleaner burn, lack of carbon buildup, and higher octane as factors that can increase engine life — reflecting an ongoing, unresolved debate in the wider Russian automotive community.

Economics and mandatory maintenance requirement (2026 pricing). Fuel cost comparison: 30L of petrol costs roughly 1,700 RUB, the same volume of LPG roughly 700 RUB (RU market, Feb 2026) — a significant per-fill saving that reinforces the long-horizon payback case already documented on this card. Critical maintenance requirement specific to gas conversion: valve clearance must be checked every 20,000-30,000 km — this is mandatory, not optional, because the valve gap increases faster on gas over time and must be adjusted or the valves will burn. This requires removing the valve cover and replacing shims (see the shim-adjustment card for the general procedure) — it needs real mechanical skill. Because the X80 has no hydraulic lifters (mechanical only, consistent with the valve-lifter card elsewhere in this section), skipping this check becomes expensive and time-consuming to recover from. One owner reports 185,000 km on gas without issues, attributed to careful, non-aggressive driving (a family member drives it gently). Not recommended for aggressive drivers8910111213141516171819202122232425262728293031. Conflict: consistent with the longevity dispute already documented on this card — some users report gas conversion works fine over high mileage (Фанис, 185,000 km), others (Фаб) warn against it specifically because of the lack of hydraulic lifters.

Long-term ownership report — 42,000 RUB unregistered install, ~150,000 RUB/year savings. One owner (Arсhi 77) installed LPG at 42,000 RUB (RU market, April 2026) (unregistered install), 4th/5th-generation propane equipment, on a car doing 30-35k km/year. Fuel cost comparison: propane 19.90 RUB/liter (RU market, April 2026) vs. 70+ RUB/liter for 95-octane petrol, yielding an estimated ~150,000 RUB/year (RU market, April 2026) savings. Maintenance cost: 1,400 RUB every 10-15k km (RU market, April 2026). After 160,000 km on propane, the engine reportedly stays clean with no carbon buildup. The system automatically switches to petrol at high RPM to protect the valves. The X80 has no valve-gap compensators, but this owner reports successful long-term use regardless; notes valve gaps still need annual monitoring. The spare tire was removed to fit the 55L toroidal propane tank in the wheel well; dual-tank range is 900-1,000 km. Many taxi/commercial drivers in the Dagestan region reportedly run the same setup long-term32333435363738394041424344454647.

Second long-term report — 70,000 km over 2 years, ~30% fuel-cost reduction, ECU tuning debate. A separate owner reports ~70,000 km over 2 years on LPG with no problems, claiming roughly 30% fuel-cost savings at 100+ RUB/liter petrol prices (June 2026). This owner notes that professional LPG installers familiar with the platform can tune the system electronically via computer, and pushes back on the concern that improper tuning damages valves — modern tuning is done electronically by a specialist service rather than manual adjustment48495051.

LPG system setup details and valve-clearance debate (July 2026). Equipment cost had roughly doubled by July 2026 due to a shortage. Typical setup: 55L toroidal balloon under the spare wheel, BRC or equivalent controller. Reported claim: valve-clearance regulation is not required during installation if the system is correctly tuned, because the ECU compensates for thermal clearance at high RPM (e.g. fuel trim adjusted at 4,000 RPM to hit a stoichiometric mix). Nonetheless, checking clearances every 30,000 km is recommended, adjusting if needed (optimal exhaust-valve clearance: 0.35mm). One owner reports 60,000 km on gas with 10-15% higher fuel consumption than petrol but roughly 300,000 RUB (RU market, July 2026) saved over 2 years vs. petrol525354555657585960616263. Conflict: fuel-mixing compensation is disputed — Victor credits ECU tuning for handling thermal valve clearance automatically; Фаб emphasizes the risk of skipping valve-clearance regulation given the X80's lack of hydraulic compensators; Arсhi 77 counters that proper professional installation and high-RPM ECU tuning handle this adequately, citing 60,000 km of trouble-free use as evidence.

Valve and thermal design considerations for LPG — restated. The X80 uses direct mechanical valve clearance with no hydraulic compensators and no built-in auto-adjustment. Safe LPG operation is reported to require: (1) ECU fuel trim at high RPM (~4,000 RPM) to reduce lean-burn tendency, (2) periodic manual clearance checks (every 30k km), (3) professional (not curbside/DIY) installation. Both methane (CNG) and propane (LPG) are viable fuel choices; methane doesn't require a spare-wheel-well tank but is rarer to find. Propane availability is tied to domestic refinery (NPZ) output rather than being independently supplied546465666768.

Comparison anecdote — 200,000 km on a different vehicle (Hover H3), shared as LPG reliability evidence. Not an X80 report, but shared in the same thread as relevant experience: one member (Niko75) ran an official BRC LPG installation (toroidal tank under the spare wheel) on a Great Wall Hover H3, installed in 2018 for 32,000 RUB (RU market, 2018), and drove 200,000 km before selling the car in 2023 with no valve burn-out or major issues, on a 30,000 km valve-adjustment interval plus periodic GBO service. Another member (Василий Егоров) noted that official installers/dealers in his region tend to drag their feet on scheduling the mandatory valve-clearance regulation service6369.

Tuning an LPG system around valve clearance, and installer quality (Oct 2026). Victor 🇷🇺 says that even where valve clearances cannot be adjusted (no hydraulic lifters), the LPG system (ГБО) can be tuned to switch to petrol injection above 4,000 rpm 70. Arсhi 77, who has an LPG installation, recalls an earlier discussion in which someone argued that gas bends valves and that gas is bad for this engine, and says theory does not always mean practice; he advises nothing, "do as prescribed", and remembers that installers are often bad 7172. Victor 🇷🇺 states what he actually wrote (the 4,000 rpm petrol switch above) rather than that LPG is harmful 70.

Does LPG still pay off? (Oct 2026). Victor 🇷🇺 drives about 14,000 km a year and says the running-cost gap on his X80 is too small to justify an installation, though he dislikes the car's consumption 73. His brother's Murano runs on LPG, but with LPG at 54 RUB (RU market, Oct 2026; unit not stated) a Peugeot is now cheaper on petrol 74. Arсhi 77 installed LPG when it cost 25 and petrol 60 (an earlier, undated period, as recalled in Oct 2026) and agrees it is not worth installing now, except in Dagestan, where he says LPG is 55-60 against petrol at 120 (as claimed in Oct 2026) 75. Victor 🇷🇺 doubts the 120 figure: in 2024 petrol there cost the same as elsewhere 76.

Where the community disagrees

  • Community disagreement on LPG's effect on engine longevity: a mechanic with 10 years' experience (Валерий) argues gas use reduces engine life and stresses the cylinder head/gasket; another owner (Игорь) argues proper ECU tuning minimizes this risk and that gas's cleaner burn and higher octane can actually extend engine life. Not resolved within this data batch — reflects an ongoing debate in the wider Russian automotive community.
  • Some users report LPG conversion works fine over high mileage without issues (Фанис, 185,000 km on gas, careful driving); others (Фаб) warn against gas conversion specifically because the X80 has no hydraulic lifters, making the mandatory 20,000-30,000 km valve-clearance check both critical and easy to neglect. Not resolved within this data batch.
  • Fuel-mixing/valve-clearance compensation on LPG is disputed: Victor credits ECU tuning at high RPM with handling thermal valve clearance automatically; Фаб emphasizes the valve-clearance regulation risk given the X80's lack of hydraulic compensators; Arсhi 77 counters that proper professional installation and ECU tuning at high RPM handle this adequately, citing 60,000 km of trouble-free use as evidence. Consistent with, and reinforces, the earlier longevity/hydraulic-lifters conflicts already documented on this card.

docs.title: LPG/GBO installation and running economics
docs.text:
Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Reducer placement and cooling integration. The LPG reducer must be positioned close to the cooling-system pipe connection points to prevent air pockets forming in the heater radiator. Critical rule: the radiator cap must remain the highest point in the cooling circuit, with the reducer mounted below it. Poor installation from untrained technicians — reducer mounted above the optimal height — is a common failure pattern. Tomasetto 09 reducer is recommended for 2.0L engines; the smaller Tomasetto 07 may lack capacity at high RPM. Proper GBO installation requires careful coordination with the cooling system to avoid overheating.123456

ECU tuning is critical, not optional (real damage case, 2025-04 report). LPG installation without proper ECU tuning is harmful: one reported case of ~220 running hours on a poorly-tuned GBO system caused engine damage, a persistent check-engine light, and jerking/hesitation under acceleration. Professional tuning at a certified LPG installation shop (adjusting the fuel map after install) resolved all the symptoms — engine ran smooth afterward, CEL cleared, and fuel consumption normalized. Takeaway: always have the fuel map professionally re-tuned after LPG installation, don't assume a default/generic map is adequate.78910

Running economics (2025-04 report). One owner reports 50 L of LPG covers 400–450 km (roughly 11.1–12.5 L/100km gas-equivalent consumption), at a cost of approximately 1,150 RUB per 400–450 km range (RU market, April 2025). This owner's car had GBO installed at 8,000 km and was at 128,000 km total mileage at time of report, with a valve inspection performed at 110,000 km (8,000 RUB service cost (RU market, April 2025), Naberezhnye Chelny). There's community debate on whether LPG economics genuinely justify the installation and tuning cost/hassle, given the X80's 2.0L engine already has reasonable fuel consumption on petrol compared to some alternatives — this is a documented open question, not a settled community consensus.11121314151617

Valve adjustment interval on LPG — corroboration and low-confidence sourcing (2025-09 report). A separate, low-confidence exchange (unnamed/unconfirmed senders) corroborates the general LPG guidance already documented on this card: LPG installation is workable on the X80, but requires valve adjustment every 50,000 km, and only high-quality installation shops should be used, since poor-quality LPG installation work causes problems. This matches the valve-sensitivity concern implied elsewhere in this KB regarding LPG's effect on valve wear (see the Duratec HE valve-clearance card for the general shim-adjustment procedure, cost, and sourcing).18192021

docs.title: MT right drive shaft — inner CV joint alternatives
docs.text:
Tags: #manual-transmission · #cv-joint · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The right drive shaft of the manual-transmission (MKPP / МКПП) X80 is a recurring pain point for Victor 🇷🇺 and others in 2026: the original inner joint is no longer sold, replacements show play, and the intermediate shaft (промежуточный вал, also called подвесной вал, with its bearing support) is awkward to service.

Original inner CV joint and tripod alternatives (Sep 2026). On MT cars the right inner CV joint (ШРУС) is a ball-type unit, original number B5DA022520, which is not on sale and probably never will be. The substitutes are of mediocre quality and use a tripod (трипоид) joint made for the Mazda 3 (BK) 2.0 MT (BKEP): Febest 0511-M320MTRH, Triali GO-816, ASVA MZIR-M3M2, Zikmar Z87755R, Sufix ST-1519 and others. Victor 🇷🇺 advises buying several and keeping the one that has the least play on the intermediate shaft (all of them will have some) 1. He also notes that the "original" outer joint is not really original either, only something more compatible; he does not think a 26-spline half-shaft exists, and decided to buy the right half-shaft complete because his outer joint already had clear play 2. He finally bought the only right drive shaft assembly for MT available on Emex and ordered a right inner CV joint separately 3. The intermediate shaft and the half-shaft are sold only separately, so a complete shaft is not the only route 4.

Fit test: Sufix ST-1519 vs Zikmar Z87755R. The Sufix played on the shaft as much as the original joint, the Zikmar even more, although the Zikmar tripod seated better on the axle. The Sufix circlip (стопорное кольцо) was of the wrong diameter, its spline seating was about 1 mm shallower and its housing smaller in diameter; Victor 🇷🇺 fitted it anyway for the lower play, but recommends neither it nor the Zikmar. He says ASVA looks like a copy of Zikmar 5. The video shows the Sufix tripod with the retaining clip from its kit 6.

Right-shaft vibration at 70,000 km (Oct 2026). Victor 🇷🇺 has driveline vibration at about 70,000 km. He bought four inner CV joints for the right shaft; on the new splines of the shaft the Febest ones hold very loosely, and Sufix holds tightest but its tripod is poor. He ordered a Chinese right half-shaft from AliExpress, due in mid-November 2026 (outcome not yet reported). He notes that many Mazda owners got rid of vibration only after replacing all drive shafts, at over 200,000 km 7.

Intermediate shaft: parts and fit. An intermediate shaft from a Mazda 6 GG manual (for example Febest 05126GG) should fit, but the bearing support must be the X80 one; Victor 🇷🇺 doubts the length, since the Mazda 6 GG shaft is about 60 cm while he measured the X80 part at about 61 or 63 cm (he could not remember which, and the shaft changes length by design) 89. For the support bearing he recommends 62062RS and says to avoid bearings with metal shields: they die from water within about 50,000 km. Measure the support seals before buying: ZVCL067 fitted properly, ZVCL135 was 0.2 mm below the bore size and spun in it (the old one was refitted); people more often fit Febest 95HDS-38620513X 10.

Service pitfalls. Do not assemble the intermediate shaft with its bearing and support before checking the dust boot (пыльник) on the gearbox side: Victor 🇷🇺 had already pressed the bearing on when he found the boot problem, and the second press, with a puller, used up part of the bearing's life. His silent video shows the gearbox-side oil seal being measured with vernier calipers against the housing 11. Removing the inner joint from the intermediate shaft is hard: Victor 🇷🇺 spent five hours without success because a circlip blocks it, and eventually took the ball-type joint apart instead 1213. Arсhi 77's service clamped the shaft in a vice and drove the bearing out with a mallet (киянка), after a long struggle 14. Victor 🇷🇺 also drove the shaft out by striking it through the joint's end cap, which is not very strong 15. Before removing a drive shaft, measure its assembled length both relaxed and pushed in until the tripod hits its stop, so the correct length is known for refitting 16.

Spline counts, AT vs MT. Victor 🇷🇺 measured: both the automatic (AKPP / АКПП) and the manual drive shafts have 28 splines at each end; the intermediate shaft differs, with 24 splines on the MT and 30 on the AT. He thinks the drive shafts mainly differ in the inner CV joint, so an AT shaft may fit an MT car, but the intermediate shafts are different 17.

Play in the shaft: how much is normal, and a fix. Валерий reported play in the right shaft: looseness of the tripod on the shaft and play in all directions inside the wheel-side joint, plus play on the splines 18. Disagreement on severity: Arсhi 77 says some play on the gearbox-side splines is normal ("pay no attention, I have it too"), and that a hand shake at the wheel is acceptable within reason 1920; Валерий measures about 1 mm at the tripod edge and some rolling, which he finds worrying on an automatic 2122. For spline play Victor 🇷🇺 describes a fix used by some Mazda owners: cut a thread in the shaft end, pass a bolt with a washer through the CV joint housing (стакан ШРУС) and draw the parts together, preferably with a new joint so that it seats tighter than the old combination. It is a near-permanent fix that stops further spline wear, but later disassembly can take about two hours of hitting the housing; he points to drive2 threads on the Mazda 6 and Mazda 3 2324.

docs.title: Manual mode downshift behavior and protection
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission

The X80 automatic transmission's manual mode (selectable via paddle shifter or the lever's "+/−" gate) can be used to downshift while driving, on the move.1

Built-in protection: the transmission has intelligent over-rev protection — it will not execute a manual downshift if doing so would rev the engine beyond a safe RPM limit. If a driver selects an unsafe gear in manual mode, the transmission automatically manages the safety limit rather than blindly obeying the driver's selection.12

docs.title: Manual transmission — cold start and clutch
docs.text:
Tags: #clutch · #manual-transmission · #cold-start

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

One X80 owner with a manual transmission reported rough shifting and hesitation specifically during cold starts, along with stiff gear engagement, stuck gear positions, and clutch slipping at low temperatures. The thread links these cold-weather symptoms to clutch wear rather than a transmission-internal problem. A community comparison point: similar symptoms on a Kia Rio were resolved by replacing the clutch basket and disc together (not the disc alone), suggesting that if the same fix applies to the X80, both parts should be replaced as a set rather than attempting a partial repair 12.

Clutch pedal vibration on the highway — possible causes and unusual clutch longevity: symptom: with light foot pressure resting on the clutch pedal during highway cruising (not fully disengaging the clutch), a vibration is felt through the pedal; this does not occur with the gas or brake pedals. Possible causes discussed: (1) a warped/unbalanced flywheel — some FWD flywheels are reportedly poorly surface-finished from the factory; (2) release-bearing run-in; (3) clutch disc runout. Mitigation: simply avoid resting your foot on the clutch pedal at speed. Data point on clutch life: one vehicle's first clutch replacement lasted 188,000 km, the second 315,000 km — unusually long, since typical clutch life on the X80 is more commonly 150,000– 200,000 km 34567.

Transmission measuring/dipstick tube — hard to source, try Avito with '09G AISIN' search terms: if the transmission fluid measuring/dipstick tube is lost or broken, search Avito for '09G AISIN measuring tube' — used-parts sellers carry it, though condition varies unit to unit. Recommend sourcing new from an automotive parts supplier or a salvage yard if a clean used one isn't available 8910.

docs.title: Manual transmission oil — capacity and spec
docs.text:
Tags: #manual-transmission · #reliability · #transmission-fluid

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

For the 2019 facelift manual-transmission X80, reported oil capacity is approximately 2.59-2.95 liters per one reference the owner recalled imprecisely ("по камасутре" — i.e. from a manual/reference document), though multiple owners in practice confirm needing about three 1-liter bottles to fill it completely, suggesting the true figure is closer to ~3L in practice12. One separate report cites needing almost 4 liters total, which may reflect a different measurement point or a topped-off/overfilled scenario rather than the nominal spec3.

Oil spec. The specified oil viscosity is the somewhat unusual 75W-85 grade — one owner double-checked this because the grade struck them as atypical enough to wonder if it was a typo, but confirmed it as correct45. An earlier, independent exchange in the group gives the same 75W-85 figure per the owner's manual, without further detail on capacity67.

Separate spec/interval report — GL4, 75W-80. A later, separate report gives a different spec: GL4 gear oil, viscosity 75W-80 (note: this differs from the 75W-85 grade confirmed above — treat as a possible source discrepancy rather than a resolved single spec). The factory change interval cited is 40,000 km, though other mentions elsewhere put it closer to ~60,000 km. This source also notes that the fluid-level check procedure differs between the AKPP (which must be warmed to a specific temperature, e.g. 60°C, before checking) and the manual transmission8910.

75W-80 synthetic — restated (MКПП only, not AKPP). Separately confirmed: the X80 manual transmission (MКПП) requires 75W-80 synthetic gear oil; this spec applies to the manual transmission only and not the automatic (AKPP)11.

Owner-manual model code and brand confirmations (CA6462ATE5TKG1). The owner's manual, under model code CA6462ATE5TKG1, specifies manual-transmission fluid as SAE 75W-80, API grade GL-4, capacity 2.95 L — consistent with the 75W-80 grade already on this card, and pinning down the API grade (GL-4) for the first time. Synthetic brands confirmed by owners: Polymerium 75W-80 (very thin, flows well in cold), ZIC 75W-80, and BARDAHL XTG 75W-80 (recommended for quality/performance across climates)121314151617181920212223242526272829.

75W-80 synthetic — another independent confirmation. A separate, later report again confirms the manual transmission uses 75W-80 synthetic gear oil, consistent with the specs above303132.

Fluid specification — 75W-80, brand and price. The FAW X80 manual transmission requires 75W-80 viscosity fluid. Recommended product: Petrol Ofisi MAXIGEAR EP 75W-80, 1L bottles, available on Ozon; price roughly 2,600 RUB as of October 2025 (RU market). One user reports successful use across two service intervals33343536.

Fill amount — restated conflict, 2.3-2.5L practical vs. 2.9L per manual. A separate exchange restates the fill-amount discrepancy: manual transmission (MT) practical drain-and-refill amount is commonly 2.3L (measured by filling from the drain plug until fluid reaches the filler hole), though the owner's manual specifies 2.9L. One user reports 2.3-2.5L actual when draining, another confirms 2.9L when the transmission is completely drained. Automatic-transmission (AT) capacity is not discussed in this batch. No specific synthetic-fluid requirement beyond general-purpose transmission fluid was mentioned373839404142434445. Conflict: the discrepancy between ~2.3-2.5L (practical, possibly incomplete drain) and 2.9L (per manual, complete drain) is not resolved — it may depend on how thoroughly the old fluid is drained.

Earlier independent capacity report — 2.9L, no filter. A separate, earlier exchange gives the same 2.9 liter capacity for the manual gearbox, consistent with the owner-manual figure already on this card. Typical drain volume during a routine oil change is closer to 2.4 liters, so buying at least 2.9L is recommended to guarantee a full refill. No transmission filter is used — the manual gearbox oil change is drain-and-refill only464748495051.

Semi-synthetic 75W-90 GL-4 — an earlier, conflicting brand/viscosity recommendation. An earlier, independent thread recommends 75W-90 semi-synthetic gear oil, API grade GL-4, specifically naming LUKOIL Turbo ТМ-4 and TATNEFT ТМ-4-18 (or an equivalent semi-synthetic 75W-90 GL-4 product) as good options, at roughly 2,000-2,100 RUB (RU market, June 2024) for a 4L bottle of LUKOIL ТМ-4. The thread warns against low-quality bulk/generic oils, which can cause difficult gear engagement once the oil is warm. Conflict: this 75W-90 GL-4 recommendation contradicts the 75W-80 (GL-4) spec confirmed elsewhere on this card via the owner's manual (model code CA6462ATE5TKG1) — not resolved within this data batch; may reflect different manual revisions, regional specs, or simply differing community opinions on an acceptable substitute viscosity52535455565758.

75W-80 factory spec confirmed again, with 75W-90 as an accepted community alternative. A later, separate report restates that the manual's factory spec is 75W-80, while noting that community consensus treats 75W-90 as an acceptable, functionally compatible alternative — reconciling (without fully resolving) the viscosity conflict noted above: both grades are in active community use, with 75W-80 as the documented factory figure and 75W-90 as a widely tolerated substitute59.

Official owner's-manual figures — restated, plus clutch fluid and AKPP fluid. Both figures below are sourced from the official owner's manual for model CA6462ATE5TKG1, consistent with the manual-transmission figures already established on this card: 2.95 liters of API GL-4 grade oil, SAE 75W-80 viscosity. The manual's transmission-section page also lists clutch fluid as DOT4. Separately, for comparison, the manual specifies the automatic transmission (AKPP) at 6.5 liters of JWS-3309 grade fluid6061.

Long-term reliability — 327,000 km on manual transmission. One owner with a manual-transmission FAW X80 reports 327,000 km on the odometer with only regular oil changes performed (per the spec documented above) — no major engine or transmission work has been required. The owner describes both the engine and transmission as remaining solid despite the high mileage, and is satisfied overall with the car's reliability62.

Where the community disagrees

  • MT fluid fill-amount discrepancy: practical drain-and-refill reports ~2.3-2.5L, while the owner's manual specifies 2.9L. Not resolved within this data batch — may depend on drain thoroughness.
  • Viscosity/grade conflict: one early thread recommends 75W-90 semi-synthetic GL-4 gear oil (LUKOIL Turbo ТМ-4, TATNEFT ТМ-4-18) for the manual transmission; the owner's manual (model code CA6462ATE5TKG1) and multiple later independent reports specify 75W-80 GL-4. A later report frames 75W-90 as a community-accepted alternative to the 75W-80 factory spec rather than a competing primary spec. Not fully resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: Manual transmission right-side seal replacement
docs.text:
Tags: #manual-transmission · #seal

Why it's hard. Right-side manual transmission (МКПП) seal replacement is described by an experienced owner as among the most difficult maintenance tasks on the X80. The engine bay, as engineered by the Chinese (Besturn)/Japanese-derived platform, has minimal clearance, and the drive shafts are packed tightly together, making them difficult to remove.1

Procedure requirement. Removing the drive shaft is necessary to access the seal — there's no shortcut that avoids this step.1

Tooling and experience level. Special tools and patience are required. The left side is reportedly more accessible than the right by comparison. The community recommendation is to reserve this job for experienced mechanics rather than attempting it as a first-time DIY repair.1

Seal part: Corteco 19016578B. Corteco 19016578B is an oil seal for the manual gearbox (МКПП), listed as TC 35x58x8/14.8 ACM; a member showed the box. For OEM versus budget seals see AKPP seal and pan-gasket leaks2.

docs.title: Manual transmission — 2nd-gear grinding
docs.text:
Tags: #manual-transmission · #problem

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Symptom. The manual transmission produces a fine-tooth grinding sensation specifically when engaging 2nd gear, accompanied by a slight vibration. 1st gear and 3rd-and-higher gears engage smoothly — this appears to be an isolated issue affecting only the 2nd-gear synchronizer/engagement, not a wider transmission problem1. Confidence: low — reported by a single owner, not yet corroborated elsewhere in this KB.

2nd/3rd gear grinding — shift-knob (gaiter) cover as the root cause. 2nd and 3rd gear downshifts producing a grinding/notching noise with audible "pinking." Root cause found in one case: the artificial-leather gear-shift boot/gaiter cover (in the transmission tunnel) dries out and shrinks, physically preventing full gear engagement. Fix: replace the shift-boot cover with a universal artificial-leather replacement (~640 RUB on Ozon, RU market, November 2025) — this fully resolved the noise. A transmission-fluid change at 83,000 km did not resolve the issue, which ruled out internal gearbox problems and pointed to the boot as the actual cause23456789101112131415.

Distinct symptom — whining noise (not grinding) on 1st and 2nd gears specifically. A separately-reported symptom, distinguished from the grinding/pinking cases already on this card: an audible whining/hissing noise (шелест), not a grinding sensation, occurring specifically on 1st and 2nd gears at mid-range RPM, and ceasing entirely on 3rd gear. This is characterized as normal gear-mesh noise rather than a bearing-failure whine. A thicker transmission oil can reduce the noise, but at the cost of increased internal resistance — a trade-off, not a clear-cut fix. Note: the X80 manual transmission has no fluid dipstick, so oil level cannot be checked directly. Confidence: medium — anecdotal reports with no confirmed permanent solution proposed1617181920.

docs.title: Manual transmission — shift points and RPM
docs.text:
Tags: #manual-transmission

Recommended shift speeds. Suggested manual-transmission shift points: 1st→2nd at roughly 20 km/h or 2,000-2,500 RPM; 2nd→3rd at roughly 40 km/h; 3rd→4th at roughly 60 km/h; 4th→5th at roughly 80 km/h; 5th→6th at 110+ km/h (highway). General rule of thumb: shift by ear when the engine sounds ready, or roughly every 20-30 km/h. In ECO mode, the dashboard displays 2,000-2,500 RPM at most speeds on the highway123456789101112.

Periodic highway driving recommended for engine cleanliness. Sustained highway driving (100+ km/h) periodically is recommended to help clean the engine, injectors, throttle body, and catalytic converter — city driving with occasional rev-matching alone is not considered sufficient for this purpose123456789101112.

docs.title: MAP sensor part number — cleaning fix
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number · #fuel-consumption · #bosch

No MAF — the X80 uses a MAP sensor instead. The FAW X80 is not equipped with a MAF (mass air flow) sensor (ДМРВ). Instead it uses a MAP sensor (manifold absolute pressure), part number L03D906051A, located in the intake manifold, which measures absolute intake pressure rather than airflow directly — a different architecture from many contemporary engines that use MAF12345.

Community sometimes calls it "MAF" — cleaning it improves AT shift quality. In a separate report, an owner describes cleaning "the MAF sensor in the intake manifold" (almost certainly referring to the same physical MAP sensor described above, given the X80 has no true MAF) and reports this improved automatic-transmission shift quality and reduced harsh shifting, especially in S-mode — a simple maintenance task with a measurable drivability improvement6.

Damage risk during cleaning — fragile internal tube. WARNING: the MAP sensor (absolute-pressure sensor, датчик абсолютного давления) has a fragile internal tube (трубка) that extends into the sensor body. During cleaning with a brush or carburetor cleaner, this tube can easily get pushed down and fail to return to its original position — caused by rough cleaning technique or excessive brush pressure. If this happens, the tube stays stuck in the deflected position and the sensor may need to be replaced entirely. Clean this sensor gently, without brushing or pressing directly on the internal tube7.

Normal operating range restated with a numeric threshold. On a warmed-up engine at idle, the MAP sensor (абсолютное давление в впускном коллекторе) should read 28-35 kPa (0.28-0.34 bar). A reading of 35 kPa is borderline/maximum; anything above 35 kPa may indicate an air leak into the intake manifold — useful as a quick numeric sanity check alongside the cleaning guidance already on this card8910.

Detailed cleaning procedure — drivability fix at 108,000 km. A step-by-step account of the same MAP-sensor cleaning already documented on this card: at higher mileage (108,000 km in this example), the sensor accumulates oil and dust, causing engine vibration, jerking during gear shifts, harder starting, and weak low-RPM power. Procedure: locate the sensor on the front of the intake manifold, roughly opposite the center of the cooling fan; remove it using a T25 star socket with a short ratchet (tight, tactile work done mostly by feel); spray carb cleaner thoroughly onto the sensor element — do not wipe or touch the sensor pin itself, only the outer housing; wipe the exterior with a cloth and reinstall. Reported results: smoother idle, fewer vibrations, better transmission shift feel, easier cold starts, and better throttle response. Cleaning the throttle body at the same time is recommended — in this case the throttle was found very dirty at 108,000 km. This is explicitly a drivability fix, not a repair for any specific fault code1112131415161718.

MAF/MAP cleaning cross-referenced from the EGR/crankcase-ventilation troubleshooting thread. In the course of unrelated EGR/PCV troubleshooting (see the EGR and crankcase-ventilation cards), an owner recommended cleaning "the MAP sensor" (referred to informally as MAF in the thread) located just below the throttle body — consistent with the location and procedure already documented on this card — as one of several checks for rough idle/jerking symptoms192021.

Excessive fuel consumption traced to a faulty MAP sensor (ДАД). In a separate, severe case — fuel consumption of about 40L/150km — the root cause was a faulty MAP sensor (referred to as ДАД, absolute pressure sensor), located near the intake manifold as documented elsewhere on this card. A properly working sensor controls fuel injection and prevents the engine from running rich; symptoms of the fault included erratic/inconsistent error codes across multiple different OBD2 scanners. Recommended diagnostic: a simple continuous fuel-consumption test — fill the tank to full, drive 100-200 km, then refill and measure the actual liters used222324252627282930313233.

Bosch 0261230245 as the MAP sensor (ДАД) replacement (Oct 2026). Печной Двор posted Bosch 0261230245 (an autopiter.ru listing) as the absolute-pressure sensor (MAP, ДАД) and says the article number is identical for the FAW X80 and the Mazda 3435.

Case: rough running and stalls after a cylinder-head repair, MAP suspected (Oct 2026). Павел's 2016 X80 2.0 petrol with an LPG (gas) system ran unevenly, stalled and reacted poorly to gas after the cylinder head (ГБЦ) was repaired, with timing-related (ГРМ) fault codes 3637. He had checked the timing marks about 10 times and the MAP sensor read 550-850 mbar 3839. Тимур suggested a poorly screwed-in sensor (or a crooked timing assembly) 40. Печной Двор replied that a MAP fault can behave this way without an error code, the engine will not go into emergency mode without the connector, and it is cured only by replacing the sensor, calling it a Mazda ailment that migrated to the X80 41. The fix was not confirmed.

Where the sensor is, and cleaning it (Oct 2026). Members disagree on the location on the 2.0 petrol engine. A screenshot of an AI search answer posted by Konstantin Руммель places it behind the plastic intake manifold, low, on the rear (bulkhead) side, reachable only through its wiring plug 42. Фаб says it sits on the front part of the intake after the throttle body, slightly lower, roughly in the centre of the radiator, and can be felt and unscrewed blind; he cleaned it and fuel consumption did not drop, "all placebo" 43. Victor 🇷🇺 removed, cleaned and refitted it, but dropped the screw (15 minutes to find) and notes that carburettor cleaner (карбклинер) eats the sensor's plastic, leaving it bubbled in places 4445. The sensor in the photo is Bosch-branded with a three-pin connector, a green O-ring and a mounting flange 46.

docs.title: Muffler flex hose specification
docs.text:
Tags: #exhaust · #heat-shield · #part-number

Facelift muffler flex-hose size. For the FAW X80 facelift, the muffler's flexible hose (gofra) specification is 55×120 mm (diameter × length). Recommendation: physically measure the existing hose before ordering, and buy slightly extra length beyond the bare minimum to give installation margin/safety.123

Muffler heat shield — part numbers and DIY alternative. A related but distinct exhaust-thermal component: the muffler assembly's heat shield/thermal screen consists of multiple panels with part numbers 5CA05615A and 5CA05615B (insulation panels) plus 5CA056444 (central heat panel). If official parts aren't available, a DIY alternative reported by owners is thermal-insulation material such as StP Hard Shell (sold in 0.5×0.5 m sheets), cut and shaped to substitute for the OEM panels.4567

docs.title: Muffler seal ring — sourcing and pricing
docs.text:
Tags: #exhaust · #part-number · #price · #cross-compatibility

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Symptom and dimensions: a disintegrated front muffler seal ring ("кольцо глушителя") causes the exhaust to roar/rattle loudly. The correct ring's parameters are 65 × 83 × 18 mm; this specific spec is associated with a Toyota cross-reference 12.

Pricing — dramatic price gap between suppliers: the same ring is listed at 4,780 RUB on KitZap versus just 376 RUB on Ozon (RU market prices as of 2026-09-07/08) — over a 12x difference for what should be the same part 12.

Cross-references: besides the Toyota-spec ring above, a "Mazda-type" ring is also commonly fitted by the community. The most popular cross-reference cited by message volume is SAT STL31540581 3. ⚠️ Conflict: one owner disputes that the cheap 376 RUB/Ozon ring (RU market, September 2026) is genuine Toyota, calling it "явно не Тойота, а левак" (clearly not Toyota, a knockoff) — he notes that genuine Toyota muffler bolts cost 278 RUB each around 6 years prior (RU market, ~6 years before September 2026) (i.e. a non-trivial per-unit OEM price), and that he'd seen a genuine Honda ring listed around 12,000 RUB and a Mazda-spec ring around ~1,000 RUB (RU market, September 2026) (also likely non-original) — suggesting the true OEM/ cross-brand price tier is well above 376 RUB, and buyers should treat budget listings with some skepticism about genuine sourcing even when the physical fitment works 4.

Temporary and permanent field fixes: as a stopgap while sourcing a proper ring, 8mm basalt rope (шнур базальтовый) packed into the seal gap along with silicone sealant was reported as an effective temporary fix (the reporting owner had basalt rope on hand from his fireplace/chimney work). For a more permanent repair, the same silicone-sealed approach secured additionally with hose clamps was reported effective 1.

Conical ring between the exhaust manifold and the resonator: alternatives and lifetime (Oct 2026). Victor 🇷🇺 says the standard ring is the one from the Mazda 6 GG 5. A member posted an Ozon listing SAT STL31540581, a muffler cone ring for the Honda CR-V 2007-2008, Civic, Mazda 3 from 2006 and Mazda 6 from 2008 6; Victor 🇷🇺 confirms it is that part and calls SAT a budget brand 7, while Konstantin Руммель calls it rather junk 8. Victor 🇷🇺 says people do not bother and fit whatever is cheaper, most often the cheapest ZZVF ZVBZ0401; in his view 40-60 thousand km should be expected from such a ring, and a ring that costs five times more is not guaranteed to last 100 thousand 9.

docs.title: Noise at 3000 RPM — air-filter-box resonance
docs.text:
Tags: #exhaust · #catalytic-converter

Symptom. A bass-like, turbine-sounding resonance appears when pressing the accelerator, roughly around 3000 RPM; releasing the throttle slightly and reapplying it makes the noise fade. Reported on a 2019 X80. The noise is present in Park/Neutral if revved to that RPM range, ruling out a purely drivetrain-in-motion cause12345678.

Leading suspect — air filter box (короб воздушного фильтра) resonance. Several owners point to the air-filter housing as the most likely source: one reports their own filter box made this exact sound around 3k RPM, silent at idle but occasionally droning under load (e.g. climbing a grade); switching to a Mann-brand filter previously made the sound disappear, but at the time of this report the owner was back on the original (orig) filter, which seemed better-made overall despite still rattling somewhat9101112131415. Separately, and consistent with the same failure family, another owner found their air-filter housing had been installed by a shop with only one of its two retaining clips fastened, leaving it loose enough to potentially draw in unfiltered air — worth checking after any service visit, and plausibly a contributor to intake-resonance noise if the housing isn't seated/clamped correctly1617. (For reference, that same report noted the engine bay was still clean at 47,000 km18.)

Other candidate causes raised in the same thread. (1) A rattling/leaking exhaust flex joint (гофра) — suggested as an alternative source, worth inspecting19. (2) A damaged/disintegrating catalytic converter — one member described an near-identical case: the noise appeared the day after buying the car, a shop visit found the catalyst had broken apart internally20. (3) General wear-point checklist offered by one member for this type of noise on Mazda-derived platforms: a poorly-seated air filter box, the belt tensioner roller, the alternator pulley, air leaks in the exhaust system's joints, and low АКПП fluid level — any of these can produce a droning/humming symptom21.

Diagnostic approach. Testing in Park/Neutral by revving to the affected RPM range helps localize the noise to the engine/intake/exhaust side versus the drivetrain: if the noise is present with the car stationary and revved, it points toward intake or exhaust; if absent stationary but present while driving, it points toward the drivetrain78.

Air filter OEM cross-reference — Mazda part number. The air filter's original part number, RF4F13Z409A, is a genuine Mazda specification (likely Mazda 6 GG/GH); it can be sourced from Mazda dealers as an alternative to generic FAW X80 suppliers22.

Air-filter resonator rattle — anti-rattle screw fix. The plastic insert inside the air-filter resonator chamber can rattle because the factory retention clip tabs are too small and fail to properly grip the thin, loose insert. Fix: use a 12mm self-tapping screw to clamp the insert tightly to the housing. Result reported: noise drops from a loud roar to a quiet hum during acceleration232425.

Air intake resonator — purpose and typical failure mode. The air intake resonator (the plastic tank/chamber positioned under the intake) is designed to reduce intake noise and keep water from reaching the filter. Its thin-walled, flexible plastic construction is an inherent weak point: it typically fails by splitting at weld seams, especially in summer traffic/heat. A failed resonator produces a loud ringing/roaring sound during operation. Some owners remove it entirely to eliminate the noise; others seal the split with epoxy2627282930.

Air-intake plastic booming — water-separator deflector as a specific cause. Beyond the air-filter-box resonance already covered on this card, the plastic water-separator deflector located under the air filter is specifically identified as a booming/humming source under load. Removing it, or damping it with resonator treatment, reduces the noise; some owners remove it completely, others just disconnect it, with minimal effect on air circulation either way. The booming is worse when driving in an underpowered/low-RPM-high-load state; proper driving technique (avoiding lugging the engine) minimizes it313233343536373839404142.

Zinging/humming under acceleration — internal air-box partition, weak snap-mount fixation. A separate, similarly-sourced acceleration noise (described as a mysterious humming or zinging sound) was traced to a plastic partition at the bottom of the air-filter box vibrating because its snap-mount clips fixation is weak. Fix: secure the partition to the housing with a self-tapping screw (drilling a small hole through to the frame/housing as needed). Alternative: remove the partition entirely if the vehicle will never be driven through deep water — the partition's only real function is to block splash-back during water fording43444546474849.

Crackling/ratcheting noise on acceleration from a stop — another loose air-box baffle case. Consistent with the internal-partition rattle already documented on this card: one owner reported a crackling/ratcheting sound (compared to a bike chain) specifically when accelerating from a stop, returning to normal once cruising. The sound originates from inside the engine compartment. Suspected cause: a loose plastic baffle/deflector at the bottom of the air-intake box resonating/vibrating against the housing during the acceleration transient. Fix, consistent with the partition-securing approach already on this card: access the bottom of the air-filter housing from under the engine compartment, locate the small deflector piece (identified by feel in the tight space), and either remove it or secure it with zip ties to stop the vibration. This is a noise-isolation fix only — no function is lost either way5051.

docs.title: Oil change procedure and filter options
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-oil · #oil-filter · #dashboard

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Drain plug vs. pump extraction. Draining oil through the sump/drain plug requires waiting an extra 5-7 minutes after the main flow stops, as residual oil continues to drip from internal channels12. Using a pump/syringe method to extract oil from the dipstick tube instead leaves roughly 200-500g (0.2-0.5L) of oil behind in the pan34. The pump method can also leave metal shavings/particles suspended in the pan (since nothing is drained from the bottom), whereas the drain-plug method lets those shavings flush out with the oil56. Opinions differ: some owners prefer the pump method for cleanliness/ease, others prefer the drain-plug method despite the longer wait, valuing that it clears out metal particles7.

Oil filter and service kit. A complete service kit (filter + gaskets) for the FAW Besturn X80 is available on Ozon; the oil filter alone costs approximately 400 RUB (September 2024, RU market), with multiple listed options/reviews89. Separately, MANN FILTER W71273 is recommended by owners as the correct oil filter to pair with synthetic oil changes, specifically referenced for X80 cars with automatic transmission10.

Dipstick markings hard to read. The factory oil dipstick has faint/unclear fill-level markings, making it difficult to distinguish the 'add' line from the 'full' line — this makes manual oil-level checks by dipstick alone unreliable without extra care or a flashlight11.

Oil grade and change interval — restated (SM factory spec outdated). The factory spec printed on the car is grade SM, considered outdated by modern standards; SN and SP grades are recommended instead for current use. ZIG (Korean brand) and Takayama oils were both tested with no excessive consumption reported. Recommended change interval: 7,000 km. Higher-grade oils showed no practical fuel-economy penalty compared to the factory SM spec12131415.

Hengst H90W27 filter — reverse-flow-friendly mount orientation. Hengst H90W27 is confirmed as a compatible oil filter. Notably, the X80's filter mounts with the threads facing upward, which eliminates the need for a reverse-flow check valve (unlike many other cars) — avoid filters that include an anti-drainback valve on this platform, since it isn't needed and may not suit this orientation. Typical price: 400-450 RUB (RU market, September 2025) on Ozon (sometimes less with loyalty points)16.

Oil drain plug washer — part number, spec, and why it must be replaced every time. FAW part number for the drain-plug washer: 100902337K. A European equivalent: Elring 115.100. Specifications: aluminum material, 14.5mm inner diameter, 20mm outer diameter, 1.5-2mm thickness. Critical rule: replace this washer at every oil change — reusing it causes thread stripping and oil leaks over time. Over-tightening the drain plug to compensate for a worn/old washer only damages the threads further rather than fixing the seal; a properly replaced washer seals leak-free without needing extra torque1718192021222324.

Oil filter — MANN W 712/73 and Mazda/Nissan cross-fit, from the second Telegram group. A separate community (FAW BESTURN X80 group) recommends MANN W 712/73 (or equivalents) as the oil filter, noting it also fits the Mazda 2/3/6, Nissan Lafesta, and Mazda CX-3/CX-5/CX-7 — available from the Ozon e-commerce marketplace25.

Resetting the service interval reminder after a change. After doing an oil change, the service interval reminder on the dashboard can be reset: press the INFO button (this opens the dashboard menu) → go to Settings → Technical status → press OK on the steering wheel → select Remaining range → press OK → then press and hold the INFO button to trigger the reset26.

docs.title: Oil consumption — reduction and decoking
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-oil

High oil consumption after catalyst removal or at high mileage — reduction strategy. For high oil consumption (масложор), especially after catalytic-converter removal or on high-mileage engines, the community-reported approach has two parts: (1) Switch to a premium, low-burn oil — specifically VMPAVTO Motive SN/CF 5W-30 was reported to not darken and produce minimal consumption. (2) Decoking: pour roughly 0.5 liters of diesel fuel into the oil filler, drive 100-200 km, then do a complete oil change. Avoid Azelit (chemically attacks aluminum pistons) and Dimexid (damages plastic components) as decoking agents. At around 143,000 km, consider replacing valve-cover seals/gaskets if leakage is also present12345678910111213141516171819202122232425262728293031323334353637. Conflict: community members disagree on Lukoil oil quality — some report recent Lukoil batches causing масложор, others report long-term trouble-free use of the same brand.

Engine decoking for ring seizure — Lavr kit procedure. Piston rings can commonly seize around the 200,000 km mark (sometimes earlier). One owner performed a decoking treatment using a Lavr kit (following the kit's instructions) at 50,000 km on a 2.0L engine, combined with an engine flush using a specialized oil and a switch to a different oil brand (ZIC mentioned). A compression check is recommended if oil consumption increases after decoking; short of a major overhaul, monitoring consumption and trying a different oil brand is a reasonable first step3839404142434445. Conflict: oil consumption after catalyst removal is disputed — one owner at 208,000 km with the catalyst removed reports no oil consumption at all, while others report noticeable consumption under the same conditions, suggesting high engine-to-engine variance.

Mobil vs. Valvoline consumption comparison on a 237,000 km high-mileage engine. A concrete brand comparison on a high-mileage (237,000 km, 2017 model) X80: Mobil synthetic showed zero consumption over a full 10,000 km oil-change interval, while Valvoline (the brand in use at the time of the report) showed 300-500g per 10,000 km on primarily city/short-distance driving. Oil change interval used: 10,000 km. General takeaway consistent with the rest of this card: consumption rate increases with mileage and driving conditions, and brand choice measurably affects the numbers464748.

Second-hand purchase — no aggressive decoking needed; basic maintenance sufficient. A separate, more conservative data point for buyers of a used, lower-mileage car: one owner bought a second-hand X80 at 53,000 km with minimal service history, and the community recommendation was not to perform aggressive chemical decoking — focus on basic maintenance instead. Supporting evidence: a separate high-mileage engine at 195,000 km that never received any decoking treatment had not suffered oil-consumption or related issues. Oil flushes and checking gasket/seal (hermetic) integrity are described as more valuable interventions than intake/combustion-chamber cleaning products for a car without symptoms4950.

Where the community disagrees

  • Community disagreement on Lukoil oil quality: some report recent-batch Lukoil causing масложор (oil consumption), others report long-term trouble-free use of the same brand. Not resolved within this data batch.
  • Oil consumption after catalytic-converter removal is disputed: one owner at 208,000 km with the catalyst removed reports zero oil consumption, while others report noticeable consumption under similar conditions. Not resolved within this data batch.

OEM dimensions. The FAW X80 oil dipstick's total metal length (excluding the handle) is 48.5cm; the measuring/graduated section is 4cm long123456789.

docs.title: Oil pressure sensor leak — symptoms and location
docs.text:
Tags: #oil-leak · #diagnostics

Symptom. After a long drive, one owner noticed the engine had lost a noticeable amount of oil, with visible oil pooling around the A/C drain-tube area on the underside of the engine1. The leak location was low on the engine, sprayed outward onto the steering rack and driveshafts — not a valve-cover gasket leak, and unrelated to the automatic transmission (the AT's own seal was clean and its fluid level normal)23.

Cause and typical loss. Another owner reports having had the identical problem: the oil pressure sensor had deteriorated/split, the oil-pressure warning lamp started flickering, and about 300g of oil was lost through the failed sensor4.

Location. The oil pressure sensor sits low on the engine block, near the oil drain line; oil from a failing sensor can spray onto and accumulate around the valve cover and nearby components. It's reported possible to spot/access the sensor without a lift, though care is needed given its low position13.

Internal seal failure — flickering lamp mimics an electrical fault, but it's mechanical. Restating and clarifying the failure mechanism already on this card: the oil pressure sensor can leak oil from inside the sensor body itself, causing the warning lamp to flicker intermittently — a symptom that looks like a loose electrical connection but is actually a seal-integrity failure within the sensor, not an electrical/wiring issue. The lamp flickers while the engine is running. Fix: replace the sensor with a new one; there's no electrical fault to chase56.

docs.title: Oxygen sensor — diagnostics and alternatives
docs.text:
Tags: #bosch

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Normal spec and fault codes. The bank-1/sensor-1 oxygen sensor's normal operating voltage is 0.2–0.8V, fluctuating during acceleration/load changes 1. A reading of 0.475–0.5V is within normal range 2. Error P0134 ("upstream O2 sensor circuit signal faulty") appears when voltage goes outside that range or the signal wire shows no activity 34. Related code P013400 has also been reported for the same sensor family, with a failed sensor showing zero voltage output 56. To diagnose: test the voltage response during throttle application, check continuity to the ECU signal wire, and verify the heater circuit 7; a faulty sensor should be replaced.

Front sensor sourcing (OEM). The factory front oxygen sensor's part number is 5DA0188G1 (Bosch OEM, the same sensor that ships with new vehicles) — purchasable on Ozon (ozon.ru/t/1xq0Gyo), price point documented 2024-12-04 89. A user confirmed a successful replacement with continued normal function 1011.

Lada/VAZ cross-compatibility alternative. A Bosch oxygen sensor made for Lada (Vesta/Granta) can substitute for the X80's, with the connector replaced/adapted — Bosch-branded units are recommended for quality, and the price was about 1500 RUB (RU market, 2024-10) 121314. Multiple sources confirm this cross-compatibility workaround 15. In one detailed report (DK1/fuel-pressure sensor context), the original FAW connector differs physically from the VAZ one, but the pins line up identically, so a connector adapter completes the swap; after replacement the P013400 error clears and the signal normalizes 161718 19202122.

P0420 (catalyst efficiency) is usually the lambda sensor. P0420 is a common code on these cars, usually caused by faulty oxygen (lambda) sensors. A commenter says the only proper fix is replacing the lambda sensor and that clearing the code with an ELM327 only hides it; he reports his first lambda had a P0420 fault from new23.

Warning light after bad petrol. An owner who filled up with bad petrol saw the engine warning light, which went off after he changed the fuel24.

docs.title: Front oxygen sensor — cost and alternatives
docs.text:
Tags: #bosch · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

OEM cost. The original front oxygen sensor costs approximately 5,000 RUB (October 2024, RU market)12.

BOSCH aftermarket alternative. BOSCH part number 0258006967 was named as one aftermarket option worth investigating3. Only around four BOSCH part numbers total are compatible with the X80 — described in the thread as "not that many" options to sort through3. One member notes the BOSCH replacement is effectively cross-sourced "from a Zhiguli/VAZ" (i.e. a Lada-family part) and requires a connector change to fit the X80's harness4. No one in this thread reported having personally done the swap themselves at time of posting3.

Bosch aftermarket equivalent — rewiring required. First and second oxygen sensors are identical in construction (same connectors and length, only the wire length differs). Bosch part 0 258 005 133 is confirmed to work as a replacement for the factory FAW X80 lambda sensor, but requires rewiring the connector (matching wire colors between the Bosch sensor and the factory harness). An alternative part number, 5DA0-18-8G1, is also available on Ozon and covers FAW X80/Haima 3/BYD F3R compatibility. Installation procedure centers on wire-color matching to the connector567891011121314.

docs.title: Power loss uphill — compression check
docs.text:
Tags: #diagnostics

Possible causes and the diagnostic path. Loss of power when climbing hills can indicate one of several underlying issues: valve clearance problems (see the valve-lifter/shim-adjustment card for the mechanical-lifter background), carbon buildup on the intake, or reduced cylinder compression. A compression test is the way to gauge severity and narrow down the cause: normal reading is 8.0-9.2 bar per cylinder. One owner's diagnostic sequence: perform a hydrogen-carbon cleaning treatment first, then re-check compression — if compression improves after cleaning, the carbon buildup was the (or a) cause; if compression remains low and unchanged, the problem is likely mechanical (valve or ring wear) and cleaning alone won't fix it, pointing toward valve work instead123.

Revs rise but the car does not pull (reported symptom). An owner reports that when accelerating off a dirt road onto asphalt the revs climb without the car gaining speed, only under power and not while coasting. Members suggest checking the drive shafts (привода) first; on a manual car this symptom would point to clutch slip. Switching to manual mode (Tiptronic) for the pull-out is a temporary workaround, and high revs without thrust in D could mean serious automatic transmission damage4567.

docs.title: Putting the automatic transmission in neutral
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission

General procedure — releasing to neutral for service. To place an X80 (automatic transmission) in neutral for service work: shift to Neutral (N), press the handbrake (parking brake) button down, then turn off the ignition while continuing to hold the handbrake — this sequence keeps the transmission out of Park without the parking brake re-engaging unexpectedly during the service.

Different procedure for rear brake pad service specifically. A distinct sequence is used when the neutral/handbrake release is specifically for rear brake pad replacement (see the dedicated rear-brake-pad-replacement card for the fuller electric-parking-brake procedure, including the pre-restyle vs. restyle model difference documented there): turn on the ignition, set the selector to Neutral, press the handbrake button, then turn off the ignition. This order differs from the general-service sequence above — using the wrong order for the specific task at hand risks the parking brake re-engaging mid-service.

Confirm Park before restarting. Regardless of which release procedure was used, always ensure the selector is back in Park (P) before attempting to start the engine again.123

docs.title: Remote engine start needs aftermarket alarm
docs.text:
Tags: #remote-start · #autostart · #alarm · #aftermarket · #key-fob

No factory remote start. The FAW X80 does not have a factory remote engine start capability via the stock key fob, at least not in the units discussed in the group. Getting remote start ("автозапуск") requires installing an aftermarket car alarm — examples mentioned include Pandora, StarLine A93, and StarLine A96 — configured via the vehicle's CAN bus. Feature availability may vary by model year and trim; a 2020+ model was mentioned as possibly having it, but this was not confirmed as a factory feature1234567.

Demonstration. A 42-second video from a 2020 model shows remote start working via an aftermarket alarm (Pandora): the engine starts when the key fob button is pressed, with a tone confirming startup. A follow-up voice note clarifies that the tones/sounds heard are from the alarm system, not a factory chime189.

Conflicting report — stock alarm autostart via a triple-press sequence. An earlier, separate report conflicts with the "no factory remote start" finding above: it describes the stock X80 alarm as having a built-in autostart function, triggered by pressing the remote lock button 3 times in quick succession (each press under 1 second apart) from a distance of at least 5-10 meters — beyond the car's normal remote-lock range. The engine reportedly starts and the doors lock. To stop it: a long press on the lock button. A long press on the lock button is also reported to open/close all windows and the sunroof. Conflict: not resolved whether this is a genuine factory feature present on some trims/model years (contradicting the "no factory remote start" finding above), a dealer-installed feature indistinguishable from factory to the owner, or a misidentified aftermarket alarm feature — worth verifying against a specific VIN/trim before relying on either claim1011121314.

Where the community disagrees

  • One report describes a stock-alarm autostart triggered by a triple-press-from-distance sequence, which conflicts with the separately documented "no factory remote start" finding on this card. Not resolved within this data batch — could be a genuine factory feature on some trims, a dealer-installed feature, or a misattributed aftermarket alarm.

A community member asked whether the serpentine (accessory) belt tensioner and idler pulleys from a Mazda 6 GG are compatible with the FAW Besturn X80. docs.title: OEM spark plug specifications
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plug · #torch · #part-number · #ignition

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

OEM part. The factory spark plug for this engine (Mazda LFF7-derived) is Torch QH5RTIP(-13) — an iridium + platinum composite-electrode design, confirmed against the 2023-2024 Torch catalog and visually by the presence of a platinum "pad" on the electrode under close inspection 1 23. Gap specification: 1.3mm per the current catalog 4 — note an older/different Torch source lists a 1.1mm gap, so double-check which catalog revision applies before gapping a replacement 5. Thread size 14x1.25, length 25mm, 16mm hex socket (per the candidate's mechanical spec, consistent with the standard OEM plug size for this engine family).

Naming/nomenclature confusion — buyer beware. There is no confirmed "QH6RTIP" plug in Torch's catalog for this engine — only QH5RTIP(-13); requests for a "6" variant in the RTIP line came back empty, and RTIP as a design generation is described as already superseded 1. A separately-referenced Wildberries listing, ostensibly for the OEM equivalent, actually pictured RIU-11 plugs rather than RTIP-13 — RIU appears to be a newer design-generation suffix replacing RTIP, but it is not confirmed to be a drop-in match for this engine's spec sheet 6. Bottom line: verify the exact suffix (RTIP vs RIU) and index number against the current Torch catalog for your engine variant before ordering, rather than trusting a marketplace listing's title alone. Iridium-plug sets run roughly 2,000 RUB (RU market, April 2025), with premium brands priced higher.

Real-world RIU purchase confirms it as a working replacement, and adds pricing data. Following on the RTIP-vs-RIU naming confusion above, multiple owners have since actually bought and installed TORCH QH5RIU-13 (a 4-pack, marketed as an analog of ILTR5A-13G, 25mm M14x1.25 thread) as a direct swap for worn factory NGK plugs — one owner reports the original NGKs lasted 80,000+ km before replacement, itself useful context on expected OEM plug life 789 1011. Pricing (Oct 2025, RU market): 2,600 RUB or 2,124 RUB depending on seller 12. Note a wrinkle in fitment terminology: one owner reports the plugs they removed were marked "QH6" (with platinum buildup on the electrode) rather than "QH5" — consistent with the naming confusion documented above, where "6" variants and generation suffixes (RTIP/RIU) create ambiguity across sources; treat exact suffix/generation matching as still unresolved and verify against your specific plug before ordering 1314.

Budget alternatives. Two further budget options reported by owners: LYNXauto SP216, bought for about 1,800 RUB during an Ozon sale (RU market, Oct 2025) 15; and VSP 2721 STARTVOLT, listed specifically for the FAW Besturn X80 (2016+) on Wildberries 16. Neither has the same depth of catalog cross-verification as the Torch QH5RTIP/QH5RIU-13 lines above, so treat them as reported-working alternatives rather than confirmed OEM-spec matches.

Independent confirmation from a second group: Denso ITV20TT also fits and performs well. Adding an alternative-brand data point to the OEM Torch spec and iridium alternatives documented above: Denso ITV20TT spark plugs are confirmed to fit and perform well on the X80 engine. One owner has run this Denso plug since the original installation with no reported issues, treat it as a second well-regarded iridium option alongside whatever alternatives are already documented in this card 1718192021.

docs.title: Spark plugs — counterfeits and authenticity
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plugs · #torch

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Part of the spark-plug series — overview: Spark plugs — options, prices, reliability.

Counterfeit / reliability warning — real-world failure case. One owner bought TORCH QH6RIU11 iridium and AMD AMD.PL116 plugs from Ozon and AliExpress; all failed (burned out) within 1,000 km12. The resulting rich fuel mixture caused hard starting (required clutch-assisted starts, which the owner notes risked damaging the transmission) and led to a cascade of paid diagnostics: 4,000 RUB for a diagnostic scan, 7,000 RUB for a valve clearance adjustment, and 3,000 RUB for an EGR cleaning (RU market, November 2024)34. Switching to spark plugs bought from a local/official shop resolved the problem completely56. Community takeaway: prefer buying from an official dealership over online marketplaces, since defective counterfeit batches of Chinese-made plugs are a recurring issue online78.

NGK 3811 counterfeits — burned electrodes at 15,000 km. Counterfeit NGK 3811 plugs are flagged as a specific risk: one owner's set had burned electrodes with a 2.5mm gap after only 15,000 km. Cheap/counterfeit plugs in general are linked to poor fuel economy and, in the worst case, piston/valve burnout and shortened engine life; genuine plugs should show a proper solder/metal overlay (напайка) on the electrode. Denso TV16TT was reported as a reliable alternative after this NGK 3811 failure9101112131415.

Genuine vs. counterfeit — burned electrodes despite a correct-looking plug. One owner's plug set (make debated in-thread as Denso or NGK) showed a burned electrode after a video/photo comparison was shared161718. A separate owner reports a set that visually looked correct — proper braze, even electrodes, matching gaps — but burned out after only 14,000 km, underscoring that counterfeits can be visually hard to distinguish from genuine plugs19. Another member notes that calorific (heat) number mismatches specifically cause incorrect operation if the wrong plug is selected, independent of counterfeiting20.

Extended electrode-type discussion — RTIP vs. RIU, iridium core vs. platinum pad, and OEM-supplier uncertainty. A long thread examines close-up photos of installed plugs to determine authenticity and type. Consensus points: (1) RTIP-suffix plugs have an iridium core plus a platinum braze/pad on the ground electrode; RIU-suffix plugs have an iridium core without the platinum pad, and use a U-shaped side electrode where a braze pad would not normally be visible anyway — so "no visible braze" is not itself proof of a fake if the plug is a RIU-type212223. (2) One owner's photographed "genuine" reference plug does show both iridium core and platinum pad with a 1.1mm gap and full part markings2425. (3) Several long-time members state they have never actually seen genuine factory RTIP plugs sold at official dealers — dealers reportedly fit the non-braze analog instead, casting some doubt on how common true OEM RTIP units are in the retail supply chain, though this is recollection rather than documented proof2627. (4) General sentiment: modern iridium-core plugs "these days" are broadly similar in quality regardless of visible braze, and the factory manual does not prohibit using non-platinum-pad plugs282930.

Counterfeit AliExpress plugs caused misfiring — verify authenticity before installing. A cautionary report: one owner (Сергей) ordered Torch QH6RTIP-13 plugs from an "official store" listing on AliExpress; one of the plugs arrived defective, causing engine misfiring and triggering error codes, and he had to revert to his original plugs. Lesson: verify plug authenticity carefully before installation, consistent with the broader counterfeit/authenticity concerns already documented on this card31.

docs.title: Spark plugs — factory spec and gap disputes
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plugs · #torch · #oem · #conflict

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Part of the spark-plug series — overview: Spark plugs — options, prices, reliability. See also OEM spark plug specifications and Torch spark plugs — codes, listings, gap rules.

OEM spec and naming convention. OEM spark plug is RTIP type with a 13-point gap, i.e. 1.3mm factory gap12. TORCH-brand part naming: the final digit(s) of the code indicate the gap in tenths of a millimeter (e.g. "13" = 1.3mm, "11" = 1.1mm); the middle letter/digit indicates heat rating34. Sources in this batch disagree on the direction: one states a higher middle number means less heat-resistant (suited to higher-load engines)34, while another states a higher middle number means the plug is more resistant to heat and runs cooler5 — treat the heat-rating direction as unconfirmed pending a manufacturer datasheet check. TORCH QH6RTIP-13 matches the factory spec exactly67. Dimensions per an OZON listing: 16mm diameter, 26mm length, 14mm reach8.

Gap adjustment debate. One user reported closing the gap from the factory 1.3mm down to 1.15mm and observing better performance and lower fuel consumption910. This is not universally verified — it was reported by a single user and is presented here as an individual data point, not a confirmed recommendation.

Gap re-confirmed at 0.6mm in a separate report. One report states factory-installed plugs are set to a 0.6mm gap (differing from the 1.3mm figure reported elsewhere in this card — treat as a possible unit/measurement discrepancy between sources, not resolved here). Gap can be adjusted with a feeler gauge and screwdriver; some owners report improved performance after verifying/adjusting the gap. In one case, iridium plugs (more expensive) failed at just 7,000-8,000 km, and the owner reverted to standard plugs111213.

QH6RTIP suffix code — a conflicting claim: heat range vs. gap. A separate report states that for factory-spec QH6RTIP plugs, the numeric suffix (e.g. -9, -13) encodes heat range — a lower suffix number meaning a hotter plug, a higher suffix number a cooler one14151617.
