Conflict: this contradicts the TORCH gap-code convention documented earlier on this card, where the same style of suffix (e.g. "13" = 1.3mm) was said to encode the electrode gap in tenths of a millimeter rather than heat range. Not resolved within this data batch — the suffix may mean different things across TORCH's various plug families.

NGK ILTR5A-13G on the CA4GD1 engine — gap debate restated with a specific engine code. NGK ILTR5A-13G is confirmed as a working alternative to the OEM QH6RTIP plug on the CA4GD1 engine (the X80's engine code). Plugs come from the factory gapped to roughly 1.3mm; the printed OEM spec calls for 0.7-0.8mm. Community consensus is that the factory 1.3mm gap works fine without re-gapping. The NGK plug's heat range (5) differs slightly from the OEM spec (6), but this reportedly functions well on this naturally-aspirated (non-turbo) engine. Conflict (echoes the OEM-manual-vs-field-gap dispute already on this card): the OEM manual specifies 0.7-0.8mm and warns against adjusting iridium plug gaps at all, yet field experience shows 1.3mm working without issue, and one user (40157) states 0.6-1.1mm is an acceptable range for iridium plugs specifically1819202122.

OEM QH6RTIP gap — a third figure: 1.1mm per manufacturer datasheet. Adding a third data point to the ongoing gap-spec confusion on this card: the official QH6RTIP datasheet reportedly specifies a 1.1mm factory gap, contradicting the printed owner's-manual figure of 0.7-0.8mm. The manual likely contains an error, or is using a different measurement reference/methodology23.

Gap specification for the 2.0L engine restated — 1.0-1.3mm, not 0.7-0.8mm. For the FAW X80 2.0L AT (2019 model), the correct spark-plug gap is 1.0-1.3mm — the commonly-cited 0.7-0.8mm figure is stated to apply only to carbureted engines, not this fuel-injected platform. Original factory Torch plugs are gapped at 0.9mm. Community reports converge on 1.1mm working well, with some aftermarket alternatives (NGK ILTR5A-13G, ILTR6A-13G) arriving pre-gapped at 1.3mm. Conflict: official Chinese factory documentation (spec sheet for model CA4GD1, plug type QH6RTIP) lists 0.7-0.8mm, with an alternative ILTR6J8 at 0.8mm — directly contradicting the 1.0-1.3mm community consensus for fuel-injected engines; some users separately report 0.8-0.9mm from original parts. The documentation itself appears to cause confusion around which gap figures apply to this engine242526272829.

Original factory spec restated — Torch QH6RTIP, 1.1mm gap, discontinued. The original OEM plug is stated to be Torch QH6RTIP, gap 1.1mm, iridium electrode with a platinum braze/pad — confirmed via a photo of manufacturer-catalog specs. This exact plug is no longer manufactured/purchasable; what is currently sold under similar codes lacks the platinum pad and commonly ships at a 1.3mm gap instead3031. Ordering the OEM part number 3707010-37K directly is reported likely to yield an unbranded/no-name plug rather than a genuine one. Two specific replacement options were named: Miles ALSP067 — an iridium-electrode, platinum-pad plug matching the original's electrode construction — and, for a budget option, LinkGlobal LQH5RIU13, a 4-plug set priced under 1,000 RUB (RU market, May 2026)31. Conflict — optimal gap range: a separate message in the same exchange states the optimal gap for the X80 is 0.8-1.1mm depending on engine (2.0L vs 2.3L) and plug type, with a reply noting this may be a typo relative to the pre-facelift manual (which the replier believes states 1.1mm without the typo) — i.e. a possible 0.8 vs 1.1mm transcription error in circulation, on top of the broader gap-figure conflicts already documented on this card3233. Separately, one contributor gives a general ignition-type gap rule (not X80-specific): distributor ("трамблёр") ignition wants the smallest gap (0.5-0.6mm), electronic ignition somewhat larger (0.7-0.8mm), and coil-pack ignition (like the X80's) largest (1.1mm+) — offered as a rule of thumb with likely exceptions34.

Gap specification — restated as still unresolved, with a "doesn't matter on modern engines" dissent. The printed manual figure is again cited as 0.8mm; dealers in Saint Petersburg reportedly gave the same 0.8mm figure initially, then said they weren't sure. One member calls the printed 0.8mm figure a likely typo ("146% a typo")3536. Garage-mechanic opinion relayed in this thread: the tight 0.7-0.8mm-class gap only matters on old carbureted engines (e.g. Zhiguli/Lada), where mechanics used to bend electrodes to hit it precisely; on modern engines, a ~2mm difference in gap is considered irrelevant by these mechanics, loosely calling any gap "fine." One member's blunt recommendation, sidestepping the gap debate entirely: buy Denso and it'll be fine3738. This restates, rather than resolves, the gap conflicts already documented above on this card.

Torch part-number pair — QH6RIU11 (1.1mm gap) vs. QH5RIU13 (1.3mm gap). For the X80, two specific Torch part numbers are distinguished: QH6RIU11 ships with a preset 1.1mm gap, while QH5RIU13 ships with a preset 1.3mm gap — matching the factory/original gap. Community recommendation leans toward QH6RIU11 (1.1mm) as the compatible Torch option for the X8039404142.

Spark plug gap adjustment — 1.1mm as shipped vs. 1.15-1.3mm target, using a gap tool. Torch QH6RIU11 iridium plugs ship with a preset 1.1mm gap, while the factory/original X80 gap is 1.3mm. Some owners use a gap-adjustment template/tool (шаблон) to reset the gap to 1.15-1.3mm before installation, since gap affects ignition timing and should be verified rather than assumed correct out of the box434445464742.

Stock spark plug article number restated: QH6RIU11. An independent, later source restates the stock spark plug article number for the FAW X80 as QH6RIU11 — consistent with the QH6RIU-11 part already extensively documented on this card48.

Where the community disagrees

  • Gap adjustment from 1.3mm to 1.15mm reported as beneficial by one user (mihail kolobanov) but not corroborated by other owners in this batch — treat as an individual report, not a verified community consensus.
  • Two sources in this batch disagree on which direction the TORCH middle-digit heat-rating code runs: one says a higher number means lower heat resistance (better for high-load engines), another says a higher number means higher heat resistance and cooler running. Not resolved within this data batch.
  • One source states the QH6RTIP numeric suffix encodes heat range (lower = hotter); an earlier source on this card states the same style of suffix encodes electrode gap in tenths of a millimeter (e.g. "13" = 1.3mm). These two claims directly conflict and are not resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: Spark plugs — installation, torque and tools
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plugs · #tools · #installation

Part of the spark-plug series — overview: Spark plugs — options, prices, reliability.

Spark plug torque spec — do not exceed 18 kgf. Installation torque for the X80 spark plugs should not exceed 18 kgf (~18 N·m / 13 lb-ft). Over-tightening risks breaking the ceramic/electrode assembly, especially on plugs already installed in a used vehicle12.

Spark plug and ignition coil socket sizes. Spark plug socket size: 16mm. Ignition coil connector socket size: 8mm3.

Thread size mix-up — ordered M12, needed M14. One owner attempted to install new plugs but discovered they had ordered the wrong thread size (M12 instead of the correct M14) and had to reorder; separately, the same owner noted that Startvolt-brand plugs already installed showed yellow staining on the insulator after only ~1,500 km4.

Factory plugs extremely tight to remove at 120k km/5 years. One owner (Niko75) reported that after 5 years and 120,000 km on the factory-installed plugs, they were extremely tight and difficult to extract from the cylinder head — barely removable, suggesting a very high factory torque56.

docs.title: Spark plugs — lifespan and wear symptoms
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plugs · #misfire · #fuel-consumption · #conflict

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Part of the spark-plug series — overview: Spark plugs — options, prices, reliability.

Claimed lifespan vs. reality. OEM-spec plugs are commonly marketed with a ~100,000 km lifespan claim, but several owners report earlier failure, around 50,000-80,000 km123. One owner running QH6RIU-11 echoed this: they declined to recommend a specific brand given how many counterfeits are on the market, and noted their own QH6RIU-11 plugs were nowhere near the claimed 100,000 km lifespan and would need replacing again soon4.

Sudden power increase then disappearance — traced to fouled spark plugs. A 2018 facelift manual-transmission car (130,000 km) experienced a sudden, temporary performance increase (felt like an extra ~10 hp, described as turbo-like) during one morning drive. The effect vanished after a spark-plug replacement, suggesting the fouled plugs had been affecting ignition timing efficiency before that5678.

Transmission jerks at 1200-1300 RPM — fixed for some by an iridium plug swap (disputed). An owner with harsh automatic-transmission jerks/kicks at 1200-1300 RPM (described as feeling like being towed by a KAMAZ truck) resolved the issue completely by switching from stock plugs to iridium alternatives — Torch QH5RIU-13 or the equivalent ILTR5A-13G. Conflict: a different owner (39209) reported the same plug swap did not fix their jerk issue, suggesting the root cause of 1200-1300 RPM jerking varies by car. A specific Ozon listing for the iridium alternative: Torch QH5RIU-13 (4-pack, 25mm reach, M14x1.25 thread), marketed as compatible across Ford/Chevy/Mazda/Opel/Volvo/Suzuki platforms including the X80 (https://ozon.ru/t/39rnCxs)91011.

Iridium plug service life varies widely — 70,000-150,000 km depending on conditions. Community experience with iridium plugs varies substantially: one owner reported 150,000 km, another failed/needed replacement at 70,000 km, and some owners replace on the standard 30,000 km interval regardless of iridium's longer marketed life. Initial community expectation was a 100,000 km service life for iridium, but actual results depend heavily on driving conditions and fuel quality — consistent with the claimed-vs-reality lifespan gap already documented on this card12131415.

Fuel consumption increase after switching to Torch iridium — inconclusive diagnosis. After replacing spark plugs with Torch iridium plugs, one owner (Niko75, 120k km mileage) reported city fuel consumption rising from 10.5 to 11.7 L/100km. A long diagnostic thread ruled out engine misfiring/rough idle (none observed) and fuel quality (tested at a different station). Possible remaining causes discussed: a defective plug, an incorrect spark gap, coil issues, or simple fuel-gauge measurement variance. Recommended proper measurement method: fill to full, drive to half tank, refill to full and compare. No root cause was confirmed within this batch1617181920212223242526.

Where the community disagrees

  • One owner resolved harsh 1200-1300 RPM automatic-transmission jerks completely by switching to iridium plugs (Torch QH5RIU-13 / ILTR5A-13G); another owner (39209) reported the same swap did not fix their jerk issue. Not resolved within this data batch — root cause of the jerking likely varies by car.

docs.title: Spark plugs — NGK, Denso and budget options
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plugs

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Part of the spark-plug series — overview: Spark plugs — options, prices, reliability.

Further alternatives — NGK reliability and outdated-NGK claim. Factory NGK QH6RTIP plugs are described by one source as outdated. Torch-brand direct replacements QH5RIU-13 and QH6RIU-11 are said to offer a higher octane/heat rating and a smaller gap (<1.1mm). Separately, NGK-brand plugs (iridium or standard) are confirmed reliable over 60,000 km with no degradation by another owner, who also noted the factory plugs had inconsistent gaps out of the box12.

Torch QH6RTI (no platinum pad) and NGK long-term test. Torch-brand QH6RTI spark plugs are officially recommended for the X80. Unlike premium Torch variants, they lack the platinum pad on the outer electrode; community testing found no practical difference vs. iridium plugs on prior vehicles. Chinese Miles-brand plugs were tested as an economical alternative. Some vehicles still run OEM plugs from a 2013 factory batch3456789. Separately, Miles ALSP067 iridium plugs were installed with a 1.2mm gap (a slight adjustment from the 1.15mm factory spec found on one plug), costing about 1,640 RUB for a set (RU market, 2025); the owner reported a possible reduction in misfires and was monitoring the fuel-economy impact10. NGK plugs tested to 70,000+ km in "excellent condition" — no need to replace until the engine runs rough; proactive replacement at 30,000 km is considered unnecessary if the engine runs smoothly11121314.

Non-iridium budget alternatives also reported reliable. Beyond the iridium options covered on the Spark plugs — Torch, Miles and Ford cross-refs card, owners also report success with plain NGC-brand plugs (no unusual symptoms reported) and with generic Russian-made domestic plugs — one owner ran domestic plugs to 50,000 km without needing replacement. Overall community sentiment: this engine is not particularly picky about spark-plug brand compared to some other platforms1516171819202122232425.

Field report — NGK plugs and a fuel smell (inconclusive, installation-related?). One owner (Aziz Marashly) reported that installing NGK ILTR5A-13G plugs caused a fuel smell from the engine and possible over-fueling, possibly related to improper thread fit or an installation error rather than the plug itself. The owner returned to factory Torch plugs, citing a thermal-range mismatch as the suspected cause. Not conclusively determined whether this was an NGK fitment issue specific to this plug or an installation error — worth a mechanical inspection if similar symptoms occur after an NGK swap26.

Field debate — IXEH22TT, Torch, and Denso all reported working, with a personal-experience split. One owner asked whether IXEH22TT plugs would fit; a Mazda-mechanic acquaintance recommended them as "top" quality. Another member pushed back in favor of Torch, citing two separate bad personal experiences with Denso plugs and having since standardized on NGK, then switching to Torch — while acknowledging "to each their own." A third owner confirmed running Torch at a 1.3mm gap with good results, and pointed to the OEM plug's "-11" suffix digits as the reference marking to match when buying27282930313233. This is a personal-preference/anecdote thread, not a resolved recommendation — it sits alongside, and does not override, the Torch QH6RTIP-13/QH6RIU-11 OEM-spec guidance documented on the Spark plugs — factory spec and gap disputes card.

DENSO ITV16TT — positive report. One owner installed DENSO ITV16TT (listing: "DENSO ITV16TT 4718 IRIDIUM" 4-plug set) and reports everything running well afterward3435.

ITV16TT (heat range 5) vs. ITV20TT (heat range 6) — reported fuel-economy and shift-smoothness gain. Denso ITV16TT (calorific number 5) and ITV20TT (calorific number 6) are both cited as compatible; heat range 5 suits city driving, heat range 6 suits sustained high-RPM/highway use. One owner reports that after switching, the car "came alive" — fuel consumption dropped from 13 L/100km to 10.5 L/100km at highway speeds (~150 km/h), and the transmission became noticeably smoother on every gear3637. A separate anecdote (different vehicle, same plug family debate) recounts a prior car where Denso plugs caused excessive fuel consumption in the city, resolved by switching to NGK38 — offered as a data point that plug-brand results can vary by vehicle/engine rather than a direct X80 conflict.

Standard (non-iridium) plugs as a cost-effective baseline — Denso vs. iridium tradeoff. A separate, earlier report frames the choice more simply as standard vs. iridium: Denso standard (non-iridium) plugs are confirmed working and recommended as a cost-effective baseline. One owner switched from unknown/cheap plugs at 59,000 km to Denso standard after experiencing a cylinder-4 misfire. The stated tradeoff: iridium plugs (TORCH QH6RIU-11 OEM-type or similar) last longer but cost 2-3x more; standard plugs need more frequent replacement but are much cheaper — for typical driving, the benefit of iridium over quality standard plugs is described as marginal394041.

DENSO TV16TT — an additional recommended cross-brand option. DENSO TV16TT spark plugs are recommended as a reliable option for X80 owners, expanding the cross-brand list beyond the Torch lines (see the Spark plugs — Torch, Miles and Ford cross-refs card) and the standard Denso plugs covered on this card. One owner (Эдуард Янонис) confirmed using this plug for a second time with normal operation, suggesting repeat satisfaction rather than a one-off trial. Suitable for the X80 2.0L engine42.

docs.title: Spark plugs — options, prices, reliability
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plugs · #torch · #part-number · #oem

Overview of spark plugs for the FAW Besturn X80 (engine CA4GD1): the factory plug, aftermarket options, prices, service life, counterfeits and fitting. The factory plug is Torch QH6RTIP-13 (OEM number 370701037K). Detailed topics have their own cards:

  • Spark plugs — factory spec and gap disputes — gap-code convention and heat-rating direction, and the unresolved gap figures (0.6, 0.7-0.8, 0.9, 1.0-1.3 mm and 1.1 mm depending on the source)
  • Spark plugs — Torch, Miles and Ford cross-refs — Torch QH5RIU-13 / QH6RIU-11, Miles ALSP067, Ford cross-reference numbers, RU-market prices and where they were bought
  • Spark plugs — NGK, Denso and budget options — NGK, Denso (TV16TT, ITV16TT/ITV20TT), IXEH22TT, domestic and standard non-iridium plugs, with owner verdicts
  • Spark plugs — lifespan and wear symptoms — claimed versus real service life, and symptoms linked to worn or fouled plugs (jerks, fuel consumption, power changes)
  • Spark plugs — counterfeits and authenticity — counterfeit failure cases, how to tell a genuine Torch (brazed joint, RTIP vs RIU) and NGK 3811 fakes
  • Spark plugs — installation, torque and tools — torque limit (18 kgf), socket sizes, thread size, and hard-to-remove factory plugs
  • OEM spark plug specifications
  • Torch spark plugs — codes, listings, gap rules

Factory spec (Torch QH6RTIP-13). Factory-installed plugs are Torch QH6RTIP-13: iridium, 1.3mm gap, pointed electrode. Approved alternatives: QH5RIU-13 (heat/caloric number 5, 1.3mm gap) or QH6RIU-11 (caloric number 6, 1.1mm gap). Critical fitment note: FAW plugs seat on a conical (tapered) seat WITHOUT a sealing washer — any plug fitted with a washer ring will not seat correctly. Factory plugs are reported to last roughly 60,000 km; iridium upgrades roughly 100,000 km. The pointed electrode design is said to improve ignition by concentrating the spark on a smaller area. One caveat noted: pre-2019 factory plugs may have shipped with rounded (not pointed) electrodes; all recent stock is iridium with the pointed design123456789101112131415. Conflict: some owners report receiving non-iridium plugs from the factory; community consensus nonetheless is that modern X80s ship with the iridium Torch QH6RTIP-13.

OEM part number confirmed — 370701037K (Torch). The factory-installed spark plug is confirmed as Torch brand, part number 370701037K. FAW sources these Torch plugs from original supply, but the exact OEM-numbered plug is hard to find at retail — buying by part number carries an estimated 90% chance of receiving a Chinese counterfeit. Genuine Torch plugs have a visible brazed joint at the electrode; counterfeits typically lack this construction detail, which is a practical way to spot fakes1617181920212223242526.

Where the community disagrees

  • Some owners in a later batch report receiving non-iridium spark plugs directly from the factory, contradicting the general claim that all X80s ship with iridium Torch QH6RTIP-13 plugs. Community consensus still favors the iridium-factory-fill claim, but the discrepancy is not resolved.

docs.title: Spark plugs — Torch, Miles and Ford cross-refs
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plugs · #torch · #price · #cross-reference

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Part of the spark-plug series — overview: Spark plugs — options, prices, reliability. See also OEM spark plug specifications and Torch spark plugs — codes, listings, gap rules.

Cross-brand / interchangeable options. - TORCH QH5RIU-13 and QH6RIU-11 are reported interchangeable with OEM; QH6RIU-11 has a lower heat rating than QH5RIU-13123. - Iridium options reported compatible: TORCH QH6RTIP-13, TR6B-13, ILTR6A-13G, PLTR6A-10G, LTR6AI13; one owner also cross-referenced a Ford part number 1202935 as an equivalent, sourced via AliExpress with reportedly good quality matching OEM spec4. - AMD AMD.PL116 also mentioned as a compatible option56.

Prices (RU market, OZON, 4-plug sets unless noted): - TORCH QH5RIU-13: 1,496 RUB on sale (regular price 3,671 RUB, 59% discount), as of 2024-11-057. - TORCH QH6RIU-11: comparable price to the above, same listing period8. - TORCH QH6RTIP-13 iridium (2-8 pack): 1,444 RUB with a 36% discount, as of 2024-09-11, RU market, on AliExpress; reported fast delivery4. - Official dealership TORCH plugs: 950 RUB per plug in-store, or 800 RUB per plug if pre-ordered (November 2024, RU market)910.

TORCH QH6RIU-11 — Ford cross-references. TORCH QH6RIU-11 iridium plugs also serve as replacements for several Ford part numbers: 41-988, 12565996, 12622561, 41-109, 1787829, 4M5G12405AA, L3BD-18-110, and L3YD18110. Available on AliExpress for 1,343 RUB (RU market, Jan 2025) with a 30% discount. Users report reliable performance: 5,000+ km and 30+ days of continuous operation without issues11121314.

Additional verified options — Torch and AliExpress iridium double plugs. (1) Torch brand — standard choice, confirmed working by multiple owners. (2) AliExpress iridium "double" spark plugs (2,899 RUB, RU market, February 2025) — one user reported 15,000 km of operation with no issues after roughly one year of use. Both options are reported reliable151617181920.

Miles ALSP067 — restated with pricing and a plug-count caution. A separate discussion reconfirms Miles ALSP067 iridium plugs as a recommended replacement, priced around 3,104 RUB (with an Ozon card discount, RU market, 2025); one owner reported 5,000 km trouble-free running on this set. The source specifically warns against buying a 4-plug set (e.g. TORCH QH5RIU-M3, shown for comparison in the same listing) by mistake — double-check the plug count needed before ordering212223242526.

TORCH QH5RIU-13 restated with dimensions and long-term result. TORCH iridium plugs model QH5RIU-13 (analog to ILTR5A-13G) are confirmed compatible: M14x1.25 thread, 25mm reach. Rated good quality by the community and available on Ozon272829. A separate long-term report: changed at 80,000 km, still performing well at 130,000 km (the original factory plugs had lasted to 80,000 km). Warning: many iridium plugs on the market are counterfeit even at low prices — verify quality before buying; over-tightening during installation can damage the plugs and the spark-plug wells3031323334.

QH5RIU-13 as a direct swap for stock QH6RIU-11 — same 1.1mm gap. Restating and refining the OEM/alternative pairing described on the Spark plugs — factory spec and gap disputes card: original spark plugs are QH6RIU-11 (conical seat). The community-recommended swap is TORCH QH5RIU-13, which keeps the same 1.1mm gap. The iridium version is available from Ozon for roughly 5,000+ RUB. Replacement takes about 15 minutes with a 16mm plug socket and an 8mm socket for the coil-pack bolts (consistent with the socket sizes on the Spark plugs — installation, torque and tools card)353637383940.

Torch QH6RIU-11 — pricing and availability restated. Torch QH6RIU-11 is confirmed as suitable, still with the same "-11" gap-code marking seen on old/original plugs. Ozon listing price around 1,000 RUB per plug (RU market, April 2026) individually, with only single-plug (not 4-pack) listings available on Ozon/Wildberries at the time; buyers were waiting for a set listing rather than buying 4 singles4142434445.

Torch QH6RIU-11 iridium +U, ordered via Emex — smoother/quieter after install. A Torch QH6RIU-11 iridium set (U-shaped side electrode, "+U" iridium type) was ordered through Emex Marketplace; Kitzap-stock alternatives were rejected as not matching the correct spec. Confirmed fitment for the X80, sold as a 4-piece set. After installing in May 2026, the reporting owner described the engine as running quieter, smoother, and with reduced knocking46474849.

TORCH QH5RIU-13 — cross-vehicle listing and confirmed fitment. A specific Ozon/marketplace listing for TORCH QH5RIU-13 iridium plugs (analog ILTR5A-13G, 25mm reach) markets them as fitting Ford, Chevrolet, Mazda, Opel, Volvo, and Suzuki models (Focus, C-Max, Fiesta, Fusion, Mondeo, Galaxy, Captiva, Vectra, Zafira, Astra, Grand Vitara, Escudo, Tribute, CX-9, S40) in addition to the X80. Multiple owners in the group confirmed having installed this exact plug with good results, including one who installed it "just recently" and reports it working perfectly50515253545556. When asked what differentiates plug variants, the answer given was: heat rating (calorific number) and electrode gap57.

TORCH QH6RIU-11 — an early, independent recommendation with 30,000+ km reports. An earlier, independent thread recommends TORCH QH6RIU-11 iridium plugs specifically, giving heat rating 6 and gap 1.1mm, describing them as superior to standard plugs and better than the cross-fit alternative QH5RTIP-13. Multiple users in this earlier thread report 30,000+ km of trouble-free service — consistent with, though earlier than, the later lifespan-variance discussion covered on the Spark plugs — lifespan and wear symptoms card5859606162.

TORCH QH6RIU-11 iridium — 4-pack purchase confirmed, with product photo. A separate owner (Che Guevara) confirmed purchasing and installing TORCH QH6RIU-11 iridium spark plugs sold as a 4-piece pack, reinforcing the reliability track record already documented for this part number on this card63.

docs.title: Speed-limiter buzzer setting
docs.text: Not a firmware speed limiter. The buzzing alert that triggers starting around 130 km/h or higher is not an engine/firmware speed limitation — the car is not actually being held back. It is a user-configurable dashboard reminder, set via the steering-wheel menu settings. It can be disabled entirely or set to a different threshold; it is not necessarily pre-set to any particular value by default123456.

docs.title: Speedometer accuracy and MT gear ratios
docs.text:
Tags: #speedometer · #mkpp

Speedometer scale and top speed by engine/transmission. The speedometer face is marked up to 240 km/h. Actual top-speed performance differs by engine and transmission: the naturally-aspirated CA4GD1 reaches 185 km/h with the manual transmission and 180 km/h with the automatic; the turbocharged CA4GC18T reaches 198 km/h. Across the range, the speedometer reads consistently 5-7% higher than actual road speed123456.

Manual transmission (MКПП) gear ratio performance. Reported speed-at-RPM figures for the manual gearbox: 2nd gear — 75 km/h at 5000 RPM (satellite/GPS-verified), 90 km/h at 6000 RPM. 3rd gear — approximately 115 km/h at 5000 RPM (calculated) and ~138 km/h at 6000 RPM. The car has an electronic rev limiter to prevent over-revving; redline is near 6500 RPM, at which point the ECU cuts throttle to protect the drivetrain78910.

docs.title: Start/Stop button modes and startup sequence
docs.text:
Tags: #ignition

Three modes. The X80's start/stop button cycles through three operating modes: OFF, ACC (Accessory), and ON. If the button defaults to the wrong mode, the engine may fail to start1.

Reliable startup without the brake pedal. To start the engine reliably without pressing the brake, press the button in sequence: first press (OFF), second press (ACC), third press (ON) — the engine then starts. This procedure is documented in the service manual and resolves no-start issues caused by the button defaulting to the wrong mode1.

docs.title: Thermostat — part number and replacement cost
docs.text:
Tags: #thermostat · #part-number · #ford-compat · #cooling

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Ford cross-compatible thermostat. Mazda/Ford thermostat part number 1505640 is confirmed as a direct drop-in replacement for the FAW Besturn X80. The FAW OEM part number is 1306010-37K12. The Ford alternative is often more readily available and cheaper than waiting for a FAW part shipped from Moscow345.

Opening temperature spec. The FAW X80 thermostat opens fully at 105°C. If the thermostat is stuck closed, the coolant pipes/hose from the thermostat will remain noticeably cold even once the engine reaches normal operating temperature — a useful diagnostic sign67.

Replacement procedure and labor cost breakdown. Thermostat replacement typically requires removing the intake manifold. Official FAW dealer cost (RU market, May 2024): 10,501-12,441 RUB, depending on whether fresh coolant is also needed (~900 RUB for 5L). Independent-shop path: thermostat part (~2,000 RUB) + coolant (~900 RUB) + independent labor (4,500 RUB) ≈ 7,400 RUB total (RU market, May 2024). Important: intake-manifold gaskets should be replaced whenever the manifold is removed for this job — many shops skip this, leading to future leaks. Improper reassembly can cause misfires afterward8910111213141516.

Reading the number on the old unit. An owner asking for the thermostat part number reads the marking on the old unit as "130, 60, 10, 30 MK" and wants to confirm it against the part; the answer 1306010-37K was given without a fitment check12.

docs.title: Throttle body adaptation after battery disconnect
docs.text:
Tags: #throttle-body · #battery · #ecu

When it's needed. After disconnecting and reconnecting the car battery (e.g. for other electrical work), the throttle body/ECU may need to re-adapt/re-learn its baseline before the car runs smoothly again.12

Shortened adaptation procedure (community-reported, not the full factory procedure). Rather than performing a full dealer-level throttle adaptation, one owner reported success with a shortened version: (1) reconnect the battery negative terminal; (2) turn the ignition on and wait approximately 60 seconds; (3) turn the ignition off; (4) leave the car completely unpowered/at rest for about 5 minutes. During this rest period, the ECU reportedly self-calibrates without needing the full formal adaptation sequence.12

Caution during the rest period. Do not leave the key in the ignition during the 5-minute rest — the procedure depends on the car being fully unpowered/undisturbed during that window.12

Result reported. Following this procedure, the car started well; the reporting owner had not yet done a longer test drive to confirm full smoothness under load, so treat this as a promising but not exhaustively validated shortcut (confidence: medium).12

docs.title: Throttle body cleaning and fuel system flush
docs.text:
Tags: #throttle-body · #cleaning · #price · #dealer

Throttle body cleaning without removal. Use a fuel-injector-type cleaner (Liqui Moly, Lavr, or Wynn's) applied via spray. The engine may stall briefly during cleaning — this is normal. This method is less thorough than removal but works for routine maintenance.12345678

Throttle body cleaning with removal. More effective, since it allows access to all sides of the throttle body. A professional-shop method: disconnect the fuel line, connect an external container with a carefully-proportioned fuel-additive cleaning mixture (do not over-dilute), and run the engine at an elevated idle (>2,000 rpm) for approximately 45 minutes, with the idle RPM floating during the process — this fluctuation is normal, not a fault.12345678

DIY alternative — fuel injector removal and individual cleaning. Remove the fuel injectors (adds labor cost/time) and clean each individually in a separate container with cleaner solution. The throttle body should be checked at every regular service as preventive maintenance.12345678

Hesitation may not be a throttle problem — check fuel pressure. Acceleration hesitation and slow power buildup at low speeds can indicate a fuel pressure regulator issue rather than a dirty throttle body alone. Symptom pattern: pressing the accelerator produces a weak initial response, then power builds only after a downshift or a delay. Cleaning the throttle body alone may not fully resolve the symptom if fuel pressure is genuinely inadequate — fuel pressure at idle should be checked directly, since insufficient pressure limits injection and power delivery regardless of throttle body condition.91011121314

DIY fuel-system pressure flush using a bottle adapter. A community-shared DIY method for fuel system cleaning: take an empty bottle (e.g. a cola bottle) and drill two holes — one for a tire valve-stem fitting, another in the cap. Connect air lines from the bottle to the fuel rail inlet, build pressure to 3.5 atmospheres, then start and rev the engine per the cleaning product's instructions while maintaining that pressure. Caution: different cleaning fluids have different follow-up maintenance requirements — some products call for an oil change and/or spark plug replacement afterward, so check the product instructions before use.15

Official-dealer labor-hour dispute over throttle body cleaning (2024-08 report; see also the dealer-service-pricing card for the broader overselling pattern). One owner reported an official FAW service center charged 2.5 extra labor hours for a routine ТО that included throttle-body cleaning alongside oil + filter, air filter, cabin filter, and serpentine-belt replacement. When queried, the service manager claimed factory labor standards required the longer time — but a subsequent inquiry directly with FAW's factory support indicated the manager should have reduced, not increased, the billed hours. Practical takeaway: verify quoted labor hours for throttle-body service against official FAW time allocations before accepting a dealer invoice, and consider photographing the throttle body's actual condition beforehand as documentation.1617

docs.title: Throttle body — part number and gasket/seal sourcing
docs.text:
Tags: #throttle-body · #part-number

OEM part number. OEM throttle body assembly (дроссельная заслонка в сборе) part number: 3603010-37K12.

Gasket/seal sourcing — no off-the-shelf option, two workarounds. No off-the-shelf throttle-body gasket is readily available. Community workarounds: (1) cut a custom gasket from sheet rubber material of the appropriate thickness — one technician does this routinely rather than waiting for an import; (2) order the assembly from China, with a longer lead time. The throttle body uses either a rubber O-ring or a sheet gasket, but exact part availability remains unclear345678910. Conflict: it's unclear whether the correct seal type is a rubber O-ring or a cut sheet gasket, and OEM sourcing for it specifically is unresolved.

Where the community disagrees

  • Unclear whether the correct throttle-body seal type is a rubber O-ring or a cut sheet gasket; exact OEM part availability for it was not resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: Throttle valve relearning procedure
docs.text:
Tags: #throttle-body

After cleaning or replacing the throttle valve, the ECU needs to relearn its position/idle adaptation, or the car may run rough, hunt for idle, or over-consume fuel. Two independent community reports converge on essentially the same manual procedure, given here as steps with timing specifications:

  1. Disconnect the negative battery terminal and leave it off for 15-20 minutes.
  2. Warm the engine to normal operating temperature (~90°C), then shut it off and remove the key.
  3. Turn the key/start button to the ON position (not START) and hold for 60 seconds — the throttle body is audibly clicking during this step as it self-calibrates.
  4. Turn off, wait 20 seconds, then remove the key again.
  5. Reinsert the key/press start, this time actually starting the engine, with all accessories off (lights, stereo, etc.).
  6. Let the engine idle undisturbed for 15 minutes. Target idle during this phase is reported as roughly 0.8 (x1000) RPM on a diagnostic scanner readout.

One report frames this as resolving a specific fuel-consumption regression: consumption dropped from 1.5-1.6 L/100 (elevated, post-cleaning) back down to 0.8-0.9 L/100 after completing the procedure, alongside restored normal operation12.

A second, independent report of the same procedure adds a couple of details: the key/ignition switch (or a start-button vehicle's equivalent) has an intermediate position equivalent to "ON" that must be used in steps 3 and 5; and a voice message from the reporting owner walks through the same wait times (15-20 min disconnect, 60 sec ON, 20 sec off) and the ~0.8 RPM idle target, confirming this as the community-validated method rather than a one-off account3456.

Conflict — is any relearning needed at all? Multiple forum posts and AI-generated summaries circulating in the community claim no adaptation procedure is needed after throttle-body service, and some point to generic Yandex-sourced instructions that differ from the above. The step-by-step procedure documented here is treated as the more credible, field-verified method (backed by a detailed voice-message walkthrough and a second independent confirmation), while the "no adaptation needed" claims are noted as circulating but unverified.

Idle fluctuation fixed by cleaning the throttle valve (DAD sensor). A separate, later report addresses idle speed fluctuation (hovering/unstable RPM at rest, with A/C off) rather than a fuel-consumption regression: the fix is to clean the throttle valve, referred to in this thread as the DAD sensor — community members here describe it as located on the center of the exhaust manifold, accessible by touch, and removable with a T25 Torx wrench. Conflict/location discrepancy: this exhaust-manifold-center location differs from the intake-manifold location already documented for the MAP/DAD sensor on the dedicated MAP-sensor card — not resolved here, and may reflect the community conflating the throttle body with the nearby MAP sensor, consistent with the "sometimes called MAF/MAP interchangeably" confusion already noted on that card. As a secondary check, A/C is confirmed to normally raise idle by roughly 100-150 RPM, and new spark plugs should also be checked as a contributing factor to rough idle. A Drive2.ru guide is referenced as documenting the MAP/DAD sensor replacement procedure in more detail789101112131415.

Cleaning schedule — around 170,000 km. A separate report gives a mileage benchmark for when the throttle valve needs cleaning in the first place, rather than relearning after the fact: at around 170,000 km, the throttle valve (throttle body) becomes heavily soiled and may need cleaning — this was discovered incidentally during unrelated intake-manifold/thermostat work, and a dedicated throttle-body cleaner spray was used. Cleaning can improve idle quality and fuel economy, provided the ECU is allowed to relearn (adapt) idle values afterward, consistent with the relearning procedure documented above16.

Where the community disagrees

  • Some forum posts / AI summaries claim no throttle relearning is needed at all after cleaning or replacement, and cite generic Yandex-sourced instructions that differ from the field-tested procedure documented above; the community's own voice-message walkthrough and a second independent confirmation are treated as more credible than the unverified "not needed" claims.
  • One report locates the "DAD sensor" (used here as shorthand for the throttle valve/area) at the center of the exhaust manifold, T25-Torx accessible; the dedicated MAP-sensor card documents the MAP/DAD sensor as located in/near the intake manifold. Not resolved here — may reflect community conflation of the throttle body with the physically nearby MAP sensor.

docs.title: Timing chain — service schedule debate
docs.text:
Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

No timing belt — it's a chain. The FAW X80 does not have a timing belt; what some call "ГРМ" here is the timing chain, along with its gears, tensioners, etc. There is a separate accessory/serpentine belt on the engine, but that's unrelated to the timing chain and is serviced based on visible wear, not a fixed interval12.

Manufacturer service schedule vs. dealer upsell. According to the maintenance schedule, the timing chain is nominally due for inspection/replacement at 50,000 km and 100,000 km3456. One dealer reportedly told an owner at ~85,000 km that the chain needed replacing at 90,000 km, quoting about 30,000 RUB (RU market, October 2024)7. Community pushback: at 90,000 km it's still "a bit early" for the chain to actually need replacement — it should start rattling audibly if genuinely worn, which is uncommon this early — and the dealer's push is seen as following the written schedule mechanically to upsell a service, rather than a response to an actual symptom16. General repair cost estimate if genuinely needed: roughly 40,000-50,000 RUB (RU market, October 2024), depending on where the work is done1.

"Don't fix what isn't broken" counterpoint. Owners recommend not replacing the timing chain preemptively — only when it audibly starts to rattle. One long-time member (Oleg) reports his own X80 has reached 240,000 km with no chain noise and no chain service ever performed48. Advice given to the asking owner: if within budget, replacing proactively with a genuine/original part isn't wrong, but if there's no rattle, it can reasonably wait62.

Timing sprocket cross-manufacturer compatibility. The X80's Duratec HE engine uses timing components compatible with Ford and Mazda equivalents. Reported compatible part numbers: Ford 2029145 and Mazda LF94-12-4X0A, both 38-tooth sprockets. Tooth count should be verified when sourcing a replacement, since timing-chain pitch may differ between otherwise similar-looking sprockets; source from Ford or Mazda OEM catalogs9101112.

Replacement kit part number and price. OEM FAW timing-chain replacement kit 1026040-37KIT13 is available from Autopiter as an 11-piece complete kit (chain, tensioners, and guides), priced around 5,000 RUB (RU market, July 2025). The chain should be replaced as a complete assembly, not on its own — a Mazda-specific kit such as Masuma MGR-4001 is not suitable for the X80141516.

Two timing chains — intake and exhaust, replacement scope if one slips. The engine actually has two timing chains (intake and exhaust), not one. A diesel-like knocking sound can indicate a chain problem. If a chain slips, the repair scope is large: both chains, the tensioner, multiple sprockets/stars, and the water pump typically all need replacement together — this is not a simple job and needs proper diagnosis first. Cross-check parts against Mazda 6 GG specs, since the engine is derived from that platform1718192021.

GRM timing chain kit — pricing and alternatives. The original FAW X80 GRM timing chain kit costs roughly 14,500 RUB (RU market, Oct 2025). Mazda alternatives cost around 13,900-14,380 RUB (RU market, October 2025), also available via Chinese auto-parts sites (kitzapchasti, ~14,380 RUB). Community consensus: prefer the original kit if the price difference is small (under ~500 RUB, RU market, October 2025)22232425262728.

Chain durability estimate — restated with tensioner-limit context. The timing chain is expected to last from 200,000 km to effectively indefinitely. Unlike belts, chains stretch over time, which is why a tensioner is required. Around 200,000 km the tensioner's adjustment range should be monitored, but the chain itself should still be functional at that point — replacement becomes necessary only once the tensioner reaches its mechanical limit293031.

Dual timing chains restated — replaced as a set, not at the standard 60,000 km service. Restating the dual-chain design already on this card: the 2.0L engine uses two timing chains with their own sprockets and tensioners, not a belt. All of these components (chains, sprockets, tensioners) are replaced together as a set, never individually. At the standard 60,000 km service interval, these are not typically changed — replacement only becomes relevant at a much higher mileage threshold, consistent with the "don't fix what isn't broken" guidance and the 200,000+ km durability estimate already documented on this card323334.

Chain durability — real-world experience up to 330,000 km, no failure reports. Additional reinforcement of the durability estimate already made on this card: the timing chain is rated for roughly 100,000-200,000 km of nominal service life. At 100,000 km, replacement is typically not needed. Around 200,000 km, the chain enters a "risk zone" for stretch/wear. Real-world durability in practice extends beyond 300,000 km — one owner reported the chain still functioning normally at 330,000 km (observed/tested over 61,000 of those km). As of May 2026, there were no community reports of timing-chain failure3536373839.

Earlier, independent mileage anecdotes — 223,000 km with no issues, wear starting past 200,000 km. An earlier, independent set of reports adds concrete mileage anecdotes consistent with the durability picture already documented on this card: one owner reported 223,000 km on the original timing chain with no rattling or wear issues. Another owner, at 86,000 km, was considering early replacement (out of caution rather than a symptom). A third owner, past 200,000 km, noted timing-chain wear beginning to appear. Overall, chain life on this engine appears to extend well beyond 200,000 km when properly maintained, consistent with the durability estimates elsewhere on this card40414243.

Timing chain (not a belt) confirmed for the 2018 restyled model — from the second Telegram group. A separate community (FAW BESTURN X80 group) confirms the "no timing belt — it's a chain" fact already established on this card, specifically for a 2018-model, restyled (facelift) X80: asked whether the restyled 2018 X80 has a belt or a chain — a question the owner notes gets conflicting answers online — a group member replies simply "chain!"4445.

Dealer work order for a timing chain (ГРМ) replacement (order dated 13 June 2026; posted Oct 2026). The photographed order, "replacement of the timing chain kit", shows labour at 30,870 RUB in total (RU market, dealer, June 2026), with an oil and filter change. Materials on the same order: four intake-manifold gaskets at about 400 RUB each, a valve cover gasket at about 1,000 RUB, a timing chain kit at about 39,200 RUB (listed price; column alignment is hard to read and the figure may be before discount), and four units of Lukoil Genesis Special Advanced 5W-40 at about 1,500 RUB each (all RU market, dealer, June 2026) 46. A commenter adds that the valve cover gasket can also be changed during this job 47.

Repair cost estimate and a high-mileage report. An owner estimated a chain repair at about 60,000 RUB (RU market, September 2024) and no longer trusts service shops to do it correctly1348. Another owner has about 230,000 km, no chain rattle, and says he will deal with problems as they arise rather than change the chain pre-emptively4950.

docs.title: Torch spark plugs — codes, listings, gap rules
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plug · #torch · #price · #conflict · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Companion to spark plugs — options, prices, reliability and OEM spark plug specifications: how to read Torch plug codes, which listings were shared, and the conflicting gap rules.

Reading Torch codes. A Torch chart decodes the electrode letters: A is a 5 mm ignition position, T is 3 mm, I is an iridium centre electrode, II is double iridium, IU is iridium centre with a U-grooved ground electrode, IP is iridium and platinum, P is a platinum centre, PP is double platinum, J is three ground electrodes, Q is four ground electrodes, IQ is an iridium centre with four ground electrodes and Y is a surface-discharge type. The poster highlighted IP and the I-to-IU group12. Searching by code can fail: the Latin Q is easily typed as G or as the Cyrillic K, which returns KH- or GH-coded listings (a search for GH5RIU13 found nothing, and an Ozon search for QH5RIU11 showed KH5RIU11 items). Members say QH5TIP and QH5RIU11 are not real Torch codes; the direct replacements they cite are QH6RIU-11 and QH5RIU-133456.

Factory plug. A photo of a FAW-branded plug box (part number 3707010-37K, dated 2018-09-06, Changchun) shows a plug marked QH6RTIP. The Torch catalog lists QH6RTIP as the FAW fit: M14x1.25 thread, 25 mm reach, 16 mm hex, 1.1 mm gap, iridium with a platinum electrode; cross-references NGK ILTR6A13G, NGK PLTR6A10G, Denso ITV20 and several Mazda codes7289. The QH6RTIP-13 four-pack was cross-listed on Yandex Market (January 2025) against Ford 1M5O-12405-CA, AYFS-092FE-C and Motorcraft AYFS22FE1J10.

Gap: three positions. The manual's ignition-system table (screenshot) gives CA4GD1: QH6RTIP, gap 0.7-0.8 mm; CA4GC18T: ILTR6J8, gap 0.8 mm, and says not to adjust the gap of iridium plugs. A member quotes a different rule, that iridium plugs may be set anywhere in 0.6-1.1 mm. Owners report in practice: NGK plugs run about 80,000 km at the factory 1.2 mm gap without adjusting, and another owner advises Denso or Torch plugs at 1.3 mm because the engine adapts. The asker, on the atmospheric CA4GD1, ran an NGK ILTR5A-13G (heat range 5) while the manual specifies heat range 6, and asked whether 0.7-0.8 mm is needed1112131415.

Alternatives and listings. - TORCH QH6RIU-11 on AliExpress, sold in lots of 2 to 8: ~1,867 RUB (RU market, November 2024, after a 40% discount); named replacement for NGK LTR6IX-11 (also written LTR6IX11, SILTR6A7G, ILTR6B11, ILTR6E11, ILTR6J11) and GM 12622561 and 1256599616. - TORCH QH6RTIP-13, 4 pcs: 2,003 RUB (RU market, January 2025), page marked out of stock; a member relayed an unconfirmed Telegram rumour that plug prices may rise or counterfeits may appear17. A member put a set of iridium plugs at about 2,000 RUB (RU market, April 2025), other variants higher7. - TORCH QH5RIU-13 (4 pcs, M14x1.25, analogue of NGK ILTR5A-13G) on Ozon, October 2025. One owner fitted a 4-pack without adjusting the gap and it runs fine; the Torch plugs were his fallback when the QH6RTIP was out of stock. Another owner replaced QH6 platinum plugs with QH5, and one had run NGK for 80,000 km before1819202122. QH5RIU13 was also posted at a Crimea parts shop without price or fitment note23. - A Wildberries listing titled as a Torch plug for the X80 (product 140394281) was shared in February 2025 without price or code; check its cross-reference codes before buying24. - Miles ALSP067: recommended by one member after 5,000 km without complaints and at a low price; a commenter warns that heat range (калильное число) and other specs matter, since cheap plugs can cost fuel economy or damage pistons and valves, and the member replies that he chose by specs and that the seller's own listed plug has the wrong heat range252627. - Price context: a plug cost about 800 RUB at a parts shop (RU market, September 2024) and dealers charge 100-200 RUB more; one order took two weeks28.

docs.title: Torx fasteners on the X80
docs.text:
Tags: #tools

Torx is uncommon on the X80. Unlike European cars (Renault, VW), which use Torx (star-pattern) fasteners extensively, the FAW X80 predominantly uses hex, square, and standard nut fasteners. Torx tools are reported as generally not essential for routine X80 maintenance12345678.

Three confirmed Torx locations. 1. Stabilizer bar mounting studs — internal T25 Torx, used specifically to prevent the pin from rotating during installation. 2. MAP (manifold absolute pressure) sensor in the intake manifold — T25 fastener. 3. Camshaft pulleys — T50 fasteners12345678.

docs.title: Transmission breather vent
docs.text:
Tags: #water-ingress

The transmission has a breather/vent (sapun, "дыхательный клапан" in Russian) whose job is to stop water getting into the transmission when driving through water crossings 1. It sits near the transmission and is marked with a yellow cap 1. Keep the vent mounted on its valve stem — removing it carelessly can damage it 23. It matters most off-road / in mud, but owners note it is important even in normal operation any time the car is near standing water 45.

Loose hose under the battery tray. A loose hose found under the battery tray was identified as the gearbox breather (сапун КПП). Members say it should hang from the battery mounting bracket bolt rather than lie under the tray678.

docs.title: Transmission drain plug leak repair
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission · #drain-plug · #water-ingress

If the transmission drain plug leaks after an oil change, the likely cause is that the plug's cone thread has been stripped (over-torqued or cross-threaded).1234567

Temporary/semi-permanent fix: apply blue anaerobic thread sealant (Сантехмастер brand or equivalent) to the threads; cure time is 10–15 minutes. Proper repair requires professional re-threading of the pan/housing or replacing the drain bolt at a service shop.1234567

The transmission drain plug has a gasket/washer that should be replaced at every oil change. Custom washers sized ø20mm × h4mm work as low-cost alternatives across various car brands, not just the FAW-specific part.1234567

docs.title: Transmission parts — VAG/Lada compat
docs.text:
Tags: #gasket · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The FAW X80's transmission gasket can be substituted with a VAG (Volkswagen) specification gasket, designed for the VAG/Aisin 4G transmission family 1. One owner reports the VAG gasket lasted 40,000+ km without leakage, through two filter/fluid drain service intervals 2.

Inner CV boot — Lada 9-series cross-fit: the inner CV boot (пыльник внутренней гранаты — the protective bellows on the inner constant-velocity joint) from the Lada 9-series fits the X80 as a direct replacement. The OEM X80 part costs 3,000 RUB (RU market, January 2026); the Lada 9-series alternative is cheaper and confirmed compatible 34.

docs.title: D vs. S fuel consumption data
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission · #fuel-consumption

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

This card gathers specific numeric owner-reported fuel-consumption comparisons between D and S modes (complementing the general D-vs-S characteristics already covered in the drive-modes card).

Refueling frequency in S mode. One owner asked whether S mode burns significantly more fuel; another confirmed yes — "higher RPM, more consumption"12. Doing the math out loud, one owner estimated that habitual S-mode driving would mean refueling roughly 3 times a month, versus about 2 times a month they were currently doing; a heavy S-mode user in the thread said they refuel every 2-3 days, typically putting in around 2,000 (RUB worth of fuel) per stop, and reported burning through roughly 20 (currency/liters, ambiguous in source) per day on some days3456. That heavy user clarified they mostly drive in D and only switch to S when anticipating an overtaking opportunity7.

Mode-switching while moving. In the same thread, a member asked whether transmission mode can only be switched at a complete stop (e.g. at a red light); another confirmed switching is possible on the move, specifically between S and D8910.

Direct D vs. S consumption test (MKAD highway, Oct. 2024). One owner ran a like-for-like comparison on the MKAD ring road — same wheels, same 92-octane fuel, same approximate route — specifically to compare which mode used more or less fuel, not to establish an absolute "ideal" figure1112. Results: D mode: 10.4 L/100km; S (Sport) mode: 9.7 L/100km; for reference, driving on the manual transmission variant came in noticeably higher, around 12 L/100km, in the same owner's estimation11. The finding that S came out more economical on the highway is attributed to fewer gear shifts at speed13. This owner's overall takeaway: which mode to drive in depends on the driver's own read of the situation and experience — there's no single universally-better answer11.

City driving trade-off (same source). In city/traffic conditions, S is described as less comfortable than D: S holds longer gears, letting RPM climb as high as ~3,500 on a single gear, producing excess engine noise; S also shows noticeably stronger engine braking on throttle lift-off, which can feel like extra "kicks"/jerks when crawling in traffic in the 1,500-2,000 RPM range14.

Manual-transmission fuel consumption — 2018 facelift typical figures. A facelift manual-transmission car (80,000 km) reports typical consumption of 12.5 L/100km in mixed city/highway driving at a steady 3-3.5k RPM. Range observed: 9 L/100km on the highway, 13.5 L/100km in city driving. Winter consumption increases by 1-2 L/100km. Consumption is reported to improve with additional mileage1516171819202122.

docs.title: AKPP seal and pan-gasket leaks
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission · #oil-leak · #seal · #gasket

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Input seal installed backward. At a service shop, the transmission input seal was installed backward, causing about 1 liter of oil loss from the gearbox over 3 days1. The seal's metal retaining ring must face inward — the shop had to pull the seal and reinstall it correctly to stop the leak23. One commenter notes this happened at roughly 230,000+ km and considers occasional service-shop mistakes like this fairly common, which is part of why they prefer doing their own maintenance ("costly experience if you mess up, but a win if you don't")45.

Pan gasket quality matters. In a separate case, an owner replaced the AT pan gasket twice: the first time with a cheap gasket sourced from kitzap.ru, which subsequently leaked; a shop then sourced a genuine VAG (Volkswagen Group) 1:1 cross-fit gasket and topped up the fluid, which resolved the leak6. The owner also reports an intermittent, occasional shift hunting between 1st and 2nd gear (shifts back and forth) that persisted after the gasket fix; plan was to have the level checked/topped up at the next shop visit6. Recommendation: don't default to the cheapest aftermarket gasket — a VAG-equivalent gasket held where the cheap one failed78.

Pan gasket part number cross-referenced and verified. Part number 35168TFA050 is identified as the correct automatic transmission pan gasket for the FAW X80. This Audi-compatible part number has been cross-checked via Chinaspare.ru and by direct visual comparison with factory reference photos; multiple users confirm close visual similarity across these cross-reference parts and report correct fitment when ordering by this number910111213141516.

Drive-axle seal/bellows part number and normal weepage. The drive-axle seal/bellows on the automatic-transmission model has part number AT 90311-40A014, available from kitparts at roughly 770 RUB (RU market, Feb 2025). This is a common wear point; a small amount of leakage — roughly 150-170g over 2 months — is considered normal rather than a fault requiring immediate repair. Only the OEM seal should be used here: Mazda-sourced alternatives are reported not compatible despite the shared engine/transmission platform171819.

Input shaft spline rust — cause and remedy. The transmission's input-shaft splines are often found completely dry and rusty even with an adequate fluid level — this dryness itself is considered a normal design characteristic (the splines aren't meant to be fluid-bathed). However, rust on the splines specifically indicates water ingress, meaning the input seal should be replaced as a preventive measure once rust is observed, to stop further water intrusion. This is described as a normal-but-preventable condition rather than an emergency, provided the seal is addressed202122232425.

Manual transmission (MКПП) right-side oil seal — OEM vs. budget alternatives. OEM right-side manual-transmission oil seal part number: FAWF00327238C. A budget alternative, Corteco 19016578B, costs roughly 5x less than OEM. Aftermarket Mazda-branded seals reportedly failed after only a few months in some cases, whereas higher-quality branded seals stayed dry long-term — about three times better performance than the cheapest alternatives262728.

Manual transmission sump ventilation. The manual transmission has no pressurized sump like the automatic — pressure stays atmospheric. The transmission relies on a sump vent to prevent vacuum buildup; if the vent is blocked, oil can be forced out through the seals as pressure builds2930.

Left drive-shaft (МКПП) seal — routine weeping, and a hard replacement job. The left transmission drive-shaft seal routinely develops a slight weep/sweat. One owner reports the seal "weeping" (потный) again after just 8,000 km, similar to its condition when the car had 48,000 km. Replacement is labor-intensive: it requires removing the wheel, suspension arm, stabilizer-bar link, upper ball joint, and brake-hose clamps, then extracting the drive shaft through the strut. Replacement part: Corteco 19016578B (a SAT-brand equivalent is available for the right-side seal)31323334.

Right drive-shaft (МКПП) removal procedure — Mazda 6 GG reference. Removing the right transmission drive shaft requires disconnecting the strut fork, the stabilizer-bar link, the upper ball joint, and all hose clamps from the strut, then unbolting the hub and moving it aside — the procedure mirrors the Mazda 6 GG service manual. One owner summarized the complexity as roughly "4x the hassle" compared to their previous car3536.

МКПП input-shaft seal — part number. The manual-transmission (МКПП) input-shaft seal part number is F00327238C, available on Ozon. This applies to manual-transmission X80s only, not automatics373839.

Oil smell under hard acceleration — front transmission seal weeping (unresolved). Some owners report an oil smell (пахнет как пыльнули маслом) during hard acceleration (4500+ RPM), intensifying in rain. A possible root cause is the front transmission mainshaft seal (промвал справа) weeping/sweating, combined with a wet hose running under the intake manifold. The exact source requires further investigation but may indicate transmission-seal degradation4041.

Front drive-shaft seal — automatic transmission part number. Drive-shaft seal part number for the automatic-transmission X80: 90311-40A014, used in the front axle drive assembly4243.

AKPP sump-pan gasket — supply-quality variability under the same part number. Separately from the pan-gasket quality issue already documented on this card: AKPP sump-pan gaskets sourced from aftermarket suppliers ("gastronomi") show highly variable quality, and the same listed part number can ship a physically different gasket on different orders due to upstream supplier changes at the seller. Fitment and material quality can vary between otherwise identically-listed purchases. Recommendation: buy from an official FAW distributor to ensure consistency rather than relying on the part number alone. One source specifically names YulSane as a reliable official-distributor source for a good-quality gasket44454647.

AKPP seal part number — confirmed suppliers (earlier, independent report). An earlier, independent confirmation of the automatic-transmission (AKPP) seal part number already documented on this card, 90311-40A014, tested on a 2017 model year X80: it is available from multiple Russian suppliers — kitzapchasti.ru, kitparts.ru, kitzap.ru — with the same part cross-referencing consistently across all three sites4849.

Output-shaft seal weeping at 237,000 km — preventive replacement recommended. At roughly 237,000 km, one owner noticed the output-shaft seal (the long-side drive shaft, passenger-side seal — sometimes called the "long drive" or right-side seal) beginning to weep oil externally, a sign of impending seal failure. Recommendation: replace proactively before complete failure to avoid oil loss and potential further transmission damage. Genuine FAW seals are available; shop around by OEM part number on auto-parts sites (e.g. Kitparts, Ozon) — prices range 700-1,700 RUB (RU market, September 2024) depending on vendor5051.

docs.title: Valve clearance adjustment (Duratec HE) shims
docs.text:
Tags: #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Engine platform. The X80 uses the Duratec HE engine, the same platform as certain Ford/Mazda applications — shims and machining know-how cross over, and shops experienced with Ford/Mazda Duratec engines are a good source for this job.123456

Shim-under-bucket procedure. (1) Remove the cam cover. (2) Identify the shim cups ("стаканчики") under the rocker arms. (3) Measure clearances and select shims sized to target approximately 0.15mm. (4) Adjustment method: a machine shop or skilled mechanic can either precisely grind the cup seat faces, or swap in differently-sized shims. Shim cup surfaces can be modified with filing/grinding, but this requires precision and patience.123456

Shim sourcing. Ford/Mazda Duratec HE shims are compatible and available on Ozon. One community member (Eduard Yanonis) offers private consultation on the grinding procedure for owners who want guidance.7891011

Is it routine at moderate mileage? Valve clearance adjustment is not a routine service item on early/mid-mileage X80s — one owner reported no prior adjustment at 115,000 km. Valve seats do sink and settle over time, which is why periodic adjustment is eventually needed regardless of mileage-based service schedules. Many owners defer this service until higher mileage or until symptoms (noise, rough idle) appear.12131415

Cost — market quote vs. overselling concern (2025-01, Moscow-area invoice). One community-reported quote: 55,900 RUB labor + 36,750 RUB parts (total 92,650 RUB) (RU market, January 2025) for work claimed to include head removal, diagnostics (2,500 RUB), compression/hermetic tests, and a gasket kit (25,000 RUB), dated 2025-01-17. The community flagged this invoice as containing many unnecessary operations — head removal is not required for a valve-clearance adjustment alone, so this quote is considered a cautionary example of a shop overselling work.16171819

More typical market cost (2025-02/03, Moscow region). For a qualified technician correctly diagnosing and performing just the adjustment (no unnecessary head work), average cost is 40,000–45,000 RUB (as of February 2025, RU market). The main challenge is finding a mechanic experienced specifically with the X80/Duratec HE who won't oversell unnecessary work.12131415

Recurring question, same consultation offer still stands (2025-11 update). The "has anyone adjusted the valves?" question recurs periodically in the group; Eduard Yanonis's private-consultation offer (see above) remains current, and a Drive2 guide continues to be shared as a reference: https://www.drive2.ru/b/659026654919674056/202122

Regional cost spread, another data point — Naberezhnye Chelny at 6,000 RUB (2024-07 report). An earlier community-reported price point adds to the regional cost comparison already documented above: 6,000 RUB for a valve clearance adjustment in Naberezhnye Chelny (2024), described by the owner as a simple adjustment without head removal, after which the car felt noticeably livelier. Other community members questioned how this compared favorably against quotes elsewhere naming 25,000 RUB (Chelyabinsk) and 30,000 RUB (Moscow) (RU market, July 2024) for what should be comparable work — reinforcing the card's existing point that cost depends heavily on whether the shop does a minimal shim-adjustment-only job versus unnecessary head removal.23242526

Pre-facelift (dorestyle) models specifically require manual adjustment. Pre-facelift ("Dorest") X80 models lack hydraulic valve compensators (lifters) entirely, so periodic manual valve-clearance adjustment (the shim procedure above) is a genuinely required maintenance item on these cars — not merely a symptom-driven repair. Facelift (restyled) models with hydraulic compensators do not need this routine procedure. Follow the service manual for the exact interval on your specific model year.27

LPG usage and a lower cost data point, another dorestyle case (2025-12 report). A dorestyle owner (120,000 km at time of the LPG usage note; 150,000 km at time of this valve-adjustment report) who runs the car on LPG reports the intake manifold gasket kit includes five gaskets. Cost for a valve-clearance adjustment on this car: 10,000 RUB (RU market, December 2025), with the owner grinding their own shims to the exact required thickness rather than buying pre-sized ones — a lower-cost data point that adds to the regional cost spread already documented above, and a further corroboration that dorestyle (no hydraulic-lifter) cars need this service periodically, including under LPG operation.28293031

CA4GD1 (2.0 L): no figure in the manual. A member notes the valve clearance cannot be found in the manual for the CA4GD1 and says it is set by choosing bucket shims (стаканчики) of different thickness, not with a screw adjuster3233.

docs.title: Valve cover gasket leak — oil drip
docs.text:
Tags: #gasket · #oil-leak · #spark-plugs · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Symptom. One owner found moisture/condensation around the valve cover in the spark-plug-coil area and, on removing the coils, discovered spark-plug wells 1, 2, and 3 were full of oil, while well 4 was dry1.

Diagnosis and fix. The cause is a failed valve cover gasket. The fix is to replace the entire gasket kit, which includes new O-rings for the spark-plug wells2. Compatible/equivalent gasket kits: Elring 001563, Mazda LF210230, and others3. The gasket seats on a conical (tapered) fitting — there's no alternative fitting style to worry about45.

Related symptom — oil pooling on the exhaust manifold. In a separate report, an owner found oil collecting on the upper exhaust manifold specifically when accelerating, while the valve cover area directly above stayed dry to the touch. Initial suspicion was a cracked cylinder head, but other members pointed to the same root cause as above: oil from the valve cover (rocker cover) gasket dripping down onto the manifold rather than a head crack. This was described as consistent with valve-cover-gasket seepage rather than a new/different failure mode; direct inspection is needed to confirm the exact leak path in any specific case67.

Cross-brand confirmation — Mazda/Ford Duratec HE heritage. Separately reconfirmed: the FAW X80 engine (Duratec HE family, shared with Ford/Mazda) accepts both Mazda- and Ford-branded valve cover gaskets, consistent with the cross-compatible gasket kits (Elring, Mazda LF210230) already noted above and confirming the shared OEM heritage8.

Oil in cylinder-4 well plus misfire at 1200-1300 RPM — gasket + well-seal replacement. A separate case: oil accumulation specifically in the cylinder 4 spark-plug well, combined with cylinder-4 misfires at 1200-1300 RPM that stop after an engine restart, points to a valve-cover-gasket leak (consistent with the wells-1-2-3 case already on this card, but here affecting well 4). Recommended fix: replace both the valve cover gasket and the individual well seals (прокладки колодцев) together — replacing only the gasket without the well seals risks leaving the misfire symptom unresolved91011.

Engine smell on inclines — possible valve-cover-gasket or oil-leak cause. Symptom: an engine smell that appears specifically when climbing hills, worsens at traffic lights, and disappears after 1-2 km of driving. Oil level checks show normal readings. Possible causes discussed: a valve cover gasket leak (consistent with the leak mechanism already documented on this card) or a more general oil leak elsewhere in the bay. Diagnosis requires physically checking gasket condition rather than relying on oil-level checks alone121314.

Oil in spark-plug wells confirms gasket failure — repair-manual detail (Ford Focus gasket, sealant, torque sequence). Restating and detailing the diagnosis already on this card: when spark-plug wells contain oil, the valve cover gasket requires replacement. Use gasket material per the official Ford Focus specification (a DURATEC-compatible ROSTECO part is available), apply sealant per the service-manual pattern, and torque to spec (roughly 4-6mm sealant bead thickness per the manual's diagrams). Allow the sealant to fully cure before running the engine1516171819.

Leaking breather connection — Rosteco gasket recommended as a reliable fix. When the valve cover gets soaked specifically at the breather-tube connection, the fix is to replace the gasket with a Rosteco brand part (OEM designation "КК Ростеко," red type). One owner's original stock gasket was leaking cartridge/blow-by gases at that connection; after switching to the Rosteco gasket, it held reliably for several years when properly installed. Caution against attempting workarounds at the breather connection without replacing the gasket itself — excessive crankcase-gas pressure at that joint is the root cause, not a symptom to patch around202122232425262728.

Fitment variability — matching part number doesn't guarantee a proper seal. Separately, valve cover (red) gaskets are reported to have fitment problems even when the part number matches and the gasket appears correct: gaskets can be oversized around the perimeter and shift/move within the mounting grooves. If installed incorrectly, the cover can "weep" oil despite being nominally the right part. Recommendation: source from a reputable/official distributor rather than an unverified aftermarket listing, and apply sealant if fitment looks marginal; some owners switched to black gaskets (vs. the red type) for a better fit. Conflict: fitment varies between manufacturers even when the listed spec matches — this is a supply-quality issue, not a spec error2930.

OEM part number and quality-variance note. A separate, earlier report gives the valve cover gasket's OEM part number directly: 1003052A37K. Multiple suppliers carry it, but quality is reported to vary roughly 50/50 between good and poor examples — consistent with the fitment-variability issue already documented on this card. Black gaskets are again reported to perform better than red versions (matching the black-vs-red preference already noted above). Alternative sourcing approach: search by the Duratec HE engine-family designation rather than the FAW part number alone, to surface more cross-compatible listings. The gasket must be replaced whenever the valve cover is removed for a clearance adjustment (see the valve-lifter/shim-adjustment card)313233.

Ford Focus 2 (2005-2010) 1.8-2.0 16V DURATEC gasket — earlier, independent confirmation. An earlier, independent report reconfirms the Ford-cross-compatibility already documented on this card, with a specific donor model: a Ford Focus 2 (2005-2010) 1.8-2.0 16V DURATEC valve cover gasket fits directly. Brand ROSTECO (the same brand already recommended elsewhere on this card for the breather-connection fix) is available via a Wildberries listing3435.

OEM gasket part number LF0210230 (silicone) — broad cross-compat list, price, and fitment confirmation. A separate, later report gives the OEM valve cover gasket part number as LF0210230 (silicone) — likely the same underlying part as the Mazda LF210230 number already documented on this card, with a formatting/OCR difference in the leading digits (not resolved as identical vs. distinct here). Reported cross-compatibility is broader than previously listed: Ford Focus 2, S-Max, C-Max, Mondeo 3/4, Escape, Galaxy, and Mazda 6, 3, CX-7, CX-5. Price: roughly 1,500 RUB (RU market, July 2026) on Russian marketplaces (Ozon), also orderable through regular auto-parts shops. One owner confirmed fitment and performance after 1,500 km: described as thick, a tight fit, and operating normally with no leaks3637383940.

docs.title: Valve cover gasket leak — warped cover cause
docs.text:
Tags: #gasket · #oil-leak · #part-number · #conflict

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Part number: valve cover gasket 1003052A37K.1

Common failure pattern. The gasket leaks when the valve cover itself is warped — multiple attempts to seal the leak with high-temperature sealant will fail if this root cause isn't addressed, because a warped cover can't seat evenly on a flat gasket no matter how much sealant is applied. One owner tried 2 different gaskets ("Гастрономы разные" — different gasket brands) and both leaked ("сопливят"), including trying an aggressive amount of high-temperature sealant on the most recent one, with no success.213

Diagnosis procedure: visually inspect the valve cover for cracks and distortion; verify the cover's edge is perfectly straight by checking it against a straightedge. In this case, the inspection was done visually and the surface "looked fine" without obvious cracks, so the owner proceeded with reassembly rather than replacing the cover — but the community's advice remains to physically check with a straightedge, not just eyeball it, before reinstalling.45

Fix: replace the gasket only after confirming the cover geometry is correct (flat, no warping). If the cover is warped, a replacement cover is required — a new gasket alone will not fix a warped-cover leak.216345

Red vs. black KitZap gasket fitment conflict, and Mazda-original recommendation (2024-07 report, corroborates the warped-cover finding above). A separate community thread specifically about gasket fitment (as opposed to the warped-cover root cause documented above): a red gasket ordered from KitZap matched the listed part number but was oversized/loose relative to the actual groove template ("больше по размеру, гуляет" — larger, doesn't seat snugly), causing a poor seal independent of cover condition. Black gaskets fit better than the red KitZap variant. Community recommendation: prefer OEM Mazda original gaskets or the black KitZap variant over the red one.
