One owner separately reported that even a black gasket sourced from a Chinese supplier failed (developed a leak) within 3 months, so gasket-brand quality varies even within the "prefer black" recommendation — inspect fit carefully regardless of color before final installation, and check the cover for warping (per the diagnosis procedure above) if a properly-fitted gasket still leaks.789

docs.title: Valve cover gasket — part number
docs.text:
Tags: #gasket · #part-number · #cross-compatibility

The valve cover gasket (прокладка клапанной крышки) part number is 1003052A37K. Community members confirmed it fits the FAW X80. Some discussion suggests Mazda gaskets may also be compatible, though this cross-compatibility was not independently confirmed in the thread 1234.

Visual reference photo: a separate photo of the valve cover gasket was shared in the community as a visual identification aid, without an accompanying part number 5.

Which version for pre-restyle cars. Gasket 1003052A37K is listed for the X80 at two shops. The poster asked which version fits pre-restyle (дорест) cars, since the same article appears with different gasket shapes in the listings; no answer is recorded6.

docs.title: Valve lifters — shim-under-bucket adjustment
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

No hydraulic lifters — confirmed by multiple independent threads. The FAW X80 engine (Duratec HE, shared with Ford/Mazda platforms) has mechanical valve lifters, not hydraulic ones. This was raised and confirmed independently at least twice in the group: once when a member asked directly "we don't have hydraulic lifters, do we? Who's adjusted them?" and got a plain "no hydraulics" reply12, and again later when another member asked "don't we have hydraulics in the engine?" and was again told simply "no"34. Because there are no hydraulic compensators, valve clearances require periodic manual adjustment using the shim-under-bucket method, with replaceable adjustment shim cups (стаканчики/стаканы толкателя клапана). The absence of hydraulic compensation also means valve-seat settling over time can reduce clearance and eventually necessitate adjustment1234.

Shim-cup part number and sourcing difficulty. The OEM part number for the valve shim cups is 1007023A37K23. These are reported available mainly as used/second-hand units from online retailers, in limited quantities — new OEM units are rarely available, and many service shops simply don't carry them in stock, making sourcing a genuine bottleneck for anyone trying to get a valve-clearance adjustment done56.

Adjustment interval — no fixed factory schedule, but ~60,000 km is the common practical point. The manual doesn't mandate a regular valve-clearance adjustment schedule; however, many owners perform an optional check/adjustment around 60,000 km as informal common practice. Method: remove the valve cover, measure clearance, swap shims as needed789. Separately confirmed at higher mileage: there is no fixed valve-adjustment interval in the maintenance schedule — adjustment is only necessary if engine noise develops or performance issues appear; at 100,000 km, an engine running smoothly needs no valve-adjustment work at all10111213.

Suggested check interval — 120,000 km (conflicts with the 300k+ threshold above). A separate report recommends checking/adjusting valve thermal clearances at around 120,000 km as preventive maintenance — noticeably earlier than the "300,000+ km or camshaft looseness" threshold already documented on this card. Conflict: not resolved whether 120,000 km or 300,000+ km is the more appropriate proactive check point; the design's self-adjusting shims argue for the higher figure, but this source recommends the earlier one as a precaution14.

Self-adjusting shim design — restated. Confirmed again: the engine uses mechanical valve lifter shims (no hydraulic compensators), pre-selected at manufacture for the engine's life, with valves self-adjusting as wear occurs. Manual adjustment is needed only if the camshaft becomes loose (which requires a new head anyway) or after extreme wear beyond 300,000+ km. Routine shops pushing valve adjustments at 95,000-100,000 km are, per this source, doing unnecessary work on this design — save the money unless clear symptoms (rough idle, fault codes) appear1516171819.

Tapping/clicking noise at 60-70 km/h — traced to loose valve clearances. A tapping or clicking noise from the engine, especially noticeable at 60-70 km/h and under acceleration, can indicate loose valve clearances in the GRM (timing gear mechanism). The noise may temporarily worsen after an oil change if a lower-quality oil is used. Fix: have a qualified mechanic adjust the valve clearances. The X80 uses individually-sized valve adjustment cups (not shims) — the job involves measuring the gaps and installing correctly-sized cups. The noise typically diminishes after the engine warms up, due to thermal expansion2021222324252627282930313233.

Service cost and mileage context (2026). A separate valve-clearance adjustment ("стаканчики"/shim-over-bucket) job was quoted at approximately 15,000 RUB (RU market, January 2026) by a service shop, in a case involving a car with 133,000 km. This confirms shim-under-bucket adjustment is the correct terminology/method already documented on this card, and gives a real-world 2026 labor price point34353637.

Repairing existing shims by grinding, and Ford/Mazda cross-compatible new shims. Instead of full replacement, an existing valve-stem shim/cup (стаканчик) can sometimes be ground/sanded down to restore correct clearance. For new shims, compatible parts are available from both Ford and Mazda parts catalogs for the shared Duratec HE 1.8/2.0/2.3/2.5 engine family, sold on Ozon under generic listings such as "толкатель 800, клапана регулировочный"38394041.

Valve lifter/tappet dimensions and Duratec cross-fit. A Duratec-compatible mechanical valve lifter/tappet (толкатель) with a 3.56 mm shim size fits the X80: 31 mm diameter, 27 mm standard height (the X80's own variant measures 27.7 mm — the 0.7 mm difference is reported negligible in practice). These lifters are available on Ozon and are used together with the shim-adjustment procedure described above42434445.

Cold valve-clearance specification — Intake 0.25mm, Exhaust 0.30mm. An earlier, independent report gives the actual cold-engine clearance specification for the X80's reference engine (Ford Duratec HE equivalent): Intake (Впускной) 0.25mm, Exhaust (Выпускной) 0.30mm. Both measurements are taken with the engine cold — this fills a gap left by the interval-focused discussion elsewhere on this card, which documents when to check clearance but not the target values themselves46.

Adjustment interval — a further, earlier data point at 40,000-45,000 km, adding to the interval conflict. A separate, earlier community report adds yet another figure to the interval conflict already documented on this card: valve-clearance inspection and adjustment every 40,000-45,000 km. The procedure requires removing both the valve cover and the timing-chain cover to access the camshafts — not every shop is equipped or experienced enough to do this work properly. Thermal clearance specs vary in practice and technicians adjust to compensate for wear observed at the time of service. Conflict: this 40,000-45,000 km figure sits between the ~60,000 km informal community practice and the 120,000 km / 300,000+ km figures already documented and flagged as conflicting on this card — not resolved within this data batch, reinforcing that there is no single agreed proactive-check interval across sources474849.

80,000-90,000 km — yet another interval figure, from the second Telegram group. A separate community (FAW BESTURN X80 group) gives a further, independent adjustment-interval figure: valve adjustment every 80,000-90,000 km. This sits between the ~60,000 km informal practice and the 120,000 km figure already documented and flagged as conflicting on this card, adding a fifth data point to the unresolved interval conflict50.

Where the community disagrees

  • Valve-clearance proactive check interval conflicts across sources: ~60,000 km (informal community practice), 40,000-45,000 km (this report), 120,000 km (a separate report), and 300,000+ km / only-if-symptomatic (the self-adjusting-shim-design report). Not resolved within this data batch.

docs.title: VVT camshaft phaser — part number
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Part number and sourcing. The variable valve timing star (VVT-i mechanism, intake cam phaser) part number is 1026015-37K. It can be sourced from Ozon, Yandex Market, AliExpress, or local specialists; some suppliers (e.g. Mastergtr) keep it in stock. Expect roughly a 1-month lead time when ordering from Russia. Clarify with the seller that you need only the star/phaser, not the full timing/valve-gear mechanism — the two are often confused1234567891011121314151617.

VVT control valve — location and seal maintenance. The VVT (Variable Valve Timing) control valve manages the VVT coupling. Diagnostic rule: if oil appears in the valve's electrical connector, the valve-cover seal needs replacement. If oil is also found inside the connector cavity itself, the VVT valve needs replacing1819.

VVT control valve for Mazda 3 and 6. An Ozon listing (October 2025) offers a VVT control valve, article STL3K914420A (SAT brand), for Mazda 3 and 6; no fitment note for the X80 is given20.

docs.title: "Zero-resistance" air filters — a myth
docs.text:
Tags: #air-filter

No measurable power gain, and a maintenance burden. So-called zero-resistance / performance air filters provide no real horsepower gain on the X80 — dyno testing is cited as confirming a placebo effect only. For genuinely lower intake resistance, an engine needs either proper stock-style filtration or a fully open intake (no filter at all); simply swapping in an aftermarket "zero" filter does not improve performance. These filters also carry a high contamination risk and require daily cleaning/washing, versus simply replacing a factory paper filter periodically — expert/community consensus is this maintenance burden isn't worth it, and the factory filter is adequate123456789. Conflict: none — community consensus is strongly against zero filters on this platform.

What proper implementation would actually require. Installing a zero-resistance filter properly — i.e. to realize any real benefit — would require increasing valve diameter, enlarging the intake and exhaust manifolds, increasing throttle-body diameter, and enlarging the exhaust system: essentially rebuilding the whole airflow path to match. None of that is practical on a stock X80, which is one more reason a standalone filter swap alone accomplishes nothing9.

Real-world failure case — engine damage after 3 months on a cheap zero filter. Reinforcing the maintenance-burden warning already on this card with a concrete failure case: zero-resistance filters require regular oiling/cleaning, or fine unfiltered particles reach the cylinders and cause engine damage (scored cylinders, broken piston rings). One owner needed an engine rebuild after just 3 months of running a cheap zero-resistance filter without keeping up with its maintenance demands. Separately, polyurethane aftermarket engine-mount bushings are recommended over OEM rubber for longevity (an unrelated but adjacent mod discussed in the same thread), though quality varies by supplier. Overall recommendation, reinforced: skip the zero-filter modification unless a full cold-air-intake system is also planned — the standard factory filter is adequate on its own1011121314.

Where the community disagrees

  • Unlike most topics in this KB, there is no meaningful disagreement here — multiple independent sources converge on the same conclusion that zero-resistance filters provide no benefit on a stock X80. Noted explicitly because the underlying source data flagged this (unusual) absence of conflict.

docs.title: Aftermarket Android head unit — models, pricing, RAM
docs.text:
Tags: #head-unit · #aliexpress · #price · #firmware

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Popular aftermarket Android head units reported by owners:

  • Teyes CC3 — 9" screen, 4GB+32GB RAM/storage; performed well when reused from a Renault Duster 12.
  • Teyes CC3L / CC3 (2K) — 2/32GB or 4/64GB options, ~24,000–35,000 RUB (October 2024 prices, RU market) 345. One TEYES CC3L full kit (frame, adapter, camera, steering-wheel control integration) sold for 35,069 RUB with a 57% discount in September 2024 (RU market) 67.
  • 10" generic units from auto-market sellers (Avtomobilny, Avito, etc.) 89.
  • Letrun/LeTrun — 10+ inch screen, 8/256GB or 8/512GB, ~50,000–60,000 RUB (2024, RU market); also a ~40,000 RUB option seen on an auto marketplace 10111213.
  • Auto Marketplace 10" 2/64GB package (frame + rear camera included): 13,500 RUB (Sept 2024, RU market) 9.
  • Professional installation labor: ~5,000 RUB (as of Sept 2024, RU market) 61415.
  • TEYES CC3 2K — 10" screen, 6/128GB, for restyle (2019+) automatic- transmission models 1617.
  • Canbox H-Line 4165-1037 — Android 10, 4/32GB, DSP, QLED, sold as a complete kit (frame + wiring) 18.
  • Canbox M-Line 4543-1037 — Android 10, 2/32GB, DSP, QLED; fast delivery, complete kit 19. See frontcam.ru's FAW X80 (2018–2020) head-unit catalog for more model options 20.
  • Aftermarket head units need ≥6GB/128GB RAM to avoid lag — a Farcar S400 with 2GB/32GB caused noticeable system lag and freezing in daily use; 6GB/128GB is the recommended minimum for smooth operation, and correct CAN-bus integration is required to avoid dashboard error codes after install 212223.

Required installation components (frame-and-CANBUS kit): compatible frame/bezel adapter for the new screen size, a CANbus adapter cable for FAW- specific integration (see canbus install card), and dashboard trim-removal tools (plastic pry tools). All commonly sourced on Ozon with free delivery; anti-squeak tape and trim clips help eliminate installation rattles/noise 2425261927.

RAM guidance: 1GB units lag noticeably in daily use. 2GB is the minimum for acceptable music/navigation performance (may stutter on video playback in traffic) 282930. 3GB+ is recommended for smooth operation across all features 28.

Recommendation: pick RAM based on actual use — music/navigation only needs less; video/apps needs 3GB+ 828.

Firmware flashing — USB format requirement: aftermarket/replacement head units may need firmware flashing. The USB drive must be formatted as FAT32 (not NTFS or other formats), or the unit won't recognize the files. After a firmware flash, radio stations, saved settings, and interface language reset to factory defaults (Chinese) — manual reconfiguration to English and re-programming radio stations is required afterward. Firmware files can be shared within the community if the original one isn't available 3132333435.

Base-trim ("bomzh") install options and limitations: upgrading from the monochrome stock radio to a modern touchscreen head unit on the X80's base trim presents compatibility challenges. Options tested: Element 5 (expensive, poor performance, USB issues); Teyes CC3 2K (Allwinner K2501 processor, some reports of limitations despite widespread support). Recommendation: Teyes Pro+ or a similar K2501-processor unit offers better stability. Key limitation: many aftermarket units restrict the app ecosystem to only 3 apps running simultaneously (including Bluetooth), which makes full functionality impossible on some models. Issues also include USB-socket compatibility on the base-trim wiring harness 36373839404142434445464748495051525354555657585960.

More head-unit options — Avito and TOPWAY: additional aftermarket head units used by owners: units branded "AutoUnit-Teyes" found secondhand on Avito, and TOPWAY TS10S. Installation can be done DIY or outsourced to a car-electronics shop. See again frontcam.ru's FAW X80 (2018–2020) head-unit catalog for the current list of compatible units — installation can be ordered together with the unit purchase 616263646566676869.

Factory display size varies by model year/edition: X80 infotainment setups vary by model year and edition. Standard models are equipped with a smaller factory head-unit display; Live Edition and later variants feature larger screens. The factory unit supports firmware updates to enable CarPlay (see the CarPlay retrofit card). Aftermarket installation options with larger touchscreen displays (Chinese tablet-style units, per the guidance above) are available but can impact dashboard aesthetics; multiple owners prefer keeping the original interface and adding wireless CarPlay via an external adapter instead of a full head-unit swap 70717273747576777879.

Android 11 DSP 8GB+128GB with CarPlay (2013–2016 model range): an AliExpress-listed unit specifically marketed for the FAW Besturn X80 2013–2016 model range — Android 11, DSP audio, 8GB RAM + 128GB storage, wired/wireless CarPlay support — priced around 15,702 RUB (shared October 2024, RU market). Fitment note: as with other aftermarket units on this page, exact fitment can vary by restyle generation/frame, so verify against your specific model year before ordering 8081.

docs.title: Aftermarket tablet head unit installation
docs.text:
Tags: #head-unit · #radio · #wiring · #infotainment · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Installing a tablet-format aftermarket head unit (car radio) on the X80 requires: - A CANBUS adapter cable specific to the FAW X80 2018+.12345 - Removal of the factory radio frame/bezel and wiring-harness adaptation.36

Challenges reported: - Factory wiring is poorly organized and too short — the harness had to be unclipped from its fixing clips in multiple locations on the panel to accommodate the new unit.36 - Antenna connector incompatibility — the factory radio antenna cable on the X80 is very short; an extension cable is required. Two Ozon extension-cable listings were confirmed to fit by different owners.78910 - Internal microphone support — the factory design may not support using a head unit's built-in mic; an external microphone connection is needed instead.56111213

Installation time: roughly 1–2 hours for an experienced installer, significantly longer for a first attempt.341112

Result reported: once correctly configured (CANBUS setup, antenna connection, external mic), everything works without issues — better music quality/volume, responsive navigation, and climate/rear-camera integration functioning correctly.24513

Stock radio removal time (2024-06 report). Removing the factory head unit from the dashboard takes roughly 20–30 minutes, with the main risk being breaking the plastic trim clips that hold the surrounding panels — go slowly and avoid excess force. One owner needed a full extra teardown-and-reassembly pass because a USB cable was forgotten during the first attempt, adding another 10–15 minutes. Multiple owners report that despite the reassembly hassle, the sound-quality/feature upgrade from a new aftermarket unit is worth it, even through the factory speakers.141516171819

Teyes CC3 2K all-in-one unit — components and total cost (2024-06 report, RU market). A complete stereo upgrade using the Teyes CC3 2K (10-inch QLED screen, 8-core processor, DSP, 4G modem, voice control, 2-DIN form factor, optional 360° camera) costs 33,000–40,000 RUB with active discounts (list price 40,000+ RUB without discounts), including a 1-year warranty. Required components beyond the head unit itself: a transition/adapter frame, a wiring harness, and optionally a camera. Buying the frame, harness, and unit separately is significantly cheaper than a bundled kit — one owner's frame purchase from Ozon ran 15,000–25,000 RUB (June 2024, RU market) cheaper via that route versus AliExpress alternatives for the same part, and another owner reported paying ~33,000 RUB total for everything combined by buying on active sales/discounts (vs. 40,000+ RUB at full price, and up to ~49,000 RUB at the high end; June 2024, RU market).2021222324252627282930

Owner's voice report on a head-unit install. An owner who fitted an aftermarket head unit says the trim clips were hard to free, and the wires were too short and had to be routed up into a free space; afterwards the climate and door-open indicators and the rear camera worked. The unit wants an external microphone: the built-in mic performs worse and causes noise. She later reports better sound, a fine navigation experience and a good frame around the display 3113.

docs.title: Aftermarket Android head unit — CANBUS wiring
docs.text:
Tags: #head-unit · #esp · #installation · #parking-sensor

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

CANBUS adapter is required on restyle X80 (2018+) when installing an aftermarket Android head unit, otherwise a false ESP error light appears on the dashboard 12345. Verified working adapters: - Hiworld CANBUS, model FW08.11 H2AGY9D30A — confirmed no false errors 67. - Raysen CANBUS — alternative option 8. - Mayifun BOS-mini A5 CANBUS — also confirmed working 9. - Cable cost: ~2,000 RUB on AliExpress (Sept 2024, RU market) 10.

If the ESP light appears despite a CANBUS adapter, an alternative/additional fix is updating the original radio's MCU firmware (file CR482XA_V1.56_20200224.MCU); some owners needed to update both the radio firmware and the CANBUS adapter firmware together 1110. TEYES CC3L/CC3 are the most commonly installed models for the 2018–2022 restyle 6.

Dashboard panel removal (to access the factory radio slot): use plastic trim-removal tools (127–1,500 RUB on OZON depending on quality; Sept 2024, RU market); improvised plastic pry tools work too, with higher risk of panel damage. Procedure: remove trim panels around the radio, disconnect electrical connectors, remove mounting clips, slide the unit out; reverse to install. Clips/connectors are fairly durable 121314151617.

CANBUS cable for tablet-style units: FAW X80 2018+ specific cable interfaces factory wiring with the aftermarket radio, available on Ozon and other retailers 1819.

Antenna: the factory antenna is very short and needs an extension when installing an aftermarket unit; extension cables with standard connectors are sold on Ozon — route the extended antenna to the upper dash or under roof trim. Complete installation kits often include the extension 202122.

Full install checklist (from a documented DIY installation): route wires through the air vents to the dash using anti-squeak tape; integrate the rear camera with parking sensors (may need to remove broken factory connector clamps); install an external microphone on the dash panel to avoid a Bluetooth feedback loop — internal mics on the factory unit are disabled by the manufacturer; expect extra time if wire channels are tight 23242526272829.

Total antenna count on a fully-loaded install: 3–6 antennas (3 GPS + 2 GSM/ GLONASS + 2 Starline + 2 head-unit, up to 6 with OTA) — plus relocating the climate control module and rerouting harnesses 3031323334353637.

Known fix — outside temperature stops showing after stereo swap: after installing an aftermarket stereo (e.g. Teyes), the outside-temperature display can disappear from the instrument cluster. Causes/fixes: (1) enable the temperature toggle in the stereo's own settings menu ("Наружная температура"); (2) verify the correct X80 model/CANBUS profile is selected in setup; (3) some trims simply lack the external temp sensor 38394041424344454647484950515253.

Parking sensor compatibility after Android head unit swap: parking sensors may stop working after installing an aftermarket Android head unit. Cause: the Android unit may not support the original CANBUS protocol, or the aftermarket parking sensors themselves lack CAN compatibility. Workarounds: (1) verify the Android unit supports CANBUS for original-sensor integration (check its settings); (2) if the sensors are aftermarket/non-OEM, they may be incompatible with the CAN adapter — some installers add an extra interface block to bridge the sensors and the stereo; (3) some installations cannot simultaneously support both parking sensors and steering-wheel controls through a single CAN interface — choose the priority based on preference 545556.

Steering-wheel button integration: when installing an aftermarket infotainment unit, the head unit auto-detects the vehicle and CANbus signals in its settings during installation — the CANbus profile must be manually configured to match the correct FAW X80 model/year, or steering-wheel buttons will not function. One owner initially skipped this step and had no button response; the fix (matching CANbus profile) was worked out via private message with another group member 57585960616263.

Aftermarket infotainment installation with factory integration: aftermarket head units can integrate with several factory systems — rear camera (where fitted), steering-wheel buttons (via CANbus), and remote control (on some trims). Installation vendors such as frontcam.ru sell pre-configured units for the X80 with mounting brackets and wiring harnesses, and offer bundle promotions (head unit + accessories such as a dash cam, voice-assistant activation, or rear camera). CANbus settings must match the vehicle's actual configuration — automatic-transmission models use a different CANbus profile than manual-transmission ones, and manual (MKPP) installs are more prone to wiring/parking-sensor/rear-camera issues that need an electrician's help to resolve. Installers report the process is well-documented ("installation for dummies"), with the CANbus profile usually obtained from the seller via chat 646566676869707172737475.

Facelift model — Teyes CC3L popular choice: Teyes CC3L (4GB RAM / 32GB storage, 10-inch screen) is a popular Android head unit for the facelift (рестайлинг) X80, sold with a CAN bus adapter included. Price on Wildberries: ~5,000–6,000 RUB for the unit alone, plus ~4,000 RUB more for a premium installation (December 2025, RU market) 7677787980818283848586. Installation notes: factory trim clips are very tight and easy to break — take your time; the plastic housing under the rear-view camera needs filing/cutting because the factory camera connector differs in size from the aftermarket one; antenna and USB wiring often can't reach the new head-unit location and must be rerouted through the dashboard, commonly via the glove-box area. The factory rear-view camera's image can look worse on the larger new screen; some owners plan to pair the head unit with a higher-resolution aftermarket camera 86.

Teyes CC3L CAN bus profile mismatch — use Mazda 6 settings: on a 2017 pre-restyle X80, a Teyes CC3L initially set to the X80 CAN bus profile left the parktronics and multifunction steering-wheel controls non-working and the climate display blank. Fix: switch the CAN bus configuration to Mazda 6 settings — this restored all controls except the climate feedback display (still blank). Installation requires careful wire routing; the climate harness is short and may need slight trim removal to reach 87888990919293949596979899100.

10-inch retrofit — universal adapter frame, rear-frame trimming, power steering cooler clearance: installing a 10-inch Android head unit requires a 10-inch universal adapter frame mounted to the factory fascia. The rear lip of the frame may need trimming to fit; resulting gaps can be sealed with epoxy resin. Before finalizing the install, verify the power steering cooler depth for clearance behind the new unit — the cooler can interfere with the larger tablet-style unit's housing depth 101102.

Teyes UIS8141E tablet-style unit — connector-damage risk and performance notes: one owner (Kirill) installed a Teyes UIS8141E Android tablet-style head unit (specs: 4 cores @ 1.3 GHz, 2GB RAM, 32GB storage, Android 8.1). Issues encountered during installation: the rear camera connector was damaged (a contact torn) and the physical radio buttons below the screen stopped working (suspected loose cable/connector) — a caution for anyone installing this specific tablet-style unit. Performance notes: Yandex Navigator v3.96 runs acceptably fast on this hardware; the newer v27.0.2 is noticeably slow. Recommendation from the reporting owner: consult the 4PDA forum for custom ROMs and hardware-specific optimizations for tablet radios. Overall, tablet-radio integration is viable but requires careful connector handling during install 103104105106107108.

10-inch head-unit mounting panel — dorestyle only: a custom mounting panel for a 10-inch aftermarket head unit ("magnetola") is available for pre-restyle FAW X80 models only — not compatible with restyle (2018+) variants. It allows installing a large modern touchscreen unit in place of the stock radio opening 109110.

BOS-MINI A2 multimedia player: the BOS-MINI A2 car multimedia player (4K AHD, CarPlay, steering-wheel control, MirrorLink, voice command) is compatible with the X80. Installation requires a CANbus adapter (purchased separately, not included) to keep steering-wheel control and dashboard integration working. The unit has a 1280×720 screen, FM radio, Bluetooth, and USB 111112113114115116117.

GU Element-5 Android head unit — pricing and features (2022): a popular aftermarket head unit, the GU Element-5 (Android OS, optional sound processor), cost 27,000 RUB (2022, reported March 2024, RU market), negotiable down to 29,000 RUB — professional installation labor added 1,700 RUB. Features: display-timeout/screen-always-off mode, adjustable time-display angle, anti-glare settings. Note: some restyle-model owners experience windshield glare reflections off the unit's screen due to a different tint angle versus pre-restyle vehicles. Compatibility is confirmed across generations 118119120121122123.

Teyes tablet head-unit — CANbus + mounting-frame requirement (2018+): to install a Teyes tablet-style head unit on a FAW Besturn X80 2018+, two additional parts are needed beyond the head unit itself: (1) a CANbus cable adapter (available on AliExpress for roughly 2,000 RUB (July 2024, RU market)); (2) an installation frame/mounting bracket sized for the X80 124125126.

9-inch to 10.1-inch mounting-frame adapter: the factory head-unit opening is 10.1 inches. Owners retrofitting a 9-inch aftermarket unit (e.g. Teyes) need an adapter frame to bridge the size gap — example: Carav 22-1200, roughly 800 RUB (Aug 2024, RU market) from Ozon. Some adapter frames use self-tapping screws for mounting; shop around for the mounting style you prefer 127128129130131.

False "drunk road" warning after head-unit replacement — CAN-bus wiring fix: after replacing the factory head unit (ГУ) with an aftermarket one, a false "drunk driving/road" warning light can appear on the dashboard. Fix: proper CAN-bus wiring connection — a video walkthrough identifies a specific pin sequence, connecting a yellow wire to a particular position on the brown connector. For one affected owner (Марина), this correct connection resolved both the false warning light and a parking-sensor malfunction simultaneously. Alternative approach if the exact pin isn't known: source the correct CANBUS connector for the vehicle, or add a specific bridging wire to the correct pins 132133134135136137138139140141142143.

Audio interface adapter codes (unverified, 2020 car). For a 2020 car, the audio interface adapter codes RZ-YQBT11 and RW-NCL-0504 were given in reply to a question; the reply adds that the exact head-unit model must be specified when buying the adapter. The thread does not say which adapter type these are, so confirm with the seller 144.

docs.title: Wireless CarPlay retrofit (Carlinkit)
docs.text:
Tags: #head-unit · #firmware

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

CarPlay can be retrofitted onto the factory head unit (no aftermarket Android unit required): (1) download the firmware from the faw-cars.ru website, which also has a detailed installation guide; (2) flash the factory unit following the included instructions; (3) purchase a Carlinkit wireless CarPlay adapter; (4) connect the Carlinkit adapter via USB to the head unit. This method works with iOS devices only. Android-phone users who want a similar wireless-mirroring experience should instead consider replacing the head unit with an aftermarket Android unit, or adding a separate Android mirroring display 123.

Carlinkit wireless adapters — general product line and pricing: Carlinkit wireless-connectivity adapters enable wireless CarPlay or Android Auto on factory radios that already support the wired versions. Model 4.0 CPC200-CP2A works with both iPhone and Android devices. Typical cost: 2,000–3,500 RUB depending on source (RU market; Ozon ~3,500 RUB in spring 2025; secondhand from local sellers ~2,000 RUB). Some cheaper models only support iPhone — dual-OS models cost more. Build quality varies between sellers (some units arrive with no manufacturer branding). Function: converts the factory unit's wired CarPlay/Android Auto port into a wireless connection. Works reliably with navigation, messaging, and music apps once paired 4567891011121314151617.

Carlinkit CP2A — Android Auto installation, features, and limitations: the CP2A (v4.0) wireless adapter enables Android Auto specifically on the factory head unit via an OTA (over-the-air) connection. Cost: approximately 3,000 RUB (July 2025, RU market). Setup: install the adapter, pair with the phone over Bluetooth — the phone then acts as the wireless bridge (no wired connection needed; phone battery drains normally, no faster than usual). Load time from ignition-on: roughly 3 seconds. Working features: navigation (Yandex.Navigator, Google Maps, 2GIS), music playback, voice control (Google Assistant), and reading/replying to SMS/Telegram messages (reply only — voice reply works, but typing/composing a new Telegram message directly is not supported). Compatibility caveats: Samsung/Huawei phones can have issues due to Knox antivirus software and the absence of Google Play Services; only apps in Android Auto's supported list work (custom apps and games are not supported); the head unit has no backup battery, so navigation state resets when the engine is turned off but resumes once restarted. Installation time: about 30 minutes with prior preparation (closer to 2 hours the first time; ~20 minutes on subsequent installs/reinstalls). Pairing is immediate on a OnePlus 11 or other "pure"/stock Android device; Samsung/Huawei users may experience pairing delays 1819202122232425.

CarlinKit X1CA/X2CA pricing and prerequisite (Baidu CarLife): the CarlinKit X1CA/X2CA wireless adapter costs 3,000–3,700 RUB on AliExpress, or roughly 20,000 RUB on Russian marketplaces (January 2026) — the large price gap makes AliExpress clearly the better source. It enables wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay via the factory head unit's USB connection. Requires the factory head unit to already support wired CarPlay/Android Auto via the Baidu CarLife protocol. It's a cheaper alternative to a full 5,000–40,000 RUB (Jan 2026, RU market) aftermarket head-unit replacement, though audio quality still depends on the factory sound preparation — aftermarket head units (4,000–40,000 RUB) offer better sound at higher cost 26272829303132.

Firmware update for wired CarPlay support (community-shared files): the factory head-unit firmware can be updated to enable wired Apple CarPlay support directly (as an alternative/precursor to the faw-cars.ru method above). Procedure: (1) download the firmware files from a Yandex Disk link shared within the community; (2) prepare two USB drives with the correct formatting; (3) follow the step-by-step visual instructions provided by the community; (4) execute the firmware update, which runs as a two-stage process. After the update, wireless CarPlay/Android Auto adapters (Carlinkit-type, see above) work seamlessly on top of the updated firmware. Some owners prefer to keep the original OEM interface for aesthetics while adding wireless functionality via the external adapter rather than switching to an aftermarket screen; professional installation is available at some service shops for owners who don't want to DIY-flash the unit 333435363738394041424344.

Carlinkit adapter tiers — basic vs. Android-OS premium model: two Carlinkit product tiers are reported, distinct from the CP2A/X1CA/X2CA models above: (1) a basic model without built-in Android — roughly 2,000 RUB (March 2026, RU market), minimal functionality (phone-mirroring connection only); (2) a premium model with a built-in Android OS — roughly 9,800 RUB on AliExpress, or ~20,000 RUB on Ozon (https://ozon.ru/t/lwvPyAx). The premium version displays a full Android interface directly on the stock monitor, with integrated navigation, music, and radar-detector ("antiradar") apps — no separate phone mount or Baidu CarLife integration is needed once installed. Works with the factory head unit after the wired-CarPlay firmware update described above 45464748.

Carlinkit Tbox Ambient (8GB/128GB) — Android head-unit-in-a-dongle: the Carlinkit Tbox Ambient is effectively a 10-inch-capable Android computer-in-a-box (8/128GB storage) that runs through the stock head unit via wireless CarPlay, working on both restyle and pre-restyle models. It requires the wired-CarPlay firmware update (above) for full functionality. Performance is rated 8–9/10, with no reported lag; occasional screen-responsiveness inconsistency is attributed to the factory touchscreen digitizer itself rather than the Tbox adapter. Available on OZON 4950515253545556575859.

Reports from other threads (2025-2026). Firmware route, secondhand: one member says a YouTube video showed an iPhone connecting by CarPlay to the X80 head unit, and that the unit needs a firmware update first; he found no working Android Auto method and says official dealers told him they cannot help if the phone does not connect. This is secondhand and unverified, but it matches the firmware-then-adapter route described above 60. Android Auto add-on: an owner reports a 3,000 RUB Android Auto add-on for the stock screen (July 2025, Russia) that adds navigation (Yandex, Google, 2GIS), music, SMS reply and voice control; it does not add arbitrary apps, Telegram shows notifications only, and voice dialling works without touching the screen. This agrees with the CP2A figures above 6162. Android box price: a CarlinKit CarPlay AI box (Android 13, 8 GB RAM, 128 GB storage) was listed at 12,594 RUB after a 56% discount (April 2026, Russia), the same 8/128 GB class as the Tbox Ambient above 63. For installing a full replacement unit instead, see the Android head unit buying guide.

docs.title: Audio and panoramic camera wiring diagrams
docs.text:
Tags: #wiring-diagram · #antenna · #fuse · #head-unit

Two pages of the factory X80 wiring-diagram set (EWD, English) cover the audio system and the panoramic view monitor. The files are in the diagnostic-manual chapter list in shared files and manuals. The text extracted from the audio page is truncated at 40,000 characters, so the rest of that diagram is missing.

Audio system (EWD page 1109, file Z009 AUDIO.pdf). Fuses as printed: Audio Si52 25A (the rating's position next to the label is ambiguous), BTN (Si1) 40A, Audio/PKE (Si60) 5A. Speakers: FL1 driver door (LH), FR4 front passenger door (RH), RL3 rear door LH, RR4 rear door RH; tweeters FL3 (LH) and FR1 (RH). Other parts: antenna assembly AN1 (with antenna power), USB-A port I24, microphone H4, multi-function control panels 1 (I20) and 2 (I23), steering-wheel spiral cable I29, LCD I7, rear view monitor SR1 (gray)-1, and LVDS links to the panoramic monitor controller I61 and the TFT I19. The gateway control unit and BCM (refer to page 1117) are on the same bus 1. For speaker sizes and upgrades see factory speakers and audio upgrades.

Panoramic view monitor (EWD page 1110, file Z010.pdf). Fuse: PKE/EPB 5A (Si58), with the main fuses (Si13 125A, Si71 generator 175A, Si72 175A) on the same feed. Cameras and monitors: F49 front camera (green), FL6 panoramic view monitor (blue), FR7 panoramic view monitor (brown), SR1 rear view monitor (gray)-1. Controller: I62 Panoramic View Monitor Controller. Connectors: I60 front (green)-2, I56 LH (blue)-2, I59 LH (gray)-2, I52 RH (brown)-2, I61 LVDS controller (green)-2, I47 audio H (green)-1. Cross-references: gateway control unit to page 1113, PKE controller to 1119, radar switch to 1125. Pin numbers are printed in the text but the connector mapping is not fully clear 2. For the aftermarket side of a 360° system see side-mirror camera installation.

docs.title: Factory speakers and audio upgrades
docs.text:
Tags: #audio · #part-number · #fitment

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Factory speaker configuration: the X80 comes with all broadband (full-range) speakers — no dedicated tweeters from the factory. Front doors have oval 5×7 in broadband speakers; rear doors have round broadband speakers. Standard oval size is confirmed as 5×7 inches across the lineup 12. Some trims (e.g. a 2019 "Luxury") include front-door tweeter mounting locations that come empty from the factory — with no tweeter actually installed — while other examples of the car don't even have the mounting position 34567.

Stock speaker quality: factory oval speakers are widely described as low quality — quiet, and they distort/sound harsh ("хрипят") at full volume 891011. Where fitted, the factory tweeters are also considered poor quality ("говно") — though even a mediocre tweeter is reported as better than no tweeter at all 12131415.

Fitment for aftermarket speakers: standard oval 5×7 in mounting locations accept round aftermarket speakers via adapter plates — 165 mm round speakers fit the front doors this way, and adapters for 160–165 mm are commonly used; rear doors have more room and can fit up to 200 mm round speakers 1617. Confirmed successful aftermarket installs: Mac Audio (front) and Mystery (rear), both in the native 5×7 in size without needing adapters 181920.

Tweeter installation: adding aftermarket tweeters to the front doors — using the empty mounting locations where present — measurably softens and balances the sound. This is a relatively easy upgrade and is reported as a significant quality improvement over stock 3. If your car has no tweeter mounting position at all, one is needed to enable this upgrade.

Amplifier vs. speaker priority for audio upgrades: multiple owners agree the amplifier matters more than the speakers for perceived audio quality — installing a Teyes aftermarket head unit/amp setup made the stock speakers "work better" without replacing them 212223. For a stronger, higher-quality amplifier, GBL brand is recommended — expensive but delivers real power (some models include a built-in amp) 24. Caution: pushing more power through stock-mounted speakers/doors risks door-panel rattling/damage ("двери треснутся") if taken too far 23. Adding sound-deadening material (vibration-damping foam + shielding layer) to the doors and trunk lid is also recommended to reduce panel vibration/rattle and improve perceived bass response when upgrading 2122241523.

Amplifier REM (remote-enable) wire — where to find it: the REM wire turns the amplifier on/off in sync with the head unit's power state. On non-restyle (pre-facelift) models, there is no dedicated REM wire location — use the ASS (ACS/Audio Control Signal) wire instead. On restyle models, the REM wire may not exist on the head unit at all; it can instead be connected to the blue power wire (ACC), or a high-level-input-detection method can be used instead. Some aftermarket amplifiers auto-detect the input signal and don't need a REM connection at all 2526272829303132.

165 mm round speaker + CARAV adapter ring fitment: standard 165 mm (6.5 in) round speakers fit the front doors without modification when paired with CARAV adapter rings (16.5 cm, sold on Ozon, link: https://ozon.ru/t/1Gg6BHd). Plastic-to-plastic fit is secure — wood spacers are not needed. Fitment depends on the speaker's basket depth and suspension travel; owners running deeper mid-bass drivers in the doors report trimming the interior door trim slightly from the inside to clear extra depth 33343536.

Recommended upgrade path: for the front, 165 mm speakers with CARAV adapter rings; for the rear, add amplified coaxial speakers or mid-bass drivers — but skip mid-bass in the rear if a subwoofer is already present, since the mid-bass becomes inaudible/redundant next to the sub. One owner successfully runs FOCAL oval speakers (front) with Ural speakers (rear) and is satisfied with the result 37. On the head-unit side, TEYES (10–12 range) is reported as a budget option that still drives the system with strong volume at only ~5/10 output setting. Audio wiring is routed through the doors and under the carpets — dampening material is recommended along the run 3334353637.

Front speaker size and drop-in-conversion adapter rings: the front door speakers are oval-shaped units, the same size as the rear speakers. Reported upgrade options: Focal brand for the front, Ural Molot for the rear (reference: a Drive2.ru article on front speaker replacement). To convert to standard round speakers, 165mm circular speaker adapter rings are available for a drop-in conversion 3839404142.

165mm speaker spacer rings — Mazda/Haima/X80 compatible: speaker adapter/spacer rings for 165mm (6.5") speakers, compatible with the X80 as well as Mazda and Haima vehicles, are available on OZON.ru 43.

5x7 inch speaker installation confirmed front and rear: one owner successfully installed 5x7 inch (13x18 cm) oval speakers in both the front and rear door positions, reporting a good fit 444546.

Speaker upgrade options and recommended setup: stock X80 audio is widely regarded as poor. The OEM system uses 5x7 inch (165mm) oval speakers in the doors, identical size front and rear. Two upgrade paths are reported: (1) staying with 5x7 speakers — rated as mediocre by users who tried it; (2) converting to 6.5 inch (165mm) round speakers using adapter rings — recommended by user Фаб. For a proper upgrade, the recommended setup is separate mid-bass drivers plus tweeter modules (component set) rather than coaxial full-range speakers; no amplifier is needed for moderate listening volumes. Mentioned brand: DL Gryphon Pro mid-bass driver 4748495051.

DL Audio component speaker upgrade — popular choice, brand comparison: another popular upgrade path is DL Audio component speakers (brand assembled in Russia, components sourced from China). Installation: a 165mm component set for the front, coaxial speakers for the rear. DL Audio is well-regarded but preference is user-dependent — one owner replaced DL Audio with Focal instead (brand preference; both are premium-tier/expensive options). Installation method: direct solder connection or crimp terminals to the factory wiring — cutting the factory connectors is often necessary since they use non-standard connector types. Aftermarket component speakers significantly improve sound quality over the factory system 52535455.

Front/rear factory oval size confirmed same, DL vs. Focal brand experience, and weight comparison: front and rear factory speaker positions use the same oval size, confirmed by multiple owners in a front-vs-rear sizing discussion. Brand experience: one owner tried DL speakers and didn't like them, switching to Focal instead; Focal units cost about 10,000 RUB (as of August 2026, RU market). A separate owner found small 5×7 in DL speakers (no adapter rings needed) and planned a Griffon front / Barracuda rear combination. Weight comparison: stock oval speakers weigh around 650 g, while aftermarket units like Focal weigh around 2,600 g — used by owners as a rough indicator that the heavier aftermarket unit should perform better. One owner installed Focal up front, was satisfied with the result, and planned to do the rear doors next; another cautioned that two pairs of 165mm round speakers might be a better use of the same budget rather than one oval pair 5657585960616263646566676869707172.

docs.title: Backup camera upgrade
docs.text:
Tags: #connector

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

A backup (reversing) camera can be upgraded to a higher-resolution model without any rewiring. The standard connector pin count on the X80 remains the same across camera models — the new camera simply plugs into the existing harness via its connector. No cable modification or rewiring is needed 12.

Aftermarket rear-camera installation — three mounting methods compared: three approaches for installing an aftermarket reversing camera: Method 1 — drill a hole in the trunk lid and seal it with sealant; this causes rust after ~3 years and is not recommended. Method 2 — route the wire through the license-plate light fixture, cutting a corner of the plastic trim to fit the wire, and mount the camera above the plate; this has proven stable for 3+ years. Method 3 — use a license-plate-light bracket with a built-in camera mount, requiring no drilling; described as the better alternative overall 34567891011.

Upgrading to a Sony 170° camera, Teyes head-unit route: the stock reversing camera can be upgraded to an aftermarket Sony 170-degree camera for improved wide-angle visibility. These aftermarket units are sold either bundled with Teyes-branded head units or as standalone accessories. Installation requires a frame adapter and a wiring harness; some fitments may require minor dashboard modifications 1213141516.

Weak backup-camera visibility — reverse-light angle mismatch (auxiliary light fix): factory reverse lights in the tail-light clusters aim upward, while the reversing camera mounted in the hatch aims downward — this angular mismatch leaves the area directly behind the car (the camera's field of view) poorly lit, so the backup-camera image on the monitor shows little to no illumination when reversing at night. Suggested fix: add an auxiliary reversing light that aims downward to properly light the area the camera is actually looking at 171819.

Recamlux AHD 1080p camera. A Recamlux AHD 1080p rear-view camera for 12-24 V vehicles is sold on Wildberries (low-confidence mention; no price or fitment report) 20. For the X80's own connector and mounting options see the sections above.

docs.title: Dashcam power supply routing — clean install options
docs.text:
Tags: #wiring · #fuse

For a clean dashboard-camera power installation without visible loose wires, several routing options are used by owners:

  1. Optimal — via the mirror mount and door jamb: run the cable from the interior ceiling along the roof-edge trim to the mirror mount, then down the door jamb, then behind the dash to the radio or a 12V accessory point. This route does not require opening any ceiling panels.
  2. Overhead light fixture: tap power from the overhead dome-light connector — requires removing the light housing (2 screws, hidden under small covers); the cable then runs under the headliner.
  3. Glove-box area: route the cable through the panel down to the glove-box area, then to the fuse box — requires running the cable through the dash panel itself.
  4. Fuse-block tap: use a mini fuse-splitter (разветвитель предохранителя) on an auxiliary fused 12V circuit (available on non-automatic-transmission models, typically ~15A). Cabin space for a fuse splitter is often tight; soldering directly to the fuse pins is a viable alternative for experienced installers.

12345678910111213141516.

Additional routing options — GLONASS-module tap and ACC-fuse tap: two more approaches reported independently: (5) ACC-circuit fuse tap: tap power directly from the ACC circuit via the fuse panel (30A), routing the cable through the pillar trim — power only when ignition is on; (6) GLONASS module tap: wire-tap the GLONASS module's power and control output, which supplies 12V with ignition-dependent logic — an equivalent alternative to tapping fuse slot 30 directly. Professional installs use T-harness (add-a-fuse) connectors in the fuse panel rather than soldering, for a reversible tap 17181920212223242526.

docs.title: Restyled X80 speaker sizes and round conversion
docs.text:
Tags: #fitment · #audio

Oval size on the restyled X80: on the restyled X80 the factory speakers are ovals, and one member said the same four ovals fit both front and rear 12. One member gave the size as 6x9, but another corrected it to 5x7 (as written) 13. A third member said 6x9 can be forced in, but then part of the speaker ends up under the trim panel 4. The 5x7 figure matches the size documented in factory speakers and audio upgrades.

Round rear speakers: one member fitted round speakers at the rear by making mounting brackets (крепления) for them, and said the round and oval units are the same size 567. Another member noted that 16 cm round speakers have a wider choice on the market than ovals 8.

docs.title: Side-mirror camera installation for 360° view system
docs.text:
Tags: #mirror · #head-unit · #installation · #wiring

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Retrofitting a 360°/around-view camera system on the FAW Besturn X80 requires both the right head unit hardware and physical camera installation in the mirrors — most factory X80 units were never wired for it.

Hardware requirement: the head unit (GU/"магистраль") must have 4 dedicated camera video inputs. A firmware flash that merely adds a "4-camera" menu option is not sufficient if the head unit's board has no physical video inputs for them — "software isn't enough, hardware support is required" 1234567. One owner found a firmware option for 4 cameras while flashing for CarPlay support, but another cautioned this only works if the unit actually has 4 video-in connectors on the board — otherwise the firmware option does nothing 678.

China-market trim difference: the Chinese-domestic-market FAW X80 "Sport" trim (1.8T engine, black roof, "Tesla-style" tablet head unit) reportedly came with cameras pre-installed from the factory; this trim was never imported to Russia 910. Some Russian-market cars had the preparation for 360° cameras built in (a molded circle at the mirror mount point) but no cameras fitted in any actual trim — comparable to the door-panel light housing that's present but never populated with a light 1112.

Mirror disassembly and camera mounting: (1) the mirror glass/element sits on movable spring clips — pull it off first 1314; (2) fully disassemble the mirror housing and remove the mirror glass entirely, or the camera cable cannot be routed through 15; (3) there is a molded circle on the inner-lower side of the mirror housing marking the correct camera drill point — drill only there, and be careful not to drill through the internal cable-retaining studs 151617.

Wiring — the hardest part: routing the camera cable through the door's wiring-loom connector is the most tedious step. Route the cable/loom from inside the car out to the door, not the other way around — the connector is narrower going that direction and passes through the larger pin housings more easily 18.

Parts sourcing: cheap camera + head-unit bundles are available on Wildberries 19.

Full kit needed: a head-unit with 4-camera hardware support + 4 cameras (front, rear, left, right) 2.

docs.title: Factory head unit: versions and limitations
docs.text:
Tags: #head-unit · #radio · #restyle

Versions. The pre-restyling X80 is equipped with a monochrome radio display unit with no Bluetooth, no aux input and no backup-camera capability — only AM/FM radio and basic controls 12. See photo 10679 of the monochrome unit. The restyled X80 (2018+) has a larger touchscreen radio as standard equipment on the "люкс" (lux) trim, including Bluetooth connectivity 3. The stock Android 6 unit has a hidden service menu accessible with password 3369, which allows changing the launcher and screensaver 45.

Media and phone limitations. The factory head unit can play video files 67, demonstrated by an owner playing a car scene video from a USB stick — but USB compatibility is inconsistent: a 32GB drive was not recognized while an 8GB drive worked 687. Supported media formats are listed in the printed owner's manual — one owner found this only after consulting the manual rather than trial-and-error 8. Bluetooth connectivity with modern Android phones is limited because the stock unit's Bluetooth protocol is outdated 910. Owners with the touchscreen unit appreciate its Bluetooth support 3. Navigation historically depended on Yandex Navigator integration, which stopped working / was deprecated in Russia 111213. Apple iPhone integration reportedly works better, but requires a paid Yandex subscription for full functionality 1415.

Why owners replace it. The lack of Bluetooth, aux and camera support on the monochrome unit is a common reason to upgrade to an aftermarket Android head unit, despite the low cost of the original unit 16. Even with the restyle's touchscreen and Bluetooth, many owners still consider an Android unit for a larger display and additional features 3. Multiple owners cite frustration with Android integration overall and recommend replacing the stock unit with an aftermarket Android Auto / Apple CarPlay unit for better media/phone support 1718 — see the head-unit installation and CAN-bus card for how to do that.

Aftermarket experience. Reverse-camera wiring (Tiyis SSS3K2): after installing a third-party Tiyis SSS3K2 head unit, one owner found the reverse camera activating automatically when shifting into Drive rather than only Reverse, since the camera's activation is tied into the vehicle's power circuit and the unit's automatic-engagement settings 19. Community troubleshooting: check whether the wiring was connected according to the official vehicle wiring schematic 20; another suggestion was to change the firmware/factory settings on the head unit itself, since some units have a configurable setting controlling camera trigger behavior 21. Long-term Teyes reliability: one owner installed a Teyes 4/64 head unit and, after continuous use, rates Teyes units as the best aftermarket option they have tried 22. Another owner notes they have wanted a similar full setup (including a proper CANBUS adapter alongside the Teyes unit) for 5 years but has been held back by budget/priority constraints — an indirect data point that the Teyes-plus-CANBUS combination is viewed by the community as the aspirational, more expensive-but-correct way to do the upgrade 23.

MCU firmware update from USB (X80F radio, guide shared 2024). The community-shared update guide for the X80F radio works as follows: put only the file CR482XA_V1.56_20200224.MCU on a clean USB stick, plus at least one music file so the unit can identify the drive, and make sure no other file with the .MCU suffix is on it. Start the engine before updating. Plug the stick in; if the radio does not switch to USB playback on its own, select USB mode manually. In USB playback, press and hold [RADIO] + [|<<] + [>>|] for more than 5 seconds to enter update mode, choose MCU, then press the right button (SEL) to start. The update takes about 1 minute, shows progress on the display and the unit reboots by itself. If the ESP warning lamp stays on afterwards, select reverse gear with the engine running (the radio volume drops) and wait a few seconds; the lamp should go out 242526. See also ESP lamp false warnings and the CarPlay retrofit, which also relies on factory-unit firmware.

docs.title: Subwoofer installation — wiring and signal sourcing
docs.text:
Tags: #audio · #head-unit · #wiring

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The stock FAW X80 head unit has no dedicated RCA subwoofer output ("no RCA/tulip jacks visible" on the factory unit) 123. Community-recommended approaches:

  • Active subwoofer (built-in amplifier): will play from any head unit, including the factory one — "the amp doesn't care what radio is in the car" 45. If there's no dedicated sub-out on the head unit, take the signal straight from the door speaker wires 67.
  • Signal without a dedicated sub-out: any audio channel — RCA/"tulip" or speaker-level wire — can feed a subwoofer if routed through a high-to-low frequency crossover/converter first 7. A suitable crossover/converter is sold on Ozon for ≈1,780 RUB (Jan 2025, RU market) (https://ozon.ru/t/q3K6Bew) 8.
  • Passive subwoofer: needs a separate amplifier and box design — treated by the community as "more of a pro/enthusiast setup," not recommended for a casual install 910.

Community view: if you've never run a subwoofer before, try an active unit first — if it's not for you, an active sub is easy to resell; if you like it, you can upgrade later 11.

Line-level converter: last resort (contrasting view). The advice above allows taking the signal from speaker wires through a converter 67. One member counters that a speaker-to-line converter should be the last resort: the signal should come from the head unit's rear output or a USB feed. A converter means disconnecting one speaker or door channel, and equaliser cuts then affect every channel, which makes tuning hard 12.

docs.title: Center armrest with cup holders
docs.text:
Tags: #low-confidence · #installation

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

A custom armrest with built-in cup holders can be installed on the FAW Besturn X80. At least one owner reports a successful DIY (кустарный/homemade) installation, though commercially pre-made versions may also be available on the market.

Documentation gap: the exact installation procedure is not fully documented in the community — one member mentioned having an installation video but did not share it, so a step-by-step guide isn't yet available from this source.

Fitment feedback: no complaints regarding fitment or functionality were reported by owners who installed it 1234567.

Factory cup-holder presence varies by model year/trim (low confidence): absence of cup holders (подстаканники) is noted on some model years — this appears to be a trim/year-specific factory feature rather than a universal omission. A 2017+ model may have introduced the cup holder as an optional upgrade, or removed it, depending on trim level. Confirm cup-holder presence against your specific vehicle's door label/spec plate rather than assuming by year alone 89.

OZ-BDBO center console box with cup holders (Ozon): a ready-made aftermarket option is the OZ-BDBO center console armrest/storage box with built-in cup holders, available on Ozon. One owner reports pre-facelift (dorest) trims already had cup holders factory-fitted, while facelift (rest) trims lack them — making this product useful specifically for facelift owners who want cup holders added back 10111213141516.

docs.title: Automatic air recirculation — disabling
docs.text:
Tags: #hvac · #part-number · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The X80 automatically switches the air intake to recirculation mode when reversing (to prevent exhaust-fume inhalation) and when the washer fluid is activated (to prevent odor). This causes window fogging during washing. Fix: disconnect the air-intake damper connector, located under the dashboard on the left side of the heater unit (requires removing the instrument-cluster binnacle). Manual control via the washer button's high-temp sensor partially manages activation; an alternative is toggling recirculation manually as needed 1234567891011.

Alternate/simpler method — pull the flap connector, ignore the dash light: a simpler variant of the disconnect fix: remove the connector/ plug on the air-intake damper flap itself (located under the dashboard, near the glove-box area) so the flap stays fixed permanently in the non-recirculating (fresh-air) position and no longer switches automatically. The dashboard indicator light for recirculation stays lit afterward, but this is cosmetic only — it doesn't indicate a fault. One owner has run the car this way for 1.5 years without issues; a second owner independently confirmed the same approach works 1213141516.

Part number and clicking noise — normal operation: the intake air-switch flap described above (street air vs. cabin recirculation) has part number GV7D61A70. The flap clicks audibly when it activates automatically during reverse gear or windshield-washer operation, and can also be triggered manually — this clicking is normal operation. If the clicking becomes excessive/frequent beyond the normal reverse/washer triggers, the actuator itself may need replacement 171819.

Recirculation-flap motor mechanical failure — stripped gear, Mazda 6 replacement: separately from the disconnect/disable workarounds above, the flap actuator motor itself can fail mechanically. Symptom: the motor makes a straining/buzzing sound but the flap doesn't move. Root cause: the factory FAW motor has a fragile plastic intermediate gear inside the gearbox that strips its teeth (one owner's motor lost 3 teeth from the intermediate gear). Fix: replace with a Mazda 6 recirculation-flap motor — physically the same part with the same 3-pin connector; a common source is a used unit from Avito 20212223.

Restyle (2019+) intake damper motor — non-response symptom and alternate part number: on a 2019 restyle model, the intake-damper motor stopped actuating entirely when the button was pressed — it makes an effort sound ("пыхтит") but the flap doesn't move, leaving the car stuck in one position (worked around by manually forcing the flap open to fresh air to stop fogging). A part number GV7D61A60 was given for this motor — close to, but not identical to, the GV7D61A70 actuator part number reported elsewhere in this card; it's unclear whether this reflects a different generation/variant or a typo, so treat both numbers as candidates to verify against your VIN/parts catalog before ordering 242526.

docs.title: Trunk cargo floor — plywood replacement
docs.text:
Tags: #trunk · #diy

The factory plastic cargo floor degrades and cracks over time. DIY replacement: use 12 mm plywood (chosen over 10 mm since the price was about the same at time of purchase) with a self-adhesive carpet layer (graphite color) on top. The plywood sheet fits within the original floor's 6 mm depth recess. If the plywood has cross-ribs underneath for rigidity, even an 8 mm sheet performs far better than the original degraded plastic. Fastening: a stapler works for attaching the carpet layer — use a stapler with sharp staples, since dull staples bend instead of driving in cleanly 12.

Reinforcement/repair options for the stock plastic floor (without replacing it): the stock plastic cargo floor flexes and develops cracks (2–4 common failure points) under cargo load. Three alternative approaches reported: (1) spare-wheel platform — place the spare wheel on a 1–1.5 cm-thick platform underneath, secured using the wheel bolts; the wheel-storage area then doubles as a rigid support that prevents flex; (2) foam/insulation reinforcement — insert foam/polystyrene insulation strips into the gaps where the floor edges meet the seat frames; (3) crack repair — repair existing cracks with fiberglass putty before applying either reinforcement method above 3456789.

OSB-3 floor with a hinged tire-access panel: an alternative DIY cargo floor uses 9mm OSB-3 board instead of plywood — 625×1250mm sheets (sold e.g. by LemanPro) fit well with the large rear seat folded down; 11mm OSB is also usable. The design adds a hinged external access panel (using a piano hinge) over the spare-wheel area so the wheel remains reachable without removing the whole floor; a support bar is attached at the rear-seat fold point. Reinforcement notes: backing/reinforcing bars are attached with the same fasteners as the hinge to prevent the hinge from tearing out under load, and compensating spacers are added under the hinge area to distribute load evenly. Dimensions should be measured in-place to match the trunk's contours rather than assumed from a template. The resulting floor supports weight but has some flex; proper bracing (as above) prevents hinge failure during loading — one owner suggested repositioning the hinges differently and offered to take precise measurements to share with the group. A telescoping/sliding design was mentioned as a possible future improvement 1011121314151617181920.

docs.title: Central dash air vent deflector
