docs.title: Stuck rear seat belt — child-seat lock mode
docs.text:
A rear seat belt that will not retract may simply be in child-seat lock mode, which engages when the belt is pulled all the way out. To clear it, push the belt fully back in and then pull it out again. If it will not move in either direction, the retractor has to be taken apart.12

Related: Rear seat removal — procedure and fuel pump access (rear seat belt hardware and sourcing).

docs.title: DIY sunglasses holder from a FixPrice glasses case
docs.text:
Tags: #diy

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

A DIY overhead sunglasses/eyeglass holder can be made from a FixPrice glasses case (~300 RUB, RU market, August 2026), motivated by wanting a fixed spot instead of keeping glasses loose in various compartments. The case itself is metal with a leather exterior and velvet interior lining, which gives it enough rigidity to double as a mount 1234.

Mounting method: drill two holes through the roof headliner's plastic frame and secure the case with M5 bolts, washers, and nuts. The plastic roof frame is awkward to work in, so it helps to weld the nut to the washer beforehand to make one-handed installation from inside the cabin easier. Washers were hand-made, roughly 1.5 × 1.5 cm, sized to fit the mounting points 5678.

Orientation note: the case has no top or bottom — its design is symmetric — so it can be mounted either way without worrying about correct orientation 7.

Why this option: buying a proper aftermarket eyeglass holder ("за косарь", i.e. for roughly 1,000 RUB) and waiting an unknown delivery time wasn't appealing; grabbing the FixPrice case at 300 RUB (RU market, August 2026) was a faster, cheaper alternative that repurposes an off-the-shelf product 6.

docs.title: Sunroof drive mechanism — part number and pricing
docs.text:
Tags: #sunroof · #part-number · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Sunroof drive mechanism (full guide-rope-and-frame assembly) part number: 5CA069830. Needed when the drive cable and plastic guide wear out or suffer freeze-damage. Pre-facelift and facelift models appear compatible (same part). Official dealer pricing is ~80,000 RUB+ (RU market, October 2024) with a long wait; secondary-market options (from Russian auto-breakers/salvage yards) are available for ~30,000 RUB (RU market, October 2024) 12345678910.

Single-side panoramic sunroof failure: one owner reported one side of the panoramic/electric sunroof failing to open while the other side continued operating normally; it was replaced under warranty. Possible causes discussed by the community: single-motor failure, hinge jam, or an electrical-connector issue affecting only one side (unconfirmed — low-confidence report) 111213141516171819.

Remote-control operation via key fob (windows + sunroof together): the panoramic sunroof and side windows can be operated together via the key fob's remote buttons: (1) press-and-hold the open button opens both side windows and the sunroof simultaneously; (2) press-and-hold the close button closes both side windows and the sunroof simultaneously. This is one-touch/automatic — no second press is needed to complete the motion. Windows can still be operated independently via the in-cabin button controls as usual 20212223.

Sunroof/skylight glass — part number and price: the sunroof/skylight glass part number for the X80 NEW is 5CA169810, priced at 22,040 RUB (RU market, September 2025). The rubber gasket is model-specific and cannot be sourced from other vehicles. Available at kitzapchasti.ru 242526.

Sunroof glass availability and drain tubes: broken glass-roof elements can be sourced from salvage yards when unavailable new. Drainage tubes exist for the glass roof system and can be cleaned or replaced as needed; specific part numbers and supplier information are available through community resources 2728.

Sunroof/panoramic-roof glass — confirmed pricing (20,000 RUB) and salvage/custom alternatives: further confirming the glass part number above (5CA169810), a second pricing report puts the new OEM glass at 20,000 RUB (RU market, May 2024). Cheaper alternatives: (1) salvage yards for used units; (2) custom glass-fabrication shops that can make a replacement from triplex glass if the standard mounts are compatible — rates vary by complexity. As a rough size reference, the X80 roof glass is close to but not identical to an Infiniti FX35's (X80 measured 86x45cm vs. FX35 87x47cm) 29303132.

Sunroof drive-gear part — cross-model compatibility: a drive gear for the sunroof-hatch mechanism is available on AliExpress, compatible across multiple FAW models — Besturn B50, B70, X80, B90 — with cross-reference compatibility also reported for Hongqi H7, Bentley, and Mazda 3. Part cost: 519 RUB (RU market, March 2026). Useful for X80 Live Edition models equipped with the panoramic-roof feature 3334.

Sunroof cap unavailable as a spare part: the X80 ships with a sunroof cap from the factory, but it is not available as a spare part either in China or on Russian aftermarket sites. Sourcing is made harder because the part is sometimes listed under mistranslated names like "проектор салонный" (salon projector) or under Pentium X80 naming variants (a related FAW-family model), making it nearly impossible to find by a direct search 3536373839.

Sunroof cable/strap misalignment — temporary and permanent fixes: sunroof misalignment where it doesn't fully close and shifts to one side (становится на перекос, не доезжает до конца) can be caused by a cable or strap coming loose from its groove near the sunroof motor. Temporary fix: remove the sunroof motor and gently straighten the cable/strap back into position without full disassembly; if the motor can't be removed, a stopgap is to position the sunroof using hand-applied rigid foam spacers and seal the gaps with tape — this allows extended driving (several months) until a proper repair, with the spacers preventing further shifting. Permanent fix: replace the entire sunroof unit with a donor assembly, costing ~15,000 RUB (RU market, 2023 pricing) when sourced from a salvage/dismantler — note this can recur if the cable slips again 4041424344.

Auto window/sunroof closing via key-fob hold — confirms and extends the remote-control note above: two independent reports confirm and extend the one-touch remote behavior described above: (1) 30-second hold to toggle the feature itself — holding the fob's close button for ~30 seconds activates auto-close mode (windows and sunroof close automatically after locking); holding the open button for ~30 seconds restores normal mode (windows/sunroof reopen when unlocking). This is a factory feature some owners are unaware of. (2) On keyless-entry (push-button start) variants specifically, simply holding the fob's lock button closes all windows and the sunroof (if equipped) — the reverse (auto-open) is not supported. ⚠️ Conflict: feature availability is unclear on base manual-key trims — at least one base-trim owner could not replicate the behavior, suggesting it may require the keyless-entry hardware 45464748495051.

Sunroof ventilation/drainage holes — location and clearing: the sunroof frame area has visible ventilation/drainage holes that need regular clearing of debris to prevent water backing up, especially after heavy rain or in dusty conditions. They can be partially covered but should not be fully blocked, to maintain proper airflow and drainage 52535455565758.

docs.title: Trunk / interior LED lighting
docs.text:
Tags: #led · #trunk · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Trunk LED light tape sourcing: LED light tape for trunk illumination is available via Ozon: https://ozon.ru/t/JTOdgil (Besturn X80 trunk LED strip). It is also available from AliExpress at roughly half the price, but with 3+ week shipping from China 1234.

Trunk light installation — routing and rattle prevention: to install an aftermarket trunk light, route the power line behind the plastic trim to the ceiling light. Secure the wiring behind the trim using foam padding inserted into the plastic slots to prevent it rattling against body panels 567.

LED interior light installation — practical experience: one owner (Artem) installed an LED light fixture inside the X80, completing the job in about 30 minutes. The main issue encountered was that the wire colors differed from what was expected/documented; aside from that, installation was straightforward 8910.

Trunk LED strip installation — detailed step-by-step procedure: (1) remove the trunk light dome/plafond; (2) connect the LED strip leads to the plafond contacts to determine correct polarity — if the plafond glows, polarity is wrong; if the LED strip lights up, polarity is correct; (3) remove the plastic latch/access hatch ("lyuchok") on the inner left side of the trunk; (4) thread a thin guide wire from the plafond opening through the lyuchok hole; (5) tape the LED strip leads to the guide wire from the lyuchok side; (6) pull the guide wire back out from the plafond side, dragging the LED leads through; (7) solder or clip the LED leads to the plafond wiring using separate connectors, respecting polarity; (8) route the LED strip under the trunk seal (уплотнитель); (9) secure/tighten the wiring; (10) push excess wire back into the lyuchok and close it. Alternative routing: run the wiring along the car's ceiling under the headliner panels for a fully hidden installation. LED strip used: a 2 m silicone-flexible strip, common brands from Ozon, priced ~300–500 RUB (RU market, December 2025). Test illumination before final sealing 11121314151617181920212223.

Alternate LED strip install procedure — stiff-wire fishing guide: a second documented procedure, consistent with the detailed steps above: (1) carefully remove the factory trunk ceiling light; (2) route LED power wires under the trim using a stiff wire guide (e.g. taped to the power wires) to thread through the body cavities; (3) connect the LED wires to the factory light's contacts using either provided clip connectors or by soldering; (4) the LED strip adheres using weatherstrip rubber along the cargo-area ceiling; (5) verify adequate clearance under the plastic trim so wires aren't crushed when the trim is reinstalled. Installation takes about 20–30 minutes. Alternative for less DIY effort: purchase pre-wired kits designed specifically for the X80, sold with detailed photos/video in their Ozon product listings 242526272829303132.

Motivation for trunk LED retrofit — visibility improvement (reinforcing report): consistent with the LED trunk-lighting installations documented above, retrofitting LED lighting in the trunk significantly improves visibility for evening loading/unloading. LED strips installed along the upper edges of the cargo opening provide bright white illumination across the entire trunk area. The light activates only when the trunk is open. The modification is described as particularly worthwhile for owners who load/unload the trunk frequently 333435.

LED interior lighting — independent wiring and relay requirement: to install LED strip lights or other custom interior lighting in the X80 cabin: (1) run both positive and negative power lines independently — there is no shared/common ground available to tap into; (2) power must be routed through a relay module to handle the LED current draw — a direct connection to door switches or existing interior circuits will likely cause relay malfunction or blown circuits; (3) many installers use the door-open signal (the door-jamb switch) as the trigger to activate the relay and illuminate the lights; (4) an alternative is a manual on/off switch wired through a relay. Multiple users report successful installs using this relay-based approach 36373839.

Interior LED lighting reference: in reply to a question about which interior bulb base (цоколь) to buy, Фаб linked a Drive2 article on installing full LED interior lighting (https://www.drive2.ru/l/580702944115032920/); the thread does not state the base size 40.

docs.title: Water intrusion under floor mats
docs.text:
Tags: #sunroof · #mazda-6-compat · #conflict

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Water pooling under the driver's and front-passenger floor mats is one of the most frequently repeated complaints in the community, but it does not affect every car and its severity varies widely.

Root cause and scope: the issue is inherited from the Mazda 6 platform design — the A/C condensate drain and sunroof drain routing can allow water to collect in the front footwells instead of draining outside the cabin. Community estimates put the affected share at roughly 10% of vehicles, not universal. It is fixable by extending/rerouting the drain hoses and making sure the drain tubes are actually connected (a common assembly-line omission) 123.

2019 automatic — mitigation via aftermarket floor mats: one 2019 automatic-transmission owner had water pooling in the rear cabin area specifically in winter. Switching from the stock factory floor mats to Evo-brand mats with raised borders ("с бортами") resolved the problem, suggesting the water had been entering through the factory mats' fastener holes rather than a structural leak. No electrical issues were reported in this case, and the owner's experience points to inadequate splash protection in the factory mat design as at least part of the problem 4.

Conflict — the problem is inconsistent across the fleet, even on restyled (2021+) models: community reports diverge sharply. Some owners on restyled (2021+) cars report they have never had any water problems at all, even in very heavy rain 5. One such owner draws a comparison to a Chevrolet Cruze they'd previously owned that suffered severe sunroof-drain flooding, and notes the whole community had reported the same Cruze issue — implying the X80's sunroof drain, while imperfect, is less failure-prone by comparison 6. Another owner offers a rule of thumb: if the interior stays dry and electrics behave normally even without rain, either a previous owner already fixed the underlying issue, or that particular unit was simply never one of the "problem" cars to begin with 7. A different owner, who had owned their (evidently problem-affected) car for only a month to six weeks and had washed it a couple of times with a Kärcher pressure washer, offers a data point on the other side of the conflict, suggesting some cars leak almost immediately under pressure-washing or heavy rain regardless of age 8. The community's overall read: first-owner care and unit-to-unit factory variation (see the assembly-quality card) matter more than model year or restyle status in determining whether a given car will leak.

docs.title: Water leaks — cowl and hood intake drains
docs.text:
Tags: #water-ingress

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Hood air-intake water ingress through drainage ports: water leaks into the cabin through the hood intake ("жаба") due to blocked drainage holes between double-wall metal sections. A small secondary drainage opening gets clogged with dirt, causing overflow into the cabin and air filter. Fix: modify the drainage using a silicone hose extended into the wheel well to bypass the blocked ports, or clean the ports regularly if the car is outdoors in dusty areas 1234567891011121314151617181920. ⚠️ Conflict: disagreement over whether the secondary small drainage port actually matters — KASPER emphasizes it clogs and causes overflow when the water level is high, but another user argues the main drainage outlet is so large that water always drains quickly unless 10+ kg of mud is blocking it. Resolution: both are correct — overflow through the small port occurs only in extreme conditions (simultaneous heavy rain plus an existing severe clog); normal operation relies on the main drainage.

Hood intake silicone-hose modification (detailed steps): complete modification to eliminate water entering through the hood intake: (1) cut and insert part of the white factory drain hose into a silicone hose; (2) install the silicone hose into the wheel-well opening, extending it deep; (3) connect the white factory hose end tightly into the silicone hose; (4) seal any technological stickers that came unstuck with adhesive to prevent water escaping there. This redirects drainage directly into the wheel well, bypassing the interior path 57.

Cabin water ingress from blocked hood intake during heavy rain: one owner reported water running through the heater directly onto the cabin air filter during the first heavy downpour after purchase, caused by a blocked hood-intake ("жаба") drain. Partial solution: use recirculation mode when raining, or reduce fan speed to minimum — this prevents water from being drawn into the cabin air filter. The factory hood cover helps but isn't sufficient on its own 212223.

Sunroof drain at the pillar — another check point: in the pillar corner there is a separate, almost invisible square sunroof drain opening — confirmed present on some cars; on others there is no visible hole, but the panel's slope drains water on its own 2425. On one car, water pooled with no slope and no visible holes — on that same car, the cowl panel's "false holes" (decorative indentations, not through-holes) turned out to be a separate problem (see below) 262728.

Standing water on the cowl panel (a molding defect, not a drain issue): the cowl panel under the windshield has oval indentation "pockets" that don't drain — they are false holes with no through-hole, so water pools in them. One owner's fix: drill through-holes in these pockets — water then drains properly. There's debate over whether these should be factory-through-holes; owners who applied the fix confirm it eliminates the standing water 26292730242528.

Water in the driver-side footwell — clogged intake drains: water pooling in the driver-side footwell can originate from the front passenger area. Common causes: clogged drainage ducts or incorrectly-installed weatherstrips at the windshield-base air intake. Repair: professional diagnosis, unclogging the drains, and weatherproofing the air intake with gasket sealing (~2cm above the intake base per expert recommendation). Service cost at a Moscow shop (DolAuto): ~18,600 RUB including diagnosis (RU market, November 2025) 313233.

See also: Water leaks — fender and cabin ingress; Water leaks — footwell diagnosis and A/C drain; Water leaks — sunroof and roof drains.

docs.title: Water leaks — door seals and body sealing
docs.text:
Tags: #water-ingress

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Silicone sealant along hood/window/door seams — simple DIY prevention: apply silicone sealant (specifically VMPAUTO 2401 silicone, 30ml bottle) along the hood edges, window seals, and door-frame gaps to stop water reaching the cabin and soaking the floor carpets — particularly important on the driver and passenger sides near the windshield. One owner reported dry carpets all spring after a single application 12345.

Root-cause explanation and DIY channel fix — door-frame seal degradation (universal, eventual issue): root cause identified via video demonstration: the original door-frame rubber seals degrade by around year 3, crumbling and losing their water-blocking ability. Water path: the roof-edge panel angles inward, collecting water and channeling it toward the cabin; the factory drain gutter at that point is too narrow, and HVAC intake suction pulls water in through it regardless of gutter capacity. Replacement seals (e.g. sourced from a Ford Fiesta) only last 6–12 months before the same failure recurs. DIY mitigation demonstrated on video: cut a strip of sheet metal from an aluminum beverage can, attach it along the water-flow line with double-sided tape plus silicone sealant, creating an improvised gutter/ channel that redirects water away from the HVAC intake. Community consensus: this problem will eventually affect all X80s to some degree, sooner or later — it's a design-level weak point, not a one-off manufacturing defect 6789101112.

Floor-mat clip gaps as a water/electrical-short source: water can leak into the cabin through inadequate sealing around the floor-mat attachment clip areas — these clips have large gaps that let water and sand enter during winter. This was the source of an electrical short in the GLONASS module's wiring when left unsealed. Fix: open the mounting clips, add rubber washers, and use adhesive for better sealing 13.

Underbody drain-plug maintenance: rubber plugs in the underbody drain holes can dry out over time and allow water to enter the cabin. Fix: replace the rubber plugs with new ones, or seal the affected areas with vibration-damping material. This is a common maintenance item that should be checked periodically 14151617181920.

Water under driver floor mat — non-hermetic internal seams: water collected under the driver's floor mat after rain, traced to non-hermetic internal body seams and mounting holes that were only sealed with tape and paint from the factory instead of proper sealant. Fix: identify and re-seal all affected seams with hermetic sealant (герметизация швов); once sealed, drainage normalizes and the mat stays dry 21.

Water pooling in cabin corners — drainage-hole checklist (rear, near fuel-tank lever): water pooling in cabin corners, especially the rear area near the fuel-tank release lever, is a known issue with several contributing causes: (1) uncleaned door drainage holes and heater air-intake drainage holes; (2) defective door seal gaskets; (3) water entering through the heater air intake (a pattern also seen on other models). Remedy: inspect and clean all drainage holes, check door seals, dry the interior thoroughly with a vacuum and towels/newspaper, and verify the BSM (body/comfort control module) hasn't been flooded, since it controls many vehicle systems. The pre-facelift model reportedly has more drainage issues than the facelift version 222324252627282930.

Water ingress through door-sill plastic plugs (front passenger): water entering the cabin at the front-passenger sill area has been traced to plastic plugs/stoppers at the bottom of the door-sill cavities that don't seal properly. Diagnosis: remove the plastic undercarriage (belly-pan) trim to access the inside of the sills from underneath the car — water flows through these plug apertures into the interior. Fix: inspect the openings, clean them, and ensure the plug apertures are properly sealed 3132333435363738.

Water under driver's pedals — firewall/bulkhead seal failure (possible warranty defect): separately, water ingress under the driver's pedals has also been attributed to a failed seal at the bulkhead between the driver's footwell and the engine bay — repair requires replacing the sealing gasket at that firewall interface. This may be a factory manufacturing defect and could be covered under warranty on newer cars, unlike the general wear-based leak causes documented elsewhere in this card 394041.

Water intrusion under carpets — left fender/wing seam (common, not fully diagnosed): water appears under the driver and passenger floor carpets after parking in rain/snow or after washing, traced to the area of a seam at the top of the left fender/wing. The community has not fully pinned down the exact ingress path; described as a "common issue, solvable but not simple" — solving it requires identifying the precise leak source and sealing the seams or checking door/body gasket integrity. Affects multiple owners 42434445.

See also: Water leaks — fender and cabin ingress; Water leaks — trunk and rear door; Water leaks — footwell diagnosis and A/C drain.

docs.title: Water leaks — fender and cabin ingress
docs.text:
Tags: #water-ingress · #fender

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Cabin water leaks are very common on the X80 and rarely have a single cause: the sources reported by owners are the fender technical drain hole, the cowl (жабо) and hood air-intake drains, sunroof and roof drain tubes, door and body seals, and the trunk/5th-door area. The paragraphs below keep the overview facts; each sub-topic has its own card.

Uncapped technical drain hole under the fender: the X80 has technical drain holes on both the driver and passenger sides under the fender, behind the wheel-opening area. One or both may be left uncovered at the factory during manufacturing/assembly, letting water that normally drains from the roof enter the interior instead 1234. This can leave standing water on the interior floor and cause damage 56. Fix: access the area from under the fender liner (снять подкрылок) and seal the uncovered hole 78.

General cabin water-ingress checklist: water can enter the cabin through several other points besides the fender hole — check all of them if a leak source isn't obvious: 1. Sunroof — inspect the roof drain system. 2. Door seals and weatherstripping. 3. Windshield frame sealing. 4. Rear door / hatch seals. 5. 5th door (liftgate) water drainage. 6. Gutter drains beside the windshield.

One owner reported water streaming directly into the luggage compartment, a persistent problem that needed a custom weatherproofing fix 910. Regular inspection of these points is recommended, especially before winter 11.

Comprehensive cabin water-leak source investigation: common ingress sources differ between pre-facelift and facelift models: (1) the rain pan drainage under the hood is normally adequate (large drain holes on both sides, slanted toward the edges) — typically not the source; (2) sunroof/roof drain tubing connections in the wheel arches become disconnected, routing water directly into the cabin; (3) door-seal drain holes (at the belt line inside the car) can become blocked; (4) on pre-facelift models, rubber seal stickers covering wheel-arch technical holes can detach, letting water flow directly into the cabin — facelift models reportedly fixed this design issue; (5) fix for drain-connection leaks: insert rubber/silicone tubing (rather than sealant) to extend the drain path away from the cabin. A properly functioning rain pan with perforated drain openings and an internal partition effectively directs water away 1213141516171819.

Three main water-intrusion sources — a quick diagnostic summary: a condensed diagnostic summary identifies three main sources of cabin water leaks on the X80: (1) rear-door/5th-door molding clip gaps if poorly refitted; (2) missing or clogged drain holes under the hood/cowl (жабо); (3) poor door-sill seals. Check all three locations during diagnosis before assuming a single cause 202122232425.

Overall water-leak prevention strategy — the four main sources: a community summary identifies the four major water-leak sources on the X80: (1) windshield seal deterioration; (2) hood/cowl (жабо) drainage and seal; (3) sunroof drain clogs; (4) heater-core housing seal. A durable fix requires addressing all four sources, not just symptoms. The community has repeatedly asked for centralized documentation (test videos for each leak location and its repair) but this remains sparse. Temporary mitigation: use silica gel or zeolite desiccant in the cabin to manage humidity and slow corrosion while diagnosing the source 2627282930.

Detailed guides:

  • Water leaks — cowl and hood intake drains — water entering through the cowl (жабо), hood air intake and its drain ports
  • Water leaks — sunroof and roof drains — sunroof and roof drain tubes, fittings and cleaning
  • Water leaks — door seals and body sealing — door seals, sill plugs, body seams and underbody drain plugs
  • Water leaks — trunk and rear door — water in the trunk, spare-tire well and 5th-door molding
  • Water leaks — footwell diagnosis and A/C drain — wet footwells and floors: diagnosis checklists and the A/C drain

docs.title: Water leaks — footwell diagnosis and A/C drain
docs.text:
Tags: #water-ingress

Passenger-side floor water — multiple candidate sources: water entering the passenger-side floor can come from several independent points: the A/C drain-tube angle (can back-flow water while driving), windshield/side-window seals, door drains, hood drain holes, a rubbing brake line, heater-core leaks, or seams in the engine-bay motor shield. Facelift/restyle models lack a manual A/C drain-angle adjustment (present on earlier models). Diagnostic tip: check the cabin (saloon) air filter — if it's wet, the water is most likely coming from the evaporator/A/C drain path rather than door or window seals. Drain tubes should have a small protective bend built in to stop wind-driven rain from being pushed back up into them 12345678910111213.

Wet driver-side carpet — possible causes checklist: water reaching carpets (especially the driver's floor mat) in rain may trace back to: (1) degraded seal on the intake tube entering the cabin; (2) a blocked drainage hole under the hood/windshield area; (3) failed windshield sealant; (4) deteriorated body-panel seals. Check hood-edge seals, verify the drainage holes under the cowl are clear, and inspect windshield and door seals — the pattern tends to track seasonal weather 14151617.

Systematic water-leak troubleshooting — full DIY fix sequence: this is a very common issue affecting most X80s to some degree, and several independent fixes are often needed together rather than one single cause: (1) extend the drain lines inside the door pillars; (2) remove sharp corners/kinks along drain paths so water flows freely; (3) reseal weatherstripping around the roof panel edge; (4) raise the intake duct under the hood, adding a small partition wall to redirect water away; (5) apply masking tape over the intake opening as a temporary water-diverter; (6) extend the A/C drain tube and seal the joint; (7) spot-seal remaining gaps with black caulk. This is a substantial, multi-step job, but owners who completed the full sequence reported achieving a genuinely dry cabin afterward 18192021222324252627282930.

Wet floor under front seats — drainage-pipe disconnection check: if experiencing wet floors under the driver and/or passenger seats, the likely cause is the underbody drainage system. Check the drainage-pipe connections at the floor on both the driver and passenger sides; these pipes can become disconnected or blocked, letting water accumulate inside. Inspect and reconnect any loose drainage joints found 3132333435.

Three-zone cabin water-intrusion summary (driver footwell, passenger footwell, trunk): a comprehensive report identifies three primary leak zones: (1) driver footwell — moisture on the GNSS/telematics connector under the driver-side carpet, which is a critical failure mode since it can disable the transmission ECU; (2) passenger footwell — water seepage through the seat-rail/sliding area; (3) trunk — accumulation despite the drain fitting. Root causes cited: (a) windshield/hood seal degradation; (b) liftgate drain-fitting issues; (c) damaged hood drip channels; (d) weak interior-panel fasteners at the door/window-frame interface; (e) low/degraded window weatherstripping. One owner at 150,000 km reports ongoing monitoring of these zones; another reports water damage required replacing the transmission ECU. Recommended fix: regular interior inspection, check the liftgate drain plug, inspect hood seals, and seal any visible gaps 36373839404142434445464748.

Water under brake pedal/dashboard — drain-tube disconnection: water collecting under the pedals and on the cabin floor is commonly caused by the drainage tube under the dashboard, near the brake pedal (близ педали тормоза), coming loose from the body. Fix: extend the silicone drainage tube with a section of copper pipe and route it properly to drain outside the cabin, preventing further accumulation 49.

Interior drainage system — quick leak-location reference: water leaking under the carpets typically flows to two main drain points: (1) front left, under the driver's feet, and front right, under the passenger's feet (plastic clip/drain point); (2) a rear drain access point also exists. All drain tubes route from the windshield cowl area downward. This drainage issue has reportedly been partially resolved on newer restyle models via factory improvements 5051525354.

Water pooling under the driver's feet — early diagnosis checklist: water pooling in the driver-side footwell is a long-known issue on the X80. Community-recommended diagnosis steps: (1) check the hood drain system — make sure it's clear and functioning; (2) inspect the engine-compartment panels on both sides of the engine (front panel and side panels) for water seepage or poor seals; (3) check the air intake area on the right side under the hood for water intrusion. If water still accumulates after these checks, the cause may be door seals, the sunroof drain (if equipped), or a windshield-gasket leak 55565758.

Water under driver's pedals — recirculation-mode mitigation: switching the HVAC intake from recirculation to fresh/outside-air mode reduces moisture accumulation under the driver's pedals, since it brings in drier external air instead of recirculating cabin humidity. A simple, no-repair mitigation rather than a root-cause fix 59.

See also: Water leaks — fender and cabin ingress; Water leaks — cowl and hood intake drains; Water leaks — sunroof and roof drains; Water leaks — door seals and body sealing; Water leaks — trunk and rear door.

docs.title: Water leaks — sunroof and roof drains
docs.text:
Tags: #water-ingress · #sunroof · #cleaning

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Sunroof/roof drain channel clog — repair: water leaking into the cabin via roof/sunroof vents despite dry weather can be caused by (1) clogged roof drain channels that let water back-flow into the interior, or (2) plastic fittings/connectors (white tubes) pulling loose from porous rubber gaskets, letting water bypass the drain. Fix: insert a brush (1.5 m is sufficient) through the roof drain openings to clear debris; for loose fittings, remove the connector, clean the porous rubber gasket, apply silicone sealant, refit firmly, and seal the perimeter with additional silicone. Also periodically spray the sunroof seal with silicone lubricant for waterproofing 12345678910.

Roof-drain connection seal failure (passenger-side prone): a primary cause of cabin flooding — drain connections at the roof/windshield interface on both sides (passenger side particularly prone) become disconnected or loose, routing water into the interior. Located at the strut area below the windshield. Preventive fix: extend the drain hoses with additional tubing before leakage occurs; check both sides, since each has its own drain connection 1112131415.

Dashboard rattle near the defroster — loose sunroof drain cover clip: intermittent whistling/rattling from the defroster area while driving (not present with the fan alone) is often caused by a loose trim/drain-cover clip on the roof panel near the windshield — specifically the "жабо" (roof rain pan) cover clip at the windshield strut. It appears/disappears with vibration; a similar issue is reported at the right corner of the жабо panel 161718.

Sunroof drain — location and cleaning: the sunroof drain is located higher up, closer to the fender; use a flexible brush to clean the drain openings (available on AliExpress) 1920. If the sealant on the drain "mushroom" fitting looks intact but water still gets in, try: gently warm the area with a hair dryer (no overheating), then apply liquid rubber sealant; verify by pouring water on the sunroof or testing at a car wash 212223242526. If removing interior trim doesn't fix a leak, check the sunroof specifically and clean its drain holes with a flexible brush 272820.

Water under the driver's floor mat: often tied to a clogged sunroof drain — clean the drain tubes 2930. Separate cause: the sunroof drain fitting sits directly above the BSM (body security module) block — the fitting loosens slightly and water starts leaking inside. Fix: apply sealant to the fitting, and thoroughly soak the sunroof gasket with silicone. The BSM block itself can be opened and its terminals treated with contact cleaner for a water-repelling effect. Desiccants used to dry the cabin: feminine hygiene pads, cat-litter gel crystals, adult incontinence pads (dog-bed absorbent pads) — plus a powerful vacuum at a self-service car wash 313233343536.

Winter sunroof-drain-hose leak at wheel-well connections: in one case, sunroof drain hose connections at the wheel-well area leaked during winter — enough water accumulated to soak the carpets completely. Consequence: moisture reached the RKE (remote key entry) module's connectors, which corroded and later caused separate electrical issues (AKPP/automatic- transmission control errors). Fix: inspect and reseal the drain hose connections, verify correct drain routing 3738.

Leak through the sunroof drain-hole seal (degraded sealant): rain-time cabin leak from the area above the glass corner (where the drain tube opens). Fix: gently heat the area with a hair dryer (no overheating), apply liquid rubber sealant to the joint between the drain and the panel, verify with a hose/car-wash spray test 3919212223242526.

Sunroof-drain fitting misalignment — front passenger-floor leak: recurring water leaks under the front passenger floor mat traced to an improperly fitted sunroof drain-line connector (фитинг) on the driver side — the fitting holes were misaligned by ~0.5mm from the body attachment points, causing water to flow directly onto the mounting point instead of into the drain tube. Diagnosis: the sunroof drain line was leaking from under the weatherstrip seal despite previous sealing attempts. Fix: disassemble the drain-fitting area completely and re-seal with proper adhesive. Additionally, the BSM (body security module) block showed oxidation from water exposure — clean with contact cleaner to remove oxidation, then protect the contacts 404142.

Water pooling under floor carpets — roof/sunroof drain and dome-light gasket checklist: water accumulates under floor carpets and interior trim after rain/snow even with a functional engine and heater. Suspected sources: (1) blocked panoramic-roof/sunroof drain channels or plugged side-window drains; (2) sunroof seal degradation; (3) failed dome-light (interior light fixture) gasket; (4) clogged windshield-wiper channel drains. A secondary symptom is corrosion (green patina) on electrical connectors once water reaches them. Diagnostic steps: inspect sunroof/skylight seals and drain tubes, check the interior-light gaskets, clear all drains, and dry the interior thoroughly with heat; a professional inspection may be needed if a structural leak is suspected. ⚠️ Conflict: several owners report the same symptoms but disagree on root cause — some suspect sunroof drainage specifically, others point to general drain blockage or seal failure more broadly 434445464748495051525354.

DIY drain-cleaning tool: for clearing a blocked roof/sunroof drain (люк) or door-sill drainage holes, use a flexible drain brush from AliExpress (PlumHOUSE brand, ~112 RUB (RU market, April 2026), link: https://ali.click/fvvz51i). Similar cleaning procedures are demonstrated in YouTube videos for other vehicles (e.g. Mercedes, Volkswagen Teramont) and apply the same way to the X80's drains 5556.

Water leakage into cabin (2019–2020 models) — sunroof drain / sealing / ventilation-intake theories: a commonly reported issue on 2019–2020 model years: water accumulates and drains into the cabin rather than outside. Candidate root causes debated in the community: (1) sunroof frame drainage blockage near the perimeter; (2) poor sealant at the roofline-to-body junction; (3) rain being drawn in via the ventilation system during heavy downpours. Workaround: seal the roof edge with a waterproof paint tracer to help locate the entry point on follow-up inspection. Note: even a stationary, unused car can accumulate cabin water after just 3 days of rain 57585960616263646566. ⚠️ Conflict: no consensus was reached — sealant failure, intake ventilation design flaw, and structural gap were all proposed, with the group agreeing the fault is difficult to diagnose without a camera/tracer technique. Some attribute it specifically to a factory defect in model-year 2019.

Sunroof drain cleaning — brake-cable method: sunroof drain tubes can be cleaned from the interior using a brake cable (or similarly stiff wire) fed through the drain channels from the top opening, with the sunroof open. Work carefully — the drain tubes are loosely fitted and can disconnect if forced. This prevents water pooling in the roof area 6768.

Sunroof drain tubes not fully seated — hermetic sealant blocking insertion: a common defect where the drainage tubes from the sunroof/ hatch aren't pushed in all the way, letting water drip under the driver's and passenger's seats. Root cause: hermetic sealant applied on a nearby seam blocks the tubes from being fully inserted. Fix requires removing the fender for proper external access to reseat and reseal the tubes; sealing from inside the cabin is possible but difficult due to poor visibility and access 6970.

Roof-drain seal cracking at A-pillar plus A/C drain-tube extension — combined leak source: water pooling under the driver/passenger floor mats can stem from two independent sources found together: (1) the roof's water-drainage outlets at the A-pillar (front fender edge) use rubber seals that dry out and crack with age, letting water past the plastic interior drainage tubes; (2) the A/C drain tube under the hood needs to be extended for proper drainage away from the cabin. A dedicated drain-cleaning kit (soft brush + flexible tubing) is available for maintaining these drains, and owners can service both points themselves 717273747576.

See also: Water leaks — fender and cabin ingress; Water leaks — cowl and hood intake drains; Water leaks — footwell diagnosis and A/C drain.

docs.title: Water leaks — trunk and rear door
docs.text:
Tags: #water-ingress · #trunk · #molding

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Water in the trunk lid through the clip holes: after repainting the trunk lid, one owner found water entering specifically through the holes where the chrome-trim retaining clips are inserted — a known issue on the X80. Pushsalo (rust-proofing wax) in hidden cavities helps as general protection 12.

Rear door/trunk water pooling under the spare tire (2): water pools under the spare tire (10–20+ mL) even without opening the rear door, in heavy rain. Root causes include: a poor rear door/trunk seal, an incorrectly-seated door card trim, or possible leakage around the rear window molding / an incompletely sealed window. Diagnosis/fix: remove the door card, check the door seals for proper fit, check window-to-body panel gaps, and apply sealant where gaps are found. Test by pouring water with the door closed and the interior stripped 34567. ⚠️ Conflict: disagreement on the leak source — some owners report water entering only when the door is opened, others report leakage without opening the door at all (background infiltration through seals).

Water under the spare tire — broader diagnosis and repair cost: water accumulating under the spare-tire location can have multiple sources: a degraded door/boot seal allowing ingress when the door opens, failed clips/seals on the door molding (especially on restyle models), or leaking rear-light seals. Diagnostic method: spray water on the sealed car while watching from inside. Common fixes include re-sealing with silicone, replacing window-molding clips with better seals, and checking rear-light gaskets. Repair cost at a Moscow shop (AutoGermes): ~18,600 RUB for diagnosis plus full repair (RU market, November 2025) 8910111213141516171819202122232425.

Trunk and baggage-area water ingress — comprehensive diagnosis: common ingress sources in the trunk/baggage area: (1) loose or poorly-sealed rear window trim molding; (2) rear spoiler/trim clips where the original sealant has been removed; (3) door/frame gaps from sloppy reassembly. Puddles form in the spare-tire well and under door trim; water absorbs into the soundproofing material and slowly leaks internally. Fixes: reseal the molding clips, reapply gaskets, and check panel alignment. Rust can appear under the molding, but the body interior stays dry if properly sealed 2627282930313233343536.

Water pooling in the spare-tire well — multiple candidate entry points (December 2025 report): water was entering the spare-tire well; one owner sealed the clip joints in the trunk lid with sealant, which helped but only partially — root cause remained unclear. Recommended diagnostic tests: (1) spray water from a hose and watch for entry points; (2) check the rear-door drain (visible on the garage floor); (3) inspect the rear-window latch seal; (4) check for entry between the rear side panels. A separate owner used wide vinyl tape as a temporary fix for gaps in the chrome trim — this sealed the symptom (reported dry for 2 months afterward) but not the confirmed root cause 37383940414243444546.

Water in trunk side pockets and under the spare tire — 5th-door molding and ventilation: water accumulates in the side trunk pockets (карманы багажника) and under the spare-tire area after rain or washing (one report of ~5 liters). Primary cause: water enters under the rubber molding on the 5th door (trunk lid/liftgate). Fixes: (1) remove and re-seal the molding with silicone hermetic sealant; (2) improve ventilation by keeping the sunroof shutter cracked open; (3) remove the drain plugs from the underbody rails (корыта) to allow drainage and prevent pooling 47484950.

Water leak from rear door/5th-door molding clips after reinstallation: if the rear-door (5th door) molding is removed and reinstalled — for example after accident repair — water can leak into the trunk because the clips lose their tight fit once disturbed. Solution: remove the molding, apply hermetic sealant around it, and reinstall to restore a tight seal; consulting an experienced service is recommended for this repair 515253.

Water pooling in the rear cargo area under door seals: water accumulates in the rear cargo area, under the door seals and in the cup-holder recesses, during rain. Causes: poor condition of the rear door seal, and roof water drainage entering the interior. Fixes: (1) inspect and clean the rear door seal — soak it in kerosene if it has hardened, to restore elasticity; (2) drill drainage holes in the cargo floor pan with an angled outlet pipe; (3) maintain the roof drainage properly. Monitor nearby electrical boxes for corrosion as a consequence 54555657.

Trunk water leak from the rear-quarter-glass seal: water entering the trunk from the upper rear corner area (near the rear-quarter window) has been traced to a failed seal between the rear-quarter glass panel and its molding. Fix: apply black sealant/silicone caulk along the gap between the glass and the mounting frame. Some owners additionally apply weatherstripping tape (sourced from AliExpress) for extra protection 5859.

See also: Water leaks — fender and cabin ingress; Water leaks — door seals and body sealing; Water leaks — sunroof and roof drains.

docs.title: Windshield interior sun shade — model and dimensions
docs.text:
Tags: #windshield

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

An interior windshield sun shade model FW-X80-VCS fits the X80 windshield precisely. Dimensions: inner working area 1350 × 965 mm; outer base width 1406 mm 1.

Reinforcing measurement — height and part-designation variant: a second measurement confirms width 1406 mm (≈1.4 m) and gives height as approximately 980 mm (≈1 m) — close to, but not identical with, the 965 mm figure above (measurement method/reference point likely differs). For sun-shade fit, approximate usable dimensions are 1.3 m × 0.75 m. Part designation recorded as FW-X80-VCS LFW/X 23.

Independent dimension report — ~120 × 75 cm: a separate report gives windshield dimensions of roughly 120 cm × 75 cm for sun-shade selection purposes — in the same range as the figures above. Custom sun-shade "umbrellas" can be ordered to these dimensions from retailers such as Wildberries 45.

Dashboard sun shade (separate product) — AliExpress pricing: a dashboard sun shade (heat/UV insulation mat, decorative — distinct from the windshield-exterior shade above) is available on AliExpress for 2,710 RUB (RU market, June 2024), sold with a custom ornament pattern 67.

  • Automatic transmission (AKPP) — ATF fluid & intervals — Overview. The Aisin G09 / 09G (TF60/TF80) automatic transmission (AKPP) of the X80 takes ATF to the JWS-3309 spec. The factory manual calls the fill lifetime, but owners… (92 sources)
  • AKPP partial ATF change — drain plug, pan, mesh — The routine partial fluid change: draining through the bottom plug, optionally dropping the pan to clean the mesh, and refilling. (61 sources)
  • ATF fluid spec JWS-3309, brands and counterfeits — Which ATF the Aisin G09 automatic (and the power steering) takes, which brands owners buy or avoid, and how to spot fake fluid. (57 sources)
  • AKPP transmission filter — part number and cost — The AKPP transmission filter on the X80 (Aisin transmission) is a coarse-mesh steel strainer, not a fine-paper cartridge. It is an all-metal design: two cork gaskets… (56 sources)

docs.title: AKPP transmission filter — part number and cost
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The AKPP transmission filter on the X80 (Aisin transmission) is a coarse-mesh steel strainer, not a fine-paper cartridge. It is an all-metal design: two cork gaskets (glued), a steel mesh, and a metal frame.12345678910

Part number and pricing. AKPP filter artisan/part number: 35330-TFA060. Price ranged from 450 RUB (Chinese-site listing) up to 7,000–8,000 RUB from two other suppliers (RU market, September 2024) — a very wide spread, so it's worth shopping around.12345678910 A tested equivalent: MAHLE HX169KIT.12345678910 Other reported pricing: replacement oil filter for the AKPP starts around 440 RUB (also seen at 400 RUB from budget suppliers); a complete assembly with housing (filter + housing together) runs about 6,000 RUB (all RU market, November 2024).11121314 Separately, one owner cited approximately 2,000 RUB (RU market, October 2024) for filter replacement as part of a transmission service.15161718

Clean or replace? The metal frame and mesh itself last 50,000+ km; the friction/filtering material eventually wears and requires replacement. There's community debate: the filter can be washed/rinsed and reused, but several owners report finding significant abrasive debris in cleaned filters pulled from service, and recommend replacing rather than cleaning to avoid reintroducing contamination back into the transmission.1234567891015161718

Is it even necessary? Because it's a coarse mesh strainer rather than a fine filtration element, changing it during an oil service is considered optional, not mandatory, by several experienced owners — the decision depends on fluid condition and service history. It's not considered critical for minor highway use; more relevant under high-wear/heavy-use conditions.151617181920

Drain plug design and when to inspect the strainer (2025-07 report). The AKPP drain plug has a magnetic insert and should have a convex feature on the fitting; there's a plastic insert under the plug (pocketed/convex design) that should be inspected and replaced if damaged. The intake strainer/filter itself does not need routine changing unless mileage exceeds 30,000–40,000 km since the last change — if changed, inspect the mesh for metal particles indicating internal wear. No strict factory drain interval is documented, but a routine fluid change is recommended at 40,000+ km.21222324252627

Filter identification varies by transmission variant (2025-10 report). AKPP filters are not one-size-fits-all across the X80 lineup — owner photos show differing filter specifications by transmission type. Filters listed on Ozon are available, but buyers must confirm the listing matches their specific transmission variant before ordering; testing/fitment confirmation on the owner's own transmission is recommended rather than assuming compatibility.282930313233

Filter + gasket kit sourced from Ozon (2025-10 report). A combined filter-and-gasket kit purchased on Ozon was confirmed to fit and install successfully on the X80.343536

Independent re-confirmation of the KNECHT/MAHLE HX169KIT (2026-03 report). In a separate transmission-fluid discussion, a community member again recommended the KNECHT/MAHLE HX169KIT filter kit (includes pan gasket) as the correct AKPP filter+gasket combo, sourced from autorus.ru — corroborating the MAHLE HX169KIT equivalent noted above.37

Alternate cross-referenced filter part number — SM-24347566358/Sumomoto (2026-06 report). A separate community-reported filter part number: SM-24347566358 (Sumomoto brand), cross-referenced to OEM 24347566358, listed for FAW Besturn X80/X80F (and, per one marketplace listing, MINI COOPER — unverified cross-fitment claim). This is a different part number from the 35330-TFA060 documented above — treat the two numbers as reflecting different transmission sub-variants or supersessions until reconciled; buyers should confirm which one matches their specific transmission before ordering, consistent with the "not one-size-fits-all" note above. Recommended paired with ZIC ATF Multi HT (4L) fluid, replaced at every fluid-change service.38394041

HX169KIT gasket color and delivery experience (2024-08 report). One owner who installed the Mahle/Knecht HX169KIT (filter + gasket, in-the-box assembly, ~2,200 RUB, RU market, August 2024) reported the gasket fit well; a black gasket is generally preferred over the red OEM-spec gasket in the community's experience (see the pan-gasket sealant/fitment discussion on the automatic-transmission ATF card for the fuller red-vs-black debate). A Vagovskaya-brand alternative gasket was also reported to work well as a substitute. Confirm whether a listing is the filter alone or the full filter+gasket assembly before ordering — both are sold separately by some sellers.4243444546474849

"Wash it, don't replace it" — early corroborating Q&A (2026-02 report). When asked which filter is needed for the AKPP on a 2019 X80, one owner reiterated the community's standard practice already documented above: "properly, it's just washed and put back — it's a metal mesh, no point replacing it. If you're changing the fluid with the pan removed and the mesh cleaned, then you just need the gasket, that's all." This corroborates the clean-vs-replace debate and the "not mandatory" framing documented elsewhere on this card.5051

Video walkthrough — pan drop, magnet inspection, and mesh cleaning procedure (2026-07 report). A five-part video walkthrough documents the full pan-off service in practice, corroborating and illustrating the "wash, don't replace" procedure above step by step: (1) the drain/filler magnet collar and drain-plug bolt collect visible metal shavings/powder as debris settles out of the fluid over time — inspecting this is a quick health check on internal wear;5253 (2) once the pan is off, the black mesh strainer and a blue plastic drainage funnel/spout are exposed inside the pan;54 (3) the pan's connector area shows the internal wiring and structure around the fluid-level/temperature sensor that must be handled carefully during removal;55 (4) the drain/filler area uses plastic fitting components that should be reinstalled correctly to avoid leaks;56 (5) after removal, the mesh strainer is cleaned thoroughly with solvent before reassembly, consistent with the community's standard "clean, don't replace the mesh" practice documented above — only the gasket is a consumable in this procedure.5254555653

docs.title: ATF and power-steering fluid — Dexron III vs JWS3309
docs.text:
Tags: #atf · #transmission-fluid · #aisin

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The question. Which fluid goes into the X80 automatic transmission (automatic transmission, AKPP / АКПП) and the power-steering system (ГУР)? Arсhi 77 first said both take ATF Dexron III, and that a Mazda 6 GG-based rack takes Dexron III power-steering fluid; the ZIC ATF 3 datasheet he posted (GM Dexron III, Ford Mercon, Allison C-4, 36.9 cSt at 40 C, flash point 226 C) is labelled for power steering.12 Later he said Dexron 6 is better for an automatic and that his own car runs Mobil Multi ATF 3309, and that spec matters less for steering than for the engine.34

The opposing position. Victor says the owner's manual does not list Dexron III and that the fluid should meet JWS3309; ZIC ATF Multi HT carries JWS3309, but he says it is not labelled for steering.56 He adds that the fluid Arсhi 77 bought (Wildberries article 556540875) has no spec at all, and that power-steering fluid should meet JWS3309.57 The thread did not settle the spec; the AKPP fluid card and the ATF specification reference document JWS-3309 as the required approval for the automatic, and the power steering fluid service card covers the steering side.

Volume and price. The power-steering system takes about 0.8 L; one 1 L bottle was enough when the old fluid was flushed through gradually.7 A 4 L container was mentioned at a promo price of 1,800 RUB (RU market, Sep 2026) against about 4,500 RUB regular price elsewhere (RU market, Sep 2026).24

Practical case — Kixx ATF Multi JWS 3309 in the AKPP. Arсhi 77 filled his automatic with Kixx ATF Multi meeting JWS 3309: he bought 8 litres and did two partial drains and refills with a filter change, while many owners do a single drain of about 4 litres.8 Victor's rule is to use any fluid that meets the specification in the owner's manual.9

Owner's reading: ATF 3309 for gearbox and steering pump (2024). The owner (Oleg Belousov) says the Aisin-built automatic takes ATF 3309 (which he writes as "mobil 33-09" and calls the JWS type) and that the power-steering pump takes 3309 too; he says the dealers chose it for the tolerance the gearbox needs, and warns against topping up with another fluid and then calling the mix 3309. This is his own wording, so check the manual before buying fluid.101112

Reference: Audi 09G. A shared Audi service-training programme for the 6-speed 09G automatic lists ATF G 052 025 A2 or Esso JWS 3309 and a dry-fill volume of 7.0 L, filled for the life of the gearbox. It concerns the Audi gearbox and is not confirmed for the X80.13 For change intervals see the ATF interval and AISIN guidance card.

docs.title: ATF change interval — AISIN guidance, owner debate
docs.text:
Tags: #atf · #automatic-transmission · #aisin · #maintenance-interval · #transmission-fluid

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

AISIN guidance. AISIN, which supplies automatic transmissions (automatic transmission, AKPP / АКПП) to more than 40 carmakers, recommends changing the ATF (automatic transmission fluid) every 2 years or 20,000 km. Its reference chart notes that carmakers often suggest 60,000-80,000 km or a lifetime fill, and AISIN considers those intervals too long for the conditions it assumes. A drain-and-fill replaces only about 2 litres, because the rest stays in the torque converter and the pan; AISIN's equipment instead pumps the old fluid out hydraulically and replaces it with new fluid.1 The chart does not list the X80 fluid, so check the owner's manual or the dealer; see the ATF specification reference and the JWS3309 vs Dexron card.1

Warning signs in the fluid. New ATF is red and darkens after about 20,000 km of normal use. The chart lists three contamination signs: metal debris (abrasion, the transmission needs repair), high temperature (wet-clutch slip), and a milky, paste-like look (water has entered the transmission, repair needed).1

Owners disagree on intervals. One commenter quotes Aisin's 20,000 km or 2 years for hot climates and ZF's 80,000-100,000 km.2 The owner (Oleg Belousov) argues the gearbox has a fixed designed wear life and more frequent changes will not extend it; KASPER counters that changes every 20-40k km let gearboxes last far beyond 250k km (citing a 700k km example) and calls a partial change every 40k km a sensible middle ground.34 The official X80 manual only asks for a level check every 30,000 km; compare the dealer 60k/120k advice on the transmission fluid intervals card.

Partial change in steps (owner practice). The owner drains about 3-4 litres through the drain plug and refills through the fill port, repeating this about every 40,000 km rather than doing a full drain; the gearbox holds about 4.5 litres. When he opened the pan at 200,000 km the filter mesh and magnet were in good shape with only fine deposits, so he replaced the filter and gasket. He says a partial change at each service is the usual approach for higher-mileage cars.567

Cost of pan gasket and filter. The owner puts the gearbox pan gasket and filter together at about 1,000-2,200 RUB (RU market, Sep 2024), a loose figure, and suggests buying them together with the fluid.8 For the filter itself see the AKPP filter card; the long fluid thread is on the AKPP ATF card.

docs.title: ATF fluid spec JWS-3309, brands and counterfeits
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission · #atf · #aisin · #counterfeit · #power-steering

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Which ATF the Aisin G09 automatic (and the power steering) takes, which brands owners buy or avoid, and how to spot fake fluid.

Fluid specification. The Aisin G09 / 09G automatic transmission (also referred to in the community as Aisin TF60/TF80) requires ATF-MV, spec JWS-3309. This spec is mandatory for both the automatic transmission (АКПП) and the power steering (ГУР) — a "universal" ATF without the 3309 spec is not compatible and should not be used. OEM factory fill in the power steering is Idemitsu brand.1234567891011 Multiple brands meet the JWS-3309 spec, not just Mobil — but quality varies significantly and counterfeit fluid exists, especially sold as Mobil.1213141516171819202122

Power steering (ГУР) and AKPP fluid spec — factory fill color varies (2025-06, documented disagreement). GUR (power steering) and AKPP use the same compatible fluid, spec JWS-3309. Factory fills vary between individual cars: some X80s ship with red "universal" 3309 fluid in both systems; others ship with green Ford-MV-type fluid in the GUR specifically. Some owners have since switched to Dexron III. No single documented manufacturer preference exists across the community's reports — a change/inspection is recommended to verify what's actually in your car. Multi ATF JWS-3309 from the CHEMPIOIL brand is available on Wildberries.2324252627282930313233

AKPP fluid brands and pricing, with counterfeit warning (2025-06 report). Recommended ATF-3309 brands beyond Mobil: Manol 3309, and ZIC ATF Multi HT (specifically marked as a 3309 equivalent). Cost varies by retailer. Caution: verify certificates and sealed metal containers with multiple seals/codes to confirm authenticity — cheaper sources or unmarked "universal" fluids have reportedly turned out to contain transformer oil rather than genuine transmission fluid.343536373839

Fluid quality — synthetic vs. lower-grade, burn-rate comparison (2025-06 report). One owner compared several ATF fluids through sequential partial changes: ZIC x9 (lower quality — turned dark brown/burnt after only 6,000 km, some oil-burn smell); Genesis + Manol 3309 (newer fill — smoother shifts, better perceived quality); HELIX (previous fill — had degraded). Conclusion: genuine ATF-3309-branded fluids (Genesis, Manol) outperformed multi-purpose substitutes in this owner's observation — the burn rate is directly observable when doing a partial fluid exchange, with premium fluids showing markedly less discoloration/burn.40414243444546

Power steering fluid color re-confirmed as red ATF (2026-03 corroboration). A separate, shorter exchange re-confirms the power steering fluid type is ATF, generally expected to be red, with Mobil 3309 again named as an acceptable brand — consistent with (and a smaller corroborating data point for) the fuller color-variance discussion above.474849505152 Separately, an owner (Victor) mentioned changing the power steering (ГУР) fluid himself as a DIY task, in the context of comparing it favorably against a shop's high labor quote for an unrelated suspension-arm job — a small corroborating data point that owners do perform the GUR fluid change themselves, not only the AKPP change (2026-08 report).53

Spec confirmation and service labor cost (2025-10 reports). Automatic transmission fluid should carry JWS3309 approval/certification for the X80.54 Separately, transmission fluid change labor was quoted at 3,000 RUB (RU market, October 2025).55 Power steering (ГУР) fluid is confirmed to be the same as AKPP fluid: JWS3309 Type IV.5657

See also: Automatic transmission (AKPP) — ATF fluid & intervals; AKPP partial ATF change — drain plug, pan, mesh; AKPP ATF service prices and shops; ATF and power-steering fluid — Dexron III vs JWS3309.

docs.title: AKPP fluid level check — plug, tube, temperature
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission · #atf · #drain-plug · #temperature

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Setting and checking the ATF level: the thin-stream test at the drain plug, the measuring/overflow tube, working temperatures and part numbers.

Fluid level check — from below only (2025-05 report). Check transmission fluid level only from underneath the car. With the engine running and fluid at operating temperature (35–45°C), unscrew the drain plug/pan: a thin steady drip means correct level; no fluid/only a trickle means underfilled; fluid pouring out like an open faucet means overfilled. The car must be level (not on a slope) before checking.1234

Drain-plug + measuring-cup/tube sequence (2026-05 report). To drain: (1) unscrew the drain plug first — a small stream begins; (2) unscrew the measuring cup/tube located at the same point — a larger stream follows. The measuring tube may be plastic and wears with age; the metal, opaque cup portion serves as the oil-measurement indicator. One community member noted the tube may be integrated with the pan on some variants.5678

Measuring/dipstick tube (мерная трубка) — sourcing, part numbers, and a contradiction worth flagging (2026-06 report). Despite the "X80 has no transmission dipstick" claim documented in the partial-change procedure card, later community threads describe and source a measuring/level tube for the 09G AISIN automatic by name — treat the two claims as reflecting different transmission variants/model years until reconciled. Sourcing options reported: (1) Avito marketplace, searching "09G AISIN measuring tube"; (2) abtomat.ru, part code 15765DT; (3) RuLi/AliExpress auto-parts listings. Tube length varies — three different lengths exist (41mm, 46mm, 50mm); the X80 is reported to need the smallest (~35–41mm depending on the specific report). Ozon pricing (RU market, June 2026): approximately 1,500 RUB. A partial-drain service that doesn't remove the pan cannot access this tube — the tube stays stuck/inaccessible from the top; a full pan removal is required for any service that involves replacing it.9101112131415161718192021222324

Fluid check without pan removal — 3L capacity confirmation (2024-08 reports). For drain-and-fill without removing the pan, capacity is approximately 3 liters. Level check via the drain tube: fluid should flow slightly, not drip, when cold; excessive flow indicates overfill. One community member's clarifying note: the tube used for level-check/refill without pan removal is the drain/fill tube, not a true dipstick — draining and topping off by level is done through it.252627282930

Two distinct level-checking methods — side plug vs. tube in pan (2026-08 report). Валерий raised a question in the community: he had learned there are two different ways owners check the АКПП fluid level on this Aisin-type automatic — via the side plug (боковая пробка) or via a tube inside the pan (трубочка в поддоне) — and asked which one is actually correct for the X80.31 Che Guevara replied that a service station ("сто") told him the tube-in-pan method is specifically what's used to set/establish the correct fluid level (i.e., it is the calibrated reference, not just an alternative check point).32 Konstantin pushed the reasoning further: if the side plug alone were the correct check, there would be no purpose in having a tube in the pan at all — implying the side plug is not a reliable stand-alone level check on this transmission.33 Caution: treat the side plug as a drain/access point only, not as the level-setting reference — using it to judge "full" without accounting for the tube-in-pan calibration risks overfilling the transmission. This exchange has not been independently corroborated beyond the three participants; treat as a documented community discussion rather than a settled procedure.

See also: Automatic transmission (AKPP) — ATF fluid & intervals; AKPP partial ATF change — drain plug, pan, mesh; ATF partial vs full exchange and volumes.

docs.title: AKPP pan gasket, filter and part numbers
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Pan gasket and filter parts for the AKPP service: part numbers, sourcing, the sealant debate and fitting checks.

Pan-gasket sealant debate (2024-05, early community discussion). During a partial AKPP fluid change with pan removal, some owners apply a thin bead of high-temperature sealant (гермети́к) along the pan-gasket perimeter as extra insurance against leaks — recommended especially once a gasket has already been through several previous changes. Others push back hard: excess sealant ("излишки") can break off inside the pan and cause internal damage, and a new, properly-torqued gasket should seal on its own without any sealant — one experienced owner has done 2 gasket changes with zero sealant and no leaks. Where sealant is used, the consensus is: apply only a thin bead on the outer perimeter, never coat the whole face, and use a genuine high-temperature product (not a ~200 RUB bargain tube, RU market, May 2024).123456789101112

AKPP fluid + filter combo used in one service (2026-05 report). Fluid: ZIC ATF Multi HT (4L). Filter: SM-24347566358 (Sumomoto), cross-referenced as OEM 24347566358, listed for FAW Besturn X80/X80F and (per the seller listing) also MINI COOPER — treat the MINI COOPER cross-reference as an unverified marketplace claim, not a confirmed fitment test. Filter replacement was recommended at every fluid-change service in this report.13141516

Pan-gasket part-number reconciliation, spacer-height check, and delivery timeline (2024-08/2026-06 reports). Two separate OEM-adjacent pan-gasket part numbers are documented across community threads for this transmission: 35168-TFA050 (referenced repeatedly in this series of cards) and 09G321370 — the latter sourced from a VW Polo listing (09G-platform commonality) and priced at approximately 700 RUB on Ozon (RU market, June 2026); needed whenever the pan is dropped for a dipstick-tube swap or a full-pan fluid service. When installing a new gasket, verify the new gasket's spacer-tube height against the original (±1mm tolerance) with calipers before final torque — if the new gasket's tubes are taller than the originals they can act as a stop and cause improper sealing; the fix is to reuse the original gasket's tubes/spacers, or bed the new gasket on silicone sealant if a height mismatch is found. Typical gasket/repair-kit delivery time reported: ~7 days from order to arrival, with installation and fluid change completed in one service visit.17181920

Pan-gasket sourcing link and "mesh, not filter" reminder (2024-07 report). A pan-gasket sourcing link was shared for kitzapchasti.ru (pre-facelift/dorest automatic). Community reminder: during a pan-drop service, what gets cleaned is the coarse mesh screen, not a paper filter — buy the gasket and fresh fluid; fluid choice itself is treated as subjective by the community (hard to verify burn/consumption without long-term testing).212223242526

Gasket is optional for a simple top-up (2024-03, earliest community reference for the 35168-TFA050 part). The 35168-TFA050 pan gasket is inexpensive; it's only actually needed if you're planning to drop the pan to inspect/clean the mesh filter. For a simple partial top-up (no pan removal), there's no need to buy the gasket at all. Part sourced via kitzapchasti.ru (listing: "35168-TFA050 — prokladka poddona AKPP FAW Besturn X80").27
