For engine misfire/knock ("тройит") diagnostics: - Private/independent shops: ~2,500 RUB (RU market, October 2024; cheaper option; includes computer diagnostics).12 - Official dealers: 4,500 RUB (RU market, October 2024) — comparison point cited: Автогермес (Moscow) at 4,500 RUB.2 - Endoscope inspection of individual cylinders (to visually check for damage): 750 RUB per cylinder (RU market, October 2024), plus disassembly/reassembly labor on top.3

Community assessment: 2,500 RUB (RU market, October 2024) for basic computer diagnostics at an independent shop is considered reasonable ("побожески") compared to dealer pricing.2

docs.title: Engine oil change interval — heavy-duty usage
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-oil

A high-utilization owner (working vehicle, 10+ hours/day usage, 1,000+ km/week) reports needing engine oil changes every 4,000–8,000 km instead of standard highway-driving intervals. This owner needed two oil changes in a single summer season due to intensive city driving combined with highway work. The takeaway: regular, more frequent fluid changes are what keep the car reliable under commercial/heavy-duty use conditions — don't apply passenger-car service intervals to a working vehicle.1

docs.title: Engine oil change — filter, plug, and DIY tools
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-oil · #oil-filter · #drain-plug · #part-number · #tools · #conflict

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Oil filter design. The X80 engine uses a mesh-type oil filter element, not a traditional paper cartridge — it acts as a coarse strainer rather than fine filtration. Flushing/blowing out the mesh is sufficient maintenance; replacing it at every oil change offers minimal benefit according to professional shop feedback, since the reusable mesh design is intentional.1234

Oil filter brand options (for those who prefer disposable cartridge-style filters or the separate filter housing). Recommended quality brands: Mahle (model OC1182, ~457 RUB on Ozon as of Nov 2024, RU market), Mann, Zekert (model OF-4196, compatible with Mazda applications), and SCT (model SM196, German brand, reported working well). Community consensus: don't economize on the filter — Mahle and Mann are preferred for quality.567891011121314

Complete filter/service kit pricing. A complete Zekkert kit (air, oil, and cabin filters together) cost approximately 1,300 RUB with Moscow delivery (RU market, September 2024). Part numbers visible on the packaging: 1377010L and 7340010A-J-TW.15

Drain plug — magnetic vs. plain. For the engine oil drain plug, a magnetic plug is preferred over a plain one — it collects metal particles from normal engine wear, which helps detect abnormal wear patterns over time by inspecting what the magnet has caught.1617

Drain plug washer/gasket. Part number 100902337K, 20mm diameter, roughly 30 RUB (RU market, November 2024) — shared between FAW Besturn X40 and X80. Should be replaced at every oil change. Copper washers should be heated to red-hot with a torch before installation (to anneal/soften the copper for a proper seal); aluminum washers do not need heating. Generic copper washers matching the diameter work as lower-cost alternatives — roughly 150 RUB (RU market, November 2024) vs. up to 1,500 RUB for the OEM part (RU market, November 2024).181920212223242526272829

Oil extraction (siphon) pump — DIY tool. For extracting engine oil or transmission fluid via the dipstick tube (when drain-plug removal is difficult or undesired), a 12V/100W electric siphon pump is available on Ozon, sold with a carrying case, clips, and suction tubes.303132

Oil filter orientation and anti-drainback valve (2025-04 discussion, unresolved). The oil filter on the X80 mounts upside-down (vertical installation, reversed from the more common orientation). This raised a community question about whether the filter element contains an anti-drainback valve — standard filters normally include this valve to prevent oil from siphoning back out of the filter when the engine is off, and its presence/absence matters more when the filter is mounted in a non-standard orientation. The question was raised but not conclusively answered in the thread.3334

Oil filter outlet hole count (2025-08 report). When choosing a replacement filter, check the number of outlet holes on the base plate — X80-compatible filters should have 6 outlet holes, not 4; the hole count matters more for proper oil distribution than the brand itself. Zekkert and Stellox are both cited as acceptable brands, provided the hole count is correct.3536

Total drain volume and un-pumpable residue (2025-09 report). A genuinely complete oil change moves more fluid than a dipstick-tube pump alone can extract. One owner's breakdown on the 2.0L engine: dipstick-pump extraction 3.7 L, residue from the filter + fuel-pump circuit 0.2 L, drain-plug drain 0.1 L — total 4.0 L. The dipstick sight-glass tube doesn't reach the lowest point of the sump, leaving roughly 0.2 L that the dipstick pump alone cannot reach — a truly complete change needs the drain plug opened, not just dipstick extraction. After 8,400 km on Sintec 9000 5W-30 A3/B4, the drained oil looked brown/dark but engine operation was unaffected.3738394041

More oil filter brand options (2025-10/11 reports). Beyond the Mahle/Mann/Zekert/SCT list above, the community also recommends Hengst H90W27 and Mazda S550143029A (cross-reference equivalents searchable on Autodoc.ru) — prioritize a filter with an integrated bypass valve and slightly oversized capacity versus OEM.4243444546 LYNXauto LC1602 is separately reported to fit the X80 and its Mazda-platform relatives (Mazda 2/Demio, 3, 5, 6, CX-3, CX-5, CX-7, MX-5) and the Nissan Lafesta; one owner uses only this brand across his cars and reports consistently good quality.4748

Oil condition and interval disagreement at 108,500 km (2025-09 report, conflict). One owner documented oil condition with four photos after 10,000 km of service on 5W-40 synthetic, at a total mileage of 108,500 km: moderate darkening (yellow/brown hue) on cylinder-head aluminum surfaces after running, but no premature deposits visible. Conflict: Олег К recommends shorter 7,000–8,000 km change intervals for this engine, while other owners (including Victor and a second commenter) maintain that 10,000 km is appropriate — and the actual oil-condition photos in this report suggest 10,000 km intervals were acceptable for this particular user's conditions. Both positions are reported here without adjudication.495051

docs.title: Engine oil selection — grades and brands
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-oil · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Official dealer fill: LUKOIL GENESIS SPECIAL SPX 5W40.12345678910111213141516

Grade recommendation. Multiple owners successfully use LUKOIL GENESIS ARMORTECH — both 5W-30 and 5W-40 (fully synthetic, API SP/CF, sold under the "SP-RC" classification in some listings). Common recommendation: 5W-40 for summer, 5W-30 for winter, to reduce engine noise and improve cold-start behavior. Several owners who switched from 5W-40 (red bottle) to 5W-30 (green bottle) for winter reported a noticeably quieter engine; one owner at 50,000 km made this switch and confirmed the quieter running.1718192021222324252627282930 The community notes some mixed results with the ARMORTECH CN 5W-40 (red) purchased from Wildberries, with concerns about counterfeits circulating on that channel — verify the API classification (SP/CF) printed on the canister and buy from authorized channels where possible.12345678910111213141516

Base stock / Euro 5 note. Major lubricant manufacturers (Mobil, Shell, Lukoil, Idemitsu) supply base oils that get repackaged under multiple brands. Euro 5 standards require specific oil characteristics matched by the additive package per manufacturer specification — cheaper "synthetic" oils may lack a proper additive package for genuine Euro 5 compliance. The X80 may use oils built on Lukoil base stock formulations, the same base stock reportedly used in some Lexus/Mercedes applications. Always cross-check the owner's manual for the required viscosity and performance spec before buying on price alone.31323334

Brand experience — Mobil vs. alternatives (conflict documented). One experienced owner (238,000 km) reports Mobil performs best on the X80: quieter engine, smoother cold start at 0°C, faster warm-up than Repsoil and Volvoil (both tried and found inferior). Oil darkening after ~1,000 km was observed and considered normal, showing good carbon-cleaning ability. On a previous Nissan, this owner got 8,000 km on Mobil without needing to top up, versus needing a top-up every 2,000 km on other oils tried. Conflict: other community members are satisfied using LUKOIL instead of Mobil — preference may be partly subjective, though Mobil is specifically praised here for cold-start behavior and reduced noise.353637

KIXX 5W-40 consumption issue. One owner reports KIXX 5W-40 showing excessive oil consumption (noticeably dropping level) at high mileage (115,000 km+). Comma XFlow 5W-40 is recommended by the community as a superior alternative with lower consumption in the same conditions.383940

Korson brand. One owner in Siberia recommends Korson motor oil, reporting acceptable oil-level retention between changes through winter driving, at a cost of roughly 40,000–50,000 RUB per oil-change interval (RU market, April 2024) (bulk purchase context unclear). The same oil was also tested by this owner on a Toyota Vitz (170,000 km) without smoking or burning issues.414243

Takayama Adaptec — another commonly used brand (2025-03 report). Takayama Adaptec oils are commonly used by X80 owners: 5W-30 (API SP, ILSAC GF-6A) and 5W-40 (API SN/CF, ACEA A3/B4). Pricing: Takayama Adaptec 5W-40 synthetic, 5L, 2,536 RUB (4+1 promotion, originally 5,200 RUB, Russian market, March 2025). Syntek is another popular brand with owners reporting reliable performance at 5,000–6,000 km change intervals. Typical oil prices for a 4L set range 1,900–2,300 RUB (RU market, March 2025). Note: Rowe 9000 (multi-spec) exists on the market but may have compatibility issues with the AKPP automatic transmission fluid if cross-used — verify spec before substituting.44454647484950

Oil condition at 6,000 km — Suntec 9000 5W30 (2025-07 report). One owner's dipstick check showed Suntec 9000 5W30 A3/B4 still dark/clean-looking after a 6,000 km interval, with the engine (53k total km) in good condition and normal wear patterns visible.51

Consumption comparison across brands (2025-07 report). Sintec oil was reported to cause engine deposits after 4+ years of continuous use (considered detrimental long-term). VMP 10W-40 showed minimal consumption over 8,000 km change intervals. ELF and Motul (quality-tier brands) performed well. Lukoil, used for 6 years by one owner, left higher deposits but the engine still worked fine. Note: oil-level drop at sustained high speed (110+ km/h) and high sustained temperature is normal evaporation, not necessarily engine oil burn-down — cheaper oils tend to show worse consumption patterns overall.52535455565758596061626364656667686970

More brand reports (2025-08, community poll). Recommended options mentioned in an August 2025 discussion: Genesis Special SPX 5W-40 (repeatedly recommended, matches the official dealer fill noted above), Idemitsu (~5,000 RUB/4L, RU market, August 2025), Lukoil, Gazprom, and ZIC X7 (one owner has run it continuously since the initial "0" service). Mirax 0W-30 was named as a very cheap option (1,750 RUB/5L, RU market, August 2025). A specific purchase example: one owner bought ZIC X7 in November 2023 for 1,200 RUB/liter (RU market, Ozon, seller UPEC) and reported excellent engine quietness after 7,700 km, at 55,000 km total engine mileage. Community advice repeated in this thread: verify the oil meets the FAW specification and suits the engine's mileage before buying.717273747576777879808182

GENESIS SPECIAL SPX 5W-40 — separate OEM confirmation (2025-09 report). A community member reports that official Mazda dealerships in Moscow use the same GENESIS SPECIAL SPX 5W-40 oil noted above as the FAW dealer fill, reinforcing it as an OEM-level-approved choice; multiple owners report "all good" results with this viscosity grade.83

Totachi — metal-canister recommendation (2025-09 report). Totachi oil in metal canisters is recommended by community members as a way to sidestep counterfeiting risk: metal containers are harder and more expensive to counterfeit than plastic ones. One owner notes Totachi is "significantly cheaper" than some premium brands (naming "Luckily" as one comparison) with comparable perceived durability; another recommends metal-can Totachi specifically for its 1,500–2,000 RUB price point.848586

NGN — dual-use engine and gearbox oil (2025-09 report). NGN, a Russian-manufactured oil, is used by at least one owner in both the engine and the gearbox ("in the motor and the box"). Available on Ozon.ru.8788

TEBOIL DIAMOND pricing (2025-09/20 report). TEBOIL DIAMOND 5W-30 synthetic (Finland), 4L: 821 RUB on Ozon using seller promotional points (250-point discount, Sept 20 2025) — versus a standard price of 1,670 RUB noted two weeks earlier. TEBOIL DIAMOND FS 5W-30 (A5/B5 spec) is also available for owners who prefer that specification. Sold by an official Ozon seller matching Teboil's own website store.899091

Counterfeit risk and sourcing (2025-10 report). Counterfeit motor oil is common on marketplaces (Ozon, WildBerries) — reported fakes include Genesis, Lukoil, and Kixx. Symptoms of counterfeit oil: unusually thin viscosity, excessive consumption (one report of ~200 g per 3,000 km), and rough/hard engine running. Community recommendation: buy from authorized gas-station retailers or the official channels listed on the manufacturer's own website — cost is higher, but counterfeit risk is essentially eliminated.9293949596

More brand/price data points (2025-10/11 reports). SINTEC ExtraLife 7000 5W-30 (SL/CF, synthetic, 4L) and the heavier 5W-40 (SN/CF) variant are both available on WildBerries with periodic manufacturer discounts. LUKOIL Armortech CN 5W-40 (synthetic, 4L) was seen at 1,199 RUB (RU market) planned for a November 2025 Ozon promotion. General advice: compare WildBerries/Ozon prices against gas-station prices before buying.979899100 Separately, in November 2025: Ozon pricing around ~4,000 RUB, Avtorusy around ~5,700 RUB (RU market); Belarusian Rosneft oil was recommended as a budget alternative (one owner runs it every 7–10 thousand km), and Obninsk-brand oil was cited as roughly 3× cheaper than metal-can premium oils. Reinforcing the counterfeit-risk note above: the community favors metal cans over plastic for lower counterfeiting risk.101102103104105106

TOTACHI Hyper Ecodrive 5W-30 (API SP / ILSAC GF-6), conflict documented (2025-11 report). TOTACHI Hyper Ecodrive 5W-30 synthetic (4L) is recommended by multiple owners with good engine performance and no reported oil consumption.107108109110 Conflict: one owner (Сергей Надёжкин) tried it and reported a louder cold start and oil consumption, then switched to a different brand — contradicting the otherwise-positive community experience with this oil.111

VMPAUTO modern SP 5W-30 — alternative brand (2025-11 report). VMPAUTO modern SP 5W-30 synthetic (5L) is available on Ozon and recommended by one community member as an alternative option.112113

Kixx and Zic — two more owners confirm reliability (2026-02 report). One owner has used Kixx 5W-30 SN for about two years with no issues; Kixx G1 5W-30 was priced around 2,835 RUB on Ozon (RU market, Feb 2026). Zic was also mentioned as a working alternative in the same thread. Community view: with regular interval discipline, the specific reputable brand matters less than sticking to the schedule.114115116117

MANNOL Energy Formula FR 5W-30 — 3-year track record (2026-02 report). A separate owner reports 3 years of continuous use of MANNOL Energy Formula FR 5W-30 fully-synthetic oil with no oil consumption or problems; multiple other community members confirmed similarly good long-term reliability with this oil on X80 engines.118119120121

Reported oil spec — "Chery 5W-30", Mobil 3309 as an alternative (2026-03 report). One owner names "Chery 5W-30" as their recommended engine oil, with Mobil 3309 cited as an acceptable alternative. Note this "3309" reference overlaps with the ATF-spec figure used elsewhere in the KB for AKPP/power-steering fluid — treat this specific engine-oil mention with caution and verify against the owner's manual before buying.122

Viscosity selection by mileage — community rule of thumb (2026-03 report). Recommended approach: 5W-30 for lower-mileage engines (under ~90,000 km) or an engine in good condition; switch to 5W-40 at higher mileage (over ~130,000 km) if the engine starts consuming oil slightly. Any synthetic meeting SN+ or SP is considered acceptable — Lukoil, VMP, and Polimerium were named as the most consistently reliable domestic options. Given the X80's naturally-aspirated, low-compression, older-design engine, the community view is that expensive premium branding matters less than matching the correct spec and viscosity to mileage. Conflict: one owner reported valve-tap noise on cold start after switching to 5W-40 at 90,000 km, suggesting the switch-over point may need to be later or more conservative for some engines.123124125126127128129130131132133134135

FAW genuine 5W-40 (G0540SNA40C) — one reported issue (2026-03 report). FAW's own-brand synthetic 5W-40, OEM part number G0540SNA40C, sells for about 1,789 RUB on Ozon (RU market, March 2026). One owner reports this specific oil caused audible valve-tap noise at engine start on their car — consistent with the wider community debate above about the 5W-30-to-5W-40 switch-over point.136137138

NGN 5W-30 — additional positive review (2026-03 report). A second, independent report on NGN 5W-30 synthetic (see also the dual-use engine/gearbox note above) describes quieter engine operation and an appropriate viscosity feel after switching to it; available on Ozon.139

Budget synthetic sighting, repeat data point (May 2026). The Ozon-sourced Finnish synthetic oil noted above (TEBOIL DIAMOND, old pre-2022 stock) was again seen at 821 RUB (RU market) in May 2026, corroborating the September 2025 price point — the seller is described as an official store. A separate owner mentioned a rough per-liter price benchmark of roughly 1.5 RUB/ml (~1,500 RUB/L) (RU market, May 2026) for comparison shopping.140141

Engine oil capacity and fill-quantity practice (2026-04 report). Spec capacity is 4.3 L. In practice, a 4.0–4.3 L range is considered acceptable — many owners run a single 4L canister with no top-up and report no issues or excess consumption. Regional guidance: in hotter climates, follow the full 4.3 L spec rather than the lower end of the range (an owner who under-filled and drove hard between changes pulled a dry-ish dipstick reading slightly below minimum, though nothing critical resulted). One owner successfully ran Totachi HYPER EcoDrive 5W-30 (API SP, ILSAC GF-6A, marketed as gasoline/diesel-compatible, 100% claimed original) with no issues after extended use.142143144145146147148149150151152153154155

Market price snapshot for 5W-30 grades, X80 2.0 NA (2026-06 report). Recommended grade for the naturally-aspirated 2.0: 5W-30, SL or better. Market prices as of June 2026 (RU market): Gazprom Neft 5W-30 A5 (seasonal/winter option); Teboil 5W-30 SL (Finland) — previously ~820 RUB/4L on promotion (RU market; as of the June 2026 report) (corroborating the earlier TEBOIL DIAMOND price points above); Takayama Adaptec 5W-30 synthetic (metal canister, higher cost — corroborates the Takayama brand already documented above); Mirax MX7 (API SP, ACEA A5/B5) 5W-30 at 1,700 RUB/5L (a simpler/cheaper spec); Liqui Moly 5W-30 molybdenum at approximately 8,000 RUB total including oil + filter replacement labor. One owner (Victor) advises against GF-5-only oils, citing shorter service life (~5,000–7,000 km). Many owners in this thread mix brands experimentally rather than sticking to one.156157158159160161162163164165

API/ACEA specification compliance — false-economy warning (2026-06 report). Using a motor oil that meets the X80 engine's actual API/ACEA specification matters — an oil that works fine in a different brand's engine is not automatically safe here if it doesn't meet the X80's requirements (Liqui Moly 5W-30 was cited as an example needing proper spec matching). Skipping spec compatibility to save money is considered false economy by the community — non-compliant oil risks engine damage. Typical all-in cost for a properly spec'd oil change (oil + filter + labor): ~7,000–8,000 RUB (RU market, June 2026).165

Consumption comparison — VMP Avto, Tatneft, Taneco (2024-03 report). One owner reports VMP Avto premium synthetic (~2,800 RUB/5L, RU market, March 2024) shows essentially zero consumption over 6,000 km. By contrast, Tatneft conventional oil showed a level drop requiring top-up after only ~5,000 km on the same owner's car. Taneco Premium Ultra Eco Synth 5W-30 was separately rated positively in independent oil-club.ru forum testing. Community 4-liter price range at the time: 2,700–3,150 RUB (RU market, March 2024). General takeaway: premium synthetic is preferable for owners running longer change intervals, since different oils show meaningfully different burn/consumption rates even within a single ownership.166167168169170171172

Lukoil Genesis ArmorTech 5W-40 — "for Chinese cars" formulation (2024-08 report). Lukoil Genesis ArmorTech 5W-40, marketed specifically as formulated for Chinese-brand vehicles (labeled "FOR CHINESE CARS"/CN designation on the bottle), meets API SP/CF and ACEA A3/B4. Multiple owners report satisfactory performance; Lukoil's published spec sheet cites a high TBN (total base number) of 9.94 mg KOH/g, supporting good anti-wear and detergency performance. Well-received by the community as a reliable OEM-equivalent choice — this is a separate product from the GENESIS SPECIAL SPX 5W-40 already documented above as the official dealer fill.173174175176177178179

Additional recommended-brands roundup (2024-08 report). Further community-reported oils with good results, supplementing the brand list already on this card: Valvoline, Liqui Moly, Rowe, Rein Well; VMPAUTO 5W-30 (synthetic, reported zero sludge); Comma XFlow (corroborates the earlier Comma XFlow recommendation above); Zic X5 5W-40; Totachi EcoDrive 5W-40 (sealed tin, imported via Kazakhstan from Japan, higher cost, reported good engine performance — a separate product line from Totachi HYPER EcoDrive noted above). Previously popular but now harder to find: Shell Eco 5W-40; long-standing standard: Idemitsu 5W-30 in a tin container. Brands the community advises avoiding: Gazpromneft and Kixx, both cited for high oil burn (corroborating the earlier KIXX 5W-40 consumption complaint documented above). Typical seasonal range recommended: 5W-30 to 5W-40 depending on availability.180181182183184185186187

Further brand corroboration and a 195,000 km reliability anecdote (2026-01 report). Lukoil Armortech JP 5W-30 synthetic was named directly by one owner as their go-to oil, reporting "no problems" with it;188189190 a separate owner at 195,000 km on regular oil changes reports having done no additional engine cleaning work in that entire distance beyond a throttle-body service, corroborating the "regular oil changes prevent major work" pattern documented elsewhere on this card;191 and two more owners name their own working choices in the same thread — any decent-brand 5W-40 works fine for one owner,192 while another runs Mobil 5W-30, noting 5W-40 is presumably thicker/heavier.193 Separately, Genesis 5W-30 for Ford was named by one owner as the best oil option they'd found for the X80, reporting excellent in-vehicle performance.194 Low-confidence, single-source anecdote on engine robustness: the same owner reports accidentally mixing roughly 15 liters of diesel into the gasoline tank and driving on the mixture with no engine problems — offered as informal evidence of engine tolerance, not a recommended practice.195

docs.title: Engine oil viscosity debate and owner interval
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-oil · #conflict

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Viscosity debate: 20 or 30? One member (KASPER) says 40 is already at the top of the range and recommends 20 for modern turbo engines, with 30 acceptable for naturally aspirated ones. He notes the owner's manual says 10W-30 with API SM, and that oil of such a grade would last only a few thousand km before deposits build up. Another member (Victor) says 30 is fine for calm driving, since aggressive driving raises the oil temperature and lowers its viscosity.12 Grade and brand experience is collected on the engine oil selection card.

Owner's change interval on synthetic oil. The owner (Oleg Belousov) runs synthetic engine oil and changes it about every 10,000 km in city driving and at 12,000-13,000 km on the highway; he once changed it at 13,000 km after long highway trips. He says he has kept this regime and has had no oil-related problems.3 For much shorter intervals under heavy use see the heavy-duty oil change interval card and the maintenance interval schedule.

docs.title: Filter part numbers and kit pricing
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number · #price · #cabin-filter · #air-filter · #mazda-6-compat · #engine-oil

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Part numbers. Cabin (salon) filter: 5DA061P11. Engine air filter: RF4F13Z40H or 5BA013Z40. Oil filter: 1012010-37K or 1012010-37K#P1. Fuel filter: FC0160950.1

ZEKKERT filter kit pricing (2025-01, Ozon). A ZEKKERT filter kit (air + oil + cabin/coal filters) was available on Ozon at 1,583 RUB (35% discount from a listed 2,467 RUB) as of January 2025 (RU market).2

Air filter material comparison (2025-04 report). Three air filter options were tested/measured by owners: Goodwill AG119 — filter element thickness 1mm, with a rare/tight rib pattern; the OEM original (unbranded) — 1.2mm thick; Purflux A 1157 — 1.5mm thick, the thickest of the three. One owner (Niko75) reports using similarly-specced filters successfully. Thicker filtration media and differing rib/spacing patterns may affect airflow and filtration efficiency, though no owner reported a functional problem from any of the three.345

Air and cabin filter supplier quality notes (2025-09 report). Cabin (salon) filter brands are largely interchangeable and not critical to get exactly right. Engine air filters need more care: Miles-brand air filters reportedly have quality issues and a high defect rate per warehouse staff feedback; Sakura is marginally better with fewer returns. General recommendation: source air filters from verified suppliers rather than open marketplaces (Ozon/Wildberries) where counterfeit/defective stock is more likely. For cabin filters, canister-style activated-charcoal filters are preferred.6789

Oil filter options and compatibility (2025-09 report). Tested oil filter options beyond the Mahle/Mann/Zekert/SCT/Hengst/LYNXauto list above: Lynx LC-1602 (Japanese Akika Kaihatsu brand — note this is the same base part as the LYNXauto LC1602 referenced elsewhere — Ozon price 373 RUB, RU market, 2025-09-20); Brave BR.F.2.20 (Korea Technology brand, rated 4.7/5 from 7 reviews, became a popular community choice); Goodwill GG 201 ua (rated 5.0/5; specs: height 120mm, diameter 76/71/62mm, thread M26x1.5; 2025-09-20). Goodwill is preferred for quality reputation, though Brave has also gained popularity on good reviews.101112131415

Cabin filter alternative — Lada X-Ray part (2025-09 report). The factory cabin filter can be replaced with a Lada X-Ray filter, which requires minor cutting to fit properly. Brave and Goodwill brands were also tested as cabin-filter alternatives and are reported as reliable, good-quality options.12161314

Air filter housing removal procedure (2025-10 report). The air filter housing assembly is held in place by rubber mounts on the bottom (similar to the engine cover mounting). Removal only requires careful pulling — no tools or bolts are involved. Pull gently to preserve the rubber mounts for reuse.17181920

Air filter cross-compatibility — MARSHALL MA8100 (2025-11 report). The MARSHALL MA8100 air filter, designed for the Mazda 6, 626, and MPV, fits the FAW X80 perfectly. One owner reports excellent quality and proper fitment after installation.2122

ZEKKERT kit — early corroborating report and charcoal-filter caveat (2024-06 report). An earlier community report already confirmed the ZEKKERT filter kit (air + oil + cabin filters) fits the FAW Besturn X80, corroborating the January 2025 pricing/availability note above from a full six months earlier. One community caveat on the charcoal cabin-filter variant specifically: charcoal (activated-carbon) cabin filters clog faster than standard non-charcoal filters, so some owners deliberately choose the standard variant for longer service intervals despite the general community preference for charcoal filtration noted elsewhere on this card.232425

Oil filter cross-reference and "no meaningful difference" community view (2024-07 report). An additional confirmed-compatible oil filter option: Zekkert, cross-referenced for Ford/Mazda applications (Wildberries listing). Broader community sentiment from this thread: after cycling through many different oil filter brands, several owners report no noticeable performance difference between them — "give or take, they're all about the same" — reinforcing the "regular timely oil changes matter more than filter brand" conclusion already documented above regarding the back-pressure/anti-drainback valve question.26272829

Air filter replacement interval and overdue symptoms (2025-11 report). The engine air filter should be changed around 100,000 km. Symptoms of an overdue filter: rough cold starts, poor acceleration, and an SVS warning light appearing on the dashboard — replacing the filter resolved all three symptoms for the reporting owner. Filters are available from Autodoc, with reliable delivery but variable pricing. Some filter designs include a washable mesh layer, which can be cleaned in place instead of doing a full replacement.30313233

MANN air filter option, Ozon-sourced (2026-06 report). A MANN-brand air filter is confirmed compatible with the FAW X80, cross-referenced as also fitting Mazda vehicles. Available for purchase on Ozon.3435

Additional cross-compatible filter options and suppliers (2026-09 report). Air filter: a Zekkert LF1444 air filter (cross-listed for the X80) is available on Ozon, though one owner (Prosto Zuev) notes it has gotten noticeably more expensive recently; a cheaper alternative is the RIGINAL RF2A13Z40 air filter (listed OEM cross-compatible for Mazda 6, 626, MPV, and FAW Bestune X80), untried by the reporting owner but priced more attractively. A further alternative confirmed by photo: the MARSHALL MA8100 air filter (Mazda 6/626/MPV/FAW Besturn X80 cross-reference, OEM RF4F13Z409A) at 416 RUB (down from 462 RUB) on Ozon (RU market, September 2026). Cabin filter: SUFIX SSC-1046 (activated-carbon/charcoal type), cross-listed for Mazda 6, Mazda 2, CX-7, and FAW Besturn X80, on Ozon. A further cabin-filter alternative confirmed by photo: SCT SA1215 (Mazda 2/6/CX-7 cross-reference) at 278 RUB (down from 309 RUB) on Ozon (RU market, September 2026). Oil filter: a listing for part 1012010-37KH (a variant of the 1012010-37K part number already documented above) was also sourced via Ozon; one owner reports buying 5 at once and verifying at least one as genuine, though cannot vouch for what's currently sold under that listing a year later. Hengst H90W27 is reiterated as the preferred oil filter choice — one owner specifically flags that Goodwill's X80 oil filter incorrectly includes an anti-drain-back rubber washer that should not be there, corroborating the earlier "no meaningful difference / Goodwill preferred" notes above with a concrete mechanical caveat against Goodwill. For sourcing beyond Ozon/Wildberries, established filter suppliers Emex, AutoDoc, Exist, and Vedro.pro were named; buying two Hengst H90W27 oil filters through a specific Ozon seller profile (which grants 250 bonus points) brought the pair down to about 600 RUB total (RU market, September 2026).363738394041

Filter kit and oil price point, 2026-09 (Фаниль Фаритович report). A separate seller offered a complete filter kit for the FAW Besturn X80 at 1,500 RUB, plus motor oil at 5,000 RUB (RU market), as of 2026-09-04 — a different, more recent price point than the ZEKKERT kit pricing documented above (2025-01); both prices should be read as independent community-observed data points rather than a single official price.424344

docs.title: Fuel consumption by driving conditions
docs.text:
Tags: #fuel-consumption · #tires

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

General ranges by driving condition (mixed AT/MT reports). Highway cruise at a comfortable pace: 8.8–9.0 L/100km. City/suburban mixed driving: 12–14 L/100km. Sport-style driving and highway acceleration: 11+ L/100km. Cold-start performance is reported as excellent with a quick engine warm-up. No consistent difference was reported between 92 and 95 octane fuel when driven equally (see octane note below for a separate subjective-preference discussion). Automatic transmission improves ride comfort over manual but tends to cost more in city fuel economy. Typical daily mileage for many owners is only 5–10 km/day, with seasonal variation.12345678

Manual transmission (MT) — city and highway figures. MT-equipped owners consistently report 7–7.5 L/100km in normal city driving. Winter consumption rises to roughly 10 L/100km due to engine warm-up time — excessive idle warm-up before driving further increases winter consumption. One driver recorded 5.6 L/100km on a ~50 km highway stretch without loading the engine, described as a "record run" achieved by not rushing; this is a best-case data point, not a typical average.910111213

Automatic transmission (AT) — city and highway figures. AT-equipped owners report 10–13.4 L/100km in city driving. One owner reported 13.4 L/100km despite claiming exclusively highway driving in "Drive" mode (no sport mode engaged) — a notably high figure for highway-only use, suggesting either heavy traffic conditions or a less economical driving style than intended. Highway-specific consumption for AT cars drops to roughly 10 L/100km for other owners. Variation is attributed to driving style, engine warm-up duration, and city traffic patterns.14151617189

Tire size increase raises consumption by roughly 1+ L/100km (2026-06 report). One owner switched to a larger tire size in the fall and observed a consumption jump from a prior 5–6 L/100km to 7–10 L/100km — the owner attributed the increase primarily to the tire-size change rather than season/weather alone. General technical takeaway: larger tires increase rolling resistance and effective gearing load, adding roughly 1+ L/100km — this should be factored in when selecting non-OEM tire sizes, alongside the OEM tire-fitment data documented on the dedicated tire-fitment card.19

Octane preference — subjective, no confirmed technical requirement (conflict/nuance noted). Multiple owners report a subjective preference for 95-octane over 92-octane: smoother engine response and better throttle feel, with some noting audible harshness specifically when running 92. One AT-equipped owner reports the car came from the factory running 95 (fueled at Gazprom stations). There is no documented technical consensus that the engine requires 95 for correct operation or is factory-tuned specifically for it — the community's own general-ranges data point above found no consistent consumption difference between the two octane grades when driven equally, so the 95-preference reports are best read as subjective smoothness/feel claims rather than an established spec requirement.202122

docs.title: Fuel filter replacement cost and contamination example
docs.text:
Tags: #fuel-filter · #price · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Pricing (RU market, November 2024): - Complete fuel filter assembly with housing: 6,000 RUB from a service center.12 - Separate filter element only, on Ozon: 1,600 RUB.2 - Cheapest option reported: 400 RUB for the filter element only, from a budget retailer.134

Prices vary significantly by supplier — shop around before buying the full housing assembly if only the element needs replacing.15234

Contamination example. One owner's photo shows a fuel filter heavily contaminated with a thick layer of black particulate soot/sludge, pulled after a fuel pump replacement — evidence that fuel-system contamination can be a root cause of hard-starting/running problems, not just the pump itself.6

Screen/strainer must also be addressed (2025-04 report). When replacing the fuel filter, the coarser pre-filter screen/strainer should also be replaced or cleaned — factory service notes it is not included in standard filter kits and must be purchased separately. Technically the screen can be cleaned rather than replaced, but the service recommendation is to replace it for optimal performance.789

Clogging depends on fuel quality more than mileage (2026-09 report). Serega found debris in the fuel filter at about 50,000 km and thinks it built up over the last couple of months; Arсhi 77 argues mileage matters less than the fuel — a filter can look fine after 100 km yet clog within 1,000 km with current, poor-quality fuel.101112

docs.title: DIY fuel consumption test procedure (octane)
docs.text:
Tags: #fuel · #octane · #diy

To compare fuel consumption between different octane ratings (e.g., 92 vs 95), the community-suggested DIY test procedure is: 1. Run the tank down close to empty and fully reset the trip odometer. 2. Fill with 30–40 L of a specific octane rating. 3. Drive exclusively in D mode for a measurable distance (avoid mixing driving modes that would skew the comparison). 4. Record fuel consumption (trip computer or manual calculation) over that tank. 5. Repeat the same process with the other octane rating for a fair back-to-back comparison.12

Reported result: the difference between octane grades can be marginal, up to about 1 L/100km — i.e., noticeable but not dramatic, so the decision of which octane to run may come down to cost and engine feel rather than a large fuel-economy gap.12

docs.title: Community consensus (owner experience)
docs.text:
Beyond the DIY test above, a broad consensus emerged from a separate group discussion among several owners: 92 and 95 octane perform essentially identically on the FAW Besturn X80, with no meaningful difference in fuel consumption or day-to-day performance.

  • "I don't feel a difference between 92 and 95" — Jürgen@73.3
  • "92 and 95 — there's no difference at all, on this car" — ꧁乂꓄𝕖ŀ𝕖𝓰𝐫𝚊ṁ乂꧂.4
  • "Consumption isn't really noticeable between 92 and 95" — Миша.5
  • "Also don't see a difference" — Николай Цветков.6
  • "Tried many times over four years, 92 and 95 from different producers — saw no difference in anything" — Sershig.7

Minority/nuance view: a few owners perceive the engine as slightly livelier on 95, even though they agree the measurable consumption difference is negligible:

  • Миша noted that while consumption isn't really different, "in terms of responsiveness I've noticed that 95 feels punchier."5
  • One owner (Aleksei Riabov) reported the engine "seems to run better" on 95 and said they exclusively fill with 95 for that reason.8
  • Another owner (Егор), while mixing 92/95 during a long trip depending on what's available at the pump, said the car "feels livelier" on 95.9

Overall: this experience-based consensus is consistent with the DIY test's finding above — 92 is safe to use with no damage risk, and the fuel-economy/performance difference versus 95 is small enough that most owners can't detect it; any perceived extra "pep" on 95 is reported as a subjective impression by a minority rather than a measured effect.3456789

docs.title: Fuel prices and regional availability
docs.text:

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Regional price snapshot, July 2026. Community-reported fuel prices and conditions across several Russian regions: - Tatarstan: 92 octane ≈ 64 RUB/L; 95 octane ≈ 68 RUB/L (RU market, July 2026). - Southern Urals (M2 highway area): ≈ 80–85 RUB/L for 92 octane ("Opti" grade) (RU market, July 2026). - Crimea (Yalta): prices spiked to ≈ 350 RUB/L amid extreme shortage conditions (RU market, July 2026). - Multiple regions reported intermittent fuel supply, with 3–5 hour queues at stations that had fuel.

Context — refinery disruptions. Community discussion attributed the shortages to damage at roughly 40% of Russian oil refineries, including some of the largest, rather than artificial/deliberate scarcity — this was raised in response to skepticism about whether the shortage was genuine.123456

Practical coping advice. Community recommendations for navigating the shortage: keep the fuel tank above half full at all times as a buffer; fill at unusual hours (early morning) when queues are shorter; be aware that some private/independent stations were charging 2–3× official prices during the shortage — cross-check against official regional pricing before paying a large premium.7891011

Fuel quality concern. Separate from the shortage itself, some owners reported sediment/poor fuel quality during this period causing engine fouling — a secondary risk of buying from unfamiliar or opportunistic sellers during a supply crunch.123456

docs.title: Regular driving prevents wear and corrosion
docs.text:
Tags: #corrosion

Core claim. The X80 does not tolerate long periods of inactivity well. Extended parking — on the order of weeks or months — causes a cluster of related problems: creeping/creaking noises develop, brake rotors rust (see the dedicated brake-disc-rust card for the specific rust-from-inactivity data point), suspension bushings develop squeaks, and overall vehicle condition deteriorates noticeably faster than with regular use.

Mechanism and recommendation. Regular driving — at minimum several times per week — keeps mechanical components moving and fluids circulating, which is credited with preventing corrosion buildup and preventing components (bushings, seals, brake surfaces) from stiffening/seizing in a static position. The community's practical takeaway: frequent short trips are better for the car than infrequent long idle periods, even if the total mileage/usage is similar — it's the regularity, not just the total km, that matters for component health.1

docs.title: Long-term ownership at 270,000 km
docs.text:
Tags: #reliability

One owner reports 270,000 km of ownership since 2018 with excellent overall reliability and a maintenance-first approach (no cutting corners). Service/repair history:

  • Engine oil: changed every 10,000 km throughout ownership.
  • Spark plugs: replaced only twice in 270,000 km.
  • Catalytic converter: failed at 170,000 km — handled by removal (see the dedicated catalytic converter removal card).
  • Transmission: partial oil change with filter at 200,000 km.
  • Fuel filter: replaced once.
  • Front brake discs: replaced at 255,000 km.
  • Rear hub: replaced at 260,000 km.
  • Front suspension: arms/struts replaced.
  • All remaining systems reported as still functional at the time of the report.

The owner attributes the car's longevity to consistent, non-deferred maintenance rather than any special repairs.12

docs.title: Maintenance interval schedule
docs.text:
A community-shared maintenance interval reference for the FAW X80:

  • Engine oil change: every 10,000 km.
  • Manual transmission (MT) fluid change: 50,000 km.
  • Automatic transmission interval: not specified in this discussion — see the dedicated AKPP fluid-change card for the fuller, disputed interval picture.
  • Drive belt inspection: 120,000–140,000 km; replace if there are visible cracks, wear/fraying, or if the belt twists more than 45 degrees under finger pressure.
  • Spark plugs: 40,000–50,000 km depending on usage — some owners have run them to 70,000 km before issues appeared.
  • Air filter and cabin filter: should be checked during routine service (no fixed km figure given).

These are community-compiled figures, not an official factory table — treat as a starting reference rather than a guarantee.12345

Corroboration — 10,000 km oil interval for long-term reliability (2025-05 report). A separate owner corroborates the 10,000 km oil-change figure above with a reliability outcome: "if you change the oil every 10,000 km, you won't have any problems" — offered in the context of avoiding oil-consumption issues and engine wear over long ownership.6

docs.title: FWD transmission/differential fluid — GL4, not GL5
docs.text:
Tags: #transmission-fluid · #price · #part-number · #mkpp

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Correct spec. The FWD transmission/differential unit on the X80 requires GL4 (75W-80) gear fluid, not GL5 (75W-90).

Why it matters. GL5 is formulated for different drivetrain applications — specifically hypoid gears found in differentials on rear-drive/live-axle setups. Using GL5 in this FWD transmission application violates the manufacturer spec, even though both GL4 and GL5 sometimes appear together on generic "allowed fluids" lists from some parts sources — that listing is misleading for this specific application.123456789101112

Widely-used product — Mannol EXTRA GETRIEBOEL 75W-90 (2024-08 report; check the dual GL-4/GL-5 rating against the GL4-only spec above before assuming compatibility). Manual gearbox capacity is 2.95 L. Mannol EXTRA GETRIEBOEL 75W-90 (marketed as API GL-4/GL-5 LS, synthetic) is the most commonly used fluid reported by owners — note it carries a dual GL-4/GL-5 rating rather than a GL-4-only rating, so buyers concerned about the GL4-vs-GL5 spec distinction documented above should independently verify this product's suitability rather than assume the GL-5 co-rating is automatically fine for this application. Fill/drain procedure: drain from the bottom, fill via the side inspection plug until level reaches the fill hole. Quality caveat: some owners report Mannol 75W-90 quality issues — one unit developed difficult gear engagement after about 1 month of use. Aral is a reported alternative for owners wanting to avoid that risk; UIDNU and QH brands were also used successfully by other owners without the same complaint.13141516171819202122

Spec, viscosity and products (2026-09/10 reports). Victor, checking the owner's manual, reads the manual gearbox (manual transmission, MKPP / МКПП) spec as GL-4 75W-80 and insists on GL-4, not GL-5 or dual GL-4/5; he fitted Gazpromneft GL-4 75W-80 (litre packs) when replacing the gearbox seal and suggests ZIC 75W-85 for a thicker oil.232425 He believes Mazda 6 manual boxes use 75W-85 (unconfirmed), and said that a higher second number (80 vs 85) means thinner oil — the opposite of the usual convention, where a higher number is thicker.2425 Andrey is more relaxed: any oil matching the manual's viscosity is fine.26 Capacity is 2.95 L: the TOM'S site lists the 5-speed MKPP at 2.95 L and has no matching TOM'S fluid, so the carmaker's spec applies.27 A search-engine answer shared in the chat suggests TOM'S 75W-90 GL-5, RAVENOL MTF-2 75W-80 and Totachi GL-4 75W-90; the GL-5 item contradicts the GL-4 spec above.28 Prices: Gazpromneft GL-4 75W-80 about 1,000 RUB per litre (RU market, Sep 2026);23 REDUX 75W-90 GL-4 "for MKPP" on a marketplace sale at 3,386 RUB, down from 9,252 RUB (RU market, Oct 2026).29

GL-5 in a manual gearbox — owner debate (2026-10). A 2022 forum screenshot (vk.ru comments) says GL-5 additives attack brass synchronizers, so only GL-4 should be used; a reply in the same screenshot says 12 years on TAD-17 in an 08 gearbox caused no problems and that the bronze fear is overstated.30 Sergey notes that GL-5 is intended for final drives (редуктор).31

Change interval. Victor says the service schedule (регламент) calls for a manual gearbox oil change at 40,000 km;32 owners do it later: Andrey every 50,000 km (he had reached 139,000 km), серега planned 52,000 km and Марина changed at 58,000 km.263334 See also the maintenance interval schedule.

Filling. Romanych filled the gearbox through the side check (контрольное) hole from a 1-litre canister with a long spout;35 Victor filled from underneath with a 160 ml syringe, describing about 20 insertions to get it all in.36

docs.title: Service center selection and transparency
docs.text:
Tags: #dealer

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Be present during service work (2024-05 report). X80 owners strongly recommend being physically present in the service area while work is performed, whenever schedule allows — this is treated as the single most effective safeguard against corner-cutting and cost inflation. One owner described booking a partial-drain AKPP fluid service and specifically asking in advance whether being present would be permitted.

Technician quality is scarce and variable. A recurring community sentiment: many service centers lack X80-specific knowledge, and some technicians attempt to upsell unnecessary services during routine visits. "Finding a good mechanic is 90% of success" is cited as community wisdom — the car itself is less of a risk factor than the shop doing the work. Recommended practices: confirm work in real time when present, and cross-reference any proposed non-standard procedure against community advice (this wiki, the Telegram group, or Drive2) before authorizing it.

Consumer protection leverage. For owners in Russia, the consumer protection law ZPPK №2300-1 was cited as a tool that can be referenced if a service center pushes back on being observed, refuses transparency, or performs unauthorized work — knowing this law exists gives owners leverage in a dispute with an uncooperative shop.12345

Inflated labor quote example — FIT service center (2026-08 report). An owner visited the FIT service center for suspension and engine diagnostics and was satisfied with the diagnostic experience, but found the shop's follow-up repair pricing "way over the top."6 The shop's quote — shown as a photo — was for 41,000 RUB (RU market, August 2026) in labor alone to replace the rear suspension (springs, shock absorbers, and rear brake pads). A second owner called this "very expensive," noting that a comparable rear suspension job on his own (different-model) car cost only 11,000 RUB (RU market, as stated in August 2026) even in a smaller town, and that even doubling that for inflation still would not reach 41,000 RUB — he said he would have shopped around further.7 A third owner agreed even more bluntly that the quote was excessive ("they're not just skinning you three times over..."), and advised that if the money matters, it's better to look for another shop.8 This reinforces the card's core recommendation: get multiple quotes and favor independent/smaller shops over large service centers for suspension-related labor.678

docs.title: Service-interval reset via steering-wheel menu
docs.text:
Reset procedure via the steering-wheel controls. To reset the maintenance/service-interval reminder, use the on-wheel steering controls: (1) press the Info button on the steering wheel, (2) navigate down to "request status", (3) press the down arrow again, (4) select the "warning" option, (5) press enter to find "service interval reset" and confirm. The dashboard menu can display up to 3 warning lines depending on the car's configuration. Known quirks: on some cars the Info button doesn't respond reliably, and the OK button may need multiple presses before it registers.12345678910

Reset increments are fixed at 5,000 km. After an oil change (including on automatic-transmission cars), the service interval can only be reset in 5,000 km increments — the display/menu is built around 5,000 km steps and there's no way to set a custom interval beyond that granularity.123

docs.title: Service reminder — 5,000 km interval and reset
docs.text:
Tags: #dashboard · #conflict

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Fixed interval, not customizable. The factory service interval reminder on the FAW X80 is fixed at 5,000 km and cannot be changed to a different interval (e.g. 7,000 km) through the dashboard menu.123456789

Reset procedure: 1. Press the Info button on the steering wheel to display the reminder. 2. Enter the Settings menu. 3. Navigate to Technical state of car (техническое состояние). 4. Press OK on the steering wheel. 5. Select Remaining mileage (остаток пробега). 6. Hold the Info button for approximately 3+ seconds to reset the interval.

The reminder must be reset manually after every service — it does not auto-reset.123456789

Additional confirmation (2025-10 report). A separate owner corroborated that pressing OK repeatedly is unnecessary — the reminder can be cleared directly via a dedicated "reset remaining mileage" option in the dashboard menu, matching the procedure above.1011

Countdown display example (2026-03 report). The reminder counts down from the 5,000 km interval — one owner's dashboard showed "change oil in 4,100 km" when about 900 km had already been driven since the last reset, confirming the fixed-interval countdown behavior described above.1213

Earlier-reported alternate procedure — ignition + OK-button hold method (2024-06 report; possible conflict with the Info-button procedure above). A separate, earlier community report describes a different-looking reset sequence: (1) press the INFO button briefly (lower-left of the steering wheel) to check remaining mileage to the next service; (2) after service is completed, press the OK button when the service symbol appears; (3) turn the ignition to ON while holding the OK button for a minimum of 10 seconds, until the symbol resets. After reset, the service light disappears and the INFO screen can no longer display the service interval countdown until the next cycle begins. This sequence does not exactly match the Info-button-hold-only procedure documented above — treat the two as possibly reflecting different model years/dashboard software revisions rather than assuming either is wrong, and try the Info-menu procedure first since it has broader corroboration on this card.1415

Reset fails without a working Info button (2026-04 report). If the steering-wheel Info button itself is non-functional, the standard reset procedure above cannot be completed — there is no alternative in-dashboard method without it. In that case, an OBD2 tool or a dealer/service-center reset is the reported workaround, though this wasn't independently confirmed as fully working in this report (confidence: low).16171819

docs.title: Suspension longevity at 237,000 km
docs.text:
Tags: #shock-absorbers · #bushings

One owner with 237,000 km on the odometer reports good ride quality after replacing the original shock absorbers and installing pneumatic air springs (баллоны) at around the 120,000 km mark — he has been running on the air springs since then ("жопа и живая" — the rear end is still in good shape).12 At high mileage he also replaced the track rod end bushings in the control arms where the springs sit (саленблоки в рычагах).1 With these interventions the vehicle maintains good ride quality without needing further major suspension work.123

docs.title: Timing chain/belt service — access and cost
docs.text:
Tags: #price · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Access. When replacing the timing drive (referred to by community members as "ремень ГРМ" — literally "timing belt," though the X80 uses a timing chain), front wheel removal is necessary for access. This is confirmed by multiple experienced community members as the standard procedure.12

Replacement cost. Timing chain replacement (parts: seals, tensioner, guides, sprockets) runs approximately 20,000–25,000 RUB for OEM parts, plus 20,000–25,000 RUB labor — a total of roughly 40,000–50,000 RUB (all RU market, October 2024). Only original FAW parts are recommended for this job.345

Conflicting dealer quote. One dealer quoted a lower total of 30,000 RUB (RU market, October 2024) for a vehicle at 85,000 km.456 Conflict noted: the community's general estimate (40,000–50,000 RUB) is roughly 1.5x the dealer's quoted price — likely explained by regional/shop pricing differences rather than a factual disagreement about the job itself.3456

Service interval confusion. One owner reported being told by a dealer that the chain should be changed at 90,000 km; another community member notes that per the official maintenance regulations, the relevant check/interval points are around 50,000 km and 100,000 km — so owners should verify the exact interval against their own market's official service schedule rather than relying on a single dealer's verbal claim.56

Chain/sprocket inspection at high mileage (2025-01 report). At a 100,000 km service, the timing chain and sprockets should be inspected for wear/stretch as a matter of course.7

Complete OEM timing kit for sale — part number reference (2026-03 report). A community member listed a complete original FAW timing-drive kit for sale, part number LF01-12-006 (a 7-piece kit), manufactured in Changchun, China, and confirmed as genuine FAW-original equipment for X80 models — offered with regional shipping within Russia. (As above, the community colloquially calls this a "timing belt" kit even though the actual drive component on the X80 is a chain.)8910

docs.title: TPMS sensor battery type and design
docs.text:
Tags: #tpms · #battery · #part-number · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

TPMS sensors are sealed units, not designed to be disassembled for battery replacement — per design, the battery is not user-serviceable, so a dead battery normally means replacing the whole sensor.1234

DIY disassembly is possible but risky. Some owners have cut the sensor casing open, replaced the battery, and re-glued it back together; community estimate for this approach is a 50/50 success rate.45

Battery type: CR2450 (also reported as BR2450, and one source cites CR2050HR / SBO-T23 (Maxell)).6789 Cost comparison: a replacement battery runs about 1,000 RUB (RU market, September 2024), versus a higher cost for a brand-new sensor — so DIY battery swap is cheaper if it works, but the community's practical recommendation is to just buy a new sensor rather than risk a failed DIY repair given the coin-flip success rate.10689

Second confirmed teardown (2025-03/28 report). A separate owner successfully opened a sensor by applying solvent along the glued seam and carefully cutting with a utility knife, confirming a PCB inside. Battery identified as CR2450 or CR2430 (CR2450 has higher capacity). After replacement, the sensor must be reprogrammed with an Autel or similar diagnostic tool to be recognized by the car.11121314151617

Replace-all-four recommendation (2025-07/31 report). Owners note that when one sensor's battery dies, the other three usually fail within days to weeks (all installed at the same time, similar wear). Sensor batteries typically last 5–6 years. DIY battery replacement (knife + soldering iron) is described as extremely difficult with a real risk of not getting the sensor open successfully — attempt only with electronics experience; most owners simply replace all four complete sensors together for proper system programming.181920212223

Earliest documented opening method — heat gun + solvent (community reference). To access the internal battery without destroying the sensor: use a heat gun or hair dryer to carefully warm the plastic seams until the adhesive softens, then inject a solvent (e.g., acetone) along the seams with a syringe and needle to dissolve the glue further. Open carefully and peel the halves apart — this allows battery replacement without breaking the housing.242526

Alternate disassembly method — hacksaw + solder points (2025-11 step-by-step, ~10–20 min/sensor). A six-photo walkthrough documents an alternative teardown: (1) do not open the white rear cap; (2) cut along the right edge with a metal-cutting hacksaw; (3) carefully separate the halves; (4) cut the solder joints on both sides of the battery with a utility knife; (5) install the new battery and re-solder or use a clip to reconnect it.272829

Long-term tolerance of a failed TPMS system (2025-11 reports). Multiple owners report driving 3+ years with the TPMS warning light blinking continuously rather than fixing it — the full fix (4 sensors + programming) costs 4,000+ RUB, which several owners view as poor value, preferring to monitor tire pressure manually instead. Some individual sensors fail within 1.5–2 years of ownership, and (consistent with the replace-all-four note above) all four sensors can fail in the same general timeframe since they're installed together.3031323334353637

Full replacement cost and process, another case (2026-01 report). During a winter-wheel swap at 58,000 km, one owner had all four sensors replaced: OEM sensor set (4x) ≈ 7,000 RUB, wheel-swap-with-sensor-fitting labor ≈ 3,700 RUB, for a total of roughly 10,700 RUB (all RU market, January 2026). Each sensor requires custom programming per wheel position after installation, done by the dealer/shop performing the service; no programming problems were reported in this case. (A separately mentioned figure of ~23,000 RUB (RU market, January 2026) for the same visit refers to unrelated insurance costs, not the TPMS work itself.)38394041

Moscow-market sensor pricing (May 2026 report). OEM TPMS sensors from a local Moscow dealer run around 6,000 RUB (RU market, May 2026). Cheap non-OEM clone sensors from AliExpress (~800 RUB, RU market, seen May 2026) are reported to frequently fail with a module error — both Ozon and AliExpress clone units show high failure rates in owner reports, so the community favors OEM despite the higher price. Confirmed compatible sensor model for the X80: FS43X0L5.4243444546

Sensor programming/cloning is possible and can be done remotely (2026-05 report). Separate from battery replacement, FAW X80 TPMS sensors can be programmed or cloned after replacement using a dedicated TPMS programmer. One owner who acquired such a programmer offered a remote programming service to the community. To reprogram or clone a sensor, you need its sensor ID number, which can be read either directly off the physical sensor body or via vehicle diagnostics from the TPMS module.47484950

Dealer resoldering/reprogramming alternative, and a headunit-swap workaround (2026-08 report). Asked whether TPMS sensor batteries can be swapped, and which battery to buy,51 one owner replied that the sensors are not user-replaceable, but official dealers can resolder the battery directly onto the sensor's board or reprogram/flash a new sensor — a lower-risk (if pricier) option than opening the sensor yourself.52 The same owner described a separate practical workaround some use to sidestep expensive official TPMS sensor replacement entirely: buy a Chinese aftermarket "magnetic" head unit (e.g., the TAIS brand) bundled with a matching set of TAIS tire-pressure sensors, which work independently of the OEM TPMS hardware.52

docs.title: Transmission fluid change intervals and costs
docs.text:
Tags: #maintenance-interval · #conflict · #automatic-transmission · #transmission-fluid · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Official guidance vs dealer advice (AKPP). The factory service manual specifies only an oil-level check at 30,000 km intervals — no scheduled full oil change is mentioned 1. Dealership-recommended intervals vary but generally suggest a partial change at 60,000 km and a full change at 120,000 km 2. This is a discrepancy between OEM documentation (level checks only, no mandated change interval) and dealer service recommendations (60k/120k km) 12. Some owners prefer earlier maintenance, doing partial changes as soon as 50,000 km 2, so actual practice depends on each owner's reading of the manufacturer's guidance versus the dealer's. For fluid specification and procedure see the ATF fluid and intervals card.

Community practice — 50,000 km interval. Multiple owners converge on a rule of thumb: change the automatic-transmission fluid roughly every 50,000 km and the AKPP holds up well with no reliability problems, including under highway driving with confident acceleration 345. One owner's detailed account: at 105,000 km all the bushings and bearings had worn out but the transmission itself continued to hold up fine, with no overheating even under aggressive and highway driving; a full bearing/bushing/brake-disc job at that mileage cost about 60,000 RUB (RU market, July 2025) 6. Community sentiment favors AKPP over manual for comfort when this maintenance interval is followed 3.

AKPP oil filter — clean and reuse. The automatic-transmission oil filter is metal (not the paper type used in many other vehicles), so instead of buying a replacement at each service it can simply be washed and thoroughly cleaned and reused — a straightforward way to reduce recurring maintenance costs 7.

ACVT (CVT-type) variant — service and cost. This applies to the ACVT (CVT-type) automatic transmission variant, distinct from the more commonly discussed Aisin AKPP torque-converter automatic above. At 200,000 km one owner had a filter change plus partial fluid replacement, with 3.5–4.5 liters of fluid extracted: labor 3,000 RUB, oil ~1,200 RUB/liter × 3 liters = 3,600 RUB, total ~6,600 RUB (RU market, Oct 2024) 89. A follow-up service at 240,000 km extracted approximately 3 liters 89. The fluid cited was Genesis Special SPX 5W-40 — note this is an engine-oil-branded product line being referenced for the CVT service; confirm the CVT-specific fluid coding with your supplier before use, since CVT fluids require a specific formulation distinct from engine oil or standard ATF 89.

docs.title: Used X80 purchase — initial maintenance checklist
docs.text:
Tags: #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Context. Recommendations for the immediate maintenance pass after buying a used X80 around 82,000 km, based on community experience — framed as a baseline "reset" service rather than waiting for symptoms to appear.

Recommended immediate actions: 1. Change engine oil and all filters (air, oil, cabin). 2. Check and change transmission oil, including filter replacement — this requires full pan removal and a new pan gasket (see the automatic-transmission ATF card for the detailed procedure and gasket part numbers). 3. Inspect suspension — shocks, wheel bearings, brake discs. 4. Check for water intrusion under the spare tire in the trunk — rust and water accumulation in this area is called out as a known problem on the X80, worth checking even if no symptoms are apparent, since it isn't something a casual pre-purchase inspection typically catches.

Cost estimate. Total parts cost for this initial pass: approximately 35,000–40,000 RUB; labor: approximately 7,000–10,000 RUB (both RU market, July 2024). This is presented as a baseline budget for a thorough "new owner" reset service, not a minimal/partial service.12345

docs.title: Windshield chip and crack repair — pricing and urgency
docs.text:
Tags: #windshield · #glass · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Chip repair: 500–1,000 RUB (RU market, November 2024) per chip, price at the master's discretion.1

Small chip sealing method. A small chip can be sealed with resin using a drilling-and-filling method, roughly 1,000 RUB (RU market, November 2024).12

Crack repair: a ~10cm-long crack trench repair does not have a fixed price — cost is assessed per case.1

Full windshield replacement: approximately 8,000 RUB total (glass ~6,000 RUB + labor ~2,000 RUB; RU market, November 2024).1

Urgency warning. A chip left untreated risks the water + frost cycle causing rapid crack expansion — one owner documented their own chip visibly growing into a spreading crack over just days.3456 Preventive drilling before water can enter the chip can arrest the crack from propagating further.17 Professional recommendation: address a chip within days of noticing it, especially heading into cold/frost conditions, rather than delaying.1267

Outcome example: one owner successfully had their chip sealed at a glass shop after it had already begun to spread, resolving the issue.8910
