docs.title: Market variants — China, Russia, North Korea
docs.text:
Chinese domestic badge name: FAW Besturn X80 is sold in the Chinese domestic market as "Pentium X80." The name is unrelated to Intel — Pentium is FAW's own budget vehicle line. Important for cross-searching Chinese parts catalogs and forums.123

China vs. Russia feature differences: the Chinese-market X80 offers a full panoramic sunroof and a large 12-inch touchscreen infotainment system that also handles climate control (replacing physical buttons). Some users criticize the touchscreen as unreliable and non-replaceable, compared to the Russian-market version where aftermarket Android head units can be swapped in easily. Reports describe the touchscreen's climate-control functionality as limited and prone to failure within about 2 weeks of initial use.4567

Model variants / limited editions: a "Live Edition" (2018 model year) featured a full-roof panoramic sunroof and a larger infotainment display than standard production models, which have a smaller factory screen. Live Edition units are reported as rare in the Russian market — most imported X80s are base or standard configurations. Exact technical specs and drivetrain options vary by production year and market edition.89

North Korean licensed variant: since 2015, Pyeonghwa Motors (North Korea) has produced the "Ppeokkugi 2405" based on the FAW X80 blueprint under a licensed CKD (complete knock-down) arrangement. Specs: 4-door, 5-seat, 4586 mm long, 2.0 L naturally-aspirated engine rated at 108 kW. Used in North Korean agricultural/rural areas. Cited by the community as evidence of the platform's durability and of FAW's international licensing reach.10

docs.title: Diagnostics & aftermarket electronics
docs.text:
Tags: #diagnostics · #cruise-control · #abs

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Diagzone diagnostic software support: Diagzone (Fawcar file) added FAW X80 support in a 2017 file-version update that became broadly available around April 2024. Recommended hardware: a Mucar BT200 adapter running Diagzone firmware, or a similar compatible OBD2 adapter — a generic OBD2 scanner alone is not enough; the launcher hardware is still required. Software can be purchased per-model (example price cited: 720 RUB (RU market, April 2024) for a single model file).12345

Cruise control retrofit (base-spec cars): cruise control can be retrofitted on base ("бомж"/budget) spec X80s that lack it from the factory, using (1) aftermarket cruise-control button switches and (2) the Diagzone software once it added REST/facelift support. One owner successfully activated cruise after dealers and independent Avito specialists initially refused the job — DIY testing over a couple of days proved it feasible. Cheap button kits are available from generic online sources.678

Cruise control — real-world usage feedback: owners report cruise control is only useful on long highway stretches (18+ hour drives); it is ineffective in stop-and-go traffic or on short city trips. Some flag a safety concern on rural roads — drowsiness risk — and suggest a speed limiter would be more useful than cruise control for highway safety.910

StarLine A93/A96 remote starter: the StarLine A93/A96 (equivalent to the A39 series) remote-start system offers roughly 200 m range with no obstacles; hold the button 5 seconds to send the start signal, with ~15 seconds for the feedback signal to reach the key fob. Manual- transmission cars require a multi-step start procedure (not detailed here); automatic-transmission cars use a simpler procedure. The A96 is reported as reliable on the X80; installation quality issues (wiring errors, incorrect fuse routing) have been reported from generic/non-specialist installation shops.11121314

ABS behavior on steep/sloped terrain: when the vehicle is high-centered or tilted at a severe angle (off-road use), false ABS activation is possible — the system is designed for normal on-road driving angles. Community reports say the vehicle levels out and ABS stabilizes once all wheels contact the ground normally. (Low-confidence, single-report observation.)15

docs.title: Fuel system — tank, range, octane, gauge
docs.text:
Tags: #octane

Tank capacity and range: official/nominal tank capacity is 58 L, but the tank holds approximately 62 L when completely full — the discrepancy is attributed to a manufacturing safety margin. Practical range in ECO mode reaches 700+ km on the highway at 100–130 km/h. With headwind and high speed (110–130 km/h), real-world consumption is roughly 9.7–10 L/100 km.1234567891011121314

Fuel grade: the 2.0 L engine with slight chip tuning requires 95 octane fuel — 92 octane is reported as unsuitable for modified/tuned engines.15

Fuel gauge accuracy: the dashboard fuel gauge (graphic bar with symbols) displays the actual remaining fuel level, read from the float sensor — it is not an estimate ("ориентировочное") based on consumption patterns. Confusion about this arises when the float sensor itself is faulty: the resulting symptoms are a sensor/gauge malfunction, not evidence that the gauge is an "estimation" feature.161718

docs.title: General specifications overview
docs.text:
Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Engine block material: the FAW X80 engine block is constructed from aluminum alloy, not cast iron.12

Weight and payload: pre-facelift curb weight is 1545 kg, GVW (gross vehicle weight) 2035 kg, payload front 972 kg, payload rear 1018 kg. Post-facelift (model CA6462ATE5AG1): curb weight 1545 kg, GVW 2035 kg, payload front 997 kg, payload rear 1038 kg.3

License plate mounting: the X80 body is designed for square license plates (type 1a), the standard in China. Rectangular plates (type 1, the Russian standard) fit with an adapter (available on Ozon). Community consensus is that rectangular plates look aesthetically better on the X80's body design — square plates look less proportional against the vehicle's curved body lines. A rubber gasket/silicone pad should be used with square plates to prevent rattling and body-panel damage. Square-plate cost reported at ~1,900 RUB (2022 pricing, RU market). The adapter allows either plate type to be fitted.45678910111213141516

docs.title: Pre-facelift vs. facelift identification
docs.text:
Tags: #restyle

The FAW X80 exists in two visual generations, referred to in the community by their Russian shorthand: Pre-Restyling / Pre-facelift (Дорестайлинг, до-рест) and Restyling / Facelift (Рестайлинг, рест).

Timing: pre-facelift production runs through August 2018; facelift from August 2018 onward (some sources say January 2019). The styling shift is described informally as going from a "softer"/"kind" (добрый) to a more "aggressive"/"angry" (злой) look, with updated front/rear fascias and headlights, a larger/simpler center console change, and different infotainment capabilities. Because of the mid-year cutover, 2018-model-year cars exist in both versions depending on the production month.1234

Visual identification between the two: headlight design, radiator grille shape, and rear light design differ. Pre-Restyling cars lack parking sensors. Community-recommended method to confirm which generation a given car is: compare photos against D2.ru or the manufacturer's specification sheets.5678910111213

Door/panel interchange caution: pre-facelift (2017–2018) and facelift (2019+) door panels differ in internal structure and taillight mounting. Both generations share the same overall frame opening and body-line alignment, so doors may visually bolt on at the frame level — but internal reinforcement, mounting points, and decorative trim differ, and mixing generations produces an incomplete or mismatched appearance. Full door replacement requires matching the door to the body generation carefully.14151617181920

Instrument cluster behavior (facelift only): on facelift-model automatics, the instrument cluster displays only the current gear-selector position (D, R, N, P) — not the actual gear the transmission has engaged. Pre-facelift models may behave differently on this point. This is described as a known display limitation on post-2019 facelift cars, not a fault.21222324

docs.title: Ownership essentials — warranty, towing, keys
docs.text:
Tags: #warranty · #towing · #key-fob

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Warranty coverage on service: manufacturer warranty is 6 years from purchase date. Doing your own oil changes (DIY maintenance) is reported to void warranty coverage. Warranty is retained only if servicing is performed at certified service centers with proper documentation (receipts and service records). However, simple oil/filter changes at certified multi-brand service centers (not necessarily the dealership itself) with documentation may preserve the warranty — though dealer dispute over this is possible. Always verify with the dealer before using a non-OEM/non-dealer service provider.1234567

Towing: the FAW X80 is not designed or approved for towing trailers. Neither the owner's manual nor the frame nameplate lists a towing capacity. Using the vehicle to tow a trailer is not recommended by the manufacturer, even if an aftermarket hitch (e.g., a SHERIFF-brand hitch) has been installed.89

Key fob loss/replacement: FAW X80 key fobs cannot be duplicated with traditional key-copying methods. Replacement options: (1) buy a new key set from an official dealer with a programming service — expensive but fully supported; (2) use a specialist key-programmer (commonly found via Avito) who scans the vehicle's chip/VIN and creates a new key with reprogramming. Specialist cost reported at 6,000–12,000 RUB (RU market, March 2026) for a complete key replacement including all security features — requires professional chip-scanning and ECU-reprogramming equipment.1011121314

Production timeline: FAW discontinued X80 production in 2020. There are no 2021+ model-year X80 vehicles in the market. Some 2020 stock vehicles were reportedly still being sold into 2022.151617

docs.title: Platform origin — Mazda 6 GG / B50 heritage
docs.text:
Tags: #mazda-6-compat

FAW Besturn X80 is built on the Mazda 6 GG platform (2nd-generation Mazda 6, 2002–2008 chassis generation). The floor pan is sourced from the Mazda CX-5; interior components (dashboard, panels) come from the Mazda 6 GG; bodywork (doors, hood, trunk, fenders) is custom-designed by FAW to give the SUV/crossover profile. Roughly 90% of mechanical components are sourced from or licensed from Mazda. The front suspension uses a full support bearing (vs. a bushing on the Mazda), and spring heights differ from Mazda due to the crossover adaptation.1234567891011

Genealogically, the X80 (restyled) shares its platform with the pre-restyled FAW B50 (1st generation, 2009–2014) — both are built on the Mazda 6 GG (4th generation Mazda 6 in this account) foundation. Shared components: floor pan, subframe, engine mounts, air filters (engine and cabin), and suspension pickup points. Differences versus the B50: the X80 has a raised suspension (20–30 cm higher), modified body panels for the SUV profile, and an updated interior. Wheelbase is identical between B50 and X80; overall length differs by ~2 cm. Practical implication: many Mazda 6 GG parts are cross-compatible — engine mounts, bushings, transmission components, filters.1213141516171819

A separate community summary states the X80 platform is based on Mazda-6 (2002–2008 generation), the automatic transmission (АКПП) is FAW-proprietary but built on Aisin principles, and many consumable parts interchange with Mazda 6, Mazda CX-5, Ford, Volvo, and the FAW B50. A pinned message in the X80 community group lists common part cross-references.20

Members (Arсhi 77, Victor) say the FAW Bestune B50 and the X80 share the same internals — engines, gearboxes and driveshafts — and differ mainly in the body, which is why B50 part listings are used as cross-references for the X80. Confidence is medium (community statement, not a factory document).2122

Caution on parts interchange: FAW X80 shares many parts with the Mazda 6 (II–III generations, 2007–2017 models sold on the Russian market) but several items require care — hubs, brake pads, CV joints, fan assembly (fan block), intake manifold, and upper control arms appear compatible but may need angle/alignment adjustment or replacement in pairs; ball joints on the upper arm do not fit the standard Mazda part; the front strut differs slightly. Differential fitment across the Mazda GG/GJ/GL generations needs individual verification before ordering.23

Engine and drivetrain component sourcing also draws on Korean suppliers and Bosch (Germany) — confirming a mixed-supplier OEM procurement strategy rather than single-source Mazda platform engineering.24

docs.title: Ownership reliability overview vs. Mazda 6
docs.text:
Tags: #reliability · #mazda-6-compat

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Community consensus: overall the X80 is regarded as "a good car" ("хорошая машина") with some "quirks" and "nuances." Main recurring themes: (1) non-standard crankcase ventilation design, (2) electronic-throttle response lag tied to ECU integration, (3) hot-weather engine performance degradation, (4) A/C compressor vibration. Many owners upgrade suspension components (shocks, control arms) using Mazda 6 GG parts. The community is described as experienced and willing to share detailed technical knowledge.123

Failure-rate comparison vs. Mazda 6 (same underlying Mazda L-series engine/platform, but the FAW X80 shows shorter service intervals on several shared components, per one long-time owner's comparison of Drive2 and other forums): - Upper engine mount: Mazda 60–110K km vs. FAW 30–60K km - Front upper-arm bushings (сайлентблоки): Mazda from ~80K km vs. FAW from 20–60K km (sometimes noisy even when new) - Front stabilizer-link mounts: Mazda from ~100K km vs. FAW from ~20K km - Steering-rack knock: Mazda from ~60K km vs. FAW from ~80K km (here FAW reported as lasting longer) - Lower control arm ("рыбка"/"гитара"): Mazda after ~100K km vs. FAW cases reported after only ~30K km - Temperature-sensor housing: Mazda from ~30–40K km, FAW is "a rare lottery" (variable, not consistently earlier or later) - RPM surging/hunting: Mazda's earliest reported case ~180K km (typically after 250K km); not yet observed on FAW at time of report - Fuel pump: reported worse (shorter life) on FAW than Mazda's 150K+ km benchmark - Water intrusion into the driver/passenger footwell — an issue specific to FAW, not seen on Mazda - Various electrical faults, windshield leaks, early rear-spring sagging, and weaker AC cooling than on the Mazda-sourced 09G transmission — all reported as more frequent on FAW than on the donor Mazda 6.4

Independent ownership report (second Telegram group): frequent non-critical issues include (1) thermostat requiring replacement with a quality aftermarket part, (2) water intrusion under the floor carpets (driver/passenger side) — common but solvable, (3) front/rear coil-spring breakage affecting many units, attributed to weak Chinese-OEM springs, (4) winter brake rattle/squeal affecting nearly all units and difficult to eliminate completely. Overall assessment from this report: a robust and reliable Chinese vehicle with extensive Mazda 6 parts compatibility and readily available service parts. Fuel economy cited: manual transmission 7–11 L/100km, automatic 11+ L/100km. Diagnostic scanners may not support advanced diagnostics at all service centers. Illustrative case: an owner with 193,000 km and 4 accidents still owns and intends to keep the vehicle.56789101112131415

docs.title: Infotainment video playback format
docs.text:
Tags: #infotainment

The factory infotainment head unit plays video files in MP4 format — confirmed by an owner who loaded downloaded cartoons for his daughter to watch on road trips 1.

By default, the head unit has a driving lockout on video playback: video stops/blacks out once the car is in motion, a common safety behavior on factory Chinese-market head units. This can be switched off from a settings menu so video keeps playing while driving — one owner shared a screenshot of the exact menu (an Enable/Disable toggle, with an "ON ▶" row below it) reached by navigating into the head unit's settings, though the specific menu path above that screen was not spelled out in the message 2. The original question asking about the screen's resolution and supported formats did not get a resolution figure answered, only the format and this workaround 3.

docs.title: VIN location — windshield vs. door jamb
docs.text:
Tags: #vin · #conflict

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Most FAW X80 units do not have a clearly visible or readable VIN embossed on the windshield, despite the owner's manual indicating one should be present there. Chinese-assembled vehicles instead have the VIN on a sticker on the door jamb. Russian-assembled vehicles (Autotors factory) may have VIN-placement issues or missing windshield embossing entirely. Some early-production units have a barely-visible window-frame area where the VIN should be, but it's either not embossed or heavily obscured. In practice, the VIN can be reliably found on the door-pillar sticker or the body plate. Vehicles have been successfully registered despite windshield VIN-visibility issues, though police acceptance of the missing embossing has varied by region/officer 1234567891011121314151617181920212223242526272829303132333435363738394041.

⚠️ Conflict: some owners did find a VIN embossed on the windshield (most likely early-production or Russian-assembled units), while the majority of Chinese-assembled X80s have no windshield VIN at all — only the door-jamb sticker. The restyling (facelift) model has an even lower likelihood of having a windshield VIN than pre-restyle units.

VIN registration difficulty — illegible/missing body VIN: some vehicles lack a legible VIN code on the body in the expected under-hood location; in some cases the code is instead embossed under the driver-side carpet. The Russian vehicle-registration authority (МРЭО) may require a visible/readable VIN on the chassis to complete registration. Solutions reported: (1) locate and point to the alternate VIN location under the carpet, with the authority's permission to inspect it; (2) try registering at a different МРЭО office/location; (3) provide supporting documentation if available. One owner reports being unable to register the car despite having an accessible VIN code under the floor covering 4243444546474849505152.

docs.title: Wheels, tires & alignment specifications
docs.text:
Tags: #wheels · #tires · #tire-pressure

OEM wheel/tire specification: standard wheel diameter is 17 inches; factory tire size 215/60R17. Bolt pattern 5×114.3 (5-lug, 114.3 mm bolt circle). Center bore 67.1 mm. Confirmed by official documentation as factory-standard for all X80 variants.123 A separate report from the other community group confirms the same factory tire size, 215/60/17.4

Tire size options in practice (varies by trim/generation/owner choice): 225/55/17 (common), 225/60/17 (factory option), 225/65 (considered oversized — noticeably reduces visibility and handling due to increased sidewall height). An 18-inch wheel option is confirmed available in the Chinese market (approximately 235/55 fitment); a newer 235/55/18 combination has also been tested by an owner. Lower-profile 215/70/16 tires are available, trading performance for ride comfort. General guidance: lower profile → sharper handling; higher profile → softer ride and more ground clearance.567

Recommended tire pressure: 2.2–2.4 bar, with 2.2 bar the most commonly used setting in the community. The exact factory specification is printed on the driver's door jamb sticker. Pressure affects handling, comfort, and fuel economy.891011

Spare tire: the rear-mounted spare uses a standard rubber valve stem with no pressure sensor. The TPMS (tire pressure monitoring system) only monitors the four road wheels, not the spare — simple rubber valve, no electronics.121314

Factory wheel alignment specs (unloaded vehicle, from the factory manual): - Front — Camber −20′±30′ (converted from source; consult manual for exact degree/minute notation), Caster 5.93°±1°, wheel steering angle 6.53°, Toe-in 0±2 mm, inside wheel angle 36.5°±3°, outside wheel angle 30°±3°, vehicle height 435±20 mm. - Rear — Camber −1°20′±30′, Toe-in 2±2 mm, vehicle height 462±20 mm. - Vehicle height is measured from wheel center to wheel-arch edge.15

docs.title: X80 "Sport" variant — Ukraine/Kazakhstan
docs.text:
Tags: #trim · #radio · #hvac

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

FAW produced a limited-edition Besturn X80 Sport variant sold only in the Ukraine and Kazakhstan markets — it was never released to the mass market in Russia or elsewhere.

Distinguishing features: - An integrated touchscreen radio/climate-control unit — no physical buttons/dials for climate control, unlike the standard X80's separate climate panel. - Front fog lights. - A unique radiator grille design, different from both the pre-restyle and restyle grilles seen on standard X80s.

Parts availability: the specific touchscreen radio/climate configuration used on the Sport variant was never released to the mass market and is reported as virtually impossible to source for standard X80 models — so this is a curiosity/rarity note rather than a practical upgrade path 1234567.

docs.title: A/C refrigerant line o-ring seals
docs.text:
Tags: #hvac · #seal · #part-number

The A/C system's refrigerant lines connect to the A/C condenser via small o-ring seals. These are proprietary FAW sizes and not readily available through general automotive parts suppliers.

One owner (Fab) documented the seal sizes and part numbers with diagrams while servicing his condenser. Practical advice from this discussion: when removing/installing the A/C condenser, bring the reference photos (or take your own measurements) to a refrigeration/AC shop to identify matching seal sizes, or source seals directly from FAW through an authorized dealer. Retail service shops may need to fabricate equivalents from generic metric o-ring kits if FAW-specific seals aren't available 12345.

Total component spend reported: roughly 85,000 RUB, not counting labor.

Heat exchanger / coolant line part numbers (May 2024). For AKPP cooling: analog part 5CA053110D and original FAW part 5CA053110E02 are both available. These heat-exchanger/coolant-line components can come with or without lower bypass tubes depending on transmission type (MKPP vs. AKPP) — verify fitment against your transmission type before ordering 2.

K2 friction-pack failure from overheating — repair options (July 2024). One owner's AKPP suffered K2 friction-pack failure after extended driving without an auxiliary cooler. Symptoms: slipping during the 3-4 gear transition, eventually leading to full transmission lockup. Repair options compared: 1. Full overhaul: ~160,000 RUB (RU market, July 2024), with solenoid condition unknown going in 2. Contract (used) transmission replacement: ~55,000 RUB (RU market, July 2024) (with a core exchange) A mandatory auxiliary cooler installation (15,000 RUB) was added afterward to prevent recurrence, and routine fluid changes every 20,000–30,000 km were flagged as essential going forward 345678.

docs.title: Automatic transmission fluid — spec 3309
docs.text:
Tags: #automatic-transmission

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The FAW X80's automatic transmission requires fluid meeting spec 3309 12. This was raised while a member was troubleshooting an AT fluid/filter service and asked about the correct spec for a 2019 model 3456.

Avoid "universal" multi-vehicle fluids — even ones that list 3309 among their specs. There is a confirmed case where using a universal multi-spec fluid caused the transmission to refuse to properly engage, and the owner had to have the fluid changed a second time to resolve it 78910. The recommendation from a longtime member: rather than a multi-fluid, use a fluid with a straightforward, confirmed 3309 spec — MANNOL MULTIVEHICLE JWS 3309 was specifically verified working in the field by community members 11121314215. Valvoline Light & Heavy Duty ATF/CVT fluid was also discussed/linked as an option, though members debated whether its labeling as "multi" fluid made it risky in the same way 161713.

Maintenance note: when the fluid is changed, regular service should also include filter sieving/cleaning ("продувка") and pan cleaning if the pan is removed 18.

Transmission seal price and labor — official dealer quote (Sept 2025). A member called the official FAW dealer (Kaliningrad) about a transmission fluid service: the transmission seal was not in stock and had to be special-ordered — cost 1,200 RUB (RU market, September 2025), with an estimated 1-week wait, and 2,800 RUB labor (same quote) for the service. Aftermarket seal options were mentioned but pricing wasn't captured 19.

Pan gasket brand recommendation for fluid changes (Feb 2026). After a complete transmission fluid change, the BRAVE BREK124 pan gasket is recommended. Cheap Chinese gaskets sourced from KitZap and similar suppliers were reported to blow out after 2–3 days. VAG-brand equivalents were also confirmed working by another member. When replacing the gasket, the spacer/washer assemblies should stay OEM — aftermarket spacers/washers are noted as slightly taller than the OEM height, which can cause fitment issues 20212223.

Transmission seal part number and cross-compatibility (Dec 2025). The automatic transmission's right-driveshaft seal part number is 90311-40A014 24. This same part number is confirmed identical for both the FAW Besturn X80 and the FAW Besturn B50, across all production years — one member asked specifically whether there was a difference between the two models' AT seals, and another confirmed the part is the same for both 252627.

docs.title: Battery — spec and replacement cost
docs.text:
Tags: #battery · #cold-weather · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Spec. The facelift ("restyle") X80 uses a 77 Ah battery 12. One example, a TUBOR ASIA SILVER 77.0 VL 650A EN (12V-77Ah B01, 3-year warranty, maintenance-free), lasted about 5 years before needing replacement — another owner with the same model reported the identical 5-year lifespan 345. Community guidance: when replacing, stick with the same 77 Ah capacity 35.

Capacity vs. cold-weather performance. Smaller-capacity batteries (below 77 Ah) charge faster because of the lower total amp-hour load (reduces pulsing current demand on the alternator), but their cranking amps (starting power) decrease proportionally — a real tradeoff, not a free lunch 678910. In extreme cold (below −35°C) gel-type batteries were noted to maintain performance better than conventional flooded types. Battery capacity matters less for short urban trips but becomes more important for winter cold-starts 78.

Battery options and pricing (January 2026). More recent battery choices and prices reported by the community (RU market, January 2026): - CHEN Asia 85D26L, 75 Ah: 13,000 RUB (2026-01-23) - AKOM Asia+EFB, 75 Ah: ~13,803 RUB, down to ~12,000 RUB with an old-battery trade-in (2026-01-22) - EBL 95D31L, 80 Ah: 8,000 RUB with old-battery trade-in (2026-01-19)

AKOM and CHEN brands were recommended by members for cold-weather reliability 111213141516171819.

docs.title: Brake disc alternatives and pricing (2026-09)
docs.text:
Tags: #brake-disc · #mazda-6-compat · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Cross-compatible rear discs — GANZ, Mazda 626/MX-5 fitment (2026-09 report). One owner (Radik) fitted a pair of rear brake discs sold for Mazda 626, MX-5, and FAW Besturn X80 (brand GANZ, perforated), bought on Wildberries, reporting the fitment works and the discs "look cool" installed at the rear.1

Sangsin SD4412 — cheaper non-perforated alternative. Another owner (Victor) uses Sangsin brake SD4412 rear discs, which cost about 4,000 RUB less per set (RU market, September 2026) than perforated alternatives like the GANZ discs above. He also runs the same Sangsin brand up front (paired with pads) and reports satisfaction with them.2 A third owner (Archi) pointed out the Sangsin discs are cheaper specifically because they are not perforated, unlike the GANZ ones.3

Perforated vs. non-perforated — community debate on rear discs (2026-09 report). Victor argues perforation matters little at the rear: rear brakes carry a much smaller share of overall braking force than the fronts and don't run hot, so he sees no functional benefit back there. He does value perforation up front, though — on mountain switchback (serpentine) roads, after about an hour of hard driving he can detect a faint whistling from the front brakes, suggesting the fronts do benefit from the extra cooling.4 Archi countered with the usual case for perforated discs: (1) the holes increase airflow through the disc and cool it faster than a solid disc; (2) perforations help vent gas building up between pad and disc; (3) lower disc mass shortens spin-up time and can improve handling; (4) braking distance is claimed to shorten by up to 10%; and (5) the biggest advantage, in his view, is simply the appearance — and if you fit perforated discs up front, he argues you should match them at the rear for looks.5 Victor pushed back skeptically on the "10% shorter braking distance" and weight-savings claims, noting the actual weight difference between a solid and perforated disc is no more than about 800 g — not enough to meaningfully change performance — while agreeing the visual appeal is real, along with painted calipers, even though he admits he rarely even looks at the rear brakes (attention goes to the fronts, checking for grooves).6

Takeaway. Both GANZ (perforated) and Sangsin SD4412 (non-perforated) rear discs are confirmed cross-compatible replacements for the FAW X80 via Mazda 626/MX-5 part matches. The main practical trade-off documented by the community: perforated discs cost more (~4,000 RUB more per set as of 2026-09, RU market) and cool/vent slightly better, which the community agrees matters mainly up front under hard/mountain driving; at the rear the functional benefit is considered marginal, with appearance being the primary reason owners choose perforated discs there too.

docs.title: Rear brake pad bore diameter — 133.1mm
docs.text:
Tags: #brake-pads · #fitment · #part-number · #mazda-6-compat

The X80's rear brake pad hole (bore) diameter is 133.1mm. Common aftermarket pads sold as Mazda-compatible (brands cited: Zekkert, Masuma, and various other Mazda-branded pads) are typically sized for 129-130mm holes instead. Even this roughly 3mm difference is enough to cause audible clunking in the calipers from the resulting play/slack. Before buying rear pads, confirm the 133.1mm bore measurement rather than trusting a "Mazda-compatible" label alone, since the X80's rear caliper bore differs from the donor-platform Mazda spec 123.

docs.title: Cabin & engine air filters
docs.text:

docs.title: Drive shafts, CV joints & axle seals
docs.text:
Tags: #drive-shaft · #cv-joint · #seal · #mazda-6-compat · #part-number · #price · #conflict

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Drive shaft seal — OEM vs. aftermarket. Drive shaft seals leak even when properly installed and correctly seated if they're aftermarket ("аналоги") — they consistently fail to hold pressure and seep oil, particularly at the right-side drive shaft. The FAW original seal design includes a special rubber skirt ("юбочка") that noticeably improves sealing versus aftermarket versions lacking this feature. Despite the higher cost, the OEM seal is recommended to avoid repeated failures and labor charges 1.

Mazda cross-compatibility. Drive/transmission seals sourced from Mazda parts are also reported to cross-fit the X80's transmission box 2.

Drive axle seal (manual transmission) sourcing. Left drive axle seals are a common wear item; MT and AT seals are different parts — do not assume interchangeability 3456. Available on Wildberries and Chinese platforms (AliExpress, Kitaisky Zapad); pricing on Wildberries is comparable to AliExpress but with more convenient local pickup points. MT-specific parts are noted as harder to find in local Russian auto-parts stores than AT parts 789101112.

Complete drive shaft assembly pricing (August 2025, RUB, RU market): - Chinese aftermarket complete assembly (left or right, MT or AT): 13,000 RUB as of August 2025, down from 25,000 RUB at the start of 2025 131415. - OEM via FAW-sourced channels: individual CV joints around 8,500 RUB each (RU market, August 2025); complete assemblies around 10,500 RUB through a member's parts contact 161718. - As of July 2026: aftermarket outer CV joint (INKO 28/30) ~2,000 RUB (RU market) on Wildberries — much cheaper than OEM, though OEM pricing is significantly higher than this aftermarket option 1920212223.

Left drive axle seal leak from tripod breakdown (Sept 2025). One member's left drive axle seal leaked because the tripod joint had broken apart inside it; the fix was replacing the part (manual transmission) and sourcing it from kitparts. Left and right drive axle seals are confirmed identical/interchangeable with each other (unlike MT vs. AT seals, which are different — see above) 2425262728293031.

External CV joint (CVJT) — part BM1122510MT (Oct 2025). FAW external CV joint (SHRUS) for the X80, part number BM1122510MT. Available from supplier "Vasily" via Ozon at 8,500 RUB, or elsewhere online at ~10,000 RUB (both RU market, October 2025). Ozon lead time reported as 2+ weeks; ordering directly via SDEK gave 3-day delivery instead 323334353637.

No exact analog for the manual-transmission CV joint. A member searching for a manual-transmission CV joint alternative found no direct analog; the Mazda 626 2.0 (1997–2002) was suggested as similar, but measurement showed its shaft is ~0.3 mm smaller in diameter, preventing a direct fit without machining 323839404142. Pricing comparison (Oct 2025, RU market): FAW OEM CV joint BM1122510MT at 8,500 RUB (Vasily) / 10,000 RUB (Ozon) vs. the impractical Mazda alternative due to the shaft mismatch 353643444546.

Inner CV joint spline-count variations. X80 models use inner CV joints with different spline counts depending on transmission and generation: automatic transmissions typically use 24 splines; manual transmissions use 26 splines (tripoid-type). Other variants with 30, 32, and 33 splines also exist. FAW's own factory cannot determine the correct type from VIN alone — physical spline-count verification is required. Manual transmissions also differ from automatics in outer-shaft geometry. The Russian market predominantly uses 24-spline units on automatics 474849505152.

Pre-restyled automatic — full spec (2017 and earlier). For pre-restyled (2017 and earlier) automatic-transmission X80s: external CV joint = 28 splines, internal CV joint = 24 splines, spline diameter ~28.8 mm. OEM part number for the automatic: BM1122510 (without the "MT" suffix used for manual-transmission units above) 535455.

Cross-model compatibility strategy. Exact OEM CV joints are hard to source given the many variants across years/transmissions, and many aftermarket units don't fit without modification. Recommended approach: identify the exact spline count and joint type from a donor vehicle first; salvage yards may stock compatible units from other brands — one X80 owner successfully used a Kia Spectra outer CV joint. Cross-model compatibility exists but always requires manually verifying spline count, shaft diameter, and attachment method before buying 5657585960.

Manual-transmission CV joints — complete assembly only. For manual-transmission X80s, CV joints (SHRUS) are only available as a complete assembly, not as separate components. Sources: KitZap, KitParts, KitZapchasti — availability varies, so check stock before ordering 6162.

CV joint dust boot — polyurethane alternative from Lada Largus (July 2026). The rubber dust boots included in Chinese aftermarket CV-joint kits are poor quality. A polyurethane dust boot from the Lada Largus (ЛАДА Ларгус) fits the X80's CV joints well — dimensions match perfectly despite the different manufacturer/model. The polyurethane version is more rigid/durable than the stock-style rubber boot. One member installed new CV joints with hubs, decided not to use either the kit's rubber boot or the KitZap-sourced rubber one (both rubber), and instead sourced the polyurethane Largus boot from the market after measuring it against the original 636465.

Outer CV joint — INKO 28/30/44, cross-model sharing, and a fitment conflict (July–August 2026). The X80 pre-facelift automatic transmission shares the same outer CV joint as the restyled X80F and the B50 66. An INKO outer CV joint (ШРУС наружный 28/30 ABS 44) bought via Wildberries (wildberries.ru/catalog/186740444) fit one member's automatic-transmission car perfectly, with matching spline count 67. Arсhi 77 confirmed the 28/30/44 spec works on automatic transmission and has INKO joints on both sides 6869; Victor separately named the specific part number INKO 319092A for the same 28/30 ABS 44 spec 70. Arсhi 77 argues the outer CV joint's geometry (spline count, diameter, length) is set by the drive shaft and wheel hub design, not by the gearbox — and since the X80's drive shaft is unified across MT and AT, the outer joint should be the same for both 71. Conflict: despite ordering the same INKO 319092A part per these published specs, Андрей Б. found it did not fit — the wheel/hub side fit perfectly, but the shaft side would not engage, forcing a return 72. Victor noted the hub side takes 28 splines 73; Андрей Б. planned to measure the OEM part on arrival, noting other members suggested fitment issues may not be explained by spline count alone 74. Net: the "same joint fits AT and MT" claim is disputed by at least one real-world fitment failure with a nominally correct part.

Inner CV joint — ball-type reported on a manual transmission (July 2026), conflicting with the tripoid design noted above. A member's mechanic, working on a manual-transmission left inner CV joint, was surprised to find it was a ball-type joint rather than the more common tripoid type, and could not find it sold separately from the complete drive shaft 757677. Vasily explained this is not unusual — manufacturers are increasingly using ball-type joints instead of tripod-type on newer designs — and noted his own replacement left-drive MT part was in transit 78. Note: this sits in tension with the "manual transmissions use 26-spline tripoid inner CV joints" finding recorded above 474849 — it is unclear whether this reflects a running change across production years, a genuinely mixed parts pool, or inconsistent terminology between reports; treat "MT = tripoid" as not universal.

Complete drive assembly sourcing — vendor and marketplace options (July 2026). After a right-side drive (with support/carrier bearing) sheared on a manual-transmission car, a member sought a complete replacement drive assembly including the support bearing. Options surfaced: vendor Vasily (contact via direct message) 798081, the Avito marketplace, and vedro.pro, which offered a complete assembly at 15,000 RUB (RU market, July 2026) 82. This is well below the 13,000–27,000+ RUB range for complete assemblies recorded elsewhere in this card, underlining how much assembly pricing varies by source/condition 79808182.

Drive shaft (ШРУС) part numbers differ by side (August 2026). External drive shafts are not the same part on both sides: 5CA02560X is the right-side shaft (longer), 5CA02550X is the left-side shaft (shorter) 8384. This surprised several members, who assumed a shared part; the explanation given is that the right side carries an additional intermediate/support shaft (промежуточный вал) — because the gearbox sits offset to one side of the engine bay, the right driveshaft run is longer and the CV joint itself is unaffected, only the shaft length and presence of the intermediate shaft differ 858687888990919293949596. Whether this left/right numbering also differs between manual and automatic transmissions was raised but not confirmed in this exchange 91. Parts can be looked up on the ZZap app by part number (not reliably by vehicle model) 868788.

docs.title: Engine mounts — owner experience and fakes
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #counterfeit · #patron · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Owners disagree about aftermarket engine mounts (подушки двигателя) on the Mazda 6 GG-based X80. For the base part number, OEM price and the Patron/Mazda alternatives see engine mounts; this card collects owner experience and counterfeit warnings (September-October 2026) 12.

Aftermarket versus original: lifetimes. Victor 🇷🇺 reports that an original mount died at about 45,000 km, that an aftermarket Patron mount on the right side lasted about a year, and that he has since run an aftermarket mount for 1.5 years without problems 134. Arсhi 77 takes the opposite view: originals last (the original lower mount lasts long and the upper one sags), and cheap analogues sagged quickly on a Mazda owner's car he knows 56. Both positions are reported as stated; no mileage-controlled comparison was posted.

GH versus GG mount type. Victor 🇷🇺 says a GH-type mount has a rubber nub that seats faster than the GG type, and that a bracket resting on a GG cushion is bad news; the thread does not spell out the full fitment consequence 7.

Right engine mount FA0139060 from Emex: a non-original box. Konstantin ordered the FAW right engine mount FA0139060 (listed for the B50) from the Emex marketplace and received a Chinese-made box branded WHCQ (Wuhu Chuangqi Auto Parts, "Опора двигателя правая") that carried the same FAW number, and the catalogue row was offered by supplier code LEWX 28. Konstantin understood the order as FAW; Victor 🇷🇺 says WHCQ is not an original brand even though the part numbers match 910.

Emex supplier codes to avoid (per Victor 🇷🇺, October 2026). LEWX (right engine mount, WHCQ), GBMH (left brake pads), SXWE (non-original spark plugs), HUTY (crooked non-original right mount), QKLT (fuel filter without FAW markings, and brake pads), GUGF (air filter that is not FAW, and left brake pads) 10. The earlier HUTY report is also in engine mounts; for how to tell genuine from copy in general see genuine vs. OEM vs. analog parts.

docs.title: Engine mounts — part number and alternatives
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #mazda-6-compat · #part-number · #patron

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Part number. OEM engine mount: 5CA139060 (also referenced as FA0139060). OEM cost is approximately 6,000 RUB (RU market, April 2025) from Chinese parts sites; a Mazda OEM hydro mount was separately reported at 10,000+ RUB (RU market, April 2025) 123.

Quality issues. Mounts sold under the FAW code FA0139060 from supplier HUTY (via the Emex platform) were found defective — uneven rubber sealing and poorly formed metal components 45. Tested alternatives from one member: Patron and Tatsumi brands were acceptable; Miles 150 was rejected for poor quality; a fake "OEM" labeled part was also rejected. Chinese-manufactured parts in general show persistent QC issues in this category 4567.

Right vs. left/lower mount, and Patron caveat. The right-side mount differs from the Mazda 6 GG equivalent and should use either the genuine OEM part or a pressed-in cartridge sourced from the GG mount — at 48,000 km no visible wear was found on a GG-sourced cartridge in one owner's report 128910. Patron should not be used for the lower engine mount — incompatibility/poor fit was confirmed when sourcing a Patron lower mount intended for a Mazda GG 1112. By contrast, the Patron right-side mount (hydraulic type) was tested on a restyled X80 and performed well after one day of use (though long-term data is still limited) 1112. At 48,000 km, a side-by-side comparison of the stock (worn) lower engine mount against a new Patron mount showed a visible difference in damping condition, favoring the fresh Patron part over the deteriorated stock one 1314.

Left engine mount — inspection note. The same member found the left engine mount to be in quite normal condition on inspection; after removing it to check, they reinstalled the original rather than replacing it, planning to re-inspect around 20,000 km later. A Jikiu-brand cartridge was kept on hand as a spare in the meantime 12.

Right engine mount alternative — Mazda 6/Atenza 2002–2007 (July 2026). Another cross-model alternative for the right-side engine mount: SAT brand part ST-GJ6G-39-060E (Mazda OEM equivalent GJ6A39060), sourced from the Mazda 6/Atenza (2002–2007). Available on Ozon for 4,141 RUB (RU market, July 2026) with next-day delivery 15. Vadim B asked how long members' mounts had lasted after buying via an Ozon link — his own lasted only 4 months before failing, which he suspected was a counterfeit or defective unit 1615. Fab, testing the same Mazda-sourced mount, reported 6 months of service with only partial reduction in vibration — better than Vadim's experience but still short of a durable fix 17.

OEM engine mount identification — QR code and bilingual markings (July 2026). OEM part number FA0139060 (matches the 5CA139060/ FA0139060 numbering already noted above). Genuine Chinese-FAW-made mounts are marked with a laser-engraved QR code and bilingual Chinese/Russian text: "一汽零件" (yīqì língjiàn — "FAW part") and "纯正部件" (chúnzhèng bùjiàn — "genuine/original component"), alongside Russian translations "запчасть FAW" and "оригинальная деталь" 1819. Victor reported finding parts marked this way on AliExpress and called it "original from China" 1820. Vasily disputed the authenticity of the specific part shown, pointing out that genuine factory mounts do not carry white-paint lettering like the one pictured, and separately cautioned that QR codes are not proof of authenticity — Chinese counterfeiters also fake QR codes and link them to look-alike websites, so a scannable code alone does not confirm a genuine part 2122.

More owner experience and fakes (September-October 2026). Lifetime reports on Patron and other aftermarket mounts, the GH/GG mount note and the Emex supplier codes to avoid are collected in engine mounts — owner experience and fakes 2324.

docs.title: FAW X80 OEM article numbers posted in chat
docs.text:

docs.title: Genuine vs. OEM vs. analog parts
docs.text:
Tags: #oem · #counterfeit

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

A recurring point of confusion in the community: what actually counts as "original," "OEM," or a "duplicate/copy" part. Community consensus reached in one discussion (Nov 2025):

  • "Original" part = bears the FAW brand, has a FAW catalog number, and comes in FAW packaging.
  • OEM parts from other suppliers (same engineering/specification, different manufacturer/supplier than FAW's own branded channel) are legitimate parts, not "fake" duplicates — a catalog/part number identifies fitment, not a single unique manufacturer. Many manufacturers can legally produce parts to the same spec.
  • Cross-supplier parts made to the same specification are therefore not "duplicates" in the counterfeit sense — duplication of a design is not the same thing as illegitimate copying.
  • Visual verification is the practical way to catch actual counterfeits: genuine OEM and counterfeit parts typically differ visibly in build quality and markings once compared side by side. Example given: the front hub assembly, part 5CA033047B, can be visually verified by removing the brake disc and comparing the hub's finish/markings against a known-genuine reference 1234567891011.

Counterfeit "originals" and risky suppliers (October 2026). Konstantin noted that a part with the original number L3A140581 can be found for about 500 RUB (RU market, October 2026) but the delivery may be a counterfeit; the function of the part is not named. Victor 🇷🇺 replies that fake "originals" are sold for rings, springs and clutches and arrive as counterfeits 1213. A concrete case is the right engine mount FA0139060 bought on Emex that came in a non-FAW WHCQ box; Victor's list of Emex supplier codes to avoid is in engine mounts — owner experience and fakes 1415.

docs.title: Intermediate shaft, 6206 bearing, AT right shaft
docs.text:
Tags: #drive-shaft · #bearing · #counterfeit · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The right-hand drive shaft of the X80 runs through an intermediate (support) shaft; this card collects what owners posted in September-October 2026 about that shaft, its bearing and the automatic-transmission right shaft. For the left/right shaft numbers, CV joints and seals see drive shafts, CV joints and axle seals 12.

Automatic-transmission right shaft 5CA12550X. Victor 🇷🇺 names the right drive shaft assembly of the automatic (AKPP / АКПП) car as 5CA12550X, listed at about 10,000 RUB at Emex (RU market, September 2026), and was not sure the listing was original. He says only the inner CV joint (ШРУС) can be replaced separately, and did not know whether the AT intermediate shaft matches the manual one. For a manual car he says a febest 0512-6gg shaft is the same length 13.

Intermediate shaft bearing. Victor 🇷🇺 names the bearing as 62062RS (i.e. 6206-2RS). In that thread he said the metal-shielded version is the 62062RS and the "2RS" version has plastic seals, and that he paid about 320 RUB (RU market, September 2026); Arсhi 77 bought the same kind for about 250-300 RUB (RU market, September 2026) and notes that dealer kits charge many times more 24567. Victor also quoted about 5,000 RUB (RU market, September 2026) for a complete febest intermediate shaft with bearing and seals, fitted to a manual car; the AT length was unknown to him 78.

Do AT and MT parts interchange? Victor 🇷🇺 says the intermediate bearing is the same across Mazda 6 applications and that factory shafts come in lengths of 398-400 mm and 410 mm, but that the intermediate support differs between manual and automatic 910. Arсhi 77 disagrees on the safe approach: part articles differ even when diameters match, a bearing or seal with a different working edge may not sit on the shaft and can leak soon, and he advises against experimenting; asked whether the bearing is the same for AT and MT he gave no certain answer 1112.

6206 bearing: brands and size. The 6206 is 30 x 62 x 16 mm; the sealed variant is written 6206-2RS (the SKF 6206-2RS1 listing Victor shared on vseinstrumenti.ru, which he described as genuine) 1314. Victor advises avoiding FAG (фаг), which he says is mostly counterfeit, and the ZZ variants, which have metal shields instead of rubber seals; Koyo is acceptable if genuine, and NTN lists the rubber-sealed version as 6206LLU 1516171819. The messages do not restate which assembly this bearing is for.

6206 prices (RU market, September 2026). About 900 RUB at the Autodoc distributor; 250-550 RUB on Ozon and Wildberries, which Victor considers counterfeit; about 1,500 RUB for a special order at a parts store; Victor also recalls a genuine SNR 6206.EE at a Renault dealer for about 800 RUB roughly five years earlier 20212223.

A Ford/Mazda crankcase ventilation hose (labeled FMVQ, ROSTECO article 21439) was mentioned as a compatible alternative for the X80, available on Ozon: https://ozon.ru/t/csYbp3P. The X80's intake manifold can be sourced from the Ford Duratec HE engine family (displacement range 1.8–2.5 L), since this engine platform is shared across multiple vehicles: Ford Fusion, Ford Mondeo (4th/5th gen), Mazda 6 (GG/GH), and Volvo S40 all use compatible manifolds 3.

Door lock fasteners (VAZ 2101/Zhiguli). Door lock screws from the 1973 VAZ 2101 (Zhiguli) are a one-to-one compatible replacement for the X80's door lock fasteners — metric M6 size, with conical washers 7. docs.title: Sourcing parts reliably — tools and caution
docs.text:
Tags: #sourcing · #cross-reference · #counterfeit

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Cross-reference lookup tool. The DROM database (Drom.ru's parts database / "Drom baza" app) provides a comprehensive cross-reference of OEM and aftermarket parts by vehicle model, including part codes and compatible alternates across manufacturers. It's useful for identifying Mazda-compatible components and confirming fitment before purchase — open the DROM database, pick the vehicle and "all cities," and it surfaces brake pads, hubs, and other parts with their codes and analogs 123.

Retailer reliability cautions, especially on Ozon and similar marketplaces 45678910: 1. Counterfeit risk exists for popular items (engines, filters, spark plugs) — one example: a refurbished engine sold as new at a discounted price (160,000 RUB, RU market, July 2025, vs. a ~230,000 RUB RU-market rate (July 2025) for genuinely new), with repair marks visible despite the "new" listing. 2. Photo mismatches are common — some sellers copy stock photos from the internet but ship a different or lower-quality item than pictured. 3. Return policies are restrictive for parts imported from outside Russia (China/Asia) — Ozon has claimed such items are non-returnable, and disputes with sellers often fail. 4. One specific specialist retailer, kitzapchasti.ru, has a mixed reputation — some community members report no issues, while others cite incomplete listings and photo-accuracy problems. Conflict: this remains disputed within the community rather than settled. 5. Best practice recommended by the community: use well-known local shops or Mazda OEM dealers for cross-fit parts, and request pre-shipment photos when ordering critical/expensive components.

Specific supplier: rear door handles/cables/locks (Sept 2025). kitzapchasti.ru carries rear door handles, cables, and locks for the X80: https://kitzapchasti.ru/catalog/Faw/FAW-X80/kuzov/ruchki-trosa-dveri-zamki/ 1112.

Specific supplier: Moscow Avito seller, 2018-model parts (April 2026). A Moscow-based Avito seller specializes in FAW X80 parts sourced from disassembled 2018-model cars, including rare items such as BSM (body control module) units. Search "X80" within the seller's profile for current inventory 1314.

Bulk OEM order experience — mastergtr75 (May 2026). One owner ordered a complete set of front-suspension-area body components (door, fender, hinges, door seals) from factory-authorized seller mastergtr75: total 85,000 RUB for parts + 13,000 RUB delivery (RU market, May 2026). Shipping was handled by the "Delovyye Linii" (Business Lines) freight carrier with cargo insurance; the buyer reported a reasonable delivery timeframe and reliable service 1516.

docs.title: Shifter knob — thread spec and fitment
docs.text:
Tags: #fitment

Thread spec. Shifter knobs use a 10 mm diameter threaded mount 1. Thread pitch varies by knob model, and no member had tools on hand to measure it precisely — generic/universal replacements may not fit due to this thread-pitch mismatch even when the diameter matches 234561.

Original knob geometry. The stock X80 knob has a flat bottom and triangular profile — some aftermarket knobs may not fit this geometry even with a compatible thread 24.

Aftermarket options. Generic knobs from AliExpress are available with LED/multicolor lighting (including 7-color, USB-charging models), fitted for both MT and AT shift patterns; some come with multiple thread adapters covering several car models simultaneously (a "3-in-1" thread adapter design) 789101112. Fitment should still be verified before buying, and adapter-based "fits-everything" knobs are considered more of a niche/enthusiast choice than a guaranteed match 11.

docs.title: Spark plug specifications and cross-references
docs.text:
Tags: #spark-plugs · #part-number · #torch · #cross-reference · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

OEM nominal part number: 370701037K (Chinese part number).1 OEM standard spec: TORCH QH5RTIP-13.1 Alternative iridium option: TORCH QH6RIU-11 — one owner at 100,000 km successfully replaced with this same model.21

Recommendation. TORCH brand is considered reliable by the community; both the standard and iridium versions are acceptable, with the choice coming down to owner preference and budget. Some owners have also used non-iridium alternatives or other brands successfully.3241

Torque specifications (2025-06 report). Spark plug tightening torque varies by thread/hex diameter: 8mm plugs → 8–15 Nm; 10mm → 15–20 Nm; 12mm → 20–25 Nm; 14mm → 20–25 Nm; 18mm → 20–30 Nm. Contact nut torque: M4 → 0.8–1.5 Nm; M5 → 3.0–4.0 Nm. Using the correct torque wrench setting is critical to avoid over-tightening and thread damage.56

Removal/installation tools and more brand data points (2025-09 report). Spark plug socket size is 16mm; a special long socket with a rubber insert or magnet is recommended to avoid dropping the plug into the cylinder. Additional brand data points from the community: NGK plugs verified working at 2,900 RUB per piece (RU market, September 2025); TORCH QH5RIU-13 also tested and confirmed working; Miles 067 verified reliable past 9,000+ km. Some owners apply spark-plug grease/vaseline to the connector and contact terminal to ease future removal — helpful but not required.789101112131415161718

QH5RIU-13 as a recommended X80 (2020) plug (2025-10 report). TORCH QH5RIU-13 is separately recommended for the FAW X80 2020, available on the Ozon marketplace by searching the code directly.19

Miles ALSP067 iridium plugs as a Ford/Mazda equivalent. Miles ALSP067 iridium-electrode plugs serve as an analog to Ford/Mazda-spec plugs; one owner reported 10,000 km of successful operation.20

Pricing (2025-10). Spark plugs cost approximately 1,600 RUB for a set of 4 when ordered from Emax (October 2025, RU market).21 Separately, LYNXauto SP216 iridium/platinum plugs were purchased for ~1,800 RUB (November 2025, RU market) — reported as high quality, with even gaps, perfect fitment, and a quieter-running engine after installation.2223

Removal difficulty at 100,000+ km (2025-11 report). At high mileage, spark plugs can be very difficult to remove due to corrosion/seizing, with a real risk of breaking the ceramic insulator if over-torqued during removal. Recommended installation torque: 18 kgf maximum — do not over-tighten. One owner spent 4.5 hours replacing a single plug after breakage during removal.24252627282930313233

Degradation by 30,000 km causing hard starts (2024-08 report). Factory-fit TORCH QH6RTIP-13 plugs (1.3mm gap) showed significant electrode wear and insulator damage by 30,000 km, causing hard starts and weak ignition on one owner's car. Community-suggested alternatives: QH6RIU-11 (0.2mm gap difference from OEM, same heat range) and QH5RIU-13 (1.3mm gap matching OEM, one heat grade lower, cheaper). Reported pricing: these alternatives run roughly ₽50–100 each on AliExpress, versus a dealership markup of ₽500–700 per plug (both RU market, August 2024) for the same/equivalent parts.34353637383940414243444546

Budget spark plug set pricing (2026-05 report). A budget spark plug set was available at approximately 900 RUB for a full set (May 2026), with Miles-brand plugs and other alternatives at similarly competitive prices.47

Wear inspection at 30,000 km — photo documentation (2026-05 report). One owner removed the spark plugs at 30,000 km for inspection; photos show typical deposit accumulation and wear patterns for that mileage, used by the community as a wear-progression reference point.48

docs.title: Suspension springs, arms and bushings
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #price · #mazda-6-compat · #bushing · #silent-block

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Upper suspension arm pricing (2024-10-16, RU market): FAW original: 3,500 RUB on Ozon, 7,125 RUB at Kitparts; Mazda 6 GG-sourced alternative: 4,500 RUB on Drom; AVT-brand alternative: 2,107 RUB each. Genuine FAW parts are significantly more expensive than cheaper alternatives, which are often Mazda-sourced or Chinese-branded 12345.

Front suspension springs — availability. Springs for the X80 have been reported as difficult to find through regular retail; often only available by special order or directly from official FAW dealers. One owner whose spring broke had limited sourcing options beyond the official dealer network 678.

Front suspension spring pricing over time (RUB, RU market): - ~1 year before 2025-04-14 (exact date unclear): roughly 5,000+ RUB per pair, from Chinese suppliers like KitParts with 2–3 day delivery; price may have risen since 9101112 - April 2025: LYNXauto brand springs 3,000 RUB per pair; OEM springs 13,000+ RUB per pair (emergency winter-failure replacement); a Mazda-compatible spring option mentioned at 50,000 RUB was called a "normal" (i.e. non-discounted) price point 13141516 - May 2025 (RU market): Kitparts 2,800 RUB per spring (non-original, may require cutting/modification to fit); official dealer ~3,000 RUB per spring; Chinese direct-import 4,800 RUB for an original-spec assembly with spring cups. Quality varies — Kitparts springs are noted as non-original and may need trimming; always confirm exact fitment with the vendor before buying 17181920

Other suspension component pricing (April 2025, RU market): notable retail vs online price gaps — longitudinal bushings 1,200 RUB in local shops vs 665 RUB on Ozon; KitParts components 15,000 RUB in local shops vs 9,000 RUB on Ozon for the same items. Ozon was consistently 30–50% cheaper than brick-and-mortar retailers for these parts 2122.

Aftermarket rear springs in development (June 2026). Community member Айрат is manufacturing replacement rear springs for the FAW X80 (restyle model) using truck-parts manufacturing technology, with plans to seek official certification. He is actively seeking used front springs from owners for expert testing/comparison. Pricing and availability were not yet announced as of this discussion — contact via private message for updates 2324252627.

Front upper-arm silent blocks: Tenacity AAMMA1017 (September 2026). Victor 🇷🇺 says the front upper-arm rubber-metal bushings (silent blocks / сайлентблоки) wear out before the ball joints on low-mileage cars; his originals failed at about 50,000 km. He replaced them with Tenacity AAMMA1017 and reports about 7,000 km without problems 2829. A review screenshot shared by Arсhi 77 claims Tenacity silent blocks last 40-60k km in calm driving and about 20-30k km on rough roads or with full load, and that the rubber is softer than many old originals 30.

Rear lower-arm bushing cross-references. For the bushing at the rear lower-arm bolts (the camber/toe bolts, развальные болты) Victor 🇷🇺 gives KIA 55215-38000 and Shin Hwa SH-129, in reply to a catalogue drawing of the rear arm with the bushing marked by a red arrow 3132.

Rear suspension diagram with Mazda numbers. Arсhi 77 posted a Mazda-catalogue exploded diagram of the rear suspension as an article-lookup aid. Its callouts include 28-010A (coil spring), 28-0A3 (spring seat), 28-300 and 28-300Z (lower arm), 28-330A (arm bushings) and 28-700 (shock top mount); check the callout-to-part mapping against a live catalogue before ordering 33.

docs.title: Thermostat — counterfeit risk and testing
docs.text:
Tags: #thermostat · #cooling · #counterfeit · #aliexpress

A buyer purchased a thermostat from a Chinese parts site (Китзапчасти, Nizhny Novgorod branch) and found the unit had no stamped temperature activation number on the shell — OEM units are normally expected to show this marking visibly on the housing 12. The buyer considered returning it as a likely counterfeit 34.

Community-suggested verification: pull the thermostat out of its housing and drop it in boiling water — a genuine unit's valve should open properly at the rated temperature; failure to open (or opening at the wrong temperature) indicates a fake or defective part 56. Note that professional-looking packaging is not proof of authenticity — it can conceal low-quality goods 5.

docs.title: Tire pressure specification and seasonal adjustment
docs.text:
Tags: #tires

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

OEM tire pressure specification for the FAW X80 is 2.4–2.6 bar (34–37 psi), per the label on the door jamb 123. Higher pressure (2.6 bar) reduces rolling resistance for better fuel economy but reduces ride comfort; lower pressure improves comfort. Community-suggested seasonal split: 2.6 bar in summer, 2.4 bar in winter to account for temperature-driven pressure changes 4.

docs.title: Summer tire sizes and pricing (R17 wheels)
docs.text:
Tags: #tires · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Factory-standard summer tire size for the FAW X80 on 17-inch (R17) wheels is 215/60 R17 1. Alternative sizes some owners run: 215/65 (a softer ride, slightly taller/higher profile) and 225/60 to 225/65 (also softer, taller profile than stock) 12.

Prices as of 2025-03-29/30, Russian market 345: - Belshina 225/60 R17: 5,900–6,500 RUB - Belshina 215/60 R17 (stock size): ~6,200 RUB via Yandex.Market, with installment payment available (4 payments over 2 months)

R18 fitment (Oct 2025). R18 225/55 tires have approximately 15 mm greater overall diameter than the OEM size and were confirmed by testing to fit the vehicle. Separately, some owners note that 235/65 R17 (Touareg-size) wheels are very heavy and not recommended, adding extra stress on the X80's suspension and engine 67891011121314151617.

Quality varies hugely by manufacturer even at the same size (July 2026). Same size (18-inch 225/80) tires show vastly different durability and quality by manufacturer despite identical external dimensions: Kama (Russia) ~5,000 RUB, Kumho (Korea) ~12,000 RUB, Bridgestone (Japan) ~18,000 RUB, Hunlun (China) ~2,500 RUB. Factory origin and manufacturing standards vary significantly between these price points; one member reported poor real-world durability with the cheap Chinese option 18.

Triangle TC101 Advantex quality-defect experience (July 2024). A member who bought Triangle TC101 Advantex 215/60 R17 96V tires experienced significant quality issues: after 2 weeks of driving and balancing work, one tire was found to be severely elliptical (oval-shaped) and imbalanced. Diagnostic inspection at a tire service station using a laser level under load confirmed the deformation, and the tire was replaced under warranty. Sourced from mosautoshina.ru; price was noted as decreasing during the period 19202122.

17-inch size comparison (Sept 2024). One commenter says 225/55R17 is about 2 cm smaller in overall diameter than 225/60R17, which is why some drivers avoid it; 235/60R17 is about 12 mm larger in overall radius and wider, and sits better in the arch; 225/65 is about 2 cm larger and rubs in the arch 2324. Another commenter notes that the stock 215/60 looks small on the car and that width should be checked on the car 25.

Owner tyre experience (Sept 2024). One owner ran Continental 225/55R17 for three seasons and found them soft with good cornering grip, better than 225/60R17. He rates the Bridgestone 225/60 and the Kama tyre as poor, and Viking tyres as soft and strong at the bead 2627. He plans Chinese winter tyres for one or two seasons, because Continental winter tyres cost about 20,000 RUB and Michelin-level ones about 23,000-24,000 RUB (RU market, September 2024; the posts do not say whether per tyre or per set) 28. See also winter tyres.

docs.title: Towing hitch (farkop) — installation
docs.text:
Tags: #installation · #availability

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Installation procedure. Fitting an aftermarket towing hitch requires removing the lower bumper skirt only — the upper bumper stays in place 123. Removal technique: pull the top part of the skirt toward you, then unscrew the self-tapping screws from the bottom 4. For the hitch's electrical wiring, there is enough space to route cables from the left side, near the rear light 56. The owner's manual does not recommend installing a tow hitch, but many owners do so anyway without reported issues 7.

Availability. - As of 2024-10-19, one owner installed a hitch himself; sourcing required searching outside official channels 12. - By 2024-10-21, an aftermarket hitch became available for retail sale on Ozon — summer 2024 had been a shortage period before that 8. - A specific model, Sheriff 3951.12 (X80 fitment), is available through nakuzov.ru and other major Russian auto-parts retailers: https://nakuzov.ru/catalog/farkopy-i-komplektuyushchie/farkopy/farkop_sherif_3951_12_dlya_faw_besturn_x80/ 9.

Towing hook (buksirovochnaya petlya/kryuk) — a different, factory recovery-loop part, not the aftermarket hitch above. OEM towing hook part 5DA050EJO (also cross-referenced from the FAW T77 platform) has thread spec M20×2.5 — confirmed by physical caliper measurement of the threads on a removed unit 1011121314151617181920212223242526. Original cost was 900 RUB in 2021 (RU market). A Lada Largus towing hook (~600 RUB, RU market, as of October 2025) has been used by one owner as a budget alternative — reportedly fitting a Besturn B50 and possibly (unconfirmed) the X80 too. Factory-price quotes were reported as fluctuating with the Yuan exchange rate, and members note that hooks matching this part number are either out of stock or priced very high through normal retail channels 27282930. Conflict: a VW Polo towing hook was also mentioned by community members as a possible fitment, but this was not confirmed within this discussion 26.

Kit contents, Sheriff 3951.12 (Russian passport sheet). The kit with article 3951.12 consists of 19 numbered items: bar (shtanga) x1; hitch hook (kryuk) x1; junction-box cover (podrozetnik, the socket plate) x1; bolt M8x30 DIN 933 x10; bolt M10x30 DIN 933 x2; bolt M12x1.25x40 DIN 961 x4; bolt M12x1.25x70 DIN 960 x2; nut M12x1.25 DIN 934 x4; washer 12 DIN 125 A x10; spring washer 8 DIN 127 x10; mounting plate (planka zakladnaya) x2; spring washer 10 DIN 127 x2; spring washer 12 DIN 127 x6; washer 8 DIN 9021 x10; washer 10 DIN 9021 x2; brackets (three different, 1 + 1 + 2 pieces); ball cap (kolpachok na shar) x1 31.

docs.title: TPMS sensors — part number and pricing
docs.text:
Tags: #tpms · #wheels · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Part number and frequency. Original TPMS sensor part number: 5GA037973 (also referenced as BM133714XA in a later message) 123. Frequency is model-year specific: post-2016 models use 434 MHz, pre-2016 models use 433 MHz 45. Aftermarket sensors from AliExpress labeled "for X80" often don't specify year and may be incompatible with 2020+ cars; sensors sold on Ozon built for the US market (different frequency) are also incompatible 678. Original sensors must be programmed/matched to the vehicle; cheap AliExpress alternatives may self-program, but a year-specific frequency mismatch will still prevent them from working 910. Installing a replacement sensor requires vehicle programming via a diagnostic scanner with an antenna module — a basic scanner is not sufficient 23.

Prices (RUB, RU market). Original sensor 5GA037973: 2,880 RUB (Naberezhnyye Chelny, 2024-10-24) 11. Aftermarket LUMER-brand sensor: 1,400 RUB (Ozon, RU market, 2024-10-24) — cheaper but carries the compatibility risk above 1213.

Battery failure and replacement (2025-05). When the TPMS warning light comes on despite normal tire pressure, the cause is often sensor battery depletion or lost programming 14. Two remedies discussed: 1. Replace the sensor outright — requires dismounting the wheel/breaking the bead, and reprogramming to the vehicle's frequency. Cost: ~4,300 RUB for an OEM sensor or ~3,200 RUB for an analog (RU market, May 2025) 1516. 2. Some sensors allow the battery itself to be swapped (CR2450-2P, 3V) by opening the housing and resoldering. One member reported success doing this on a Fiat Doblo, but the X80 sensor housing is epoxy-sealed, making non-destructive opening difficult 17181920.

Disagreement: some members report the X80 sensor housings are fully epoxy-sealed (forcing full replacement), while others say the battery can be changed with sufficient skill and soldering. A battery swap is considered a temporary fix at best; OEM sensor replacement is the recommended solution 1719.

docs.title: Wheel discs — Mazda-branded discs fit X80
docs.text:
Tags: #wheels · #mazda-6-compat

docs.title: Aftermarket wheel fitment — bolt pattern & bore
docs.text:
Tags: #wheels · #fitment

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Required aftermarket wheel specs for the FAW X80: 5×114.3 bolt pattern, and center bore (DIA) of not less than 67.1 mm. Other parameters (width, offset/ET, diameter) are flexible and can be chosen for looks/handling preference 1. If a wheel's center bore is larger than the hub (e.g. 76 mm DIA), centering rings are required to take up the gap. Example: an Alutec DTM 17" wheel (7.5J width, 38 ET offset, 76 mm center bore, 5×114.3 bolt spacing) fits the X80 but needs centering rings 12.

Offset (ET) guidance. ET45 wheels sit narrower/more inboard; smaller ET values (ET35/38/40/42) push the wheel further out toward the arch (flush look) — with these smaller ET values, the wheel looks wider on the car. For a disc width of 7–7.5 inches, the lower ET values (35–42) are recommended for a flush "stance" look 3.

Comprehensive factory wheel/tire fitment spec. FAW X80 factory parameters: R17 radius, 5×114.3 mm bolt pattern (PCD), 67.1 mm center bore (DIA), offset ET +50 to +52 (lower ET = more outboard/flush, consistent with the offset guidance above). Stock tire size is 215/60 R17. Fitment range: rim width 6.5–8.0 inches; acceptable tire sizes 215/60, 215/65, 225/55, 225/60 (225/65 is too wide and rubs the wheel arches at stock ET); ET can vary from 35–52 with wider aftermarket options available. Winter wheel options: steel stamped wheels (with optional wheel caps, ~1,300–1,400 RUB per wheel) or alloy wheels (nicer look, 1,000–3,000 RUB per wheel); both prices RU market, September 2024. A center bore (DIA) up to 70+ mm can be adapted with included plastic centering-reducer rings. General advice: use an online tire-fitment calculator to verify profile/diameter match before buying 4567891011121314.

docs.title: Wheel hub bearings — part numbers and defects
docs.text:
Tags: #wheel-hub · #bearing · #mazda-6-compat · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Assembly design. The front wheel hub on the X80 is a complete, sealed assembly — bearings cannot be replaced individually; only the whole hub is exchanged 1. Some hub variants differ only in whether they carry an ABS sensor (marked with an "A" or "B" suffix on the part code), but the core bearing assembly itself is the same across those variants 12.

Part numbers. Front hub: 5CA033047B 34. An earlier message reported part numbers FA012615X and FA012615XB as functionally equivalent — the hub is double-sided and the "B" suffix appears to reflect catalog/documentation differences rather than an actual functional difference between suppliers 56.

Quality / defect check. A correctly assembled rear hub bearing's outer race must be firmly pressed in and should not move by hand. Maximum allowable rim runout is 0.3 mm (equivalent to 0.09 mm of bearing radial play). If the bearing race can be pulled out by hand, this indicates an improper press fit or a counterfeit part — such hubs are considered 100% defective and should be rejected before installation. Cheap suppliers have been reported to grind serial numbers off defective units to obscure their origin 478910.

Mazda cross-compatibility. A rear wheel hub bearing that failed (audible noise) was successfully replaced with a Mazda-sourced part and has worked fine since 1112.

Availability. Rear wheel hub bearing sourcing was reported as difficult in Siberia: typical wait was 1+ week from major cities (Moscow, Kemerovo, Krasnoyarsk). One user searched roughly 1,500 km across Biysk, Kemerovo, and Krasnoyarsk without finding local stock. Suggested alternatives: check Kia-branded parts if regionally available (exact cross-model unclear), or order via nationwide online retailers (e.g. Wildberries) for 2–4 day delivery 1314151617181920.
