External Drive2 article on chip-tuning/power increase for the FAW Besturn X80 2.0 142hp, shared as a reference — it describes work done through Ecotune.ru (the same tuning brand referenced above); low confidence, single share with no in-chat discussion of results 4.

docs.title: Diagnostic tools, adapters and head-unit updates
docs.text:
Tags: #diagnostics · #elm327 · #obd · #firmware · #head-unit

Overview. Members shared three diagnostic-related files: an ELM327 adapter manual, a head-unit (radio) firmware update guide and a workshop diagnostic report. The scanner brands, Diagzone and the Car Scanner app are covered in OBD scanners, software and TPMS tools, Diagzone Pro and ECU scan tools; this card only summarises the shared files. All files are listed in Shared files and manuals. 123

ELM327 Bluetooth adapter guide. A 6-page Russian manual from the importer ORION (orionspb.ru) for the ELM 327 Bluetooth and ELM 327 Bluetooth Mini OBD-II adapters. The adapter converts OBD-II signals from the engine ECU into Bluetooth (a virtual COM port) so that diagnostic software on a PC, smartphone or tablet can talk to the car. With suitable software it can read and clear fault codes, show live values (RPM, engine temperature, supply voltage, sensor states), log trips (speed, distance, fuel use, time) and watch the cold-start warm-up. The manual covers PC and Android pairing, specifications and warranty, but lists no fault codes. 1

Head-unit (radio) firmware update, how-to summary. A one-page Russian guide for the FAW X80F radio, file name referring to the "BASIK MT ESP" variant, shared three times. Steps as written: (1) use a clean USB stick; (2) copy the file CR482XA_V1.56_20200224.MCU onto it; (3) also put at least one music file on the stick, and keep no duplicate .MCU names; (4) start the car engine before updating; (5) plug the stick in and switch the radio to USB playback if it did not switch itself; (6) hold RADIO + previous-track + next-track for more than 5 seconds to enter update mode; (7) choose MCU and press the right (SEL) button - the update takes about 1 minute and the radio then restarts by itself; (8) if the ESP warning lamp stays on afterwards, with the engine running select reverse gear (the radio volume drops) and wait a few seconds until the lamp goes out. The firmware file itself is not in the shared document. 245

For what the stock radio can and cannot do, and the aftermarket alternatives, see stock head unit limitations and head units and firmware resources. 2

Workshop diagnostic report. A shared PDF health report from the FAW diagnostic application (version V2.00.027) for a Bestune X80 (2016 and later), vehicle software V13.70, 44,328.10 km, run on 2024-11-05 and marked "before repair", under the path Health Report > ABS/EPS. It shows what an official-style report looks like and lists one fault code, C131000. The fault itself is discussed in ABS/ESP warnings. 3

docs.title: Head units, multimedia, and firmware resources
docs.text:
Tags: #head-unit · #firmware

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Stock (Baidu) head unit — Android Auto workaround. The factory Baidu multimedia unit doesn't run Android Auto natively, and Carlinkit dongles do not work with it 1. A wireless adapter sold on AliExpress (~3,800 RUB (RU market, April 2024), listed as "FAW X80 X40 T77 T33 WIZCAR A1 multimedia block adapter") adds wireless Android Auto to the stock unit without replacing the stereo or flashing firmware, and works with both iPhone and Android 23.

CarlinKit wireless adapter options and pricing (as of 2026-03-04). For owners running an aftermarket Android head unit (where wired Carlinkit dongles work, unlike on the stock Baidu unit above), three CarlinKit tiers were compared in-chat 4567: 1. A premium unit sold on OZON is CarPlay-only with higher specs but is expensive — likely 20,000+ RUB (RU market, March 2026) once Russian VAT/import markup is added 5. 2. CarlinKit Ultra2 (Android 15, SM6350 chipset, 8GB+128GB) on AliExpress at 11,128 RUB (RU market, March 2026) with a -53% discount applied 6. 3. CarlinKit X1CA/X2CA, a budget wireless CarPlay/Android Auto adapter supporting the Baidu Carlife protocol (relevant for better compatibility with Chinese-platform head units), on AliExpress at 3,659 RUB (RU market, March 2026) with a -48% discount — one owner confirmed running this exact model, noting the same unit runs ~20,000 RUB (RU market, March 2026) on Yandex Market once VAT/import markup is applied 7. Separately noted: Android Auto video playback is limited to "parked vehicle" mode unless using an app like CarStream or Fermata Auto to unlock in-motion video.

Firmware and technical documentation. - fawforum.ru — a broad community-run resource with head-unit/camera firmware, patches, activation codes for OEM electronics, wiring/electrical schematics, tuning guides, and modification write-ups 8. - A Yandex.Disk archive ("FAW_X80_UPD") shared in-chat contains head-unit firmware files (including a firmware for the 4-camera system) and TPMS diagnostic data 910. - 4PDA forum (4pda.to) has an extensive collection of aftermarket radio firmware, update procedures, and CAN-bus adapter info for radios compatible with the X80 — useful when the factory unit is swapped for an aftermarket Android head unit 11.

OEM-shape replacement head units. - Canbox H-Line 5612-1083, sold on OZON, is an Android-10 unit shaped for the pre-facelift X80 (2013–2018): 4G/SIM, 4GB/64GB RAM/storage, DSP audio, QLED display, "Tesla-style" interface (as of 2025-01-04) 12. Note: the China-market X80 "Sport" trim (1.8L engine) instead ships with a factory Tesla-style unit with full climate-control integration on-screen, no Android, and a proprietary Chinese mapping app — not comparable to this aftermarket product 12. - Teyes head units are widely used and well regarded in the community for the 2018–2022 (facelift, "CC3L" variant) X80: 4GB/64GB RAM/storage, 8-core Android 10, IPS screen, DSP, EN7388 amplifier chip, 4G+Wi-Fi, 2-DIN, bundled CAN-bus adapter and steering-wheel-control frame 1314. One owner who also ran a Teyes unit on a Duster called it reliable 14; a second owner confirmed it installs and works well, with camera and parking-sensor integration functioning correctly — but reported an intermittent, device-specific issue where the head unit fails to pair with an OBD2 Bluetooth adapter (while the same adapter pairs fine with a phone); no confirmed workaround 15. A community member (Валерий) who bought a Teyes unit points to the seller's Avito profile ("Teyes/AutoUnit") for automotive electronics and installation 16. - Generic Android head units + CAN-bus adapters are notably cheaper on AliExpress than Russian retailers (Wildberries/OZON): roughly 1,200–1,500₽ on Ali vs. 4,000–8,000₽ in Russia for comparable frame+CAN-bus kits — trade- off is 2–3 weeks shipping from China vs. 1–2 days domestically. Frame and CAN-bus adapter can be bought separately from different vendors if needed 17.

Dashcam/multimedia fitment guide. frontcam.ru hosts a dashcam installation guide specific to the X80 2018–2020, and is also referenced generally for multimedia unit compatibility/installation research on the X80 1819.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

A collection of external videos and articles shared in-chat as references for specific maintenance jobs.

  • Serpentine belt squealing — diagnosis and fix. Article/guide covering checking belt tension, inspecting condition, and distinguishing temporary fixes (e.g. belt dressing/silicone spray — works, but only temporarily) from a proper permanent fix (replacement) 1.
  • Air filter brand comparison video. Compares multiple aftermarket air filter brands usable on the X80/similar platforms: Mann, Filtron, Marshall, Fortech, Finwhale, Kortex, Miles 2.
  • Radiator fan removal / intake manifold work — video guide. Answers a member's question about how much disassembly is needed to remove the radiator fan; video also covers thermostat replacement and intake manifold work as related context 34.
  • Rear longitudinal-arm bushing replacement — video guide 5.
  • Door panel soundproofing (shumoizolyatsiya), part 1 — Drive2 article by a community member, covering door-panel sound deadening 6.
  • Motor oil authenticity — "oil scammer exposure" article. Drive2 article explaining how to identify counterfeit motor oil and naming manufacturers implicated in counterfeiting 7.
  • Antifreeze G13 — specification and compatibility article. Covers G13 antifreeze specs, its environmental profile, and what it can/cannot be safely mixed with 8.
  • AKPP (automatic transmission) reference. Drive2 article with detail on the X80's automatic transmission: fluid capacity, part numbering, filter specs, and maintenance procedure 9. A second, dedicated Drive2 write-up ("AKPP X80, part 2") by the same kind of owner-documentation covers the fluid change procedure itself with filler/drain locations 10. A separate site, MirSmazok.ru, covers the Aisin 09G (09G-TripTronic) transmission specifically — fluid spec and recommended change interval — and discusses the gap between conservative manufacturer intervals and real-world owner practice, citing Wikipedia and other fluid-spec databases as cross-references 11. Kixx ATF Multi (product page: kixxlube.ru/products/34) was shared as a fluid confirmed to meet the JWS 3309 specification needed for FAW automatic-transmission applications 12. Separately, a Pravda.ru article argues for using AKPP "Sport"/S mode in stop-and-go traffic, on the reasoning that it reduces wear from constant shifting — shared as a discussion point, not a verified recommendation (low confidence) 13.
  • Sunroof lubricant guidance — Drive2 article. Covers proper lubricants for sunroof mechanisms, alongside related transmission-fluid guidance; shared as reference for sunroof maintenance 14.
  • Windshield/cowl drain cleaning. An AliExpress brush tool for clearing windshield drains/gutters to prevent water leaking into the cabin during rain or winter, ~110 RUB (RU market, February 2025) 15. Related: a YouTube Shorts video on avoiding electrical water damage in modern vehicles with sealed electronics, relevant to the X80's known water-leak issues 16.
  • Engine insulation blanket for extreme cold. "Автотепло" brand blanket from mirdopov.ru, recommended for Arctic/far-north conditions to improve warm-up time and heat retention 1718.
  • Tire/wheel sizing calculator. mosautoshina.ru/calc/ — lets you compare different tire/wheel size combinations and profiles and see the resulting change in vehicle ride height 19.
  • Driver's door trim removal video. Yandex Video-hosted (source: RuTube) tutorial demonstrating removal and reinstallation of the driver's door trim panel, including correct clip-removal technique to avoid breaking fasteners 20.
  • Engine-bay water leak (monoblock) — diagnostic video. YouTube Short showing a water leak at the monoblock/firewall area on a weathered X80, used in-chat to illustrate what this known leak point looks like 21. Related to the windshield/cowl drain cleaning entry above, which addresses a similar water-intrusion path.
  • Dashboard warning messages — RuTube video. "Essential warning messages for all FAW BESTURN X80 owners" — walks through the vehicle's warning lights/messages (service reminder, TPMS fault, turn-signal bulb fault, low battery voltage, overspeed, prolonged-driving alert) with timestamps for each 22.
  • Fuel filter replacement — YouTube video. Step-by-step walkthrough ("How to change the FUEL filter on FAW X80"): accessing the filter cover, removing the filter, pump disassembly, correct reinstallation, and post-replacement startup 2324.
  • DIY radiator cleaning tool — T-shaped tube design (low confidence). A member's suggested approach for cleaning the radiator without removing it: inject water via a T-shaped tube entering from the middle, perpendicular to the fins; since the radiator fins are mounted vertically, a horizontal tube in this orientation causes less fin damage than a single flat-tube pass 25.
  • Oil/air/cabin filter part numbers — pinned group message. The exact part numbers for the engine oil filter, air filter, and cabin filter are maintained in a pinned message at the top of the Telegram group chat rather than a single external site — check pinned messages first before asking 2627.
  • Fuel-standards article (Auto.ru, low confidence, general context, not X80-specific). "Fuel norms 2026: why refineries were allowed to produce Euro-3" — discusses Russian refineries being permitted to produce lower-grade Euro-3 fuel instead of Euro-5, attributed to refinery damage and capacity constraints; shared as background on fuel-quality risk rather than a car-specific fact 28.
  • Fuse and relay diagram database. vsepredohraniteli.ru hosts a comprehensive, X80-specific fuse/relay location reference with schematic diagrams, descriptions, and photos of block locations (e.g. headlight fuses, instrument-cluster fuses, cigarette-lighter fuse) — useful for electrical troubleshooting 29. Independently re-shared and endorsed again about a year later; the poster noted the site is thorough enough in Russian that non-Russian speakers shouldn't bother trying to translate it — everything needed is there 303132.
  • "Slippery road" warning light — Drive2 forum post. Community-written post detailing causes and fixes for the "скользкая дорога" (slippery-road) dashboard warning 33.

docs.title: OBD diagnostic scanners, software, and TPMS tools
docs.text:
Tags: #obd · #diagnostics · #scanner · #tpms · #elm327 · #battery

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Software/platform. Diagzone (X431 ecosystem) is the community's main diagnostic software; the Diagzone Pro subscription covers 650+ vehicle brands and includes the X80 12. It pairs with a cheap Mucar BT200 Wi-Fi/OBD dongle re-flashed to run the Diagzone backend, which can read the whole car (not just the engine) 12. A "FAWCARS" module for Diagzone with updates specific to facelift (2019+) models is needed to read those cars correctly 3. The Android app CarMin contains wiring schematics (electrical diagrams) for the X80, separate from any scan tool 4.

Hardware options. - Mucar/Makar BT200 + Diagzone Pro: the community's default budget combo, ~8,000 RUB for the dongle alone (RU market, October 2024) 5; needs the Diagzone firmware flashed onto it (or paying an extra 8,000–10,000 RUB (RU market, October 2024) for a pre-flashed unit) to unlock full-vehicle diagnostics 6. Bought without flashing, it reads engine (ECU) codes only, and even then not on every model 7. For transmission/electrical fault diagnosis, professional shop diagnostics (with a mechanic, not just the scanner) is recommended 8. As of 2024-12-27, community pricing for a minimal working setup was: Mucar BT200 hardware (~10,000–25,000 RUB retail) + Diagzone software/FAWCARS module (~720 RUB) (RU market, December 2024) + a smartphone/tablet to run it 9. Several members bought units via Ozon links shared in-chat around that date 10. - Thinkdiag 2: an alternative first-generation scanner that uses the same server/database backend as Diagzone-flashed Mucar units, so it should support the same vehicle list 11. - Autel TS508: a separate, dedicated tool — not a general OBD scanner — used specifically for TPMS (tire pressure sensor) programming/cloning 12. - ELM327 Bluetooth Mini v1.5 (Ozon product 929042666): a cheap generic Bluetooth OBD2 adapter confirmed to pair with the X80 without issues 13. Recommended free companion apps: Car Scanner or ScanMaster 14. Limitation: this class of adapter reads/clears only engine (ECU) codes over the OBD2 protocol — it cannot read mileage, airbag status, or other body-control-module data 15. The same class of generic ELM327 adapter was also independently confirmed to work for reading Opel and Škoda vehicles, not just FAW — i.e. it isn't FAW-specific hardware 16.

OBD-II port location. Under the steering wheel, slightly to the right of center, pointing downward. No trim/plastic needs to be removed to access it 1718.

ELM327 adapters — a separate cheap tier from Diagzone/Mucar. Distinct from the Diagzone-ecosystem hardware above, plain ELM327 clones are the budget default many owners simply keep in the glovebox: a "ELM327 OBD2 WI-FI v1.5, chip PIC18F25K80" unit sold on Ozon (https://ozon.ru/t/ynzRtEQ) pairs with the free Car Scanner Android app 1920. Reliability is inconsistent — quality control on ELM327 clones is "luck of the draw": one owner's unit connected intermittently and dropped every 5 minutes and was called unusable, while another reported the same class of adapter working without issues since 2015; a third bought a v2.1 model hoping for better luck 212223. Cost is low enough (~900 RUB (RU market, March 2024)) that replacing a bad unit isn't a big loss 22. - Car Scanner ELM OBD2 (Google Play: com.ovz.carscanner) is the community's preferred free app over the alternative OBD Mari, per an owner who tried both 2425. It displays lambda-sensor readings, engine load %, intake-manifold pressure, long- and short-term fuel-trim correction, coolant temperature and idle RPM, in addition to reading/clearing engine codes 2526. - Hard limit, confirmed by two different owners independently: a plain ELM327 can read/clear engine (ECU) codes only — it cannot read the airbag module, the AKPP (AISIN automatic transmission) module, or other body-control-module data, matching the limitation already noted for the ELM327 Bluetooth Mini above 2728. No Android app exists that surfaces X80-specific real-time parameters beyond the generic OBD2 PIDs — asked directly in-chat, the answer was a flat "no" 2930. - Battery-drain false codes. A flat/weak battery can trigger a wave of simultaneous fault codes (including on the AKPP) that clear on their own once the battery is reconnected/recharged. One owner had an airbag warning come on, took the car to a shop, was shown a long list of fault codes, and paid 1,500 RUB (RU market, February 2026) for a "diagnosis" that turned out to be exactly this — a fully discharged battery, not a real fault; afterwards they bought a cheap ELM327 adapter off AliExpress to check codes themselves in future and haven't seen any errors on it since 3132. A second, independent report corroborates the pattern: another owner's AKPP threw a low-voltage fault code after their battery went flat, and it likewise cleared once the battery issue was resolved 33. - Erasing (not just reading) codes may need a "dual-board" ELM327. One owner who bought an extended-chip ELM327 (paired with PC/phone software) a few years earlier noted that clearing/erasing fault codes needs a "2-плата" (two-PCB) version of the adapter — the listing has to say this explicitly; a plain single-board unit reportedly can read but not reliably erase 34. - FCAR CW700 — a separate professional-tier OBD2 scanner marketed for Chinese brands (Chery, Haval, Geely, Changan) with full-system code reading and free updates; suggested as an alternative when an ELM327 isn't enough, sold on Ozon (https://ozon.ru/t/b2ThFxa) 35.

TPMS (tire pressure sensors). - Sensor batteries are normally sealed inside the sensor housing and not meant to be user-replaceable, though a video exists showing a practical workaround for opening a sensor and replacing its battery 36. - A Moscow-based Avito service listing offers professional TPMS sensor programming, cloning, and adaptation to the vehicle — relevant for owners who buy generic/used replacement sensors and need them matched to the car 37. - A RuTube video walks through TPMS sensor installation and programming for the X80, including adapting universal (non-OEM) sensors 3839.

docs.title: Parts suppliers and catalogs directory (Russia)
docs.text:
Tags: #part-number · #catalog

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community-recommended suppliers and catalogs for sourcing FAW X80 parts in Russia, gathered from repeated recommendations over the chat's history. Reliability/trust levels below reflect what posters said at the time — always re-verify before ordering, since sites and stock come and go (one 2025-07-06 report found a previously-cited site no longer maintained 1).

Specialist FAW/Chinese-car parts retailers (most frequently recommended): - kitzapchasti.ru (also mirrored per-city, e.g. irkutsk.kitzapchasti.ru, cherkessk...) — general FAW X80 parts catalog, incl. suspension/steering section; stocked brake disc 5DA033251 at 3,140 RUB (RU market, April 2025) and caliper repair kits B5CA0339KIT/B5CA0339NAP in one supplier check 2345. Also stocks steering-rack dust boot (пыльник рулевой рейки), part 5AA032122, at 530 RUB (RU market, June 2025) with delivery to Naberezhnye Chelny 6. One member found some parts showed as available but were actually out of stock 7. Also stocks a complete GRM (timing chain) replacement kit, part 1026040-37KIT, with full assembly (chain, gears, tensioners, seals) 8. A front-suppport repair kit for the related B50 model (seals + piston, FC013501020) was also pointed to on this site when a member asked whether X80/B50 parts overlap 9. Independently confirmed multiple times over the chat's history as a first-stop catalog link 1011. - kitparts.ru — FAW Besturn X80 and X80F (facelift) catalog by section (bumpers, fenders, hoods, headlights, air filter housing, fuse blocks, hood hinges, door seals/window regulators, etc.); allows pre-orders with ~4-day wait 121314. Multiple members pointed newcomers here as the default first stop 1516. - kitzap.ru — sister/related FAW parts catalog (rear bumper trim, heater resistor/rheostat, hood — e.g. hood/bonnet for the FAW Bestune X80 NEW, part 5CA152310-#M3 — etc.) 1718192010. Disagreement: one member later cautioned against this site (referred to in-chat as "Китзап"/Kitzap), saying many parts listed as compatible do not actually fit despite the site claiming they do, quality on some items is inconsistent, and shipping deadlines are often missed — recommending kitparts.ru or other sellers instead 21. This is the opposite of the generally positive mentions above, so treat compatibility claims on this site with extra caution and verify before ordering. Also trades under the KITZAP brand name with its own Avito storefront (avito.ru/brands/kitzap) 22; the vendor has directly shared its own FAW Besturn X80 category page (kitzap.ru/spares/faw/faw_besturn_x80/) with members in-chat 23. - autocraft-kzn.ru (Kazan-based) — sells parts unpackaged (no OEM packaging), which keeps prices low; one member called it "a good shop, no issues so far"; front suspension/drivetrain parts confirmed sourced from here 2425. - chinaspare.ru and ooove.ru — Chinese-vehicle parts wholesalers; chinaspare recommended by a member who sources both parts and body panels there 262710. ooove.ru specifically was used by one member to cross-check a right-side engine mount (опора двигателя): the seller confirmed the FAW X80 and FAW Besturn B50 right engine mounts are identical parts despite being priced differently in ooove's own catalog (X80 catalog page vs. B50 catalog page) — a concrete example of why it's worth checking the B50 catalog for X80-compatible parts 28. - HemenPro (OZON marketplace store) — extensive FAW X80 plastic trim (moldings, grilles) primarily for pre-restyle models 29. - KitZapchasti (Irkutsk mirror) — brake disc pricing/availability specifically 30.

Aggregators / price comparison: - zzap.ru — parts aggregator; search by part number shows prices across multiple stores and regions 31. - emex.ru — an online parts database where entering the needed part brings up all compatible cross-referenced alternatives with prices; useful for finding fitments from other brands (Mazda GG6, early-2000s Ford Focus, etc. commonly turn up as cheaper analogs) — one member noted ordering through emex directly, versus Ozon where the same analog parts can be a bit pricier but returns are easier and delivery faster 32. Example product page: front shock absorber, part 5CA034700 (emex.ru/products/5CA034700/faw/40358) 33. - DRIVE2.ru parts database (drive2.ru/parts) — cross-referenced part numbers and alternatives, e.g. rear shock absorber reference for part 5CA028700A; useful for finding equivalents and comparing prices 34. - Drive2.ru "Part codes for FAW Besturn X80 2.0" article (drive2.ru/l/504151646054384568) — a frequently-reshared FAQ-style post listing OEM part codes (e.g. rear hatch struts, extended hood struts); shared independently at least twice, including once pinned as a standard answer to "where do I find part numbers" 3536. - Drive2.ru community write-ups (blog posts, not the parts DB) — owner guides covering trunk water drainage, fuel filter replacement, thermostat work, LED lighting upgrades, engine mount replacement, and emissions-system mods, each with photos and step-by-step instructions 37. One member also pointed newcomers generally to Drive2 as the best-documented community knowledge base for the X80, noting owner guides there go back to 2018-model-year cars — though a second member cautioned the forum also contains some incorrect information, so cross-check claims 3839. - Telegraph-hosted catalog mirrors — a community-maintained, section-by- section FAW X80 parts catalog (Body / Engine & Transmission / Suspension & Chassis / Cabin / Maintenance) with part-number search; open to correction 4041. - Pinned in-group PDF parts catalog. Separately from any external site, the Telegram group's own "catalog" tab has a PDF parts catalog pinned — members are encouraged to check it first before asking part-number questions in chat 42.

Marketplace/classifieds routes: - Drom.ru classifieds — useful for sourcing used suspension arms and other components, with part-number cross-referencing 19. - Avito — individual sellers list used/new body panels and other parts regionally (see the marketplace-part-listings card for specific examples). Example: a rear spring-mount control arm for Mazda 6 GG/GY (cross- compatible), Japan-made (Mibu), listed on Avito Moscow 43. - Wildberries and Ozon as general-marketplace routes (distinct from the specialist FAW shops above) — used for hub assemblies, springs, gaskets, and other parts that don't require the specialist catalogs; Ozon in particular is favored for CV boots, filters, and oil because returns are easier even if price is sometimes slightly higher 32. - vedro.pro — a marketplace where individual sellers list parts matched to the original FAW part number; one member noted that ordering a branded "FAW" part rarely gets you a genuinely FAW-branded item regardless of source, so treated as roughly equivalent to other aftermarket routes; example item found there at 3,990 RUB (RU market, July 2026) 44. - KitZap (kitzap.ru/kitzapchasti.ru), buying experience. One member who couldn't get a local market vendor to even measure/compare CV-joint and drive-shaft sizes for him ended up ordering from KitZap instead, on the basis that "it just needs to fit and work" — while waiting on a parallel order of a complete CV joint + hubs from another seller (Василий) 45. Another regular seller of the same parts (Arсhi 77) noted members generally test-fit parts themselves and offered to share links directly next time, saying he has swapped this type of dust boot "more than once" 4647. General guidance from this exchange: Chinese-import routes (chinaspare, KitZap, etc.) run roughly 10–30% cheaper than OEM/branded parts but typically add 500+ RUB (RU market, July 2026) shipping, and returns can incur additional fees — factor total cost, not just sticker price 4546.

Dealer/group-buy and community-vetted individual sellers: - Mastrgtr / mastergtr75 (VK group vk.com/mastrgtr, Telegram @mastergtr75) — official FAW dealer based in Chita; sells original parts with nationwide courier delivery; multiple members report successful purchases and recommend contacting the group directly with questions 484950. One member cautioned that some pushback on this seller came from people invested in selling Mazda-sourced "alternative" parts instead, suggesting bias in that criticism 51. - VK group vk.com/zapchasti_bez_natsenki ("parts without markup") — raised in-chat as a possible source; a member noted the group had posted specifically about the X80, but no first-hand purchase confirmation is on record yet 5.

Adjacent specialist retailers (single item, still useful as a channel): - Autochehly.ru — aftermarket plastic wheel-arch trim (podkrylki) from 1,150 RUB (RU market, December 2024), an alternative to OEM 52. - AutoMarket116 — multi-platform seller (OZON, Yandex Market, AliExpress) for window deflectors, radio frames, and general parts, with occasional discounts 53. - delot.ru — general tool retailer; useful for individual open-end wrenches (17–19mm sizes needed for suspension work) rather than buying a full wrench set 54. - Ashot-X80 — not a shop but an individual community member who makes custom-designed radiator-grille emblems and trunk badges for owners wanting non-OEM styling; contacted via the Telegram group directly for design/ordering 55. - izap24.ru — used/OEM-parts marketplace that ships Europe-sourced auto parts across Russia; referenced in-chat for a used catalytic converter for the X80 (2019), listed at 35,360 RUB (RU market, October 2025) 56. - nakuzov.ru — tow-hook (farkop) specialist retailer; stocks the Sheriff 3951.12 farkop specifically fitted for the FAW Besturn X80, with installation service and delivery/pickup options in Moscow 57.

General buying-route guidance. - Members repeatedly emphasize buying locally/in-region first when a local supplier stocks the part, to avoid long delivery waits from internet retailers — with kitzapchasti.ru, kitzap.ru, and ooove.ru as the fallback online catalogs when nothing local is available 1158. - Most parts for the X80, original or aftermarket, ultimately come from China; only smaller consumables (filters etc.) are commonly sourced from other manufacturers. Mazda 6 (2002–2008)-compatible parts are another common cross-reference route, though specific manufacturers for those weren't identified in this exchange 58. - Community forums and groups (general, not a shop). Beyond the parts catalogs above, owners point newcomers to: fawforum.ru (general discussion forum), the Drive2.ru FAW Besturn X80 section (drive2.ru/r/faw/besturn_x80/503628553397469808/, individual owner write-ups and technical discussion), and regional WhatsApp/Telegram owner groups — with this Telegram group cited as the most active one for the model 596061.

Tags: #tpms

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community knowledge base. A community member built a free, ad-free X80 knowledge base in Russian at fawx80.car.atjed.com/ru from this group and the sister group "FAW BESTURN X80". It covers repairs, part numbers and cross-references, prices, typical faults and maintenance, and every fact links back to its source message. The author asked for feedback, missing sources and removal requests, and warned the content is machine-generated, so errors are possible 1.

Outside forums and owner logs. - Owner reviews and logbooks on the Drive2 X80 page (drive2.ru/experience/faw/g5413) are a useful outside source; an auto.ironhorse.ru forum thread on the FAW Besturn X80 (comment page 6) is another. The poster suggested feeding such forum content into the knowledge base 234. - A drive2.ru article (https://www.drive2.ru/l/634094129248225421/) tabulates unsprung-mass parts (неподрессоренная масса) of the Mazda 6 GG and which brands fit them. Victor notes the X80 is not identical to the GG, and that the article itself puts compatibility near 70%, not 80% 56. See Mazda 6 platform parts compatibility. - Victor's Drive2 blog, entry 14, covers the rear springs and shock absorbers; he points to the second photo and the text for the setup 7. - Victor's Drive2 blog, entry 12, describes restoring the tyre-pressure sensors (TPMS) so they work on his X80; it is a first-hand reference in Russian 8.

TPMS services on Avito. Che Guevara posted two Avito listings as examples of local offers: a TPMS sensor cloning service in Aleksin (клонирование датчиков давления) and a Tula seller of universal TPMS sensors for any car 910. See TPMS sensor cloning.

Dismantler. RazborNF, a dismantler with an Avito page, lists original FAW X80 parts; search "faw x80" on its page to see the stock 11. Victor clarifies that these listings (including drive shafts) come from automatic transmission (AKPP / АКПП) cars, so check the gearbox type before buying 12.

Parts shops named in the chat. Members named kitzapchasti.ru (catalogue with photo-based listings), chinaspare.ru (Chinese car parts, Trialli belts) and frontcam.ru (a catalogue for the Besturn X80 2018-2020); one message adds that the Vostochny Express shop had a fender at a discount and that Kitparts shows prices. Details in parts suppliers directory 131415.

Shop and importer sites on shared files. The shared order exports come from hapbryansk.ru and the ELM327 manual is published by ORION (orionspb.ru); see Shared files and manuals 161718.

docs.title: Workshop quality: chains vs. private mechanics
docs.text:
Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

A community thread comparing named repair shops in the Moscow area, sparked by a member about to visit FIT before a suspension job. General takeaway: large chain service centers tend to oversell work, while independent/private mechanics are cheaper and often better, but hard to find.

  • Remtech (ЮВАО district, Moscow) — not recommended 1.
  • FIT — the most-discussed and most-criticized chain in this thread. Repeated complaints of overselling and inflated quotes: one member was quoted about 100,000 RUB (RU market, August 2026) to rebuild the entire rear suspension for a problem that a different (unnamed) shop fixed properly for roughly 5,000 RUB (RU market, August 2026) 2345. Another member was told the whole suspension needed replacing at a cost of 100,000+ RUB (RU market, August 2026), and when they asked what happens if that doesn't fix the issue, the mechanic's answer was only "we'll see" 678. FIT reportedly won't let customers supply their own parts unless ordered through the shop — and stock is often unavailable 9. A separate member (Victor) reports FIT billed a friend for repairs the friend had already had done elsewhere two months earlier, after a diagnostic visit 10. FIT also failed to set wheel alignment correctly for one member, unlike a shop in their home city 11. One member noted this behavior isn't unique to FIT — "basically every shop does this, just to charge more" 12 — though another pointed out shops may vary by city/region 13. Even going through personal connections at a shop, one member was still quoted a large round sum 14.
  • Автопилот (Autopilot) — reported as usable but expensive; notably it does allow customers to bring their own parts, unlike FIT 115.
  • Private/independent mechanics ("частники"). Consistently described as 3-5x cheaper than chain shops, often with better quality, but rare and hard to find — mainly locatable through friends/word of mouth rather than ads, and the good ones have waiting lists of 1-2 weeks 1617. One member's concrete comparison: a full upper front control-arm replacement cost 5,000 RUB (RU market, August 2026) at a large chain shop vs. an estimated 1,500 RUB (RU market, August 2026) from their usual private mechanic — they used the chain shop only because they needed the work done urgently and didn't want to wait out the private shop's queue 18. Another member who moved to the FAW never managed to find a trustworthy private option after their previous go-to shop closed 192021. A member from Saransk separately vouches for a good mechanic there, without naming the shop 22.
  • Bottom line from the thread: no single honest/cheap chain shop was ever actually named in response to a direct request for one 23 — the community's practical answer is "find a private mechanic through someone you know," not "go to a specific chain."

docs.title: Coil springs — aftermarket numbers and sag
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #part-number · #mazda-6-compat · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Broken springs. One owner heard a rattle over bumps and found a broken coil spring (пружина лопнула) on one side that needed replacing; a member notes that a partly cracked spring can click while looking intact, so a visual check may miss it.12

SUFIX SZ1303. A member replaced a suspension spring with SUFIX SZ1303 (yellow) and says it fitted correctly; others recommended it as reinforced by 20%.3 It is a front spring that a member confirms fits the restyled car, and an owner has run it since summer 2025 without the car sagging.45 A KYB RA3347 front spring (L=R, Mazda 6 II, 2007 onward) was photographed at 5,370 RUB (RU market, August 2025), and a member preferred it to SUFIX.67 OBK C4T21642H is a reinforced Japanese-made spring listed as the Toyota Mark 2000-2004 part and commonly fitted to the Subaru Tribeca; the member who found it thinks the stiffness is more than the lighter X80 needs, though it could suit a heavier load.89

Soft springs and sag. An owner at 262,000 km found that weak springs bottom out on the internal bump stop (buffer), which spoils comfort on small bumps and fails under full load; he says no shims help, so the choice is air bags (пневмобаллоны) or stiffer springs. He reports that Mazda 6 wagon (GG) springs with the same wire thickness fit and work, and that a simple solution of air bags with 200 x 85 side-nipple fittings costs about 4,500 RUB (RU market, June 2025); another owner uses only Atenza springs for the same purpose.10111213 Another owner fitted two aftermarket springs and both lost height within a month; he went back to stock springs with air bags and says Stepwagon springs with a trimmed Zhiguli rubber spacer work, but the air bags carry most of the load.14

See also: Front coil springs — failure and sourcing, Rear springs — failure and pneumatic fixes, Front suspension lift spacers.

docs.title: Control arm (bearing/full arm) replacement
docs.text:
Tags: #price · #control-arm

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

A service shop quoted 16,000 RUB (RU market, October 2025) for lower control-arm bearing replacement labor. The owner reporting this noted that service shops tend to price X80 work relatively high because of general unfamiliarity with the model — worth getting a second quote before accepting a similar price elsewhere.1

Full front upper control arm replacement — wider price range (2026-08 report). One owner reported paying 5,000 RUB (RU market, August 2026) for labor to replace the full front upper control arm (рычаг) at a large service center, noting he could have had the same job done by "his own" (a trusted private mechanic) for ~1,500 RUB, but chose the large shop to avoid a week-long wait for an appointment.2 A second owner reacted that 5,000 RUB was excessive for a part held on by just two bolts and one nut plus a wheel removal, saying he does all his own repairs to avoid being overcharged.3 This is a separate, lower price point than the 16,000 RUB bearing-only quote above — presented alongside it rather than reconciled, since the two shops may not have quoted the same scope of work. The same discussion also mentioned that some large service centers have quoted 100,000+ RUB (RU market, August 2026) for a full suspension rebuild when only the arm replacement (~5,000 RUB) was actually needed — reinforcing the general advice to get a second, independent quote before authorizing suspension work (see also service-center-selection-and-transparency).23

docs.title: Engine hydro mount diagnosis
docs.text:
Tags: #engine-mount · #mazda-6-compat · #diagnostic

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Diagnosing a failed hydro-mount: two checks were suggested for the front engine hydro-mount: (1) reach a hand underneath and feel for a bulge/swelling ("udder-like" protrusion) on the rubber element — if present, the mount is dead; (2) check the position of the upper shaft relative to the mount — a gap of roughly 1cm at rest is the normal condition. One owner at 90,000 km with light residual vibration after a mount replacement suspected the other (left) mount might also be starting to fail 123.

Cross-brand alternative — SWAG (VW Golf) welded in: a SWAG-brand hydro-mount sourced from a VW Golf was welded into the mount housing as a replacement, following the same general design as a similar Mazda-based swap. Some residual vibration reportedly remained even after this fix. One contributor noted that Chery-platform vehicles don't seem to exhibit the same vibration issue, possibly due to differences in transmission type 456.

Engine knock/roar under load at low speed — possibly mount-related: a separate but related symptom — a "roaring" or knocking noise when driving in a high gear at low speed (i.e. under load, low RPM) — occurs only within a specific RPM range and cannot be reproduced with the engine off or idling. It was not reliably associated with an exhaust smell underhood (one owner's exhaust-leak theory was disputed). Community hypothesis: the noise may be related to engine-mount movement under asymmetric load — either worn mounts generally, or the engine tilting/ shifting position due to a failed hydro-mount transferring load differently through the transmission — though this was not conclusively confirmed in the thread 78910.

GUD-brand (German, VW-spec) mount replacement — mixed results on noise: a GUD-brand engine mount (described in the group as a German brand made for Volkswagen applications) was installed specifically to fix an uneven/tilted engine idle; after replacement, the engine sits level again, which several owners view as a straightforward win. Its effect on the roaring/knock noise above is disputed: one owner (who replaced the right mount with GUD) reported the roaring noise persisted essentially unchanged, suggesting the mount was not the root cause in his case; a different owner reported the roaring became somewhat quieter after his own mount work. Possible confound raised by the community: engine/exhaust acoustic characteristics inherent to the design, rather than mount condition, may explain some of the noise variance between cars 1112131415.

Right engine mount — OEM Mazda recommended, ~8,000 RUB (RU market, October 2025), quality varies even for genuine parts (Oct 2025): for a right engine mount replacement (a common source of knock/rattle), the community recommendation is genuine OEM Mazda, at roughly 8,000 RUB — but even buying genuine, quality can vary noticeably between individual units, so this is not a guaranteed fix-and-forget purchase. Non-OEM options exist at lower price points but were not further detailed in this report 1617.

Rear engine mount — check for cracks as a cold-weather clunk source: cross-referencing the extensive cold-weather suspension-clunking diagnostic thread on the suspension noise checklist, the rear engine mount (задняя опора ДВС) is specifically called out as worth inspecting for cracks or deterioration when diagnosing clunking that appears or worsens in cold weather — see that card for the full, disputed multi-cause diagnostic discussion 18.

Hydro mounts as a known platform weakness ("Mazda drivers"): hydro mounts are described by the community as a recurring weak point on this platform, affecting cars colloquially referred to as "Mazda drivers" (i.e. this X80/Mazda-derived drivetrain layout). Replacement mounts fail fast: genuine Mazda mounts cost 12,000–14,000₽ each (RU market) but lose their internal clearance (зазор) after only a few months of use, requiring repeat replacement. Community workarounds attempted: hybrid mounts combining the X80's mounting block with a VW Golf or Lada Vesta mount assembly — but these are also reported as temporary fixes, not a permanent solution. Replacing all mounts at once does not by itself stop the recurring failure pattern 192021222324.

Combined fix: front springs + 20mm rear spacers + Tzerli engine mount: one owner's combined suspension/mount upgrade — new front springs (Suffix brand), 20mm rear spacer plates (see rear springs and front lift spacers), and a Tzerli-brand engine mount — produced a noticeable reduction in cabin vibration, eliminated a window rattle, and reduced cold-weather exhaust drone. A minor residual vibration remained afterward, attributed to the rear motor mount specifically (not yet replaced in this combo) 2526.

Engine mount bearing — Джукм brand, ~2,500₽, typical lifespan 100,000 km: the engine mount support bearing (опора двигателя) from the Джукм brand costs roughly 2,500₽ (RU market) and typically lasts to about 100,000 km, though some cars keep the original to 200,000 km. Replacement or re-pressing becomes necessary once the rubber deteriorates; the part is available through repair shops 2728.

Engine mount silentblock replacement — requires destroying the old unit and a press tool: replacing the rubber silentblock insert inside an engine mount is not a simple pull-out job — the old unit must be destroyed by cutting the rubber and drilling out the retaining pin; simple press-out or pull methods do not work. A dedicated press tool is needed for the new insert; some shops substitute a drill/rotary tool. One mechanic (Сергей Елисеев) notes that because of the silentblock's thickness and the curved mounting surfaces, the replacement procedure also slightly shifts the engine's resting position 293031.

Rattle at 1800–2200 RPM after spring/spacer install — check mounts and exhaust: a rattle (дребезжание) appearing at 1800–2200 RPM on a manual-transmission car, present in all gears, that developed after installing front springs with 30mm spacers, was linked by the community to possible engine-mount stress or exhaust resonance rather than the springs themselves. Diagnostic clue: the noise occurs at constant throttle/RPM but disappears under acceleration (i.e. it tracks engine load, not road input) — check engine mounts first, then exhaust fastening and clearance points; spacers are suspected of increasing stress transmitted to the mounts. See also the cat converter dust-shield rattle for a related exhaust-side rattle source 32333435.

Another VW-fabrication success, plus Mazda hydro-mount pricing: another instance of the VW-donor fabrication approach already documented on this card: a owner successfully retrofitted a Mazda-type hydraulic mount by custom-fabricating from a VW-spec mount, taking dimensions off the OEM mount and modifying the VW part accordingly — cost for the VW donor mount was roughly ~880₽ (2024 pricing). As a simpler, no-fabrication alternative, genuine Mazda hydraulic mounts are also available, priced at 9,000–11,000₽ — versus the retrofit's much lower parts cost but added labor/fabrication effort 363738394041.

Left engine mount, automatic transmission only — part 5CA139070A, notoriously expensive: for automatic-transmission X80s specifically, the left engine mount part number is 5CA139070A. Owners describe it as strikingly expensive — one joked it costs "like an airplane wing" — making it a candidate for the cross-brand/fabrication alternatives documented elsewhere on this card before paying full OEM price 424344.

Owner customization — swapping a too-soft support cartridge for a stiffer polyurethane silent block: one owner (Victor) bought a soft engine-support cartridge (патрон) intended for the GG platform for 1,300₽ (RU market), but found it noticeably softer than the original worn mount he was replacing — "worse than the old stock one." He then bought a separate polyurethane silent block for 600₽, intending to press it into the mount housing himself to get a stiffer result, saying he personally prefers a firmer engine mount feel. This is a personal-preference data point rather than a recommended fix: it shows that not all aftermarket "GG-spec" mount cartridges match OEM stiffness, and that some owners deliberately trade ride comfort for a firmer, more performance-oriented mount using a cheaper polyurethane insert 45.

docs.title: Front dampers — gas-filled type and brands
docs.text:
Tags: #shock-absorbers · #part-number

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Factory type — gas-filled (gas-oil). The FAW Besturn X80 factory installs gas-filled (gas-oil / gas-charged) dampers on the front axle. This is confirmed by an OZON product-listing description for the front-left gas damper, a part specific to the X8012345.

Aftermarket brand experience — Stelekс negatively reviewed, Mazda dampers used unofficially. Stelekс-brand dampers are negatively reviewed by the community, described as inferior quality and characterized as being made "for resellers" rather than for genuine durability. Separately, Mazda dampers (not an official cross-listed part) are reportedly used by some owners despite not fitting exactly — an unofficial substitution rather than a confirmed drop-in replacement12345.

docs.title: Front springs — aftermarket brands and prices
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #price · #part-number · #fitment

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

LINX SC1590 fitment (2025): LINX SC1590 front springs are compatible and fit stock X80 suspension mounts without modification. Recommendation: always buy new damper dust-boot seals (piston rod boots) when replacing springs, as they frequently tear during removal/installation. Context/date: 2025-05-02 1.

SUFIX SZ1303 — confirmed direct fit, no modification: SUFIX-brand yellow front coil springs, part SZ1303 (also written SZ-1303, "20% stiffer" per the seller's listing), are confirmed to fit the X80 without cutting or welding. Reported pricing: ~3,600 RUB (RU market, July 2025) per pair as of 2025-07-28, sourced from the chitparts/kitparts online retailer. Perceived effect: raises the front stance and improves overall appearance. Conflict: this contradicts part of the coil-count note above where Mazda 6 springs were mentioned as an option with fit issues — SUFIX SZ1303 is the option the community confirms works without caveats 23.

SUFIX SZ1303 — additional install confirmations (Oct–Nov 2025): further owners confirm the SUFIX SZ1303 yellow front spring noticeably raises the front and holds its height 4567, adding to the SUFIX SZ1303 fitment already documented above; one later report specifically reconfirms fitment on the restyle (facelift) body 8.

Front spring cross-fit — further Mazda GG/GH dispute and compression data (Dec 2025): a fresh round of the GG-vs-GH cross-fit disagreement: one owner assumed the front springs sold as SUFIX SZ1303 are the Mazda GH part number 9; Sergey Arapkin disputes any blanket rule, noting that neither GG nor GH springs universally seat correctly on the X80 strut — fitment varies by the specific spring, not simply by generation 10. A seller/owner adds that Mazda 6 has roughly six different spring variants across its production run (consistent with the earlier model-year note on this card) and confirms, after considerable difficulty ("on the metro in a bag"), that the specific SUFIX SZ1303 spring does fit the restyle 11. Another owner reports riding on SUFIX springs since summer 2025 with no sagging 12, and a third notes they kept their old struts when fitting these springs, in hindsight considering the new struts they'd bought unnecessary 13. A press-compression test comparing stock and SUFIX springs found: stock front spring compresses at ~500kg load, SUFIX (yellow) at ~700kg — but on a vibration-table test the SUFIX springs actually rode slightly softer despite the higher static compression rating 14; one buyer reports being told at purchase that these springs were "reinforced" 15.

Front spring and bushing sourcing — Moscow, KitParts/Ozon (Dec 2025): for sourcing front springs together with related bushings (upper control-arm silentblocks, rear longitudinal-arm silentblocks) in Moscow: SUFIX SZ1303 (yellow) front springs are suggested as fitting the restyle 16, and the community's pinned product links (Ozon) are recommended as a starting point for both springs and silentblocks 1718.

Other replacement front spring options compared (March 2026): besides Sufix SZ1303 (~5,300–5,500 RUB/pair on Wildberries, RU market, most proven in the community with consistent positive reports), other 14mm wire-rate alternatives include OBK C5Z7971 (~7,500 RUB) and ST119063F (~8,000 RUB); Turkish-made 14mm springs are also available via Chip-Dip for ~5,500 RUB/pair. Higher-rate springs than stock may require rebalancing with matched shock absorbers to avoid an overly stiff ride 19202122.

LYNX SC 1590 — alternative sourcing channel (May 2025): when official front springs were unavailable, one owner successfully sourced a replacement through the LYNX SC 1590 brand — a Chinese supplier who provided the complete original-spec spring assembly (spring plus spring cups) for 4,800 RUB (RU market, May 2025). The export restrictions cited as the reason for unavailability were described as temporary at the time 2324.

Standard Springs ST119063F — 14mm aftermarket, requires press to install: Standard Springs ST119063F (cross-referenced to FAW part 5CA134011) are 14mm-thick springs (vs 13mm stock) with roughly 25% more coils than the factory spring. Price: 9,533₽ (April 2026). Installing them without a proper spring compressor is very difficult — cable ties alone are not enough; a pneumatic press at 2.5 atm is recommended, and a rubber support piece must be placed under the spring cup during installation 25262728.

Sukhoi 1303 springs — thicker aftermarket, direct fit, ~3hr install per side: Sukhoi 1303 springs are a cross-brand front replacement option. They look visibly thicker than the OEM spring (roughly 13–13.5mm rod diameter), fit directly without modification, and can be installed one side at a time in about 3 hours per side. After installation, the suspension became higher and softer, handling improved on rough surfaces, and there was no noise at speed over bumps; measurement showed roughly 13mm rod diameter on both OEM and the Sukhoi spring 2930313233343536.

Turkish 14mm-rod spring — stiffer, more body-roll control, more lift: a separate Turkish-made spring option with a 14mm rod diameter is noticeably stiffer than OEM, significantly reduces body roll in corners, and raises ride height more than the other aftermarket alternatives on this card 3738.

SUFIX SZ1303 front springs — yellow, direct fit, ~1 year positive feedback: SUFIX-brand front springs (yellow-painted, part SZ1303) fit FAW Besturn X80 stock struts without modification. Multiple owners confirm successful fitment and roughly a year of trouble-free operation. They're slightly stiffer than OEM. Installation note: at the shop, these springs compress harder during fitting (need more force/load) than OEM, and afterward the front sits noticeably higher — some owners added rear spacers (+20mm) to level the resulting front/rear height imbalance (see the rear springs card for that spacer fix). Overall considered suitable for daily driving and moderate loads 394041424344.

Front spring replacement pricing — dealer quote vs. LYNXauto alternative (June 2024): when a front spring breaks, KitZapchasti quoted 24,000₽ (June 2024) for a complete replacement kit/pair. LYNXauto SC-1590 springs (already documented above as a confirmed direct-fit option) are available on Ozon as a substantially cheaper alternative to that dealer-kit price 454647.

Front spring cross-brand sourcing example — Mazda 6 (GH), JAPKO ZCJ3346A: as one purchase example (order history screenshot) for a front-spring cross-brand alternative, a JAPKO ZCJ3346A front spring for Mazda 6 (GH), 2007–2013 was ordered by an owner researching replacement options 48.

SUFIX Mazda 6 front kit. A SUFIX front spring kit (2 pieces) for the Mazda 6 Atenza Saloon (GG) 2002-2008 2.3 was shown in a marketplace screenshot at about 5,593 RUB (RU market, Oct 2026), marked out of stock 49. Миша, who fitted these springs, says they are more than enough and have stood for two years 50; Тимур also fitted them and calls them good springs 51. Миша's one complaint is not the springs: his non-original struts are Mazda-analog Zekkert units, thinner than the FAW originals, and although new they cannot take full compression, so speed bumps must be crossed slowly or the rebound hits hard 52. Николай Цветков fitted rubber bump stops (буфера) and says they are coping with the problem so far 53.

Related cards: Front springs overview; Coil springs — aftermarket numbers and sag (all springs)

docs.title: Front springs — breakage reports and causes
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #diagnostics · #low-confidence

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Material-quality concern — breakage in warm weather: multiple owners report OEM springs breaking during warm weather or even at idle (e.g. while changing spark plugs, with the car on ramps). The breakage is attributed to poor material quality and fatigue stress rather than insufficient thickness — some springs cracked despite being of the "thick" design, suggesting inconsistent quality control in OEM production batches. Aftermarket springs (genuine Mazda or LYNXauto alternatives) are reportedly more reliable, though they change suspension stiffness somewhat 1.

Failure pattern — lower-coil fracture: front springs commonly fail with a fracture in the lowest half-turn or full turn of the coil. The typical symptom is a periodic clunking sound over bumps while turning, which is sometimes mistaken for a failed stabilizer rod. Visual inspection may not reveal the crack until examined closely 2.

Spring failure with no impact — confirmed possible (April 2026): a community member asked whether a spring can simply snap while the car is parked, with no pothole or rough road involved. Confirmed: one owner had exactly this happen in autumn — got in the car, sat down, and heard a loud snapping sound; inspection found the front spring had broken. Supports the "material fatigue" explanation elsewhere on this card over an impact-based cause 34.

Front spring failure at 61,000 km: a stock front spring broke at 61,000 km. The owner drove for about a year accepting reduced comfort before deciding to upgrade to aftermarket springs 5.

Front spring broke at 62,000 km — upper control arm bushings fell out during the same job: a front spring broke (one side) at 62,000 km. During replacement, the upper control arm's sway-bar ball joints simply fell out of their bushings on removal, requiring re-pressing; the ball joints themselves were still serviceable (rated to last to ~100,000 km) but the upper control arm showed rust. KYB dampers were purchased for the same job but not yet installed at time of report. Recommendation: replace dampers and ball joints together around 100,000 km, since re-pressed ball-joint boots may only last another 30,000–40,000 km — see the upper control arm card for the ball-joint/bushing side of this job 6789101112.

Front spring failures — a recurring, established problem: front springs are a known, recurring failure point on the X80. One owner's spring failed at 61,000 km after 6 years of ownership; multiple other community members report the same failure pattern, with some moving to aftermarket springs as a result 131415.

Front coil failure at 200,400 km (both sides) — Suffix 1303 replacement; second failure timeline: one owner (А5) reported front coil-spring failure at 200,400 km: the left spring broke in two places, the right in one place; the suspension had felt very firm beforehand. Replacement: Suffix 1303 springs, which fit as a direct OEM-shape replacement. A second owner (Victor) reports his own springs lasted 61,000 km before failure — the left spring detached while the car was parked waiting at a school, and he continued driving about 800 km on only one working spring before replacing both. After replacement and roughly 7 precharge/settle cycles, the suspension became noticeably livelier 1617181920.

Front spring failures — 50,000–120,000 km range, ~5,000₽/pair (April 2024): another cluster of front coil-spring failure reports, mostly on the left spring, at mileages ranging from 50,000 to 120,000 km. Symptoms: sagging stance and visible cracks. Replacement springs sourced from Ozon for roughly 5,000₽ per pair (April 2024). Some owners note rear springs from other Mazda-platform models also fit as cross-brand replacements when needed 212223242526.

Front spring fracture — hidden break inside the rubber isolator section: a front spring broke while driving, with the fracture located in the lower section where the rubber isolator seats/compresses the spring — this location makes the crack not visible on casual inspection; it required close inspection (feeling by hand) to find, since it was hidden inside the rubber isolator area rather than on an exposed coil. Reported symptom before the crack was found: a steering-area noise/clunk during acceleration, initially suspected as brake pads or an engine mount before the spring break was located 272829.

Front spring break after 6 months parked, unrelated to driving stress: a front spring failed/broke after the car sat parked for six months in an underground garage, with no unusual driving stress reported beforehand — the owner only noticed the car sitting crooked when it was next taken in for service. This is a low-confidence, single report but suggests the possibility of fatigue/corrosion-driven failure even without active driving, not just a load- or road-shock-driven failure mode. Replacement spring ordered to spec SZ1303 3031.

Related cards: Front springs overview; Coil springs — aftermarket numbers and sag (all springs)

docs.title: Front coil springs — failure and sourcing
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #price · #mazda-6-compat · #conflict

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Front coil springs on the X80 are a known failure point, and the parts market is split between scarce genuine FAW springs, aftermarket analogs and Mazda 6 cross-fits. This card holds the core failure and price facts; the details are split into the sibling cards listed at the end.

Failure pattern: front springs can break as early as ~45,000 km, and multiple later reports confirm ongoing failures well past that (one owner's left and right springs both failed by 196,000 km combined mileage) 12. Where the spring breaks matters for safety: a break at the coil ends still allows some further driving, but a break in the middle section calls for immediate replacement 2. A separate report describes a right front spring failing with a loud metallic sound audible inside the cabin — the vehicle may show only slight settling, not obviously visible without close inspection, and a spring can fail even while the car is parked 3. Fatigue cracking at the mid-coil is the reported failure mode in another case 4. When replacing, both front springs are typically done together 2.

When replacing shocks, also replace the springs — this is standard practice reported by the community when doing front suspension work 1.

Front vs rear parts availability (disputed): sources indicate that if a rear shock leaks, only OEM parts are available with no cross-brand alternative, while front analogs from other brands are more commonly available — but the thread does not fully resolve whether this rule applies equally to both axles 1 (conflict, see below).

Pricing: OEM front springs cost 11,000–12,000 RUB per unit (RU market, mid/late 2024) 5; a later report cites ~5,000 RUB each (RU market, November 2024) from an official dealer for the fatigue-crack repair 4; a January 2025 dealer purchase of one front (right) spring cost 3,000 RUB (RU market, January 2025), with a free car wash included 6; Kitparts sold a full front spring set for ~3,000 RUB in January 2025 (RU market), noting slightly different pricing/coils between manual (MKPP) and automatic (AKPP) transmission variants without detailing the exact spec difference 7.

Aftermarket alternative: part number 5CA1340011, sold by KITZAP, at ~2,100 RUB (RU market, September 2024) — reported as lasting 30,000–50,000 km versus the OEM spring, which is harder to find used and generally outlasts the analog 5. As a workaround for repeated failures, some owners use spacers (prostavki) to reduce spring compression and extend service life, at the cost of some ride comfort and possible suspension-geometry effects 4.

Disagreement — do Mazda 6 springs cross-fit? Some owners report that Mazda 6 springs (per the Exist parts catalog) may fit. Sergey Arapkin explicitly disputes this, stating the X80's springs are thicker and use different fork/mounting connectors than Mazda 6's, so they do not fit. The community's practical recommendation is to source from an official FAW dealer or specialized retailers (KitParts, Exist), and to buy a complete strut assembly rather than a bare spring where possible 89.

docs.title: Front springs — Mazda 6 GG/GH compatibility
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #mazda-6-compat · #conflict · #fitment

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Mazda GG/GH springs — 1.5cm shorter, spacers needed: Mazda 6 GG/GH front springs are approximately 1.5cm shorter than the X80-spec spring; if used, spacers should be installed to maintain correct suspension geometry. One owner's order from the "esprings" company (Barnaul, Russia) had long lead times and pricing errors. A Mazda 6 wagon ("6wagon") spring was separately suggested as a compatible alternative 12.

Front spring coil count and further Mazda-fit caveats: OEM front springs have 8–9 coils depending on model year. Mazda 6 first/second generation springs (12.5–12.75mm wire, consistent with the wire-thickness mismatch noted above) are sometimes used but may not seat/fit properly. Springs bought from KitZap were reported as an inconsistent fit — one owner had to return a set of Mazda-sourced springs that did not seat fully — while springs from Ozon fit better than the KitZap set on the same vehicle 3.

Front spring — Mazda 6 (2005-2007) cross-fit, model-year dependent: front springs from Mazda 6 model years 2005-2007 can be fitted to the X80. Mazda 6 has roughly 6 different spring variants across its production run, and fitment should be verified before purchase — some sources say 2008- onward Mazda springs may not fit, while others say model year matters less; the safest choice reported is a 2005-2007 Mazda 6 spring. If a Mazda spring sits too low once installed, some owners cut one coil off to compensate 4.

Front spring GG-vs-GH fitment dispute (Sept 2025): one owner asked whether GG-generation front springs fit after a right spring broke; a reply confirmed a spring fit "exactly" 56, but on follow-up the same contributor clarified the X80 runs its own OEM springs and that it is GH-generation Mazda springs which cross-fit — not GG 78. When replacing, change both springs as a pair 9.

Front suspension upgrade — Mazda springs plus forks (Oct 2025): one owner replaced front springs together with Mazda forks (and other parts) in the same session; Mazda-sourced springs are considered softer than stock 1011, and are reported to ride better than the factory units, though full fork/strut replacement at a garage (not driveway) is recommended for this swap 12.

Conflict — Mazda 6 GG front springs do NOT fit pre-restyle X80 (Jan 2026): Mazda 6 GG front springs are sometimes cited as a compatible cross-fit, but a detailed community test found they do not fit the pre-restyle (2017) X80: the GG springs have fewer coils than the X80 originals, which results in improper ride height 131415161718192021222324. For reliable fitment, use OEM FAW X80 springs or verify fitment carefully before buying an aftermarket alternative; OEM parts availability from online retailers (КитЗап, КитПартс, OZON) was reported as 4–7 days 1315. This directly conflicts with the separately confirmed Mazda 6 GH compatibility reported immediately below — the two Mazda 6 generations (GG vs. GH) behave differently and must not be confused.

Mazda 6 GH front springs — confirmed direct fit (Jan 2026): unlike the GG generation above, front springs from the Mazda 6 GH install as a direct, original-fitment replacement. The X80's own front springs have 10 coils; the Mazda GH version has 8 coils and a slightly different lower mounting position, but both seat and function correctly on installation. Zekkert SF2667 is verified by the community as a good-quality GH-spec option 25262728.

Mazda 6 GH springs preferred over GG for front fitment (rod diameter, weight): Mazda 6 GH springs are the preferred cross-fit for the X80 front and mount properly, with the correct rod diameter (13.5mm typical, vs the X80's 14mm stock). Mazda 6 GG springs can be made to work only if the bottom coil is cut to match the rod diameter — this reduces comfort or load capacity depending on exactly where the cut is made. GH springs are significantly heavier-duty (~250kg more load-rated) and a better match for the X80's weight; direct GH installation (no cutting) is the recommended route. Disagreement: some owners report successfully running cut GG springs, while others insist on GH-only for load-capacity reasons 293031323334353637.

Community consensus: don't use Mazda 6 (GG) springs on the X80 — they're too weak: contrary to an initial suggestion to use Mazda 6 springs, more experienced members pushed back — Mazda 6 GG springs (see the GG-vs-GH entry above) are considered too weak for the X80's curb weight and should be avoided in favor of proper FAW-spec springs. The catch: genuine FAW springs are rarely available at a reasonable price (most "FAW" springs on the market are counterfeit), so the practical alternatives are verified sellers or 8-turn FAW springs when available (very limited supply) 38394041.

Mazda strut/spring diameter mismatch (~5mm) — no universal cross-brand solution, complete-assembly debate: an earlier (2024) discussion of the same GG/GH strut-diameter incompatibility documented elsewhere on this platform: Mazda GG-sedan and Mazda GH components reportedly have struts roughly 5mm different in diameter from the X80's own struts, so springs alone sourced from Mazda will not seat properly on factory X80 struts — a complete strut+spring assembly from the same Mazda generation may be needed instead. Conflict: whether a complete assembly swap is actually required, or whether carefully diameter-matched springs alone are sufficient, was debated without full resolution in this thread — the diameter mismatch itself was not disputed, only what to do about it 424344454647.

Oct 2026 update — fitment of Mazda 6 and aftermarket front springs. Marina L bought front springs under FAW part number 5CA134011 from Armtek and had them fitted without trimming anything 48. IBRAIM only relayed (hearsay, "so they write") that Mazda 6 springs seem to fit but may need trimming 49; owners should check the fit on their own car before cutting. Mazda 6 shock absorbers are a different matter: they do not fit the X80 front fork (вилка) because the Mazda unit is thinner at the bottom 50. Тимур advised not to over-think it and buy the original FAW shock absorber, saying the price is fine and the quality good 51.

Ozon "FAW Besturn X80" springs need trimming. Serega fitted front springs sold on Ozon as "FAW Besturn X80" and still had to file off about half a coil so they would seat on the stock strut 52. Victor pointed out that the listing claims a 400 mm free height while the stock spring is about 380 mm 53, and that reviews describe them as Mazda GG springs whose bottom coil does not go over the shock absorber, which is why people cut them 54. Serega paid roughly 5,500 RUB (RU market, Sep 2026) 55. Victor said the Suffix (Sufix) springs derived from the Mazda GH chassis fit with no modification and cost about 5,500 RUB per set (RU market, Sep 2026) 56; he states there is no official Suffix equivalent for the X80 — owners simply fit them by trial 57.

Related cards: Front springs overview; Coil springs — aftermarket numbers and sag (all springs)

docs.title: Front springs — OEM specs and part numbers
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #part-number · #counterfeit

OEM vs. Mazda wire-thickness mismatch: OEM front springs use 14mm wire thickness; Mazda alternative springs measure 12.5–12.75mm — a meaningful difference that can affect suspension geometry and ride characteristics. Some owners report the Mazda springs ride softer as a result. Consider the wire-thickness gap carefully before substituting 1.

Original front spring dimensions (spec, March 2026): OEM FAW X80 front spring measurements — outer diameters D1=86mm, D2=112mm, D3=64mm, D4=92mm; free height H=384mm; wire pitch p=14mm; 10 coils. Many owners replace the OEM spring with the Sufix SZ1303 aftermarket spring (spring rate 13.5, height ~379mm), which sits slightly shorter but still raises the front end by roughly 20mm compared to stock once installed, because of its stiffer rate — this typically requires progressive spacers to bring the ride height back to normal for correct suspension geometry 23456.

FAW front spring part numbers by engine/transmission: original FAW catalog part numbers differ by drivetrain: 5CA034011 for manual transmission, 5CA134011 for automatic and naturally-aspirated 2.0L, 5CA234011 for turbocharged versions — the differences account for engine-weight distribution. A separate community grouping: 1.8L MT and 2.0L MT reportedly share the same spring; 2.0L AT and 2.0L Diesel differ; 2.3L and 2.5L each have their own distinct spring 78.

Stock spring coil count — 9 turns; genuine FAW springs are rare/counterfeited: stock FAW X80 front springs have 9 coil turns. Some owners tried 8-turn springs (for a lower stance) but found them unavailable after their initial purchase, so 9-turn remains the practical standard due to consistent availability. Caution: genuine FAW springs with the factory white-blue-green label are extremely rare; most springs sold as "FAW" are Chinese counterfeits with reproduced markings 910111213.

Front spring/X40 incompatibility — do not cross-shop: the X80 and the smaller FAW X40 use different front suspension designs and are not spring-interchangeable — do not fit X40 front springs to an X80 expecting a match, even though aftermarket brands (e.g. Fobos) list springs for both models separately. (Wheel hubs/bolt pattern are also incompatible between X80 and X40 — see the wheel bolt pattern card.) 1415.

Front spring dimensions for custom manufacturing (Sept 2026): for owners considering a custom-made replacement spring rather than sourcing a cross-brand part, community-measured front spring dimensions are: rod (wire) diameter 13mm (measured on an MT-transmission car), lower coil diameter approximately 62/91mm, upper coil diameter approximately 87/116mm, and roughly 9.4 total coils; exact free height was not recorded. These dimensions can be handed to a custom spring manufacturer to produce a replacement matching the original specification 16.

Automatic vs manual. Victor states the automatic (AKPP / АКПП) X80 is about 35 kg heavier than the manual, so the front springs differ between the two versions 17.

Related cards: Front springs overview; Coil springs — aftermarket numbers and sag (all springs)

docs.title: Front springs — replacement and refitting
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #installation

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Replacement procedure and time: front spring replacement is straightforward — about 40 minutes per spring, requiring full strut removal. The critical step is reinstalling per the alignment marks. The main difficulty reported is procuring quality spring clamps/compressors (described as "problematic to find") — the left spring may need 4 clamps and a second technician's help, while the right side typically needs only 2 clamps. DIY is possible with the proper tools and experience, but professionals recommend a service visit given the safety risk of stored spring force 1.

Torn damper protective boot causes spring damage (June 2025): a torn shock-absorber protective boot (пыльник амортизатора) lets water into the strut and can bend/damage the spring underneath it. Repair procedure reported step by step: fully unscrew the strut rod nut; jack the vehicle so the wheel is just barely off the ground; jack it a little further to keep the spring under tension; slowly extend the rod; quickly slide the torn boot off the rod; work the boot out from between the spring coils; fit the new boot; release the rod; lower the vehicle; reinstall the nut. One owner at 91,000 km found a second-coil fracture caused by this failure mode and bought two replacement springs from KitZap at 2,800 RUB (RU market, June 2025) each (as of 2025-06-03) 234567.

Single broken front spring — pair-replacement recommendation (May 2024): one owner reported the front-right spring snapped 1.5 coils from the top; the car was still driveable (no clunking, nothing felt over bumps) but the break was noticed while changing tires. Community recommendation: if buying new springs, replace the pair together to keep ride height balanced, though a used/refurbished single spring can be sourced and fitted alone if cost is the priority. Installation reported as straightforward, with the main difficulty being that the spring compressor bites tightly during installation — one owner who has done the swap several times still finds it tight going onto the strut. Photos shared show the fractured original next to a new LYNX SC1590 spring for comparison 891011121314.

Reinstalling a spring after accidentally releasing it (guide): if the horizontal bolt that secures the strut to the lower control arm is accidentally removed and the compressed spring pops free/relaxes, it can be reseated without a spring compressor: place a jack under the brake disc (hub) and push down to compress the suspension, then continue jacking to draw the lower control arm upward — the spring typically re-seats into position by hand once the arm is raised enough. An alternative variant of the same technique is to also jack up the opposite wheel, which makes realignment easier 15161718192021.

Related cards: Front springs overview; Coil springs — aftermarket numbers and sag (all springs)

docs.title: Front springs — ride height and settling
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #fitment
