Reservoir location. The power-steering fluid reservoir (бочок ГУРа) is located under the hood on the left side, behind the radiator.3839

docs.title: Power steering hose — replacement vs. re-crimping
docs.text:
Tags: #power-steering · #gur · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Two hose types. The power steering system has two hoses: the main high-pressure line ("трубка ГУР") and a separate return line ("обратка") — they are distinct parts, so when sourcing a replacement, confirm which one is actually failing before ordering.12345

Full replacement cost. An OEM/genuine power steering high-pressure hose costs roughly 13,000–16,000 RUB (RU market, February 2026) through Chinese-parts suppliers (Kitszap quoted at ~13,000 RUB specifically).12345

Cheaper alternative — re-crimping (перепрессовка) at a hydraulics shop. Rather than buying a full new hose, an existing hose can be re-crimped/re-pressed at a hydraulic-hose shop for roughly 500 RUB (RU market, February 2026) labor plus the cost of the replacement hose core. This approach was reported as successful on a Nissan Teana (a similar/related platform), and hydraulic shops that routinely handle tractor/combine hose re-pressurization are well-equipped to do this job on a car hose too — worth checking a local agricultural-equipment hydraulics shop, not just auto-parts specialists.12345

Mazda 6 (GG) pressure hose cross-references. The power-steering pressure tube (ГУРа трубка) for the Mazda 6 GG 2002-2007 is cross-referenced by brand: Dominant MZGJ06A32420E; ASParts AS1262; RUEI RU6A32420EM; Patron PSH012; Mazda GJ6A-32-420E or GJ6G-32-410D; ZZVF ZVGJ420E. A member asked whether the X80 hose resembles the Mazda one; the post does not confirm fitment.6

docs.title: Power steering pump and line issues
docs.text:
Tags: #power-steering · #oil-leak · #diagnostics

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Pulley bearing noise — progressive, cold-start-linked. A squealing/rustling noise from the engine bay, especially noticeable on cold starts and disappearing once the engine warms up, is commonly traced to a failing power-steering pump pulley bearing (ролик на насосе гидроусилителя). The condition worsens gradually: initially the noise disappears entirely once warm, but over time it stops disappearing and becomes constant, with visible bearing wobble/runout ("биение") eventually developing as the bearing degrades further. One owner's case started around 50,000 km. Lubrication is not a real fix — the pulley/bearing itself needs replacing12345678.

Separate issue — burnt-oil smell traced to the power-steering line. A persistent, strong burnt-oil smell from the exhaust-manifold area (present for about a month in one report, with no visible smoke) can be caused by a leak in the power-steering oil supply line (маслопровод рейки), specifically the rubber hose section that routes directly over the exhaust. A leaking hose drips oil onto the hot exhaust surface, producing the burnt smell without necessarily producing visible smoke. Check underneath for a wet/oily rubber hose routed above the exhaust as the first diagnostic step9101112.

Power steering fluid specification. X80 power-steering fluid must meet spec 3309 or Toyota Type IV; a multigrade specification can also be used as an alternative. This is the same specification as the automatic transmission fluid (AKPP)1314.

Fluid spec restated — Mazda ATF-MV or Dexron 3; caution on generic "MV" fluids. The correct fluid for the X80's power-steering system is Mazda ATF-MV (Mazda Automatic Transmission Fluid Multi-Vehicle). An accepted alternative: Dexron 3. Caution: generic multi-vehicle fluids marked simply "MV" alone may not meet the actual specification — use only fluids explicitly rated for Mazda ATF-MV or Dexron 3, not just any bottle labeled "MV"15161718.

Fluid compatibility restated — Mobil 3309, Toyota T4, or multi-spec ATF. Further community-confirmed compatible fluid options for the X80's power steering: Mobil 3309, Toyota T4 spec, or a multi-specification ATF. Community experience confirms these multi-ATF options work in practice, consistent with the 3309/Toyota Type IV/Mazda ATF-MV/Dexron 3 options already documented on this card192021222324.

Steering rack seal leak — OEM cost vs. Mazda 6 cross-fit vs. specialist repair. Separately from the pump/line issues above, the steering rack (рулевая рейка) itself can develop a seal leak from both sides. A new OEM rack costs approximately 25,000 RUB (RU market, February 2026) (price reported by an owner at 318,000 km). Mazda 6 I racks can be used as a cross-compatible substitute. Before committing to a full replacement, check the cost of a specialized steering-rack repair shop — repair may be more cost-effective than a new part2526272829303132.

Fluid spec — earlier, independent report ties it to the manual-transmission fluid too, adds Dixtron-III. An earlier, independent thread gives the same spec 3309 figure already documented on this card, framing it as: the X80's power steering uses the same fluid as the manual transmission — ATF spec 3309, or an equivalent Type-4/multigrade ATF meeting that spec. Dixtron-III is also named as acceptable. The same spec applying to the AKPP reservoir (already noted above) suggests potential fluid interchangeability across the power-steering, manual-transmission, and AKPP systems — though always verify against the specific fluid's full spec sheet before cross-using33343536.

Oct 2026 update — return hose leaking at the reservoir. Sergei Rogov found the power steering (ГУР) return hose (обратка) leaking at the reservoir (бачок) end 3738. His photo shows a wet, oily area with reddish stains around a pulley and the drive belt, though the hose itself is not clearly visible 39. He asked whether Mazda 6 hoses fit or only FAW originals; nobody answered that part.

Oct 2026 — DAGGER steering rack: air and hiss. Valerii replaced the rack together with tie-rod ends using a DAGGER rack; bleeding the air was a struggle and the steering did not become lighter, which he puts down to the car's suspension loading 40. He bled on a raised car and there was no noise at first 41, but after driving a hiss from the valve (золотник) of the fluid transfer appeared; the fluid showed no foam, so he suspects air is hiding somewhere and will wait to see whether it runs in 4241. Victor says his own car always hisses from the rack and power-steering pump, and another car he looked at did as well, so the hiss may be normal — only the engine is not audible while the hiss from under the wheel annoys 43. See also the hiss-versus-whistle guidance in the power-steering fluid card.

docs.title: Rear air suspension (pneumatic bags) installation
docs.text:
Community-shared reference. A Drive2 blog post documents installing pneumatic air suspension balloons (пневмобаллоны) inside the X80's rear coil springs — a DIY modification for load-leveling/adjustable ride height rather than a factory or dealer-supported option. Link: https://www.drive2.ru/l/544082609840325184/1

Scope of the guide. The referenced post covers fitment details (how the air bags fit inside the existing rear spring) and the installation procedure. This entry is a pointer to that external guide rather than a full step-by-step reproduction — consult the Drive2 post directly for the complete procedure, part sourcing, and any fitment caveats.1

Sizing notes from an owner. One owner with air bags (пневмобаллоны) says 285 bellows from Novosibirsk are stiff and do not roll well, while Belarusian bellows are softer. To fit a 200 bellow on a 185 spring, cut the flared end of the bump-stop tube (отбойник); smaller bump stops should also be trimmed.2 See Rear springs — failure and pneumatic fixes for more.

docs.title: Rear spring replacement — spacers and alignment
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #mazda-6-compat · #conflict

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Community members disagree on this topic — both positions are reported.

Parts note. Rear spring part numbers were found on kitzapchasti.ru at around 3,310 RUB (RU market, October 2024) each (left and right).1

Updated pricing and sourcing (2025-03 report). OEM rear springs run approximately 3,000–7,000 RUB (RU market, March 2025) per piece. Available on OZON under part number 5CA028011 (https://ozon.ru/t/5VDGPXX). A quality aftermarket option from kitparts.ru costs 7,000 RUB (RU market, March 2025) per piece, described as matching original thickness. For reference, an earlier winter-2024 price point was 3,000 RUB (RU market, winter 2024, as reported in March 2025) for OEM springs — prices have trended up since.23

Spacer recommendation. A 2 cm spacer installed with the springs is recommended by an owner with direct experience — without spacers the ride/geometry is reportedly "not great."456

Alignment is mandatory after the job. After rear suspension spring replacement, a wheel alignment (сход-развал) must be performed, done with the car in a proper loaded/settled state and with the wheel size that will actually be used.7689

Alignment shop debate — wheel-size claims. Some budget alignment shops incorrectly claim that only the OEM/factory wheels can be used for the alignment procedure. Community members with technical understanding push back: alignment angles (camber/toe) are geometric properties of the suspension and are independent of wheel type or thickness — this claim from some shops is considered a misunderstanding or an excuse for equipment limitations.10111213

Recommended shops: Autopilot chain (Moscow) reported reliable by one owner for X80 alignment;8 a specific independent shop near Lyublino metro station (Moscow) also reported reliable.14 Reviews on Autopilot specifically are mixed ("двоякие") among other community members, so results may vary by branch.15

Practical tip: when booking with any alignment shop unfamiliar with the X80, bring the correct alignment spec parameters (camber/toe/caster angles) with you — technicians will generally be able to hit the numbers if given them.1617

Video reference — rear spring replacement in under 10 minutes (2024-03 report). A YouTube video demonstrating rear spring replacement on the X80 in under 10 minutes was shared in the group: https://youtube.com/shorts/fvVYyvg6faY?feature=share3 — useful as a quick visual overview alongside the spacer/alignment guidance above.18

Mazda 6 GG/GH rear spring fitment — disputed, not a straightforward swap (2026-05 report, conflict documented). Community members tested/discussed using Mazda 6 GG (generations GG/GH/GY) rear springs as X80 replacements. The experienced-owner consensus: OEM X80 rear springs measure 13mm rod diameter, 350mm length. Mazda 6 GG springs have different geometry and are lighter-duty; the front springs specifically "from GG" are described as weaker than what the X80 uses (closer to the GH variant). Using GG springs with +40mm spacers may cause excessive ride height and poor handling. If a Mazda-based swap is attempted at all, community members lean toward parts from the GY (universal/wagon) Mazda 6 variant as the closer match — but this still needs verification via direct measurement or 3D scan of the actual spring parameters before assuming fitment. Conflict: two members (Jürgen and Denis) suggested Mazda 6 GH rear springs would work with spacers; a third member (Victor) disagreed strongly, citing sedan-vs-SUV suspension geometry differences and lower Mazda spring constants — Victor's position is that this is not recommended as a straightforward swap without engineering review.192021222324252627282930

Spacers instead of auto-bumpers. KASPER says auto-bumpers (автобаферы) stiffen the ride and overload the springs unevenly, and recommends simple spring spacers (проставки) under the rear springs and strut spacers at the front; his father's car was raised about 4 cm this way.3132

docs.title: Rear springs — failure symptoms and diagnosis
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #rear-suspension · #diagnostics

Sagging despite new shocks and springs: if the rear suspension still sags after replacing both shock absorbers and springs, inspect all the rubber bushings (сайлентблоки) too: the rear lower control arm's longitudinal bushing, the stabilizer bar bushings, and the ball joints. Sagging after a shocks/springs-only replacement can indicate (1) worn bushings letting the geometry shift, or (2) asymmetric wear requiring the whole alignment (развал-схождение) to be rechecked — which may itself need adjustment of several bushings and stabilizer components, not just the shocks/springs 12.

Early rear-spring failure and Mazda 6 GG fix (April–May 2024): one of the community's earliest rear-spring reports — a left rear spring's upper coil cracked. Advice given at the time: if sourcing from Mazda, take the spring from a Mazda 6 wagon/estate variant ("сарай") 345. The owner then fitted used (contract) Mazda 6 GG rear springs, which installed "like original" 6, prompted by another owner separately wondering about reinforced/stiffer springs since the stock rear bottoms out on speed bumps with 2 passengers aboard 7. Ride height rose slightly on both sides afterward 8, with one commenter guessing the Mazda metal might simply be denser 9. The exact Mazda model/generation was not fully confirmed in the thread 10.

Metallic rattle from a partially broken rear spring coil: a distinct diagnostic point — a metallic rattling/clanging noise from the rear can indicate that a rear spring coil has partially broken, with the loose metal fragment striking the suspension component on movement. This is a mechanical-failure symptom, not a bushing/mount noise, and requires rear spring inspection and replacement 1112. Cross-reference: see the suspension noise diagnostic checklist for distinguishing this from other rattle sources.

Soft OEM rear springs bottom out under heavy load: when heavily loaded (cargo, passengers, mountain-pass driving), the soft OEM rear springs bottom out on the bump stops. Reinforced/stiffer springs or a pneumatic-suspension add-on are needed to stop the chassis or suspension from contacting the terrain or rubbing under load; pneumatic suspenders are reported as a better fix for this specific weak-spring/ overload scenario than static spacer blocks alone 1314151617181920.

Suspension geometry — X80 is heavier than the Mazda 6 the parts were designed for: the X80 weighs roughly 1,600 kg, but shares its spring and shock design lineage with the considerably lighter Mazda 6 GG (~200-250 kg lighter). This partly explains why stock springs can feel soft and handling can feel light, and why heavier-vehicle donor springs (e.g. the Kia Sorento cross-fit documented above) can noticeably firm up handling. Any major spring/shock swap changes ride characteristics and should be considered carefully for safety and controllability implications, not just fitment 212223.

OEM rear spring — upper-coil edge collapses under load; diagonal-cut fix: OEM rear springs can show upper-coil collapse/folding almost immediately once loaded. The sharp edge at the top of the coil acts as a stress-concentration point that scores the coil surface and eventually leads to breakage there. Community fix: carefully cut the corner edge of the top coil diagonally to remove the stress concentration point. Caution: this is a permanent modification to a safety-relevant part and may affect warranty 242526.

Front sits visibly higher than rear after independent front and rear spring replacement — unresolved cosmetic vs. structural question: after replacing both front springs (broken, OEM parts from the official FAW warehouse) and later both rear springs (correct part numbers but not purchased from an official dealer), one owner still sees the front arch sitting visibly higher than the rear ("as if rearing up") even though both axles now have "new" springs. Another owner reports the identical symptom: after fitting new Mazda-wagon rear springs plus spacers (not yet installed), the ride is firm and doesn't bottom out badly on rough bumps, but the thinner rear-spring rod diameter (versus the thicker Mazda rod) is blamed for occasional bottoming. Neither owner has confirmed whether the front/rear imbalance is purely cosmetic or affects the suspension's structural geometry; it remains an open question in the thread 272829.

Loaded behaviour. Victor finds the stock rear firm and good at smoothing bumps 30, yet with four people (340 kg) and about 150 kg of cargo he measured 42 cm to the wheel arch and set the headlight corrector to 2 31. Another owner whose springs were intact but sagging fitted 40 mm spacers 32. Victor ties rear sag and the front spring choice to the automatic (AKPP / АКПП) being about 35 kg heavier than the manual 31.

docs.title: Rear springs from Mazda 6 — cross-fit reports
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #mazda-6-compat · #price · #cross-compatibility

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Rear spring — Mazda 6 GG universal-coil alternative: FAW X80 rear springs can be replaced with Mazda 6 GG (2002-2008 generation) universal coil springs as a cost-effective alternative to OEM, available in auto-parts markets from ~3,000 RUB (RU market, March 2025). Both types reportedly have 6 coils — verify fitment with the supplier before purchase 1.

Suspension-upgrade weight mismatch and pneumatic conclusion (disputed): Mazda 6 GG suspension components (donor car ~1,250 kg) are considered inadequate for the heavier X80 (~1,600 kg — a 350 kg / 28% difference that stresses components not engineered for the load, accelerating spring, damper, and linkage wear) 23. Mazda 6 GH components are stronger but physically too large for the X80's suspension geometry and do not fit. A pneumatic air-bag system added to the rear is reported to resolve load-dependent bounce/bounce-back and provide a rear lift, tested successfully over 2 years by one owner. A full aftermarket-upgrade service is available but expensive. Disagreement: it is debated whether GH-sourced suspension is a viable upgrade path versus the pneumatic solution; the community consensus leans toward the weight difference making GH parts too large to fit, favoring the pneumatic route instead 45.

Rear spring — Mazda 6 GH fits, GG does not (fitment by generation): rear springs from the Mazda 6 GH generation (post-2007) fit and work on the X80; springs from the older Mazda 6 GG generation are reported as shorter and do not fit in this account. Some owners have sourced OEM Mazda springs this way as a lower-cost alternative. Conflict: this contradicts the separate report elsewhere on this card that Mazda 6 GG (2002-2008) universal-coil springs work as a cost-effective rear alternative 1 — treat GG-generation rear-spring fitment as disputed and verify the specific spring/generation before buying 6.

Conflict — Mazda 6 GG wagon rear springs "obligatory" vs. GG "does not fit" reported elsewhere on this card: a separate report insists that if sourcing rear springs from a Mazda 6 GG, they must come from the wagon/estate body specifically (обязательно) — sedan and hatchback GG variants also physically fit but do not provide proper support. This account frames the whole X80 rear suspension architecture as fundamentally Mazda-6-GG-based 7. This is in tension with the separate GG-vs-GH conflict already documented above 16 — treat GG-generation body-style (wagon vs. sedan/hatchback) as an additional, unresolved variable when sourcing Mazda 6 GG rear springs, on top of the existing GG-vs-GH generation dispute.

Rear spring failure and sagging — Mazda 6 GY-generation cross-fit (March 2026): a further round of reports on rear springs sagging over time (requiring the проставки/spacer fix documented throughout this card) adds two more aftermarket cross-fit options: springs from the Mazda 6 GY platform (2002–2007), specifically Fobos part 56023, and Zekkert-brand reinforced springs. Conflict: as with other entries on this card, some owners in this thread report the original springs losing compression while others report satisfactory durability — likely depends on driving conditions and load 8910111213.

Reinforced (усиленные) rear spring variant also exists from Mazda 6 GG universal: alongside the standard Mazda 6 GG-universal rear spring (too soft, see below), a reinforced (усиленные) variant is also sold for the same Mazda 6 GG-universal application and is reported to give upgraded (stiffer) suspension performance versus both stock X80 (13mm rod) and the standard-softness GG-universal spring — worth specifically asking for the reinforced version when sourcing 14.

Mazda 6 sedan rear springs (12.3mm) — one success, one strong warning (conflict): Mazda 6 sedan (GG, 2002+) rear springs (12.3mm wire vs. the X80's own 13mm) are sold on Ozon as a rear-spring option. Conflict: one owner reports installing them on a facelift car with no issues, "went in like stock" 15; a second, more experienced contributor warns that these are sedan springs, not suited to an SUV/wagon use case — the thinner wire will likely sag quickly, and cargo load in the trunk will compress them hard; he recommends looking at wagon (universal)-sourced Mazda 6 springs instead for the X80's SUV-type loading 1617.

Rear springs from Mazda 6 GG — confirmed native fit on a facelift car: a separate, simpler confirmation (independent of the wire/coil-spec debate above): Mazda 6 GG rear springs "went in like factory" on a facelift X80. For alignment reference after any spring swap, use the X80's own manual figures where available; Mazda CX-5 specs are an acceptable fallback if X80-specific data isn't at hand (see the wheel alignment card) 181920.

Rear spring dimensions and cross-brand debate — Mazda 6 sedan too soft, wagon/universal preferred: asked for rear spring dimensions, one owner reported that springs are a known weak point on this car — all owners eventually have them crack — and that he personally has struggled with rear springs since summer: SAT-brand Mazda 6 springs (bought new from Avtotrade) sagged and started bottoming out with just one rear passenger after only a couple of months of use — "completely dead springs." He was searching specifically for reinforced Mazda 6 wagon ("универсал") springs, but reports these are mostly only available at wrecking yards near Moscow, with limited availability near Irkutsk 212223. Separately, he clarified that Mazda 6 sedan springs are too soft; he recommends wagon or Mazda CX-5 springs instead 24. A specific part was linked: rear spring for Mazda 6 (GY) 2002–2007 wagon, cross-referenced for FAW Besturn X80 2014–2021, part ST119065R, via an Ozon listing — confirmed by the poster as a fitting option ("вот такие подходят") 2526.

Mazda 6 GY rear springs (ST119065R) — detailed install, cost, and stiffness trade-off (Aug 2026): a Mazda 6 GY (2002-2007) universal-wagon rear spring, part ST119065R, was fitted after a rear spring broke at 58,000 km, alongside new rear shocks, rear brake pads, front shocks, and a gearbox/engine oil change. Total parts cost 24,000 RUB (RU market, August 2026), labor 8,000 RUB. Result: rear end raised to a reasonable level and the ride is much softer than the cracked stock spring's harsh "bang-bang" over every speed bump. Conflict on stiffness: a separate owner who fitted the same ST119065R part (rod stated as 12.75mm, matching the Mazda 6 GG-universal spec) reports it sat just as low as the stock spring once installed, still striking the bump stops occasionally past 60,000 km; a third owner who instead fitted a 13.3mm-rod, 269mm spring (6 coils vs. the stock 6.5) got a full-tank height of 470mm but found the ride noticeably stiffer, reasoning that fewer coils makes for a slightly harder spring 2728293031.

Rear springs — Standard Springs ST119065R gives near-stock comfort (Aug 2026): a further confirmation of the Standard Springs-brand ST119065R rear spring (same part number documented elsewhere on this card): installed with no spacers, ride comfort and handling were reported as close to the original spring's, with a measured wheel-center-to-fender-edge height of about 43cm. Suitable for normal driving with typical loads rather than heavy hauling 3233343536.

Oct 2026 update — Mazda 6 parts for the rear, rod diameters and spacers. Asked whether the X80 rear suspension can be taken from a Mazda 6, Тимур answered "practically" (all of it) 37 and Миша thinks everything fits 38; no exceptions or part numbers were given.

docs.title: Rear springs — other donors, rod sizes, ride height
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #cross-compatibility · #price · #rear-suspension

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Rear spring alternative — LESJOFORS (Mazda 6 Gen 1): LESJOFORS part 4255452 (for the Mazda 6 Wagon, 2002+) fits the X80's rear. Specs: 6.2 coils, 359mm length, diameters 131/125.5/127.5mm, 12mm wire diameter. It is an expensive option at 6,000+ RUB (RU market, March 2025) per piece, but maintains OEM-level quality; one community member installed it without modification, though some consider the cost prohibitive 1.

Aftermarket quality warning — thinner rod diameter: a separate report warns that certain aftermarket suppliers (referenced as an "Ozon supplier") sell rear springs with a rod diameter roughly 1mm thinner than OEM; over time these visibly sag compared to originals. The recommendation is to research thoroughly before purchase and avoid cheap aftermarket springs, favoring OEM or a verified-quality source such as kitparts.ru 2.

Rear springs from Mazda CX-5 — confirmed working alternative: rear springs from a Mazda CX-5 were installed as a direct replacement alternative when original FAW rear springs were unavailable. Multiple reports confirm good fitment, with one owner reporting 60,000 km without problems. The swap raises rear ride height (measured wheel-to-arch clearance of 12cm after installation), and no modification was required for fitment 34.

Rear springs — Japan Parts catalog option: rear spring replacement is also available through the Japan Parts catalog (searchable via zzap.ru, e.g. partnumber ZC6416H, class JAPANPARTS). One community member confirmed successful installation with proper fitment, reporting the selected springs "all fit well" 5.

Rear springs — Kia Sorento cross-fit (CAT-21642H): Kia Sorento rear springs, part CAT-21642H, fit the X80 rear suspension. Coil wire thickness is 14.3mm — close to the X80's own ~13.7-14mm spec noted elsewhere on this card — and the springs seat perfectly in the lower cups without modification. Installed together with 3cm spacer blocks, they noticeably raise the rear ride height and improve suspension response versus worn stock springs, without the ride becoming excessively stiff. Multiple users in the same thread confirmed good fitment and proper seating 6.

Correction — Kia Sorento rear-spring part number: the Kia Sorento cross-fit rear spring documented above under part number CAT-21642H should read C4T-21642H (community correction to the earlier report) 7.

Rear spring reviews mixed; wire-thickness data point (Sept 2025): prompted by mixed community reviews (some call the rear springs good, others report bottoming out on speed bumps) 8 — brand was reported as not critical as long as the correct spring is matched by measurement 9 — a drive2.ru cross-reference mentions owners fitting KYB RH6416 rear shocks/springs; measured wire thickness: X80 stock spring 13.23mm vs. the GG-wagon-sourced KYB-compatible spring at 12.75mm — thinner than the ~13.6mm option mentioned elsewhere on this card 10. A separate, unconfirmed lead: Honda Accord (7th gen) front springs cross-reference to KYB part RC3427 in a parts catalog, but no community member has confirmed actually fitting them 11.

Rear springs from Mazda CX-5 — independent confirmation with different clearance figure: reinforcing the CX-5 rear-spring report already on this card 34, a separate owner confirms the swap noticeably raised the rear — about 15cm of wheel-to-arch clearance after installation (vs. the 12cm figure reported elsewhere on this card, likely reflecting measurement-point or ride-height differences). The CX-5 spring's upper-coil diameter is larger than stock, and a wheel alignment was performed afterward with no reported handling issues 12.

Suffix-brand rear springs — sagged within 2 weeks (low confidence, single secondhand report): a report relayed via WhatsApp (not a direct community post) states that Suffix-brand rear springs sagged within 2 weeks of installation and were considered too soft. Not recommended for the rear based on this account; the community lacks further data to confirm or refute it 1314.

Measuring ride-height/clearance correctly: when checking suspension ride height or wheel-arch clearance, measure from the wheel center to the arch, not an absolute floor-to-arch distance — because tire size changes the reference point. With a 225/65/17 tire, a rough rule of thumb is a palm-width hand-opening (~8-9cm) of clearance as a healthy reference 1516.

OEM rear spring wire thickness — 14mm, vs. thinner aftermarket options (April 2026): OEM FAW X80 rear springs use 14mm wire thickness (some sources say the wire itself measures closer to 13.5mm). Common aftermarket rear springs measure only 12.7–13mm wire diameter, which changes spring rate and ride height versus the original. Community-cited part numbers for 14mm-wire alternatives include KYB RA3345, Lesjöfors 40 554 60, and Standard Springs ST119063F (the Turkish-made ST119063F is specifically advertised as fitting the FAW), but fitment reports are inconsistent — one member states these parts do not fit the X80 at all and suggests mismatched part-number claims like this may explain why some owners end up replacing their rear suspension repeatedly; checking Ozon reviews before buying is recommended 1718192021.

Rear spring cross-fit catalog — GG, GH, CX-5, and 2.3L variants compared by wire/coil spec (July 2026): a consolidated community spec comparison for rear-spring cross-shopping. X80 OEM: ~13mm wire diameter, ~9.4 coils, 435mm hub-center-to-arch height (stock, unloaded). Mazda 6 GG universal: 12.5mm wire, 8.3 coils — too soft, raises the car only 1–2cm and sags again within weeks (see the failed swap below). Mazda 6 GH: wider spring base than GG. Mazda CX-5: 13.25–14mm wire in various batches, 365–370mm height. Suffix SZ1303 (already documented on the front springs card) actually originates from GH, not GG. Mazda 6 GG 2.3L-engine variant: 12.75mm wire, 9 coils — closer to stock and reported to lift the rear by roughly +2cm. One owner also test-fit Zekkert SF-2322 (CX-5-cross-referenced, 13.3mm wire, 369mm height per the manufacturer site) but could not confirm its narrow-end diameter matched the X80's factory spacer/seat. Bottom line reiterated by the community: stop trading brand names and match wire diameter + coil count + free height against these numbers before buying 2223242526272829303132333435.

Mazda 6 GG universal rear spring swap — disappointing real-world result: one owner's full write-up of installing Mazda 6 GG-universal ("Klakson") rear springs: expected a large lift (sagged stock height 348mm → new spring's rated 384mm) but actual gain was only +1cm (with spacers adding another +15mm) — "no miracle happened." Cost: ~3,000₽ + 5 hours of labor. Conclusion: GG-universal springs are not a good rear fix for the X80 due to their thinner wire and lower coil count versus stock 31.

Rear ride-height measurement method — 435mm stock reference, three ways to check it: to evaluate spring wear or test a new spring: raise the rear wheel completely off the ground and measure from the wheel center to the top of the wheel arch — stock spec is 435mm. Cross-check note: measuring the same car from different reference points (from above at the fender lip vs. from below at the rocker panel vs. eye-level at the fender) gave noticeably different numbers on the same vehicle (465mm / 445mm / 455mm respectively in one example) — pick one consistent method and don't compare numbers across methods 283637.

Rear springs from Mazda CX-5 — adapter-plate obstacle (July 2026): reinforcing the CX-5 rear-spring cross-fit already documented on this card, one owner who went ahead with a CX-5 swap reports it is workable but not simple: a custom adapter plate is needed because off-the-shelf automotive adapters (VAZ/UAZ/GAZ patterns) do not fit. Needed adapter specifications: hole diameter 71-75mm, outer diameter 128-130mm (matching the spring's perimeter), inner diameter for the spring seat 100-102mm. Springs from a Gazelle Business/GAZ Nexxt donor almost fit but have an oversized center hole 383940.

Alternative rear springs from BMW X3 (new cross-fit, Aug 2026): a further cross-fit candidate for the rear: BMW X3 rear springs, height 375-380mm, rod diameter 13-13.3mm, maximum outer diameter 122mm (versus the X80's stock 131mm), with a slight narrowing at both edges and 7.2 coils (versus the X80's stock 6.5). Non-original (aftermarket) pricing is reported as significantly cheaper than other options. Untested prediction from the poster: it may seat on the transverse rear arm and stock rubber mounts (or the "classic"/VAZ-style spacers already discussed elsewhere on this card), or may need spacers — not yet confirmed by an actual installation 41.

Rear spring development/manufacturing project announced (Sept 2026): a community member (Айрат) who had previously mentioned developing a rear spring for the FAW Besturn X80 reports the factory has now quoted him a price, and he can sell the springs at 3,500 RUB (RU market, September 2026) each with quality described as excellent; he is deciding between a polymer/powder coating and a standard anticorrosion treatment, and is looking for beta testers before a wider production run (he plans to fit a set himself). In the same thread, another owner reports his own rear coils have partially collapsed ("half a turn folded over") at 25,000 km but is not yet bothered enough to replace them since he drives alone; he'd be interested in a set from this new run and separately asks whether the "polymer coating" mentioned is powder coating. Contact for this project is via VK/Max direct message rather than the Telegram group, due to intermittent VPN access 4243444546.

Rear spring rod diameters (Victor, Sep 2026). Stock X80: 13 mm; Mazda 6 GG estate: 12.75 mm; hatchback: 12.5 mm; sedan: 12 mm, the softest — so Mazda GG rear springs are not a like-for-like fit 4748. Владимир Хохлов said that ordering by VIN he received springs with only an 11.5 mm rod and the rear sat lower than the front, so he bought estate springs (12.5 mm by his figure) 49; Victor ran 12.75 mm and found it not enough, and says 12.5 mm is the hatchback spring, which will sag just the same 50. Serega fitted Mazda 6 GG estate rear springs (a Zekkert pair, listed at about 3,479 RUB, RU market, Sep 2026) together with Ozon spacers; they are very soft, with two children in the back the rear sat down and he had to lower the headlights with the corrector 5152. He then bought one slightly used original spring and 3 mm spacers, which he calls excellent 51. Victor agrees estate springs are soft but not suited to loads or passengers 53.

See also: - Rear springs — failure and pneumatic fixes (Hub) - Rear springs — failure symptoms and diagnosis - Rear springs from Mazda 6 — cross-fit reports - Rear spring spacers and lift - Rear pneumatic bellows — field reports and pressures

docs.title: Rear pneumatic bellows — field reports and pressures
docs.text:
Tags: #springs

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Pneumatic air-spring bellows — general characteristics: available from different manufacturers (Russian, Belarusian brands). Typical operating pressure 0.9–1.0 bar; a 0.1 bar change in pressure noticeably changes ride height. Russian-brand bellows are stiffer, handle bumps better, and hold body height more consistently. Belarusian-brand bellows are softer and more compliant but less stiff in response. Bellows are rubber, 1–1.5cm wall thickness. Cold weather (-20°C) has minimal impact on performance — they warm up quickly once driven. Overall, bellows are more resistant to bumps and speed bumps than the standard suspension 1.

Rear-specific Belarusian air spring spec: size 200×85, described as softer than the stock spring, good quality, reliable installation 2.

Sagging-fix using Lanos/Sens/Nexia bellows: for sagging under heavy cargo, a full tank, and an LPG cylinder (59L), install 85×160mm pneumatic bellows sourced from Lanos/Sens/Nexia together with 2cm spacers. The factory bump stop must be removed and the spacer tip lightly machined to fit properly. Tested over 15,000 km without issues, described as performing like the factory suspension 3.

Bottoming-out ("probivanie") fix with cut-in bump-stop bellows: when the rear suspension still bottoms out on bumps even with new springs/struts/ buffers/spacers, one solution is installing pneumatic bellows in place of the standard bump stops. This requires cutting off the shock absorber's bump stop with a plasma cutter and welding a large washer in its place. Typical pressure ~0.8 atm, adjustable upward if needed. The same struts fit multiple donor vehicles (e.g. Nexia), but spacers must be matched. One owner reported 2+ years of successful use carrying 4 passengers plus full cargo without the suspension settling; springs/buffers alone did not solve the problem for this owner 4.

Pneumatic balloons (air springs) for the rear coil — fitment conflict: Fenox-brand pneumatic balloons with a side valve, sourced from Ozon, are sold in a "standard" 230x110mm size. Ozon product comments report this standard size does not fit directly inside the X80 rear coil spring. Workaround reported to make them fit: remove the factory bump stops/buffer spacers from the suspension to create clearance. Conflict: one user reported a successful installation with good results two months prior with no modification, while the product's own comments describe incompatibility without the bump-stop removal — treat direct fitment as unconfirmed and the bump-stop-removal workaround as the safer starting point 567.

Pneumatic suspension (Mazda-swap) size spec: for pneumatic suspension used together with a Mazda-donor rear suspension (see the Mazda 6 GG swap discussion), the reported balloon size is 200×85mm with a side-mounted valve (боковой сосок) — a different size than the Fenox 230×110mm balloon discussed above; match the balloon size to the specific installation rather than assuming one size fits both setups 89.

Side-valve pneumatic bags for rear coil — positive report (March 2026): a second, separate positive report for pneumatic (air) bags installed inside the rear coil springs — 2 bags + 2 bump stops, side-mounted valve, sold specifically for FAW Besturn X80 model years 2020 onward. The owner reports being very satisfied: for hauling something heavy, simply inflate the bags as needed. This corroborates the pneumatic-bellow fix already documented above as an effective solution for the soft-rear-spring/ overload scenario 1011.

Rear pneumatic air-spring conversion — general approach and Drive2.ru guide: an alternative rear-suspension modification replaces the coil springs with pneumatic air springs (пневмобаллоны) for adjustable ride height/characteristics: remove the bump stops (отбойники), install the air springs, and inflate to the desired pressure. A detailed step-by-step guide is published on Drive2.ru: 'Доработка задней подвески, установка пневмобаллонов' (https://www.drive2.ru/l/523642963557877749/), covering suspension disassembly, spring removal, and air-spring mounting. This is an advanced modification requiring real technical knowledge and equipment; community discussion at the time indicated some fitment details were still being worked out 12131415.

Pneumatic balloons for rear springs — 2020+ FAW-specific kit: pneumatic air suspension balloons (пневмобаллоны) sold specifically for the X80's rear springs (2020-present) are spring-integrated air units with a side-mounted check valve, sold as a 2-pack including bump stops, available on the Ozon marketplace. They improve suspension compliance and give adjustable load-carrying capacity 1617.

Pneumatic balloon conversion — before/after clearance at 0.6 atm: a separate first-hand pneumatic-balloon install report (same modification documented elsewhere on this card): inflated to only ~0.6 atm, ground clearance increased from "3 fingers" to "5 fingers," the ride felt slightly softer, cornering improved, and railroad crossings were noticeably smoother. The install required cutting/removing the bump stops (отбойники), and the system includes a manual inflation valve. The owner flagged some uncertainty about long-term durability, but reported still liking the setup after a longer trip a few days later 18192021222324.

Rear pneumatic-balloon install and pressure — detailed field notes (Sept 2024): one long-term pneumatic-balloon user (Женя) described his rear setup as "a fantastic thing." Asked for size and pressure, another owner (Олег Белоусов) gave detailed voice-note guidance: the factory bump stop needs to be removed (not the rычаг/arm itself — only a suspension-geometry re-check via alignment is needed after, not arm work); the spring itself is removed and reinstalled with the balloon fitted with its side valve. Pressure notes from his own experience: started at 1.1 atm ("colotushka" — jarring/harsh ride); settled on the brand's recommended minimum of ~0.8 atm; personally runs 0.9 atm and finds it "great" — still gets some bottoming-out on speed bumps at that pressure, but it's a major improvement overall. With 2–3 passengers aboard the ride firms up like leaf-spring suspension. He stress-tested it loaded with roughly 360 kg of cargo (12 sacks), and even at that load with pressure raised to ~1.1 atm, the ride stayed smooth. Warning against overinflating: pressure too high stiffens the ride into the body structure and causes harsh "bottoming-out" impacts rather than cushioning — 0.9 atm was his practical sweet spot. He also tried fitting OEM-spec ("obechaynye"/OEM-pattern) 16mm-wire Honda Stepwagon-sourced springs as an alternative to balloons; those sagged noticeably within one month, so he reverted to stock springs plus balloons 252627282930.

Valve/nipple choice — use a Lada ("Zhiguli") gold valve core, not the Chinese-supplied one: for the balloon's inflation valve/nipple, avoid the short-lived nipple that ships with cheap Chinese balloon kits — one owner who fitted Belarusian balloons switched to a Lada/"Zhiguli" gold valve core ("Жигулевский золотник") specifically, and reports it has lasted genuinely long-term (9 years, on a Peugeot wagon fitted with the same type of balloon, with zero maintenance) — versus the stock Chinese nipple, which reportedly fails within about a year 30.

"Broke something today" — where owners are sourcing rear springs (2024 thread): a rear-spring-failure report prompted a burst of replacement advice from Олег Белоусов: buy only from official dealers for a genuinely OEM part, or search wrecking yards ("контрактные разборки") for Mazda 6 springs specifically with at least 13–13.5mm wire thickness and 7 coils — cheap "obechaynye"/generic-brand springs are reported as reliably weak, sagging within about a month and leading to the bump stops striking inside the spring. Kayaba no longer manufactures a rear spring for this application; Bilstein was suggested as an alternative worth checking. OEM spring price at the time: ~1,700 RUB (RU market, September 2024). The same owner's practical recommendation: fit pneumatic balloons inside the springs regardless of which spring you use — even OEM-grade 7-coil springs — as extra insurance against exactly this kind of failure recurring 313233. A separate contributor (Олег Белоусов, continuing the same thread) reported a full day of driving, including ~30km of highway, on the balloon setup with no cornering lean and a noticeably quieter ride ("shelestит" — light rustling sound, no harshness); pairing 7-coil OEM-pattern springs with an added internal balloon was described as giving lasting, "forget about it" reliability 3435.

Balloon install procedure — bump-stop trimming detail (voice-note walkthrough): expanding on the install steps documented elsewhere on this card, for a 285mm balloon specifically: cut the factory rubber bump stop cleanly around the ring where the expanded/wider upper section begins — remove only that expanded portion, leaving the constant-diameter tube base intact; a rubber pad/spacer then sits in that spot. If the bump stop is left un-trimmed (just pulled out whole instead), the balloon seats crookedly/off-axis inside the spring and doesn't fit properly. Done correctly, the balloon seats snugly ("тюка в тюку") against the trimmed bump-stop base when the spring is compressed and the arm reinstalled, and inflates and performs correctly. Recommend sourcing Belarusian-brand balloons over Novosibirsk-brand — the Novosibirsk ones are reported as overly stiff/hard ("дубовые") and prone to problems 3637383940.

Pneumatic airbags in rear spring cavities — updated field report (Aug 2026): reinforcing the pneumatic-bellow reports already documented on this card, a further owner (Женя) reports the setup as "a wonderful thing." Installation detail specific to this report: the stock rubber bump stop must be cut off and replaced with the bump stop supplied in the balloon kit — the only real hurdle, since the X80's own rear springs are narrowed at both the top and bottom, limiting how a balloon can be fitted. Pressure guidance: about 0.6 bar for everyday driving, raised to 1.0+ bar when hauling heavy cargo (tested carrying 15 bundles of thick laminate flooring). Side effect: the rear end sits noticeably higher after install, requiring the headlights to be re-aimed 41424344.

Air bellows inside the coils. Женя fitted air bellows (пневмобаллоны) inside the rear coils of a 2020-onward X80 using a Yandex Market bellows kit and a single-circuit inflation kit with side nipple 4546. He inflated them to about 1 atm and loaded 15 packs of 12 mm laminate plus 200 kg of cement with no sag; the bump stop (отбойник) had to be cut shorter 4748. He quoted about 5,000 RUB or more for the installation service (RU market, Sep 2026) 47.

docs.title: Rear springs — failure and pneumatic fixes
docs.text:
Tags: #springs · #price · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Summary: the X80's stock rear springs are a known weak point (cracked or sagging coils, bottoming out under load). The community's fixes fall into four groups: replacement springs from other cars (Mazda 6, CX-5, Kia Sorento and others), spacers under the springs for lift, air bellows (пневмобаллоны) inside the coils, and diagnosis of what actually failed. The hub keeps the core failure, sourcing and part-number facts; the detail sits in the sibling cards listed at the bottom.

Failure pattern: rear springs have a reputation for weak reliability. One owner had both rear springs fail at 75,000 km. Spec for reference: 13.7mm wire thickness (community treats ~13mm+ as acceptable), 6–7 coil turns per side. Overloading — e.g. 4 people plus cargo in a vehicle rated for a lighter load per its registration — contributes to premature failure 1.

OEM availability/cost: original rear springs were available (Oct 2024) at the FAW official dealership in Moscow (Autogermés, Sormovskaya branch, reachable via the main website → transfer to parts department → reserve). Stock was limited — 6 units found in October 2024 — and reported to sell out quickly 2.

Aftermarket alternative: Chinese aftermarket springs from Kitparts.ru, ~3,310 RUB (RU market, October 2024) per pair (left/right identical), matching the original 13.7mm rod diameter. Inferior-quality copies (12.6–12.8mm rod) reportedly fail within 1.5–3 months. Other cross-fit sources: Mazda OEM springs (16mm rod, compatible) and Honda Stepwgn springs (16mm rod, need a minor custom spacer with rubber pads to fit). Toyota/Honda alternatives beyond the Stepwgn require significant customization and are not recommended 3.

Disagreement — springs alone vs. spacers vs. pneumatic bellows: one contributor (Олег Белоусов) recommends pneumatic air-spring bellows (Belarusian brand) as the primary fix over stronger springs; others argue 2cm spacers are essential for proper fitment regardless of spring choice. Two owners (Сергей Куликов, Олег) both experienced failure with weak aftermarket springs, but had success either with original springs plus pneumatic bellows, or with Mazda donor parts 3.

OEM rear spring part number — 5CA028011: the rear spring's own OEM FAW part number, referenced in catalogs for all X80 model years (2013–2021), is 5CA028011; cross-brand analogs sold under this listing include SF2598 / ZC6416H / ST119065R (see the cross-brand options documented elsewhere on this card) 4. The community's earliest recorded mention of the Kayaba/KYB 6416 cross-brand rear spring/shock option (see the detailed KYB RH6416 wire-thickness comparison elsewhere on this card) dates back to an early, terse report simply citing "Kayaba 6416" for the rear springs 5.

Reference. Victor's Drive2 post "14. Эпопея с задними пружинами и амортизаторами" (rear springs and shocks saga) documents his work in detail: https://www.drive2.ru/l/741593106217980020/ 6.

See also: - Rear springs — failure symptoms and diagnosis — Symptoms, causes and diagnosis of failing or sagging rear springs: sag, bottoming out, rattles, coil collapse. - Rear springs from Mazda 6 — cross-fit reports — Mazda 6 GG, GH and GY rear springs on the X80: fitment by generation and body style, ST119065R, results and conflicts. - Rear springs — other donors, rod sizes, ride height — Non-Mazda-6 donors (CX-5, Kia Sorento, BMW X3, Lesjöfors, KYB), wire diameters, coil counts, ride-height measurement and a new spring project. - Rear spring spacers and lift — Rubber, PTFE and polyurethane spacers under the rear springs: thickness, real lift, brands, fitment limits and prices. - Rear pneumatic bellows — field reports and pressures — Owner reports on air bellows inside the rear coils: sizes, valves, bump-stop trimming, working pressures and load tests.

Related existing cards: - Rear air suspension — pneumatic installation guide - Rear spring replacement and alignment - Coil springs — aftermarket numbers and sag

docs.title: Rear spring spacers and lift
docs.text:
Tags: #springs

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Rear spring spacer — Mazda 6 GH (2007-2013) rubber spacers: 30mm-thick rubber spring spacers (проставки) from a Mazda 6 GH (2007-2013) fit under the X80's rear springs. Purpose: (1) stiffen the rear suspension for carrying heavy loads; (2) prepare the suspension for a future air-bag/pneumatic-bellow upgrade. Installation is simple — the spacer just sits under the spring, no extra hardware needed. Caution: it increases spring preload and may increase shock-absorber stroke, so owners debate whether higher-rate springs and new shocks should be fitted at the same time. After a 2-week parking period the rubber can briefly squeak on the first drive, then lubricates itself with use. One load test — 300 kg of cargo plus 2 passengers — did not draw police attention for improper lowering 1.

40mm rear spacer — AutoDVC brand: an alternative rear spring spacer, 40mm thick, AutoDVC brand from Ozon. Reported: VAZ Classic-family spacers do not fit. The 40mm AutoDVC spacer raises the vehicle by about 3cm; the original factory spacer measures 10mm. Fitment is direct, with no modification needed 23.

Rear suspension is fully loaded even at rest — lift-spacer attempt unsuccessful: the X80's rear suspension is described as fully packed/ loaded even unladen (no sag margin). An attempt to install 30mm lift spacers under the rear springs failed due to suspension-geometry constraints — minimum clearance between the bump stop and the lower control arm was only ~13cm, which prevented spacer installation without a full geometry modification (adverse camber/caster changes). The owner reports 20mm spacers (mentioned as available from Mazda-parts suppliers on Ozon) would likely be more suitable. Recommendation: do not attempt aggressive rear lift modifications without professional geometry analysis and correction first 4.

Spacers preferred over spring-top bushings for raising rear ride height: when raising the rear, spacers installed between the spring and subframe are preferred over spring-top bushings — spacers preserve the spring's natural compliance/softness while still raising clearance, whereas bushings alter spring geometry unfavorably. One contributor (KASPER) recommends spacers as the correct approach specifically to avoid degrading suspension characteristics while gaining clearance 56.

Weak rear springs even after a complete rebuild, fixed with stiffer springs + spacer blocks (Jan 2026): after a complete rear suspension rebuild (new springs, shocks, bushings, and stabilizer components), one owner's vehicle still bounced excessively and bottomed out on speed bumps. Root cause: the replacement springs, despite being new, were weaker than the originals. Fix: substitute stiffer springs (again sourced from the Mazda universal-fit options documented elsewhere on this card) and add polyurethane spacer/lift blocks (бафферы) to increase clearance and damping 789101112. The spacer blocks used add up to 40mm of ground clearance and can be cut/halved to customize the lift height — one owner split factory 40mm blocks in half for 20mm each; available on OZON, compatible with aftermarket spring setups 131415.

Rear suspension spacer shims — Clearance-Plus, Mazda 6 GH-spec (March 2026): 30mm rubber spacer shims (проставки), Clearance-Plus brand, designed for the Mazda 6 GH (2007–2013), available via Ozon (https://ozon.ru/t/TztOuYQ). These add +30mm at the rear and were used specifically to correct the front/rear height imbalance that followed a front-spring replacement — see the front springs card for the full context. They eliminate body scraping while restoring a balanced stance; tested by multiple users with positive results 1617181920.

Rear spring + 20mm spacer combo — installed report (Zekkert, March 2026): one owner installed new Zekkert-brand rear springs together with 20mm polyurethane clearance spacers under them in the same session (product: "Проставки увеличения клиренса задних пружин ... +20мм", polyurethane, listed for FAW Besturn X80 2013–2021 on Ozon). This is the same springs-plus-spacer combination documented in general terms elsewhere on this card, confirmed here as a specific completed installation 212223.

Rear spacer rated +20mm delivers only +10mm real lift; PTFE spacers need trimming: rear suspension spacers advertised as +20mm may only deliver about +10mm of real lift if the factory rubber mounts are already ~10mm thick — actual results can be well short of the advertised figure. PTFE/plastic spacers often need their edges cut/filed down to clear the surrounding rubber components before they'll seat properly. One owner bought a cheap Ant-brand PTFE spacer for about 1,000₽ as an experiment for the rear lift; a discussion partner separately tried a thicker 40mm spacer on the same basis. See the front lift-spacers card for the front-specific version of this same effective-vs-advertised-lift issue 242526272829.

Rear spacers +15mm combined with Mazda GG/GY spring packs — softer ride, ~2.5cm lower: installing +15mm rear spacers together with Mazda 6 GG or GY spring packs produces a noticeably softer, "wallowy" rear end and lowers the car by roughly 2.5cm compared to stock. One owner reported this combination made the rear feel too soft for speed bumps (more pronounced bounce landing off them) but better suited to hauling cargo (tested with a load of pumpkins) 3031323334353637.

Rear spacers (lift and material). Ozon sells 30 mm polyurethane rear clearance spacers for the X80 (2013-2021) 38. Owners report that 30 mm spacers give about 2 cm of extra height 3940. Serega says rubber spacers compress about 1 cm under load while polyurethane (PU) holds much better, so he advises at least 3 cm of PU; rubber ones are "complete junk" 4041. For 20 mm sets, an AutoDVC set (red banner, labelled for the 2018-2022 restyle, 2 pieces, 5-year warranty) and a Polimer set (orange banner, labelled for 2013-2021) were compared 4243; the Ozon card lists article 2063221107, part number 2061-20-82304, polyurethane, made in Russia 44. Victor says the orange-banner type needs reworking and the red-banner set has the better shape 4546. The material is disputed: Serega says the "left" (orange) spacers are plain rubber and polymer (polyurethane) is better 47, while Владимир Хохлов points out the listing for those on the left reads polyurethane 48. Владимир bought new 20 mm spacers on Ozon for about 2,000 RUB per pair (RU market, Sep 2026) 49; Victor estimated shipping a set to Kaliningrad at about 800 RUB (Sep 2026) and warned it is awkward 50.

See also: - Rear springs — failure and pneumatic fixes (Hub) - Rear springs — failure symptoms and diagnosis - Rear springs from Mazda 6 — cross-fit reports - Rear springs — other donors, rod sizes, ride height - Rear pneumatic bellows — field reports and pressures

Part of the rear-springs set; mentions of "this card" or "elsewhere on this card" may refer to the sibling cards below.

docs.title: Rear suspension bushing overhaul
docs.text:
Tags: #bushing · #part-number · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Complete rear suspension overhaul — parts list (2025-09 report). A full rear suspension bushing/hardware job was documented with the following parts: 1. "Ushastiy" (eared) bushing: Masuma RU-511 (2 units). 2. Serpentine/trailing-arm bushing: Masuma RU-512 (4 units). 3. Camber-adjustment arm bushing: Masuma MA-103 (2 units). 4. Spring cup, rubber type: Jikiu BH25077 (4 units) — better to find a version with an integrated ball race. 5. Stretched/stuck center bolts: may require heating, cutting off with a grinder, then replacing with new Masuma MLS584 bolts. 6. Rear bumper stops: Torr DR0148 (2 units). 7. Stabilizer bushings: Jikiu BL25024 (2 units) — note: slightly higher profile and different retention than OEM; functional equivalence unconfirmed.

Assembly tip: lubricate all bolts with WD-40, graphite grease, copper grease, and a rust converter before assembly to ease future removal.123

Tools and difficulty (2025-10 report). Rear longitudinal suspension bushings (сайлентблоки) can be replaced by an owner, but require specialized tools: a frame/press holder on both sides plus hammer strikes, or a hydraulic press. Rubber-lined bushings are harder to press out than rubber-lined hub bushings. When shopping for replacement bushings, prefer versions with an integral sleeve to avoid a difficult press-out later. One experienced owner spent 3 days completing a rear bushing job, including dealing with difficult alignment bolts — confirming this is a complex, multi-day job even with reasonable mechanical skill.4567

Labor cost vs. DIY (2025-10 report). Shop labor for a rear bushing press-installation was typically quoted around 11,000 RUB (RU market, October 2025). One owner instead did the job himself near his home in about 2 hours — but only after buying the correct press/frame tooling — saving the labor cost while requiring both mechanical skill and the right equipment.8910

docs.title: Rear trailing arm bushing
docs.text:
Tags: #bushing · #rear-suspension · #part-number · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Rear longitudinal arms holding up to 160,000 km with no attention beyond the stabilizer bar: in a durability discussion, one owner (Arсhi 77) reported his rear longitudinal control arms were still fine at 160,000 km. Pressed on this by another member, he clarified the context: on the front lower control arms he had already replaced the whole assembly twice in that time (see the lower control arm bushings card for that side of the same conversation), but on the rear axle he had touched nothing except the stabilizer bar up to 160,000 km — i.e. the rear longitudinal arm/bushing itself needed no service at all over that mileage 12.

Part number — 5CA028430: the bushing (silentblock) for the rear trailing/longitudinal control arm, mounted under the rear spring, is FAW part 5CA028430. This is the same part for both the left and right side (front and rear positions on the longitudinal arm) 34567.

No published dimensions — buy the OEM part rather than trying to measure/replicate it: one owner asked for the bushing's internal dimensions specifically so he could source a generic aftermarket replacement without buying the branded part. The community's answer was blunt: exact dimensions are unlikely to be published anywhere — the only reliable way to get them is to remove the old bushing and measure it yourself. The simpler, recommended path is to just order the catalog-listed part by number rather than trying to reverse-engineer a generic substitute 34.

Sourcing and price — ~1,098 RUB via Kitparts.ru, also listed on Kitzapchasti.ru: part 5CA028430 is available from Kitparts.ru (Moscow) at roughly 1,098 RUB (RU market, December 2025) (https://kitparts.ru/zapchasti/faw/faw-besturn-x80/shassi.-podveska/podveska-zadnyaya/sajlent-blok-rychaga-zadnej-podveski-5ca028430/), and separately confirmed as listed on Kitzapchasti.ru (https://kitzapchasti.ru/catalog/Faw/FAW-X80/hodovaya-chast/podveska-zadnyaya/5CA028430-sajlentblok-zadnego-rychaga-pod-pruzhinu-zadnij-Faw-X80-5CA028430.html) under the description "rear arm bushing, under the spring" — confirming this is the same part referenced by both community questions on this card 467.

Oct 2026 update — rear lower transverse arm silent blocks: numbers, analogues, labour. For the rear lower transverse arm silent block (сайлентблок) Arсhi 77 again cites FAW 5CA028430 ("I think these are the ones") 8, but Che Guevara reported that Emex cannot find the FAW number 9. Romanych cites the analogue ASVA 0501-098 10; a shop lists the same as 0501098 11. Andrey Gamodin bought bushings (two per arm) that fit according to the manual, and advises not to search under FAW at all but for Mazda or Ford analogues, saying they are identical to the X80 suspension 1213. Che Guevara found a matching bushing on Emex for about 350 RUB each (RU market, Oct 2026) 14.

Rubberised or metal-sleeve? Romanych warns to make sure the ASVA ones arrive with a metal sleeve (металлическая обойма), not rubberised, because press-in types seat better and last longer 1516. A member reports that the rubberised ones press in very badly and suggests looking for something else that fits the housing 17.

Labour. A shop quoted about 5,000 RUB per side for replacing the rear silent blocks (RU market, Oct 2026); it was unclear whether parts were included 18. Victor says that is not expensive, since this is the most awkward silent block 19. Romanych adds that some masters replace them without removing the arm, which is cheaper, whereas removing the arm means dismantling the whole rear suspension 20.

Replace or keep driving? At 108,000 km a service wrote a long list for the rear suspension — silent blocks of the longitudinal arms and of the spring arms — and the owner (Вадим Ратников) asked whether to buy complete arms instead 2122. Arсhi 77 reports that one service condemned all his silent blocks, but another judged them alive and he drove another 40,000 km without replacing them, adding that a service sells work volume, not quality 23. Victor advises that a service should shake the part or show the fault rather than hand over a paper listing everything to replace 24. The services disagree, so the wiki records both views.

Further owner reports and numbers. A B50 rear longitudinal arm silent block is cited as FA0128200-1; a member said the silent-block assembly itself costs about 1,300 RUB (RU market, April 2024), so pressing a new bushing in is unnecessary. A YouTube guide is linked; one owner said the job took half a day without a lift, while he estimated 15 minutes with a lift.252627 A member changing a boot on a FAW found the rear silent blocks worn except one type; another, checking his own, found them fine except the longitudinal arm bushings and bump stops, and said light peeling at the edges is not a sign of failure. A photo showed a bushing with cracked, rust-stained rubber, and that owner was told to replace both sides.28293031 For the rear lower arm bushing where the camber (развальные) bolts sit, a member gave the cross-references KIA 55215-38000 and Shin Hwa SH-129, with a catalogue screenshot of the rear suspension arm (item numbers 14-28); another gave only the number 0501098. Fitment was not confirmed.323334 See also Lower control arm — wear and aftermarket parts.

docs.title: Rear wheel hub bearing
docs.text:
Tags: #mazda-6-compat · #part-number · #wheel-hub · #bearing · #price · #rear-axle

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

The X80 rear wheel hub is a press-fit hub-and-bearing assembly (part FC012615X / FA012615XB) that is shared with the Mazda 6 GG and the FAW B50, so cross-brand and used units are common. The front hub is a different, bolt-on design — see the front wheel hub bearing card.

docs.title: Part numbers and what is sold
docs.text:
Part number: FC012615X, the rear wheel bearing/hub assembly.12 A rear hub assembly listed under FA012615XB (marked "NEW" on the marketplace listing, sold on Ozon) appears to be a labeling variant of the same part rather than a different one; treat FC012615X and FA012615XB as the same assembly until a discrepancy is confirmed.345 A later, independent report (March 2026) reconfirmed FA012615XB as the complete rear hub assembly, available on OZON.67

It is sold only as a complete sealed assembly — individual bearings cannot be serviced, reamed or replaced separately.28 A follow-up question about a standalone rear-right bearing part number was answered directly: the rear hub bearing is not sold separately and must be replaced as the full assembly (FA012615XB, "NEW" on marketplace listings), available on Ozon and similar retailers.91011 The assembly is also available from Wildberries and Avito.1

docs.title: Design and serviceability
docs.text:
The rear hub is press-fitted onto the rear axle spindle with a single retaining bolt, and no easy Chinese-brand analog exists yet; Krauf appears as a generic option. (The front hub bolts directly to the steering knuckle — a different design with more limited aftermarket options.)121314151617

Reports disagree on whether the rear unit may be opened:

  • One report says not to disassemble and re-grease the bearing: it develops wear grooves and fails prematurely, and a replacement hub assembly is reported as cheaper than a quality bearing alone anyway.8
  • Another says that, unlike the front hub, the rear hub is disassemblable.1819
  • When installing a swapped or used hub, one 2025-11 report advises to fully disassemble it and repack it with high-quality grease, since original hubs need proper greasing to avoid premature wear.2021222324 The used Mazda 6 hub in a separate case also "required minor disassembly and re-lubrication" before it fitted and worked reliably.25
  • A further report contrasts the X80 with the B50, which has a partially serviceable hub: the X80 rear hub is described as a sealed, non-disassemblable unit.2627282930313233343536373839404142

docs.title: Symptoms and service life
docs.text:
The bearing typically develops play around 70,000–100,000 km with an audible grinding noise (гул). The noise can persist for an extended distance (7,000+ km) before outright failure, but prompt replacement is recommended to avoid secondary damage to other drivetrain components (front CV joints, potential rear-axle effects).2

A case from Dec 2025 describes a growling/turbo-like sound starting around 60 km/h and increasing with acceleration, with no steering-wheel vibration; on inspection the rear hub bearing had disintegrated. The community treats this as a known X80 failure mode consistent with the 70,000–100,000 km pattern.434445

Reported service life varies widely. Owners report the rear hub bearing commonly wears out around 256,000 km.464748 One rear replacement was documented at 130,000 km total mileage (the owner had already replaced both front bearings).495051525354 Conflict: the rear hubs on the X80 reportedly fail prematurely for some owners even with regular tire rotation and routine maintenance — one owner's left rear hub failed repeatedly before reaching 30,000 km each time, replacement costing ~2,500₽ per hub — while a second owner reports the rear hubs still original at 167,000 km. No consensus root cause emerged; possibly a defective batch or differences in driving/maintenance pattern.2627282930313233343536373839404142

docs.title: Cross-fit and alternatives
docs.text:
Mazda 6. The same hub/bearing assembly is used on the Mazda 6 GG (2002–2008 in one report, 2003–2007 generation in another), so a used Mazda 6 rear hub can be substituted.251819 The rear hub of the Mazda 6 MPV GG/LW also fits the FAW X80 (2025-11 report) — unlike the front hub, which is not swappable.3452021222324 Rear wheel bearings sourced from the Mazda 6 may fit; Ildgin (a Korean Mazda-parts supplier) bearings have been used successfully for a rear wheel bearing replacement.55565753 When buying a Mazda 6-sourced used unit or a no-name aftermarket assembly, confirm exact compatibility before installing — some no-name analogs are reported as equivalent in quality to branded versions.158

FAW B50. The rear wheel hub (ступица) is reported as identical between the X80 and the FAW B50 (Feb 2026), so it can be sourced from B50 parts catalogs — often at a lower cost than X80-specific listings.5960

Used donor units. One owner sourced a used Mazda 6 hub via Avito for ~1,000 RUB (RU market, September 2024) including delivery; it required minor disassembly and re-lubrication but fitted and worked reliably.25 Another fitted a used Mazda 6GG rear hub from Avito for 910 RUB, which installed "like original" and carries Japanese markings. Caution: out of curiosity about a humming noise, the owner later disassembled it and found deep indentation marks of unknown origin on the inner race — inspect a used donor's races carefully before trusting it long-term; its longevity was not yet established.61

Selecting a unit (Aug 2026). An owner choosing between two listings — a Mazda 6 rear hub assembly SAT ST-G14V-26-15X at 2,240 RUB (RU market, August 2026) (Irkutsk, 2026-08-20) and a Tatsumi-brand Mazda 6/CX-7 (2007+) rear hub TDE5062 at 7,430 RUB (discounted from 7,660 RUB, same seller/date) — was advised to buy the hub with the ABS sensor connector already attached (a plain non-ABS hub will not work on ABS-equipped cars) and specifically the left-side hub, not the right, since front and rear hubs on this platform are handed and the two sides are not interchangeable.6263646566 This conflicts with the front card, which reports front hubs as identical on both sides; the left/right remark may apply to the rear hub only, and no one reconciled the two.

Other options and prices.

  • Stellox part 43-29349-SX (wheel hub bearing kit): a marketplace listing sold it as "ORIGINAL" for 14,924 RUB (2025).1819
  • OEM FAW replacement via chinaspare.ru for approximately 4,000 RUB (as of 2025-03-28). Budget cross-brand alternatives beyond Mazda are also reported to work if fitment (tooth count on the ABS ring, physical dimensions) is verified first — sources include KitZap, KitParts and Chinaspare.464748
  • ILJIN IJ122042 (Mazda-based) at ~5,450₽ via Emex (2026), or the lower-cost B-ring BK3913 at ~2,500₽.121314151617 A real install of the ILJIN unit cost ~5,450₽ in parts plus ~4,000₽ labor, and the lower hub-mounting bolts came out easily without needing to be cut or drilled.67
  • Adapting or customizing non-matching aftermarket hub parts is discouraged: one such attempt (~1,000₽) still ended in failure. Stick to the complete, correctly matched assembly (FC012615X / FA012615XB).6869

Durability by brand — mixed results. B-ring BK3913 bearings on a FAW B50 (the X80's platform mate) show good durability in two reported cases: one unit at 200,000+ km with no noise, a second at 15,000 km with no issues yet — though one commenter (Victor) is skeptical of B-ring quality overall. Pricing recap: ILJIN rear hub ~5,450₽ vs. B-ring ~2,500₽. Cheaper bearings can fail early (an Astra-brand example: noise after only 7,000 km) while expensive brands can also fail unpredictably (a Koyo example: failure at just 2,000 km on a B50). Takeaway: quality is inconsistent across brands regardless of price; waterproofing grease during installation is reported to improve longevity.70717273747576

docs.title: Replacement procedure
docs.text:
Quick method (no special tools, about 1 hour at most). Remove the caliper, insert a bolt into a hole in the brake disc to stop it rotating while breaking the hub nut loose (36 mm socket, with leverage), then pull the hub off by hand — it comes free easily. Install the new hub, torque the nut and peen (stake) the nut collar to lock it. No puller or other special tool is required. Reassemble the caliper and wheel and drive.77787980

Other accounts. A 2025-04 report describes the same job as removing the brake caliper (суппорт) and unbolting the hub, with no difference between the left and right sides.818283 A detailed 2026-05 walkthrough corrects the socket size: use a 36 mm socket, not 32 mm, which is easy to assume incorrectly. Remove the caliper together with its mounting bracket (keep the two assembled), leave the brake disc in place (it is held on by friction alone; no bolts secure it to the hub), then replace the bearing. Clean the brake pads after removal with a dedicated pad-spreader tool. Hub nut torque is 240–270 Nm, achievable with a battery-powered impact driver. ILDJIN bearings (a Korean Mazda OEM supplier) were confirmed to work well and are endorsed by the community as a good-quality choice.495051525354

Cross-reference and swap notes. The rear hub assembly is listed for the X80 under FC012615X; a member says it also appears for the B50 under G14V2615XB or FA012615XB and looks identical, and a photographed YVA box is labelled FAW B50 FC012615X.848586 A complete rear hub for the FAW Besturn X80 NEW is listed under FA012615XB on Ozon (October 2025).87 One owner's rear hub swap took about one hour; the axle nut needed a 36 mm socket and a breaker pipe, which he had to borrow from neighbours.88

docs.title: Shock absorber fitment/quality issues
docs.text:
Tags: #shock-absorber · #price

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Some advice here concerns sub-zero winters and is less relevant in a hot climate.

Some shock absorbers (particularly budget-brand units) may arrive as a pair with visible inconsistencies: one strut carrying the factory barcode/labeling and the other without, or with different paint finishes (one painted, one bare metal). This may indicate mixed sourcing from different production runs within the same "pair." Recommendation: inspect both units on arrival and, where possible, install shock absorbers as a matched pair from the same supplier/batch 123456.

Cheap and unusual units. A front strut bought for about 1,900 RUB (RU market, September 2024) failed after a few kilometres: the piston rod bent and oil leaked, while a strut from another maker held; the owner adds that FAW springs do not fit the Mazda-type strut, so Mazda springs were used.7 A member bought the last KYB "New SR Special" units in Russia (NSF2065) and reports them better than stock; another owner who fitted them agreed, but one strut leaked after a small pothole in winter.89 More brand detail is in Shock absorbers — brand comparison and prices.

docs.title: Shock absorber replacement — parts and rear job
docs.text:
Tags: #shock-absorber · #mazda-6-compat

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.

Choosing replacement shocks. On pre-restyling (pre-facelift) X80 models, shock absorbers from the Mazda 6 GG / Mazda Atenza (1st generation, 2002–2007) can be used as direct replacements 123. Reported prices (RU market, 2024-09): shock absorbers approx. 1700 RUB (RU market, September 2024) per unit 45. Owners often install pneumatic air springs (пневмобалоны) at the same time as the shocks, to improve ride quality and load handling 6; they cost approx. 4500 RUB per pair (RU market, 2024-09), and a Belarusian brand was preferred for a softer ride 78.

Rear shock removal on a lift (2026-06 report). With the car on a lift, removing or installing a rear shock absorber is quick: using an air gun with an extension socket and a universal joint, all three mounting bolts take about 3 seconds each to remove. Access from below is generally straightforward; the main friction point is maneuvering the shock itself out through the wheel-well/mounting gap once unbolted, not the bolts themselves. The top shock-mount bolts are reachable but somewhat hidden and awkward — budget extra time for them versus the more straightforward bottom bolts 91011.

Rear shock removal without a lift — compress and tie. Rear shocks can be removed from underneath without a lift: compress the shock absorber (by hand or with a jack), bind it in the compressed position with cord or a tie-wrap, then extract it through the available clearance. Key safety point: the shock must stay bound while it is handled, since it will extend suddenly and forcefully if released — a real safety hazard, not just a convenience tip. Use the same compress-and-bind approach on the new shock before installation to make it easier to maneuver into place, and release the tie once it is seated. One owner successfully replaced both sides without a lift, cutting/trimming access where needed to fit tools and hands. This takes roughly 5–15 minutes per side, depending on bolt condition (seized bolts add significant time) and how much cutting/trimming for access is required 121314.

Part and bolt numbers. FAW X80 front shock absorbers: right 5CA034700 and left 5CA034900, shown in a December 2025 listing and in the catalogue; the catalogue lists the rear shock as 5CA028700A, with a store photo linking it.15161718 The rear shock mounting bolt cited for the X80 is Mazda 9YA0-2A-209 (also listed as FQ9YA02A209), as shown by exist.ru.19

docs.title: Shock absorber brands — owner verdicts
docs.text:
Tags: #shock-absorbers

Prices and suppliers on this page are Russian-market (RUB, at the dates shown). Verify locally before relying on them in Syria.
